Project Description and Technical Architecture

| 6.66 | **Built: the ANT stick works on Windows through Garmin's own libusb-win32 driver, and on Linux `ocw-desktop --install-udev-rule` (or *Install access for the ANT stick* on the Devices page) installs the access rule through `pkexec`** (14 Phase 17 Q7 (d), Q8 (b) *built (v6.61)*; 3.4.1, 17D *Built (Q7 / Q8)*). Windows: `ant::libusb0` loads the system's `libusb0.dll` (from the system folder only; nothing of libusb-win32 shipped or linked), finds `0fcf:1008` / `1009` by id, configuration 1, interface 0, the bulk endpoints from the configuration descriptor; `ant::Fallback` tries `nusb` (WinUSB) first, then it; a stick neither opens says *the stick needs a driver* and the Devices page explains Windows Update (Optional updates), Zadig as the fallback and one program at a time. Linux: the rule (`SUBSYSTEM=="usb"` and `=="tty"`, `0fcf:1004|1008|1009`, `MODE="0660"`, `TAG+="uaccess"`) in `/etc/udev/rules.d/60-ocw-ant.rules`, written by a root shell script through `pkexec` that then runs `udevadm control --reload-rules && udevadm trigger`; idempotent, never replaces a different rule without asking, refuses cleanly without pkexec / polkit (shows the rule and the manual command). Tested with a fake `libusb0` and a fake `pkexec`; the real-stick run waits for A4. |

| 6.54 | **Fixed: browsers join the Fly.io server reliably – the browser app opens a new connection (a new UDP flow) when a WebTransport handshake gets no answer, up to 3 more times; the cause is outside our control: Fly's UDP path now and then loses a whole new UDP flow, more often after many new flows in a row** (11.5 *Lost UDP flows*; may be renumbered at merge). New optional package section `PLCE` (`ocw_world::places`, pure and wasm-safe): OSM `place=city … isolated_dwelling` with `name`, the `name:*` of six languages, `population`, `capital` / `admin_level`, the position in package metres and a rank (city 0 … locality 5; capitals of countries and states one higher), from nodes and, where a place is only an area, the area's centroid; older readers skip it, packages without it load with no places, skeletons keep it. `world-builder package` writes it; `world-builder places --world PKG --pbf …` adds it to a built package with every other section unchanged. The studio's 2D map draws the names sized and weighted by rank and zoom through a greedy decluttering pass every frame (`layout_labels`: rank, population, last frame's labels, distance to the view's centre; a label only where its box overlaps none placed before it; a 4-point hysteresis so panning does not flicker); `studio map X Z M_PER_PX` sets the map's view. The **HUD navigation map** (both apps) fills its labels hook from the loaded packages' places and draws up to 8 names chosen by `ocw_map::labels::navi_labels`: cities and towns at every zoom level, villages from 6.5 m per point, hamlets and suburbs from 4, neighbourhoods from 2.5, localities from 1.6, decluttered by the same pass with its hysteresis and kept off the compass, scale, zoom and rider arrow; UI text over the turning map, so upright, with a day or night halo, and no tile redraws (3.2 Q8 stays open; this is the default meanwhile). Marge's packages rebuilt with the section into `data/places-build/` (not deployed): Liechtenstein 107 places (+4 KB), Black Forest north 1,418 / middle 1,994 / south 2,209 (+56 / +80 / +89 KB), Tenerife 1,823 (+76 KB); only `PLCE` differs. Root cause: the tests' `wait_for` drained the backend with `poll()` and returned at the first matching event, dropping the rest of that batch; `ocw_voice::livekit` reports `Connected` and the riders already in the room in one batch, so the waits for `Connected` threw the joins away (and the server's later `ParticipantUpdate`s, which it did send – seen in its debug log, protocol 17, SDK 0.10.1 single-PC path – arrived in the same batch). The app's `VoiceController` processes every polled event and was never affected. Fix: one shared `tests/support::wait_for` that keeps every polled event; no change to the backend, the SDK (`livekit` 0.10.1 stays) or the server pin. Tests: `backend_events` (the batch case, no network, part of `cargo test --workspace`); `livekit_two_participants` now starts its own `livekit-server` on free loopback ports when it finds the binary (`OCW_LIVEKIT_SERVER`, `~/.local/bin`, `PATH`; skipped without one), both riders must see and hear each other, and a second test runs two desktop `VoiceController`s through token, join, spatial subscription and hearing; `bundled_voice_server` / `make test-voice-bundled` check both directions instead of the KNOWN skip; new `make test-voice-livekit` |

A device is **remembered once it connected** (`devices.toml` in the config dir, or `--devices-file`; a `kind` per device; a file that cannot be written is named in the message), a trainer or power meter replaces the virtual trainer once connected, forgetting the last one brings it back; the HUD marks devices *connecting* / *reconnecting* / *not connected*. The browser's page has *Add a trainer / power meter / heart-rate strap* (its chooser), the same list and device pages, and remembers in `localStorage` once connected. Checked on marge with the Wahoo KICKR |

3.2.1 *Shared rides from the menu*, 6.2 *Join links*). **Join links** (`ocw_protocol::join`, pure and wasm-safe): `ocw://HOST[:PORT]?cert=SHA256[&world=ID[@VERSION]][&route=NAME][&name=…]` (port 47800), also `https://HOST:PORT?cert-hash=…` (WebTransport, 47801), a bare `HOST[:PORT]` with the fingerprint entered separately and a pasted `ocw-desktop --server … --server-cert …` line; plain errors ("the certificate fingerprint has 64 hex digits; got 12"); without a fingerprint only `localhost` / 127.x / `::1`. `ocw-server` prints the link(s) (the machine's LAN addresses for an unspecified bind) above "Clients connect with"; `ocw-kiosk.sh` puts them into `server-connect.txt`; `ocw-desktop --join LINK`. **The Ride page** became Events (the four event rows moved to their own page), Workouts, *Join a ride* / *Leave shared ride*, *Host a ride* (or, while hosting, *Hosting – N riders*, *Show join link*, *Stop hosting*), Restart, Back – at most seven items in every mode (`menu::model::RideMode`, items shown by `When`). **Join** (`ocw_client::join::JoinFlow`, `menu::join`, `ocw_ui::join`): a text field row (Enter types, Ctrl+V / ⌘V / the browser's paste event / *Paste link*; a gamepad character wheel), the fingerprint field when needed, Join, the last five servers (`joins.txt` / `localStorage`); the desktop connects in the background with the rider's hello without a world, learns the course from the `Welcome` (10 s timeout), finds the package among the installed worlds (missing: says so, with `--fetch-world URL` for a `world=` manifest URL), asks the trust dialog for an unknown key, loads it through the ride switch, checks the road graph's fingerprint and switches in one frame onto the same connection (the received messages are replayed to the new client); failures keep the ride (timeout, certificate, refusal / sign-in, world missing or another version). *Leave* rides on alone on the same course. The browser joins WebTransport links by starting the page again with `server=` / `cert-hash=` (an `ocw://` link: "no WebTransport … use the desktop app"; `?join=LINK` as a page option). **Host a ride** (`ocw_client::host`: world, route, date and time from the time machine's presets and day steps, weather simulated / real / a preset, bots 0–20 default 5, who changes time and weather, the port; summary, *Start hosting*): the desktop binds `0.0.0.0:PORT` first (a port in use offers to join the server there), keeps the certificate in `<data dir>/ocw/host-tls`, loads the course and runs it **in-process** (`LocalServer::spawn_hosting`: the local server's thread pumps a `NetServer`; no separate binary to package), rides on it as the host and shows the join links with the firewall / port forwarding hint (`host status`, *Copy link* via `arboard`); *Stop hosting* closes it ("server shutting down") and rides on alone with the same time and weather. Console: `join`, `leave`, `ride.join`, `ride.leave`, `join.edit|paste|go|cancel|continue`, `host start|status|stop|copy`, `host.plan`. Open: sign-in required on a hosted server (the row stays hidden until the app has the accounts backend's keys), the browser's join reloads the page (its ride ends then), the in-app world switch while hosting (stop hosting first). |

| 3.71 | **The trust dialog for user keys built** (asked by the user 2026-11-15: "implement showing a dialog that requires trusting the key (show fingerprint)"; 4.7 *User keys*, 12, 14 Phase 16, 16C): a user's own key (`world-builder keys init-user`: a root of their own, its signing key embeds the root's public key in every manifest) is checked with that root, so an intact package by an unknown user key is a new trust failure `UntrustedKey` that **no policy lets through** – the apps ask. The **fingerprint** is the SHA-256 of the raw public key in 16 groups of four hex digits (the key id is its first four); the signer's name is shown as claimed ("signed by 'Ada Rider' (unverified name)"). The **trust dialog** (shared menu model `ConfirmTrust`, both apps, keys / pad / mouse / touch, ten-foot sizes, the fingerprint drawn large): world, id, version, claimed signer, warning, data sources and licences; *Trust this key* (remembered), *Load once* (until the app quits), *Cancel* (focused; Back / Esc / B / closing decline). The **trusted user keys** (`ocw_worldstore::userkeys`: name, key, fingerprint, date, note) in `<data dir>/ocw/trusted-keys.json` (`$OCW_TRUSTED_KEYS`) or the browser's `localStorage`; a corrupt store trusts none and is not overwritten; built-in roots can neither be added nor overridden. *Settings → Account → Trusted world keys* lists and removes them (asks first); `world trust list | add | remove | show | accept | once | decline`. The World menu marks user-signed packages *unofficial, 'name'* or *unknown key, 'name'*. **Shared rides:** the server trusts only what its operator configured (`ocw-server --trust-key`, its account's `trusted-keys.json`; never a client); a client that does not trust the host's new world is asked and leaves the ride when it declines. Bad signatures and files that do not match are refused as before, never asked about. Tests: fingerprint, store, decision, dialog model, the shared-session path, screenshots |

Measured on Liechtenstein / Black Forest north / Tenerife: visible steps at T junctions with a median of 0.14 / 0.11 / 0.25 m (> 10 cm at 56 / 52 / 85 %, max 1.8–2.3 m, growing with the grade); z-fighting overlaps at about 70 %; verges on the other road at 53–84 %; wedge gaps at 61–77 % of way splits (the roundabout ring in Vaduz: 66 m²). Analysis test `junction_seams`, scenes `junction-*`; open questions 4.8.8 Q1–Q5 |

Tab in the console (desktop and browser) completes the word before the cursor: command names, subcommands, long flags and `PossibleValue`s from each command's clap definition, values known only at run time from per-command value providers (`ConsoleAppExt::console_values`: setting keys and values for `set` / `get`, world ids and test routes for `world switch`, the routes and worlds of `ride.switch`, weather presets / subcommands / fields / data sources / days, time presets and speeds, saved `camera.path` files, `help COMMAND`), only commands the session may run (no `dev` commands on a remote server).
