- *Tests:* `hud_fit` (desktop, tablet and VR-mirror sizes keep the scale 1 and the setting; the iPhone portrait / landscape fits, compact and narrow; the system on a window turned from portrait to landscape), `hud` (the compact top panel on the iPhone: at most 2 big and 5 lines, every line inside, in the top fifth / third; the HUD text on a desktop window unchanged and compact on a phone, the keys back after a key), the unchanged desktop fit tests; WebKit (`make test-web-webkit`): in both iPhone cases compact, at most 2 big and 5 lines, the top panel in the top quarter / third, no key line, nothing over the road's middle (35 – 65 % of the width, 40 – 75 % of the height), the top panel, top-right column, profile, map, Devices button and power buttons apart and on screen, the Devices panel collapsed; Safari on macOS (1280 × 720) not compact, scale 1, the keys shown, the Devices panel open, no power buttons.
- *Still open for phones:* a try on a real iPhone; the navigation map finds no room on a phone and stays hidden there (its rule: right of the junction fan's column and below the touch chevrons, at least 120 px) – a phone place for it is not decided; in portrait the touch tip's last line touches the page's Add to Home Screen tip (both go after the first touch); the junction fan, the workout and event panels and the menu were not looked at on a phone; the HUD size setting's 100 % on a phone is the compact size (a rider who wants it larger sets 150 %).

**Timestamp on every capture (decided 2026-11-12, v2.30):** the top-right column starts with a small ISO 8601 local time with UTC offset and seconds, e.g. `2026-11-12T22:14:05+01:00` (Fira Mono 14 px on a dark pill, above REC, the app message and the FPS counter; the event panel starts at 21 % of the height, below them), so every screenshot and every video frame shows when it was taken (the build diary, `ART-PROJECT.md` of [OCW-ART](https://github.com/newkit/OCW-ART)). It is **part of the capture, not of the optional HUD**: `hud off` and `display.hud` do not hide it, and it is drawn above every other UI (menus). Options considered: only while a screenshot or video is being taken (cleaner screen, but a screenshot captures the frame it is requested in, so the stamp would have to appear one frame early, and pictures the app does not take itself – OS screenshots, screen recorders, the kiosk photographed – would carry none), a setting (one more thing a test could leave off), **always visible (chosen):** a clock in the corner is common in games and costs a line of pixels. Clock: the wall clock in normal play, for screenshots and for live recordings (V); during frame capture (`--capture`) the wall clock at the start of the run plus the stepped game time (`Time<Real>`, advanced exactly 1/fps per frame), so the seconds advance once per 25 frames however slowly the frames render (`ocw-core::timestamp::MediaClock`). Formatting, the clock and the UTC offset (chrono's local zone, looked up once a second, daylight saving included) are pure functions with unit tests; the file metadata is described in 11.4.

**Photo preview (asked by the user 2026-11-17: "when a photo was taken, show it for 3 seconds in HUD"; built v4.74):** whenever a photo is saved – a screenshot (`screenshot`, its key and menu row; in the browser into the photos folder or as a download) or a ride photographer's photo (a person's or the drone's, 2.11) – a small framed thumbnail of it shows in the HUD for **3 s**, like a camera's review: a white polaroid-like frame with a soft drop shadow, the caption under the picture (*Photo saved* / *Photographer* / *Drone*, and where it went: "Saved to Pictures/OCW", "…, added to your ride", "Downloaded OCW-….jpg"), sliding in from the right and fading in and out over 0.2 s (`ocw_render::photo_preview`, both apps, WebGPU and WebGL 2). *Where:* the last item of the top-right column, under the time stamp, the app message, the Strava badge and the FPS counter – it moves with them, scales with the HUD size, and the bike computer's panel stays clear of it as of the rest of the column; its picture (192 px wide) narrows (down to 96 px) so the card ends above the lowest 40 % of the window (with the smallest picture under a full column on a small window with a large HUD: above the lowest quarter) – the lower right (the navigation map, the workout bar), the elevation profile, the voice HUD and the junction arrow stay free (test `the_card_fits_every_window`: every 16:9 and 4:3 size from 1280 × 720 to 3840 × 2160, HUD 100 – 200 % (over 150 % from 900 px high), a full column). *Several photos in a row:* the newest replaces the one shown at full opacity and shows its own 3 s; never a pile. *The picture:* the captured image already in memory, downscaled to a 384 px texture (3 × 3 samples per pixel), nothing read from disk. *Never in a photo or a video:* the preview is made after the capture (the screenshot's observer); the frame of the next photo has none (hidden while a `PhotoShot` screenshot of the window waits for its frame); the photographer's photos are rendered off-screen without UI. **While a video is recorded (desktop V, the browser's MediaRecorder) no preview shows at all** – videos take the HUD as seen (REC and the app message are in them), so a preview would be burned in; test captures (`--screenshot`, `--capture`) show the HUD as it is, the preview included. Setting `display.photo_preview` (default on; Settings → Display → Accessibility → *Photo preview*; console `hud.photo_preview on|off`); hidden with `hud off`. **VR:** to be off – the `vr` feature lives on the VR branch, which sets `PhotoPreview::enabled` false at start; the preview belongs on the VR bike computer later (14 Phase 11 X3). Tests: the lifetime (3 s, the fades and the slide), the newest wins (also during a fade-in), the thumbnail (averaged, BGRA → RGBA, the aspect kept), the switch, the HUD fit, and the preview never in the photo (none before the capture, hidden in the next photo's frame, none while recording). Open questions: Q10 and Q11 below.

- **Q10 – Open the photo from the preview: decided (2026-11-19, the user):** no – "no just show it for 3s"; the card stays a glimpse. *Was asked:* the small card that shows a new photo for 3 s (top right) is only a glimpse – nothing can be done with it. Should a click on it (or a key while it shows) open the photo full size – on the desktop in the system's image viewer, in the browser from the chosen folder – or should it stay a glimpse? Nothing built. Proposal: open it on a click; no extra key.
- **Q11 – The preview during events: decided (2026-11-19, the user):** keep it over the panel – "Put it over, it's only visible for a short time" (c, as built). *Was asked:* in an event (a race or a group ride) the standings panel sits in the top right corner, and the photo card appears in the same corner, covering the panel's top for its 3 s. Options: (a) move the card left of the panel; (b) show no card during events; (c) keep it as built, it is only 3 s. Proposal: a.


**GPS position:** bottom-left, the HUD shows the local rider's position as latitude / longitude (5 decimals, N/S, E/W) and altitude in metres, unprojected from the predicted position with the route's or world package's geographic origin (the same as the FIT track); hidden on routes without one (built-in test routes), and with `hud.gps off` / setting `display.gps` (on by default). Console: `rider.gps` (both apps; the browser's `?origin=LAT,LON` gives its test route a geographic origin). Its place: the bottom-left column, under the elevation profile (the damage widget is in the top-left panel, the junction overlay at the bottom centre). **Restored in v3.43:** route rides on world packages had lost it since fae1547 (the route ride's placeholder route dropped the package's geographic origin); regression tests check the view fill and the HUD. The HUD panel never extends past the window: long lines break at their " | " separators (then at commas) to fit the window width.

**Navigation map (planning and built, 2026-11-17, v4.73; asked by the user: "add a map similar to the 2d map in the world builder to the HUD (lower right corner). make it look like on a bike navi."):** both apps show a bike computer's map screen in the lower right corner of the HUD.
- *The device:* a rounded dark bezel (radius 14 px, 2 px edge) holding, on top, the **next-turn banner** – a turn arrow drawn at the exit's real angle (U-turn hook beyond ±150°), the distance rounded as a navi does (5 m steps below 100 m, 10 m below 300 m, 50 m below 1 km, then 0.1 km; imperial: 50 ft steps, then 0.1 mi; "now" at the junction) and the street after the turn ("↱ 250 m Street name"; the exit that will be taken – the selected one in free ride, in route rides the junction view's selection); without a junction ahead the street ridden now with a straight arrow. Below it the **map screen** (240 × 264 px at 100 %), **heading-up**: the map turns with the road's direction (smoothed, 0.45 s; a U-turn turns it at once), the rider's arrow fixed at 70 % of its height (the lower third) and turned by the rider's own heading against the road; a compass needle (top right), a scale bar (bottom left: 1, 2, 5 × 10ⁿ m / ft / mi) and the zoom ("AUTO 4" / "ZOOM 3", bottom right).
- *The map:* land use as soft fills (forest, meadow, farmland, settled, industrial, park, rock, glacier) and water from the package's land-use cells, buildings as small blocks from zoom 2.2 m/px in, roads by class with a casing (trunk / primary / secondary wider and yellow, minor roads white, tracks and paths brown and thinner, cycleways blue; minor classes leave as the map zooms out; tunnels dashed), the **route bold in magenta with a white casing** (route rides: the route 4 km ahead; free ride: the path chosen through the junctions so far and the preview ahead with the selected exit and the defaults after it), the path behind dimmer, the **next junction's other exits** thin in grey-blue for 200 m, other riders as blue dots. **Day / night:** a dark palette from civil twilight (sun below −4°, back to day above −2°, `ocw_map::navi::Daylight`). Only the package's own data (spec 4), never map tiles.
- *Zoom:* seven levels (0.6, 1.0, 1.6, 2.5, 4, 6.5, 10 m per map point: about 150 m to 2.4 km across). **Auto zoom** (`ocw_map::navi::AutoZoom`): the road of the next 25 s at the rider's speed (at least 120 m) above the rider; a junction closer than 250 m zooms in to show it and 80 m beyond; it zooms in at once and out only after 2.5 s; the shown scale eases (0.35 s). Key **Z** (`keys.map_zoom`, Settings → Controls → Keys and buttons → Navigation map) steps auto → 1 … 7 → auto; console `hud.map.zoom auto|1-7|in|out|next`; setting `display.map_zoom` (auto).
- *On / off:* key **N** (`keys.map`), console `hud.map [on|off]`, setting `display.map` (on by default); Settings → Display → **HUD** is a page now (HUD, Navigation map, Map zoom, GPS line; the Display page keeps six rows). Hidden with `hud off`, without a local rider (the studio) and when the window has no room for the least map (120 px wide); **shown in Unicorn flight** (v5.06, Q7, below).
- *Unicorn flight (v5.06, Q7):* **north-up, centred on the unicorn** (`navi_map::map_pose`: the unicorn's position, its arrow turned to its heading, `FLIGHT_ANCHOR` 0.5 / 0.5 eased from the riding anchor in 0.35 s) – not heading-up: the unicorn banks, circles and looks around freely, so a heading-up map would spin with every turn, and from the air a map that stays put reads like the land below. The banner gives the height above the ground and the speed with the compass heading ("120 m up", "54 km/h, heading 080 E"); the **auto zoom** (`AutoZoom::update_flight`, `ocw_map::navi::flight_level`) shows the ground of 25 s of flight at its speed, at least three times the height above the ground and 120 m, over half the map's height, with the same 2.5 s hold before zooming out. N and the zoom keys work in flight too.
- *Layout* (`ocw_render::navi_map::fit_map`, pure): right 12 px, bottom 24 px (the version label stays visible), always right of the junction fan and of the elevation profile, below every HUD box of its column (the top panel, the top-right column with time stamp / REC / FPS, the event panel, the touch chevrons: marked `MapAvoid`, their boxes of the last frame); the widest map that fits (down to 120 px), all in UI px so it scales with the HUD size. The workout panel no longer shares the corner (v5.06, Q1): it keeps clear of the map instead. Browser: the Devices panel and its button step above the map (`window.ocw.hudMap()`: shown, its box in CSS px, the banner, the zoom, night, `flight` and `centre`, the workout panel's box).
- *The workout panel's place (v5.06, Q1):* **the left column, under the bike computer's panel** (and the damage widget in it), above the voice panel and the elevation profile. `ocw_render::workout::fit_workout` (pure) drops the panel from the top margin (12 px) of the left column to the first place 8 px clear of every HUD box – the `MapAvoid` boxes (top panel, top-right column with the photo preview, event panel, touch chevrons), the voice panel and the elevation profile's column (`WorkoutAvoid`), the map and, while a junction is ahead, the junction fan – so on an everyday ride it sits right under the top panel; where the full panel (320 × about 190 px at 100 %) does not fit it is shown **compact** (the target and the lines, without the title and the profile chart, 6 px padding, about 100 px high), then the same in the middle column; where even that finds no room the **elevation profile yields** (with the GPS line; the workout's own profile replaces it while the workout runs – `place_workout`, the profile's last box kept so hiding it does not bring it back at once); only when nothing is free it is hidden rather than drawn over another box. Measured over every supported size (`the_workout_panel_fits_every_window_beside_the_map`): in full under the top panel at every size up to 125 % on an everyday ride and at 150 % from 1600 × 900 up, compact at 150 % on 1280 × 720 and 1366 × 768 (in the scene `navi-workout-720p-150`, whose top panel is taller, the elevation profile yields); without voice and junction fan always shown, except 1024 × 768 at 150 % with the longest top-panel lines (the top panel then reaches 24 px above the bottom); hidden with the voice panel on the small windows at 125 – 150 % and while a junction fan shows there. Why there: the top panel is as wide as the window minus the top-right column, so the top centre lies under it; the top-right column holds the time stamp, REC, the FPS counter, the photo preview and the event standings, and is the map's column; the bottom centre is the junction fan's – the left column is the one place free on every window, its 300 px profile chart lines up with the elevation profile of the same width below it, and the target and the time left stay near the bike computer's numbers.
- *Drawing:* the map is rasterised on the CPU (tiny-skia, pure Rust, the same pixels everywhere) into tiles of 128² texels, cached in a **wrap-around ring texture** per zoom level and look (`ocw_map::ring::Ring`: tile (ix, iz) in slot (ix mod n, iz mod n), n from the map's reach, 4 – 16); as the rider moves only the tiles coming in are drawn, nearest first, within 2.5 ms per frame (the visible ones always). A UI material (`navi_map.wesl`) turns the north-up texture heading-up on the GPU every frame, masks undrawn slots and rounds the screen's corners. A new zoom level or look fills a second ring in the background and swaps when its visible tiles are there; the route layer is its own ring texture, redrawn when the route changes (every 400 m, a junction choice). Texel density follows the screen (HUD scale × window scale, 1 – 1.5 texels per point). Nothing is re-tessellated per frame. WebGPU and WebGL 2 alike (two textures, one uniform block of vec4s).
- *Shared with the studio:* crate **`ocw-map`** (Bevy-free, wasm): the projections (`MapView` of the studio, `NaviView` heading-up), the studio map's data (`MapData`, moved from `apps/studio/src/map.rs`, which keeps its egui painting), road styles and the scale bar, the navigation map's source (the world set's loaded packages read in place, the joined road graph with a 250 m grid index), ring, rasteriser, icons, zoom / banner / route rules and the place-name hook.
- *Place names (v4.77):* the loaded packages' places (section `PLCE`, 4.7) fill `NaviMapLabels` whenever the world set changes (`ocw_map::labels::labels_of`: in home metres through each package's frame, each place once). `ocw_map::labels::navi_labels` picks what to draw: by the zoom – cities and towns at every level, villages from 6.5 m per point (levels 1–6), hamlets and suburbs from 4, neighbourhoods from 2.5, localities and isolated dwellings from 1.6 –, the name's box inside the screen (6 points in) and clear of the compass, the scale, the zoom and the rider's arrow (`navi_marks`), then decluttered by the studio map's `layout_labels` (rank, population, last frame's names as hysteresis, distance to the rider), at most 8. They are UI text nodes over the map (centred above the place, 13.5 / 12.5 / 11.5 / 10.5 / 10 points by rank), so they stay upright while the map turns heading-up and cost no tile redraws; dark with a white halo by day, light with a black halo at night. Packages without `PLCE` have no names. **Peaks and passes (v5.03, Q8):** the packages' section `LMRK` (4.7) adds the named peaks as "▲ Teide 3715 m" and the passes as ")( Boca de Tauce 2055 m" (")( 1800 m" for a pass without a name; the elevation from `ele`, else the terrain's), in the same pills and colours as the settlements, at 10.5 points; decluttered together with them by `layout_labels` with towns keeping their priority (`ocw_map::labels::layout_rank`: cities, towns, then a pass the route crosses, villages, then the peaks and passes – the higher first –, then the smaller places); named from 6.5 m per point in (levels 1–6, with the villages: in the mountains a peak lies mostly 1–3 km off the road, out of the closer levels' 1 km); **a pass the route crosses** (within 80 m of the route's path ahead or behind, `route_crosses`, recomputed with the route layer) is named at every zoom whenever it is on the map. Viewpoints are not named on the maps. Tests: the names at the zoom levels, no overlap with each other or the marks at four headings, steady while riding on, the labels from packages with frames and overlaps.
- *Tests:* the projection and the heading-up rotation (to_screen / to_world, the shader's texel axes, north), the heading smoothing, auto zoom (speed, junction, hold), zoom modes, the banner's distance and street, day / night with hysteresis, route highlighting (layers, widths, colours; route ahead / behind, free ride exits; the cache key), the ring (window, wrap-around slots, only new tiles missing), deterministic tile rendering for a fixed position (the same bytes twice; forest, water, building, roads, outside at their pixels; night; far zoom), the route layer, the icons, the road index, the toggle and zoom commands, the settings and menu rows, and **no overlap** with the elevation profile, the junction fan, the voice panel, the top panel (its tallest case) and the top-right column at every 16:9 size from 1280 × 720 to 3840 × 2160 and 4:3, HUD at 100 – 150 %; the workout panel at the same sizes with the map, an everyday and the tallest top panel, with and without voice (never over another box, in full on an everyday ride, compact or hidden only where nothing else fits; v5.06), the flight's pose, banner and zoom, D-pad down's zoom binding. Scenes `navi-*` (Liechtenstein, Black Forest, Tenerife; free ride and route; day and night; 1280 × 720 at 150 %).
- *Cost:* measured on marge (release, headless Wayland on software Vulkan, 1920 × 1080, 40 s of free ride through Vaduz with three bots; scenes `navi-fps-on` / `navi-fps-off`): 38.6 fps with the map, 38.5 fps without – within the noise; the tiles of a zoom change or of the first frame show as one longer frame (92 ms worst against 69 ms). **On the AMD GPU on a quiet machine (v4.87; 4.6.2 *Frame-rate cost* has the method and the table):** at 1920 × 1080 High the map costs +0.02 ms in the Black Forest, +0.02 ms on a Vaduz street, +0.02 ms at Masca and +0.06 ms at Puerto de la Cruz – Teide (three rounds each, single rounds −0.16 … +0.14 ms); at Medium +0.04 … +0.09 ms, at 1280 × 720 at most +0.15 ms (one Black Forest round +0.46) – within or near the noise, nothing to cut. `hud.map` without an argument toggles the map (a benchmark must not ask it for the state). Not yet measured in the browser.
- **Open questions of the navigation map (not decided):**
  - **Q1 – Size and place: decided (2026-11-19, the user), built (v5.06):** "find a better location for the workout panel" – the map keeps its size and place; the workout panel moves elsewhere so the two no longer compete. *Built:* the workout panel's place is the left column under the bike computer's panel (*The workout panel's place* above). *Was asked:* the navi map is 240 × 264 px at 100 % HUD size in the lower right corner. Should it be larger, smaller, or a setting? There is also a space conflict: during a **workout** the workout panel needs the same corner, and the map shrinks or hides when there is no room; during an **event** the standings can push it out. Should the map take precedence, or the other panel move? Proposal: a size setting (small / medium / large); the workout panel and the standings keep precedence.
  - **Q2 – The browser's Devices panel: decided (2026-11-19, the user), built (v5.06):** (b) and a transparent overlay – "b and make it an transparent overlay": once a device is connected the panel collapses to a button, and the panel is a transparent overlay. *Built:* a 32 % veil with a text shadow and translucent buttons, the ride shows through and clicks beside the buttons reach it; 2 s after a device connects it collapses to a "Devices ● name 250 W" button, a click opens it again (× collapses it by hand); it still steps above the map and aside for the menu (`window.ocwDevicesPanel()` for the tests). *Was asked:* in the browser app the panel for connecting the trainer or the heart-rate strap sat in the lower right too; it now steps up above the map. Options: (a) keep it there; (b) once a device is connected, collapse it to a small button so it is out of the way; (c) move it elsewhere. Proposal: b.
  - **Q3 – The look: decided (2026-11-19, the user):** keep the colours. *Was asked:* the colours now: the route magenta with a white edge (as on many Garmin / Wahoo computers), the rider's arrow orange, the turn banner dark green, and a dark map from dusk on. Keep them, choose others, or follow a general HUD colour setting (e.g. colour-blind-safe or high contrast)? Proposal: keep them; high contrast later with the other HUD settings.
  - **Q4 – Auto zoom: decided (2026-11-19, the user):** keep the numbers. *Was asked:* in auto mode the map shows about 25 s of road ahead at the current speed, zooms in from 250 m before a junction, and waits 2.5 s before zooming out again. Are these numbers right, and should it also zoom in on steep climbs or descents, e.g. to show hairpins? Proposal: keep the numbers; zoom in on hairpins on descents.
  - **Q5 – Route rides: decided (2026-11-19, the user):** nothing – the banner stays as built (junction turns and the street name). *Was asked:* on a fixed route the banner shows the next turn only at real junctions, otherwise the street name. A route can also bend sharply without a junction. Should the banner also (a) announce the route's own sharp bends, computed from its shape, and (b) show the distance to the finish? Proposal: b always, a only for hairpins.
  - **Q6 – Gamepad: decided (2026-11-19, the user), built (v5.06):** yes, the zoom on a d-pad direction. *Built:* **D-pad down** steps the zoom (auto → 1 … 7 → auto; `pad.map_zoom`, in flight too). No d-pad direction was free (up: faster, down: stop, left / right: the junction exits); "stop" gives up D-pad down and keeps the left stick down and the left trigger (`pad.stop` none, rebindable) – the exits have no other pad input and "faster" adds 25 W per press, which the stick and the trigger do not. *Was asked:* on the keyboard N turns the map on and off and Z steps the zoom; a gamepad has no buttons for them yet. Give them gamepad buttons (e.g. a long press on a shoulder button, the zoom on a d-pad direction)? Proposal: yes, the zoom on a d-pad direction.
  - **Q7 – Unicorn flight: decided (2026-11-19, the user), built (v5.06):** show the map centred on the unicorn – "show the map centred on the unicorn". *Built:* north-up, centred on the unicorn, auto zoom by speed and height (*Unicorn flight* above). *Was asked:* while flying the unicorn (Unicorn mode) the map is hidden. Should it show instead – north up, centred on the unicorn – to help find the way from the air? Proposal: yes.
  - **Q8 – Place names: decided in part (2026-11-19, the user: "yes" to adding peaks and passes):** the navi map also names **mountain peaks and passes** once the packages carry them (2.11 Q4); the settlement defaults below stay. **Peaks and passes built (v5.03)**, see *Place names* above. Was: when the place data lands, which places (towns only, villages, peaks, passes) and from which zoom? *Built in v4.77 as the default until answered:* settlements only (no peaks or passes – the package has no such data yet), cities and towns at every zoom, villages and smaller places closer in (thresholds above).
  - **Q9 – The studio map: decided (2026-11-19, the user):** yes, as a View option, low priority. *Was asked:* OCW Studio's 2D map is drawn its own way (egui) but shares the geometry, projection and styles with the game's navi map. Should the studio also offer a navi-look preview (the same rasteriser), showing exactly how an area will look on the bike computer? Proposal: yes, as a View option, low priority.

**Camera and avatar (v1.9):** the chase camera follows the avatar itself (on the terrain when off the road) along the rider's own heading; it can be orbited with the mouse. It stays above everything camera-solid and lifts until the line of sight to the rider clears it; its look-at point is smoothed. **Tunnels:** where the road runs under the terrain (the terrain more than 0.5 m above the road centre over at least 10 m, gaps under 20 m merged; found by the client from its track and the ground, so route files, package routes and free ride all work without extra package data), the client draws a simple tube (floor, walls, arch, 1 m beside the road edge, 6 m high, unlit and dark with a strip of lamps along the crown, since sunlight and tree shadows would reach through the hill) reaching 4 m out of the hill at each end as the portal. From 15 m before it until 12 m after it the camera (any mode) blends over 0.4 s into a tunnel camera on the road 4.5 m behind and 2.2 m above the rider, looking 10 m ahead; terrain and buildings above do not lift it, the mouse orbit is ignored there. **Portals cut into the terrain (decided, replaces the eye under the hillside):** at a portal the hillside slopes through the tube (the 10 m terrain grid cannot form a vertical face), so riding in, the camera saw a dark-green wall of hillside inside the tube for a second or more (scene `tunnel-video`, Steg tunnel at km 8.77). The terrain is now drawn with its own material (`ocw-render::tunnel_cut`, a `StandardMaterial` extension) whose fragment shader discards terrain fragments inside the tube – walls up to 4 m, then the arch up to the 6 m crown, from the road surface up, following the gradient – given as up to 64 straight 2 m pieces along the track where the terrain beside or over the road is less than 1.5 m above the crown (the portals; the nearest to the rider, updated with the tunnel scan). The cut is exact to the pixel along the tube, which is drawn double-sided, so the portal shows the tube's mouth in the hillside and the eye stays at its place behind the rider (before, it dived close behind the rider and under the terrain once the wheels were covered, which still showed the hillside for a few frames and then jumped). Regression test: `the_terrain_inside_the_tube_is_cut_at_the_portal` (`ocw-render`). Considered and not chosen: tunnel stretches written into the route file / taken from the graph's `tunnel` flag (route files have no flags; tunnels the terrain does not cover need no special camera), removing whole terrain cells around the tube (10 m holes larger than the tube show the inside of the hill), and lowering the camera only (rider still hidden by the hill in curves without a tube). The avatar stands on the surface under both wheel contacts (front wheel first over a bump), leans by atan(v² κ / g) for the curve it rides, and is blended from road height onto the ground over 2 m beside the road.

**Sun, overlays and tunnels (v2.41):** with the sun following the time of day (v2.33) shadows are long at low sun, so what lies flat on a surface casts none: road markings, package road strips and the test-route ribbon carry `FlatOverlay`, which requires `NotShadowCaster` (they still receive shadows, so a marking in a tree's shadow stays shaded; regression test `markings_and_flat_overlays_cast_no_shadows`). The terrain casts no shadows in the renderer (for speed), so only the tube's thin shell stood between a low sun and the rider in a tunnel, and light leaked through in shadow-map squares: the direct sun now fades out over the first 25 m behind a portal (`tunnel::daylight_share`) and is off deeper inside, with the bike lights on there in `auto` mode (tests `no_direct_sun_inside_a_tunnel`, `no_direct_sun_on_the_rider_in_a_tunnel`). **Route files in world packages:** a route file (`world-builder route`) and a package built from different terrain (swissALTI3D vs SRTM: the kiosk on 2026-11-13, after a deploy rebuilt the package with an older builder) differ by metres in height while their roads coincide in plan; the rider sank up to 15 m into the drawn road before the Steg tunnel and the tunnel finder made one 1.7 km tunnel from km 8.2, whose tube the hillside and the real road cut through (broken ceiling, terrain squares inside). The desktop therefore fits a route file's heights onto the package's road strips when they differ anywhere by more than 0.25 m (`ocw_world::route_fit`: the strip under each point that continues the route's height, the offset interpolated across tunnels and gaps; with a warning in the log; not for a remote server, which rides the file as it is). Test `pilot_tunnel` (`ocw-render`) checks it on the real pilot data: the rider on the road at km 8.40–8.77 and one Steg tunnel at km 8.80–9.52.

**Gradient feel:** the gradient at the rider alone does not tell how the road goes on, and a level chase camera makes climbs look flat (the terrain beside the road is a surface model and need not follow the road's gradient, 4.3). Three aids, computed Bevy-free in `ocw-world::gradient` on the rider's `Track`:

- **Average gradient ahead:** the main HUD line shows the gradient at the rider and, in brackets, the average over the next 100 m (height difference over horizontal distance), e.g. `+9.4 % (100 m +7.8 %)`. Where the track ends sooner (a route's finish), the known part counts (at least 10 m, else the gradient at the rider).
- **Mini elevation profile** (bottom left, above the GPS line; console `hud.profile on|off`, on by default): the road from 150 m behind to 1.5 km ahead, sampled every 15 m on a fixed grid of the track distance (the samples stay on the road while the rider moves), drawn as bars with a white rider marker and a caption with the climbing and descending ahead. Heights are scaled to their range, widened to at least 40 m so a flat road stays flat (≈ 8× vertical exaggeration on the 300 × 56 px box); the lowest point keeps 8 % of the height. Bars are coloured by gradient band: < −2 % blue (descent), −2 … 3 % green, 3 … 6 % yellow, 6 … 9 % orange, 9 … 12 % red, ≥ 12 % wine red; behind the rider dimmed. Nothing is drawn where the track is not known (before the start, after a route's finish).
- **Look-ahead in free ride:** the path is only known up to the next undecided junction (5.2), so the HUD looks ahead on a display-only copy, `RidePath::preview`: extended as if the rider rode on, at the next junction with the exit currently selected (the default if none), at later ones with the default exit (route mode: the route's exit), with the automatic U-turns at dead ends and the region border. It is rebuilt when the path or the selection changes; a different choice later simply changes the preview.
- **Camera tilt** (console `camera.tilt on|off|FRACTION`): the chase orbit is turned around the rider's right axis by 0.7 of the road's slope angle (gradient averaged from 5 m behind to 20 m ahead, low-pass with a 1.2 s time constant, capped at ±8°; snapped after a teleport). Uphill the eye drops behind the rider and looks up the road, downhill it rises. The tilt is applied before the solid-object rules below, so the camera still stays above the slope and buildings; mouse orbit and C (reset) are relative to the tilted frame. Side and top views are not tilted.

**What moves the camera:** every world object is in one of two classes (`CameraInteraction` in `ocw-render::camera`):

| Class | Objects | Camera |
|---|---|---|
| **Solid** | Terrain, road, buildings | Avoids them: stays above them (and 0.5 m away from walls) and lifts until the line of sight to the rider clears them. Terrain comes from the ground height function; every other solid object registers the height of its top per tile as a camera obstacle layer, removed with the tile (buildings: footprint prisms up to the ridge, courtyards counted as solid, grid-indexed). |
| **See-through** | Trees; later bushes, signs, other riders | Never change the camera position. Where one would block the view – within ~3 m of the lens, or in a cone around the line of sight from the camera to the rider (≈0.8 m radius at the camera, 2 m at the rider, ending 1 m before the rider) – it is faded out with screen-door transparency (ordered dither in the fragment shader; no blending, so depth sorting stays opaque and the shadow stays). |

The interface is divided into modules:

- Dashboard.
- Training view.
- Multiplayer lobby.
- Device management.
- Bicycle editor.
- Character editor.
- Settings.
- Route selection.

These modules are reached through the in-game menu (3.2.1); the dashboard of 2.1 is its start page once accounts exist (Phase 5).

#### 3.2.1 In-Game Menu

One menu, reachable during a ride and (later) as the start screen, replaces command-line options and console commands for everyday use. The console (2.9) stays the power-user path; both drive the same functions.

**Opening and pausing**

| | Keyboard / mouse | Gamepad | Touch (v2.54, 3.2.2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open / close | Esc (closes the console first if it is open) | Start / Menu (☰, Options) | tap ☰ (top left) |
| Move focus | ↑ ↓ ← →, Tab / Shift+Tab, mouse hover | D-pad, left stick (with repeat) | – (taps act directly) |
| Confirm | Enter, Space, click | South (A / ✕) | tap |
| Back (one page up; closes at the top) | Esc, Backspace, right click | East (B / ○) | on-screen Back button, swipe in from the left |
| Change a value (slider, choice) | ← / → on the focused row, mouse drag / wheel | D-pad / stick left / right, shoulder buttons for big steps | tap ‹ ›, drag the slider |
| Switch tab | Q / E, PgUp / PgDn | LB / RB (L1 / R1) | tap the tab, swipe on the tab bar |

- While the menu is open, ride inputs (↑ power, ← → steering, A, W, U, R, V, …) are **not** passed to the ride; one input-context resource (`Ride`, `Menu`, `Console`) replaces today's per-system `console.is_open()` checks. The power from the trainer keeps flowing.
- **The ride never pauses (decided, v2.2):** the menu is an overlay over the running ride, in single-player exactly as in multiplayer (in a shared ride the others keep riding, so one rider's menu cannot stop time). The trainer is left as it is (SIM keeps following the road, ERG keeps its target), the ride time and the FIT recording continue. While the menu is open, steering falls back to autodrive and junctions take the default exit (2.2.1), so the rider stays on the road; the previous steering mode is restored on closing. Pages that would end the ride (Ride, Restart) ask for confirmation.
- **Esc never quits** (decided, v2.2): only *Quit* in the menu ends the app (kiosk-safe).
- The top page shows a status strip: power, speed, connected trainer, Strava sync state.

**Interaction design**

- **Ten-foot UI:** the app is used on a trainer, often from 2–3 m away and with a gamepad. Text at least 3 % of the window height (scales with it), high contrast, a clearly visible focus frame, at most about seven rows per page, no hover-only functions, no text input where a choice works (names and titles get an on-screen keyboard on the gamepad).
- **Every page fits the window (decided):** all menu sizes are in % of the window height, so a page that fits a 16:9 window fits every 16:9 size (1280 × 720 and up). The panel is 110 % of the window height wide (at most 94 % of its width), an empty status or description line takes no room, and the description texts are short enough that every page – sub pages with the full seven items of a paged list too – fits into 94 % of the height with all its text (unit test `every_menu_page_fits_a_16_9_window_with_its_text`; `ocw-render::menu::page_height_vh` adds up the layout, wrapping text as the monospaced UI font does). In a narrower window a page that would still be too tall drops description paragraphs from the end, never items. Before, the Ride page (seven items, two paragraphs) ran off the bottom at 1280 × 720 and cut off *Back*.
- **Focus navigation** works identically for keyboard and gamepad (spatial navigation between focusable items, a page stack for Back); the mouse is optional. Mouse and touch reach every item too (v2.54, 3.2.2: reachability tested per device on every page; touch-mode hit targets ≥ 9 mm / 48 px). Every item is reachable without a mouse, in the kiosk's borderless fullscreen (11.2).
- **Values change in place** (slider, ← / → choice) and apply immediately; there is no "Apply" button. Settings are saved when the menu closes. Device scans and Strava actions show their progress inline.
- **Rendering: Bevy UI** for the whole menu, as for the HUD (3.2): it shares the HUD's theme and scaling, renders in the same window and screenshot / capture paths, and Bevy's input-focus and directional-navigation support fits gamepad control; egui's gamepad navigation is weak and it looks like a tool, not a game. egui stays for the console, dev panels and, in Phase 4, the advanced parameter panels of the editors (3.2); the Workshop's main selection is Bevy UI.

**Architecture**

- **State:** a Bevy state `UiMode { Ride, Menu }` (the console stays an overlay flag); ride systems run only in `Ride` or check the input context. The menu itself is a **Bevy-free model** in `apps/desktop` (like `ClientCore`): the page tree, page stack, focused item, item values. Input is translated into abstract actions (`Up`, `Down`, `Left`, `Right`, `Confirm`, `Back`, `TabNext`, `TabPrev`); `ocw-render::menu` only draws a `MenuView` resource, as the HUD draws `RideView`.
- **Actions are console commands.** Each menu item either runs a command line (`trainer.difficulty 60`, `devices.connect 2`, `strava.sync`, `reset`) through `ConsoleState::queue`, or reads / writes a setting variable. Menu, console, `--cmd` and `autoexec.cfg` therefore share one code path, and every menu function is scriptable and testable headless.
- **Settings: one registry, one file.** Settings are variables with a name, type, range, default and an apply function (`set controls.autodrive_default on`, `get trainer.difficulty`, 2.9). They persist in `<user config dir>/ocw/settings.toml` (sections like the menu: `[controls]`, `[trainer]`, `[audio]`, `[display]`, `[profile]`, `[ride]` for the last world / route). Precedence: defaults < `settings.toml` < `autoexec.cfg` < command-line options; command-line options and `set --temp` apply only to the session and are not saved. Unknown keys are kept and reported, invalid values fall back to the default with a warning. Device memory (`devices.toml`), Strava credentials and tokens (`strava.toml`, `strava-token.toml`) stay in their own files – tokens never go into the settings file.
- **Starting another ride** (Ride page; decided in M3): an **in-app switch**, not the restart path – the process, the window and the devices stay. (The earlier plan, writing the choice to `[ride]` and re-executing the app, was dropped: a re-exec reconnects the BLE trainer, which takes seconds and can fail.) Nothing is written to `[ride]` yet; the app still starts with its command line.
- **Implemented (M3):**
  - *Ride choice* (`apps/desktop/src/ride/choice.rs`, Bevy-free): a test route (hills, loop), a route file, or a world package in free ride (random start or `--start X,Z`), on a route of the package by name or an `ocw-graph-route` file, on a GPX file matched at the start, or with a route file. It is built from the command line, from the console command `ride.switch --route NAME | --route-file FILE | --world PKG [--free-ride] [--start X,Z] | --world PKG --route NAME|FILE | --world PKG --route-gpx FILE` (a world alone is a free ride) and turns back into the ride options of the arguments; on the command line `--world PKG` without a route option (`--route`, `--route-file`, `--route-gpx`, `--free-ride`, `--start`) rides the package's first route (section `ROUT`), else a free ride (with `--server` always a free ride, as `ocw-server --world` alone), and logs which (before, it rode the built-in hills test route through the package's terrain, with the camera in a hillside; a package without a road graph still gets the test route); any route option wins, e.g. the kiosk's own `--route-file` over a `--world` from its defaults file, so the start and the switch share one setup (`ride/setup.rs`: route, route-file terrain, package with neighbours and road network, free-ride start or route plan; errors are messages, not exits). `ride.current` prints the current ride as a `ride.switch` line; `ride.restart` starts it again.
  - *Switch sequence* (`ride/mod.rs`): the new ride is loaded on a background thread (package reading and verification, neighbours, road network, GPX matching) while the old one goes on; the HUD notice says "Loading … ". A failed load keeps the ride and says why. When it is loaded, in one frame: the ride so far is saved as a FIT file like on exit (under a minute: dropped) and handed to the Strava sync; the ride options, `WorldInfo`, `PackageWorld` and `FreeRideSetup` are replaced and the `RideView` gets the new route; a new session starts (`connection::start_session`: dropping the old local server's link ends its thread, a new local server – threaded, or stepped in frame capture – and a new `ClientCore` join, with the rider profile active *now*: the Workshop's rider and bike choice applies from the next ride, not only the next start); the recorder starts a new ride, the ride time starts at 0 (`SessionStart`), and `ocw_render::rebuild_scene` despawns the old world (light, terrain, road, trees, streamed tiles, camera obstacles, avatars) and spawns the new one from the new `RideView` / `PackageWorld`. Devices (BLE trainer, sensors, gamepads), the trainer mode (SIM / ERG, difficulty), a running workout, the camera, HUD, menu and console stay; a running local event (2.3) ends with its session (server and client are new) and its HUD state is cleared. **A video recording continues** (decided): it records the window, and the switch is part of what the user sees; V stops it as before. With `--server` (a remote server) the switch is refused: the server chooses the course.
  - *R after a switch* restarts the current ride **in the app** (decided): the process' command line would start the first ride again. Without a switch, R still re-executes the app.
  - *Menu:* Ride → *Change ride* (a sub page next to the event rows; since v2.39 *World → Change world*, see *World menu*) lists *World packages* (the newest version of each package in the cache and the `.ocwpkg` files next to the executable – the kiosk installs one there –, in `data/` and `data/pilot/` of the working directory and in the directory of the package ridden now; one package: *Free ride* from a random road, *Free ride from here* (the current position, in the package ridden now) and its *Routes*) and the test routes. Navi has *Routes* (the routes of the loaded package from section `ROUT` with their length, and the user's routes for this package), *Rides* (`rides/*.fit`, newest first, with the route from the sidecar and the Strava state from `strava-sync.toml`), *GPX import* and *Strava* (a page describing what comes with the backend; no network calls). Rows that start another ride ask first (*Change the ride?*, Cancel focused); confirmed, the menu closes and the switch runs. The lists are read from disk when the menu opens and after a switch or import, not every frame.
  - *Paging (ten-foot rule):* a list with more than six rows shows four rows per page with *Previous (n/m)* / *Next (n/m)* and Back (at most seven items); ← / → on a row without a value turn the page. This also covers the Workshop and Riders pages with many rider profiles.
  - *GPX import* (`ride.import-gpx FILE [--ride]`, 2.7): the file is matched onto the road graph of the loaded package (and its joined neighbours) with the HMM matcher of `ocw-world::matching` – the same as `--route-gpx` and `world-builder gpx` – and saved as an `ocw-graph-route` file with the package name and graph fingerprint in `<data dir>/ocw/routes/` (listed under Navi → Routes for that package; re-matched by stable edge IDs after a package rebuild); the matching report (length, off-road stretches, U-turns) is printed. `--ride` rides it at once. The menu offers the `.gpx` files in `<data dir>/ocw/gpx/` and the downloads folder (no file dialog on the gamepad). Without a loaded package with a road graph there is nothing to match onto, and the import is refused (a plain GPX-to-route-file conversion would need terrain data the client does not have). The matching runs on the main thread (a long track can stall a frame for a moment); the import report with highlighted problem sections is M4.
  - *Not yet:* the number of bots per ride (the `ride.bots` setting applies), the start point on a map (Phase 7), named start places, renaming / deleting routes, FIT / GPX export rows, package downloads from the menu.
- **Rider weight affects the physics (decided, v2.2):** the active rider's weight (and later the bike's physics profile, 2.5) goes to the server in the join message (new field) – the server stays the truth (6.1) – and to the trainer (SIM total mass); today's fixed 75 kg + 8 kg profile becomes the default rider. Riders are created in *Settings → Riders* and selected in the *Workshop* (the Workshop's rider choice comes before Phase 4's editors).
- **Implemented (M2, v2.7):**
  - *Registry* (`apps/desktop/src/settings/registry.rs`): each setting has a key `section.name`, a type (switch, whole number with range and step, choice), a default, a description and a scope – *live* (an apply command runs on every change and at the start, e.g. `display.fps` → `fps on`) or *next start* (read when the app starts: `ride.bots`, `trainer.virtual_power`, `ride.record`, `ride.random_start`, `display.fullscreen` fill in the command-line option of the same meaning; `controls.autodrive`). Initial set: `controls.autodrive`, `trainer.difficulty`, `trainer.virtual_power`, `display.hud`, `display.units` (metric / imperial), `display.fps`, `display.camera`, `display.fullscreen`, `ride.bots`, `ride.random_start`, `ride.record`. The key is `controls.autodrive`, not `controls.autodrive_default`.
  - *Layers:* a command-line option the user gave (clap's value source, the args file included) becomes the setting's session value; a setting only replaces an option's default when it is in the file, so screenshot and capture runs keep their reproducible defaults. `set` saves at once (not only when the menu closes) and replaces a session value; `set --temp` is session-only. `autoexec.cfg` runs after the settings' startup commands, so its commands win; a `set` in it is saved like one typed in the console (use `set --temp` there for session-only values). The settings' apply commands are queued before `autoexec.cfg`, `--exec` and `--cmd`.
  - *Files:* a broken `settings.toml` (not TOML) is left untouched; the app uses the defaults and does not save. Invalid entries stay in the file until set again. `--settings-file` names another file; `riders.toml` is read next to it.
  - *Rider profiles* are not in `settings.toml` but in `riders.toml` (`active = NAME` and `[[rider]]` tables: `name`, `weight_kg`, optional `height_cm`, `ftp_w`) next to it, since they are a list rather than variables. Weight 30–200 kg (`ocw_core::MIN/MAX_RIDER_WEIGHT_KG`; entered values outside are refused, values in the file and from the network are clamped), height 100–250 cm, FTP 30–700 W, names up to 32 characters without quotes. Without profiles the rider is the default (75 kg). `--rider NAME` rides another profile for the session, `--name` still sets only the display name. Units are one global setting (`display.units`), not per rider.
  - *Join message:* `Hello.rider_weight_kg` (field 5). The server builds the physics profile from its curated default (2.5) with that weight (clamped); the client's `Hello.profile` (drag, rolling resistance, bike mass) is deprecated and ignored except for its rider mass when field 5 is absent. The client predicts with the same profile.
  - *Trainer:* the SIM mass is rider weight + 8 kg bike; Wahoo's SIM mode carries it (sent again when it changes); FTMS has no mass field (its Indoor Bike Simulation parameters are wind, grade, crr, cw), so FTMS trainers get only the gradient. The FTMS User Data Service (weight) is not used.
  - *When it applies:* a changed or newly selected rider applies from the next start (R restarts); the server has no message to change a rider's mass mid-session.
- **Workshop → Bike (Phase 4 groundwork, M6 in part):** the Workshop lists the riders, then a *Bike* row with the chosen rider's bike and colours that opens the *Bike* page of that rider (`Page::Bike`, Back goes to the Workshop): *Bike* (← / → step through the six profiles, named by bike type and setup: Road – standard / aero / climbing, Time trial, Gravel, Mountain bike; one row instead of separate type and setup rows keeps the page at six rows), *Physics* (the profile's bike mass, CdA and Crr, read only – shown separately as planned), *Frame / Jersey / Helmet colour* (← / → step through a 12-colour palette; any `#RRGGBB` from the console) and *Kit* (plain, band, sash). Each row runs `riders.edit "NAME" --bike ID | --frame-color #RRGGBB | --jersey-color … | --helmet-color … | --kit …`, the same options as on the console (`riders.add` takes them too). Like the weight, bike and look apply **from the next start** (decided): the server has no message to change a rider's profile mid-session, and a live change of only the own avatar would show the others something else; a live preview comes with the 3D preview. Without rider profiles the Bike row only shows the default bike (add a rider to change it). Still open in M6: the 3D preview, components (wheels, tyres, saddle, …) and the character page.
  - *Pages:* the Settings sub pages and the Workshop are a Bevy-free model (`settings/pages.rs`): each row has a label, a value and the command lines for ← / → / Confirm (or a page to open); the menu (`menu::model`, `Page::Sub`) shows value rows as "Label:  < value >", ← / → run the row's command, Q / E, PgUp / PgDn and LB / RB switch between the tabs Workshop, Riders, Controls, Trainer, Display, Strava (replacing the page, so Back still goes to the parent); the rows are read again every frame, so values changed from the console show at once. A rider editor whose rider was deleted goes back to the list. Renaming is a console command for now (`riders.edit NAME --rename NEW`; the on-screen keyboard comes later). The Workshop lists the riders (Confirm = `riders.select`); *Riders* lists them for editing (weight ±1 kg, height ±1 cm, FTP ±5 W, rename, delete, add). Console: `riders.list / add / edit / remove / select`.
- **Devices (v3.74, Settings → Trainer → Devices; `ocw_client::menu::devices`, the same page in both apps; `ocw_ui::menu::DevicesMenu` is filled by the app):**
  - *List:* first the way to find devices – desktop: *Scan for devices* (`devices.scan`, 10 s; while it runs *Stop the scan*, `devices.scan --stop`, with the seconds left); browser: *Add a trainer*, *Add a power meter*, *Add a heart-rate strap* (`devices.connect trainer|power|hr`, the browser's chooser; dimmed without Web Bluetooth). Then every device, in a stable order (remembered ones first, then as the scan finds them – the list grows **while the scan runs**, `ocw_devices::ble::scan_live` reports each device as it appears and again when its name or signal changes): name and a value "trainer, -61 dBm, connected, remembered". Remembered devices are listed also when they are not in range. The Trainer page's *Devices* row shows the connected device (else "virtual trainer").
  - *Role* from the advertised services: FTMS → trainer; Cycling Power → power meter, except a name with "KICKR" → trainer (Wahoo KICKRs advertise only Cycling Power; their control point is found after connecting, 3.4); CSC → cadence / speed; Heart Rate → heart rate.
  - *A device's page:* kind, state (*not connected*, *connecting*, *connected, Wahoo KICKR (…)*, *reconnecting*, *failed: why; trying again*), signal (desktop), remembered; *Connect* (`devices.connect <id>`; the browser: its chooser of that kind) and *Disconnect and forget* (`devices.forget <id>`, back to the list). Why a connection failed comes from the backend: `DeviceEvent::Failed { reason }` before the `Disconnected` of a failed attempt – *no Bluetooth adapter (or Bluetooth is off)*, *not found (out of range, asleep, or connected to another app)*, *the connection failed (busy with another app?)*.
  - *Status:* the status line shows the scan ("Scanning ... 7 s left, 2 found"), else the newest message (connecting, connected, failed, scan results), else where the devices are remembered (a page of seven rows has no room for more text).
  - *Remembering:* a device is remembered **once it connected** (not when the attempt starts): the desktop writes `devices.toml` (TOML, `[[device]]` tables with `id`, `name` and – since v3.74, optional – `kind` = `trainer` / `power` / `cadence` / `hr`) in the config directory (`~/.config/ocw/devices.toml` on Linux, `OCW_CONFIG_DIR` overrides it) or the file `--devices-file` names (when that file does not exist the default is used, as before); a file that cannot be written is named with the error in the message ("connected …, not remembered: …"). The browser keeps them in its `localStorage` (`ocw.devices`). At the next start the remembered devices connect by themselves (`--virtual` ignores them).
  - *The virtual trainer:* a trainer or power meter (or a device of unknown role connected by id) replaces it **once it is connected**; forgetting the last one brings it back. The HUD's status marks devices that are *connecting*, *reconnecting* or *not connected*.
  - *Tests:* the page's rows and the menu path (`menu::devices`), the shared glue (`ocw_ui::menu`), the desktop flow against a mock Bluetooth stack (`devices::DeviceIo`: scan → live list → connect → remembered in a temp `devices.toml` → virtual trainer replaced → forget → the next start reconnects from the file; a read-only file), the browser's `WebDevices` (remembered once connected, failures, the page's model). With real hardware: `scripts/test-devices-menu.sh [shot|shot-wayland] DIR` drives the page headless (scan, choose the first device, connect; a screenshot per step; its own `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) and prints the `devices.toml` it wrote – on marge the Wahoo KICKR is found as a trainer, connects with Wahoo control, replaces the virtual trainer and is written with `kind = "trainer"` (X11 and Wayland).
- **Implemented (M5):** *Settings → Audio* (between Trainer and Display, also a tab): *Master volume*, *Effects (bike, wind)*, *Music*, *Voice* (← / → in 5 % steps; Enter plays a test sound on that bus), *Mute*, *Output* (← / → step through `default`, a saved but missing device, and the devices the engine lists; the value shows "default", "default (none)", "DEVICE" or "DEVICE (gone)", names cut to 16 characters – the row has no room for more in the ten-foot layout; `audio.status` and `audio.devices` show the full names). Six rows and Back, so no paging. Each row runs `set audio.KEY VALUE`; the device list is read again when the page opens. The menu plays the UI cues (move, value, page, back) itself, from the change of what it shows. Game audio and the engine: 3.3.
- **Settings entries (decided 2026-11-12):** with Audio (M5) and Voice (M8) the Settings page would exceed the ten-foot limit of 7 entries, so the Strava account page moved to *Navi → Strava* (it replaces the former placeholder there; it stays a Q / E tab). Settings: Riders, Controls, Trainer, Audio, Display, Voice, Back. Option not taken: one combined *Sound* page for Audio and Voice (an extra level).
- **Local now vs. backend later:** settings, devices, routes, GPX import, rides, the interim Strava upload and the Workshop configuration are local. Accounts and profile sync (2.1), Events and sessions (2.3), the backend Strava upload (2.8), sharing routes and friends need the Phase 5 backend; those pages appear disabled with a short hint until it exists.

**World menu (decided 2026-11-13, v2.39)**

The user asked for a *World* entry where the rider chooses the world they ride in and sees its conditions (time, weather) and its data. Decisions:

- **Shared rides from the menu (v3.73).** The Ride page: *Events* (the local events' page: race, group ride, time trial, end the event), *Workouts*, *Join a ride* (alone) or *Leave shared ride* (joined), *Host a ride* (alone; dimmed in the browser: "Hosting needs the desktop app"), while hosting *Hosting – N riders* (the rider list), *Show join link* and *Stop hosting*, *Restart*, Back – at most seven items in every mode. **Join:** a *Link* row is a text field (Enter starts typing, Enter / Esc end; typed text, ← / →, Home / End, Backspace / Delete, Ctrl+V / ⌘V and the browser's paste event; on a gamepad a character wheel: ↑ / ↓ the character, ← / → the cursor, B deletes, A ends; touch: *Paste link*), a *Fingerprint* row when the link has none and is not for this machine (the page says why), *Join* (dimmed while empty; *Cancel joining* while connecting), then the last five servers (host and what it rode; Enter joins again; `joins.txt` in the config directory, `localStorage` in the browser). The page's text is the join's status: connecting (seconds), loading the server's ride, riding, or why not – the 10 s timeout, a certificate that is not the link's, a refusal (sign-in: Settings → Account), a world that is not installed (with `--fetch-world URL` for a link's manifest URL) or another version of it; the current ride goes on until the shared one is loaded and switches through the ride switch (the old ride saved). The browser joins WebTransport links by starting its page again with them. **Host a ride** (desktop): a wizard – world, route or free ride, date and time (real, or a time machine preset and day steps), weather (simulated, real, a preset; who changes time and weather – on the Options page before v5.20), options (bots 0–20, default 5; *Voice*; the UDP port, default 47800; *Open the router's ports*), summary – then *Start hosting*: the app opens UDP `0.0.0.0:PORT` with a certificate kept in `<data dir>/ocw/host-tls`, runs the session on its own local server with the network endpoint (in-process, no separate binary) and rides on it as the host; the join link page shows the links with the machine's addresses, *Copy link* and the firewall / port forwarding hint. A port in use is reported with the offer to join the server there; *Stop hosting* closes the server and rides on alone with the same course, time and weather. *Built (v4.31, 7.1.9):* hosting also starts the bundled voice server (stopped with *Stop hosting* and at quit); the Options page has *Open the router's ports* (UPnP, setting `host.upnp`, on by default), the summary's text lists the ports (UDP PORT game, TCP 7880, TCP 7881, UDP 7882 voice) with the hint, and the join link page has the rows *Ports* and *Router* (opened / no UPnP router / failed) and the first link on the router's public address when there is one. *Built (v5.20, 7.1.7 Q15):* the Options page's **Voice** row (setting `host.voice`, on by default): off, no voice server starts, no voice port is opened and the hosted ride has no voice (the riders' apps: "no voice on this server"). *Built (v6.81, 11.5 *The public server as the default*):* the Join page's **first row is *Public server (ocw-server.fly.dev)*** (desktop; the host comes from the setting `net.public_server`, the row is gone when it is `off`): Enter fetches the server's join info and checks its world before connecting – the page says "Finding the public server (ocw-server.fly.dev) … N s", then joins its link like any other (the usual status lines), or says why not: the join info not reached, or the server's world (e.g. `liechtenstein@10`) not installed here or another build of it, with what to install; *Download the world and join* is offered when the join info names a download. Console and command line: `join public`, `join.public [--download]`, `ocw-desktop --join public`.
- **Menu tree:** the top page has seven items, the ten-foot maximum: Resume, Ride, **World**, Workshop, Navi, Settings, Quit. *Restart* moved to the Ride page (then Race, Group ride, Time trial, End the event, Workouts, Restart, Back – seven items; *Change ride* left it; since v3.73 Events, Workouts, the shared-ride items, Restart, Back), so every page still fits 16:9 (the page-fit test `every_menu_page_fits_a_16_9_window_with_its_text` covers all new pages, the data-source pages with the longest notice, the OSM one). Options not taken: a combined *Restart / Quit* page (Quit is the kiosk-safe exit and stays one step away), World under Ride (an extra level for something every rider uses).
- **World** (`settings::pages::Page::WorldHome`, rows from `apps/desktop/src/ride/world.rs`): *Change world* (value: the world ridden now), *About this world*, *Routes* (the same page as Navi → Routes), *Time* (value: world time and mode, e.g. "14:05 CET, x600"), *Weather* (value: "clear"), Back.
- **The time machine moved to World → Time** (decided): time of day, date and speed are conditions of the world, like the weather; Navi keeps routes, rides, GPX import and Strava. The page itself is unchanged (14 Phase 9, 9I).
- **Change world** lists what `ocw_worldstore::discover` finds, read when the menu opens and after a switch:
  - *sources:* the world cache (`<data dir>/ocw/worlds`, the newest version of each id), the package given with `--world` or ridden now, the packages **next to it** (the kiosk installs several in `/var/tmp/ocw/`), and the `.ocwpkg` files next to the executable, in `data/` and `data/pilot/` (one level of sub directories);
  - *each entry* shows its name, size and – when not verified – "unsigned" / "untrusted" (a user-signed world: "unofficial, 'name'" or "unknown key, 'name'", choosing it opens the trust dialog, 4.7 *User keys*); its page shows the version, the size, the signature state and the routes. The package is **not loaded** for the list: the manifest (id, name, version, date, credits, size; its signature is checked – cheap) and a summary of the package file (`ocw_world::summary::summarize`: header, tile count, the small sections `ROUT`, `REGN`, `TZID`; the terrain, the road graph, land use and buildings are skipped with seeks, so a 260 MB package takes milliseconds; summaries are kept per file by size and time). The full verification (hashes) happens when it is ridden; a package the list could not judge fails then, and the ride goes on with a message;
  - *duplicates:* a file reached twice is listed once (canonical path); packages with a manifest are one entry per id – the highest version, on a tie the one given with `--world`, then the cache, then a file (`world list` shows the others as "also"); packages without a manifest are told apart by their file, and two entries with the same name show their file names;
  - *broken and blocked packages* are listed with the reason and cannot be chosen: not a package, a version this build cannot read, truncated, a size that differs from the manifest, an unreadable manifest, a bad signature; an unsigned package in the cache without `--allow-unsigned`, an unsigned file with `--require-signed` (the trust policy of 4.7 / 12);
  - *parts:* packages whose regions meet at a border (boxes touching within 0.01°, less than 10 % of the smaller region shared – sampled on the region polygons) are **one world with parts**; riding one joins the installed neighbours anyway (2.2.2). Two cuts of the same area (a test build next to the release) stay two worlds;
  - the **built-in test routes** (Hills, Loop) come last.
- **A world's page:** *Ride* (its default: the package's first route, else a free ride – as `--world` alone does, M3), *Free ride* (random start), *Free ride from here* (the world ridden now), *Routes* (of the world ridden now: Navi's list with length and climbing; of another world: its routes from the summary), *Parts* (a free ride in one of them), *Package*. Every row asks *Change the ride?* first and then runs the M3 in-app switch (`ride.switch …`): process, window and devices stay, the ride so far is saved.
- **About this world:** *World* (region name, signature state, parts), *Package* (id, version, build date), *Area* (km² of the regions, else of the tiles; the lowest and highest terrain), *Sun and time* (a page: the time zone with its UTC offset, the world time, sunrise / sunset with solar noon, civil, nautical and astronomical twilight at the rider's position on the world's local date, from `ocw-sky`, recomputed when the date or the place changes), *Data sources* (one row per attribution of the package and its parts, licence as the value; a source's page shows source, licence, web address and the **full notice** as its text – the same texts as the manifest's credits, which the package's `LICENSE-DATA.md` and the credits screen carry, 13), *Routes*. A test route has no package: the page says so and shows the sun.
- **Weather** (`apps/desktop/src/weather.rs`): the **weather machine** (Phase 9 S5, 9I-S5) over the session weather (since S4 `WeatherState` comes from the server like the world clock). Under the title the weather now (condition, temperature, wind, road) and who sets it; rows *Mode* (fixed ↔ simulated with the seed; "-> rain in 40 s" during a transition), *Real weather* (S7, 9I-S7: opens its page – on / off, the data source, ride a day; the attribution under the title and in the HUD), *Presets* (a grid page), *Custom* (two pages), *Transition* (instant / 1 / 5 / 15 min), *Random weather* (← / → the seed, Enter applies it). Every row is a console line (`weather …`, `weather.transition`, `weather.seed`, `weather.real`, `weather.provider`, `weather.day`); rows the rider may not use are dimmed (`Activate::Disabled`).
- **Shared sessions (decided):** the server owns the session (6.1), so in a shared ride the switch is a request to the server, and **only the host** may switch the world, checked on the server like the time machine: `ClientMessage.world` = `WorldRequest` (the package's manifest id – or the file name of a local build – and a route; empty: free ride), answered with a `DevCommandResult`; `ServerConfig.world_access` (`ClockAccess`: anyone on the local servers, the host by default, nobody for organizer-set sessions; `ocw-server --world-control host|anyone|nobody`), sent in `Welcome.world_access` so the menu can say who decides. The server resolves the request in **its own catalog** (`ocw_server::worlds::resolve`: its cache and the packages next to its `--world`; it never loads a path a client names), loads the package on a thread while the session goes on, then `GameServer::switch_world` starts a new session on it (bots again, the world clock goes on: session time is kept across the switch) and sends `ServerMessage.world_change` = `WorldChange` (manifest id, version, name, graph id, route, package SHA-256, who asked) to every rider. The riders leave the old session (their rider ids belong to it), and each client loads the same package from what it has installed (by id and version; the SHA-256 must match) and **joins again with a Hello on the same connection**, so the host stays the host; a client without the package says so ("The host rides … which is not installed here") and waits. Test routes and the rider's own route files are not offered to a shared ride. Local servers keep the client-driven M3 switch.
- **Console:** `world list` (numbered, with id, version, size, signature state, routes, source, parts, other copies), `world info` (the About page as text, with the full notices and the sun times), `world switch N|ID|NAME|PATH` (a number of `world list`, an id, `id@version`, a name or file name, a package path, or a test route; the world's default ride) – user commands, like `ride.switch`, with the same rules (asking the server in a shared ride).
- **Kiosk:** `scripts/deploy-test.sh` installs every world package built on the machine side by side in `/var/tmp/ocw/` (v2.36), so the kiosk's World → Change world lists Liechtenstein and the Black Forest – south, middle and north as **one world with three parts** (their regions meet on 48.12 N and 48.45 N) – and switches between them in the app; the kiosk's default ride (`ocw-desktop.args`, `OCW_KIOSK_WORLD`) is unchanged.
- **Not yet:** downloading packages from the list (Phase 5 backend), a map of the worlds and start places (Phase 7), the `LICENSE-DATA.md` file inside packages (the notices come from the manifest), the weather itself (S4 / S5), following a server's switch to a route file or a test route (the server rides packages only).

**M9 implemented (Phase 7, v3.42; renamed *Input mapping* and changed in v5.21, see 3.2.5 – up to two keys per action, the power ±10 W actions removed, a captured key moves from the action that had it, only changed bindings saved in `ocw.toml`):**

- *Bindings* (`ocw_client::bindings`, pure; the Bevy keys and buttons in `ocw_ui::bindings`, shared by both apps): one keyboard key and one gamepad button for each of 19 ride actions – faster, stop, steer left / right, power ±10 W; autodrive, wild mode, U-turn, back to the route, junction exit left / right; camera, video, fullscreen, restart, unicorn mode; mute microphone, mute voices. They are settings of the registry (`keys.<id>`, `pad.<id>`; `[keys]` and `[pad]` of `settings.toml`, the browser's `localStorage`), so `set keys.autodrive Z`, the menu and `autoexec.cfg` share one path; the defaults are today's keys (README table). Key names are positions (US-layout names: `A`, `Up`, `PageUp`, `Num+`, `Shift+M`); a `Shift+X` binding needs Shift, and a plain `X` then does not fire with Shift held. Desktop-only actions (video, fullscreen, restart) are not offered in the browser; unicorn mode's key works in both since Phase 13 G5.
- *Fixed (proposal P7-5):* Esc, \` and F12 (menu, console) and the pad's Start cannot be bound; the menu's own keys (arrows, Enter, Q / E …), the analog stick and triggers (steering, throttle, brake) and the pad's god mode chords (Select + North / West) stay; **unicorn mode's flight keys** (cursor keys, the + / − keys, L) are fixed and never W / A / S / D (Phase 13 Q3, decided).
- *Conflicts (P7-4):* two actions on one key or button, or an action that also works in flight (camera, video, fullscreen, unicorn mode, the voice mutes) on a flight key. They are allowed – a rider swapping two keys passes through one – but marked: "(!)" in the row's value with the warning dot (▲), the list in the page's status line, the count on the Controls row, and `bind` prints them; both actions fire meanwhile.
- *Menu:* Settings → Controls → *Keys and buttons* (`Page::Bindings`): the groups *Power and steering*, *Autodrive and junctions*, *Camera, video, app*, *Voice chat* (each a page of at most six actions), *Pad Confirm button* and *Reset to defaults* (a page that asks first). A group's row shows "key | button"; Enter waits for the new key or pad button (the status line says so; Esc / Start cancel), ← / → step the key through the list (no keyboard needed for a gamepad user). To make room on Controls (six rows), the two unicorn mode settings moved to *Controls → Unicorn mode* (P7-8).
- *Console:* `bind` (all bindings and conflicts), `bind ACTION KEY`, `bind ACTION BUTTON --pad`, `bind --capture ACTION`, `bind --reset`.
- *Confirm / Back swap (P7-6):* `controls.pad_confirm south|east` – one setting for all pads (east = the Nintendo layout); per pad (by vendor id) later with the glyph sets of 3.2.2.
- *Accessibility* (Settings → Display → *Accessibility*; the FPS counter moved to Display → Graphics to make room, P7-8): *HUD size* (`display.ui_scale` 100–200 %, Bevy's `UiScale`: the HUD's pixel sizes scale; the menu is sized in % of the window height already and stays, so every page still fits 16:9 – P7-7), *Status colours* (`display.palette standard|colour-safe`: the damage levels, the voice indicator and the workout zones take blue – yellow – orange – reddish purple twins after Okabe & Ito; icons and words stay, `ocw_render::access`), *High-contrast HUD* (`display.high_contrast`: the HUD's see-through panels opaque, grey text white), *Reduced motion* (`display.reduced_motion`: no camera shake, no flashing warning or damage flash), *Camera shake* (the existing `display.camera_shake`). The bike computer's panel narrows to the room left of the top-right column (timestamp, REC, FPS) and wraps, so no HUD size from 100 to 200 % makes them overlap (test `the_top_panel_stays_clear_of_the_top_right_column`). Console: `ui.scale`, `ui.palette`, `ui.contrast`, `ui.motion` (what the settings run).
- *Tests:* the bindings' defaults (= the registry's), reserved inputs, conflicts both ways, the no-WASD rule, the Shift rule, settings round trip and reset, the capture (key, Shift, Esc), the swap, the palette twins and their restore, high contrast, reduced motion and the shake; every new page in the 16:9 page-fit test.

**M8 implemented (Phase 6, first increment):** Settings → Voice (`Page::Voice`, rows from `apps/desktop/src/voice/page.rs`): *Microphone* and *Speaker (voices)* toggles (`voice.mute-mic`, `voice.mute-speaker`), *Voice volume (%)*, *Participants (n)* (a sub page: each rider with "heard 40 %", "too far away", "microphone off" or "muted by you"; Confirm = `voice.mute IDENTITY`), *Devices and options* (a sub page: microphone and speaker – ← / → step through *default* and the present devices, a saved device that is missing shows "(not found: default)" –, *Spatial voice*, *Voices heard at most*) and *Voice chat* (on / off with the status). Settings: `voice.enabled`, `voice.mic_muted`, `voice.speaker_muted`, `voice.volume` (0–200 %), `voice.spatial`, `voice.max_voices` (1–20), `voice.input`, `voice.output` (device names; a new registry kind *text*). The Settings top page now has seven items (Riders, Controls, Trainer, Display, Strava, Voice, Back): the ten-foot maximum; Settings → Audio (M5) needs a slot (e.g. Strava, which is also under Navi, could leave Settings).

**M1 implemented:** Esc / Start opens the menu over the running ride: Resume, Ride, Workshop, Navi, Settings, Restart, Quit; Ride, Workshop, Navi and Settings are placeholder pages that say what their increment brings (Settings already toggles the FPS counter). Restart and Quit ask first, with *Cancel* focused, and run the console commands `reset` / `quit`; the console command `menu open|close|toggle|up|down|select|back` drives the menu from scripts and `--cmd`. Code: the Bevy-free model (`apps/desktop/src/menu/model.rs`: pages, page stack, focus with wrap-around), the key / button → action mapping with hold repeat (`menu/controls.rs`), the drawing of a `MenuView` in `ocw-render::menu` (text sizes in % of the window height). Deviations from the plan above:

- No Bevy state `UiMode`: one resource `InputContext { Ride, Menu, Console }` (console over menu over ride) is decided once per frame in `PreUpdate`, and the ride's input systems (power, steering, A / W / U / J / Q / E, R, V, F11, the mouse camera and C) run only in `Ride` (`run_if(ride_input)`); a key that closes the menu is therefore not also seen by the ride in that frame. The console keeps its own open flag.
- Steering while the menu is open (`ClientCore::hold_steering` / `release_steering`, so server and prediction agree): wild mode off, autodrive on – from manual steering at the rider's current lateral position (no swerve), an autodrive line stays where it was; the next junction's choice is reset to its default exit and not restored on closing. Closing restores manual steering upright (the lean is not carried over) and wild mode; autodrive keeps its line. The HUD shows "autodrive (menu)".
- The mouse hover moves the focus only while the mouse moves (rows of a new page appearing under a resting pointer do not take the focus); right click = Back.
- ← / → and tab switching (Q / E, PgUp / PgDn, LB / RB) had no rows or tabs to act on in M1; M2 (v2.7) uses them on the Settings sub pages and the Workshop (see *Implemented (M2)* above). The FPS toggle moved to *Settings → Display*.
- The status strip shows power, speed and the device / trainer / steering status line; the Strava sync state joins it with the Navi pages (M3).
- Smoke screenshots of the open menu are taken on Wayland (1280×720 and 800×600); the build machines with a GPU have no X11 server.

**Open questions**

Decided (v2.2): no pause (trainer unchanged, ride time and recording continue); Esc never quits; rider weight affects physics, riders managed in Settings and chosen in the Workshop. Decided: local events before the backend (2.3.1) - the Ride page starts a race, a group ride or a time trial on the current route (console command lines `event race --bots 5`, `event group --watts 150`, `event tt`, `event cancel`; the starts ask first, then the menu closes for the countdown). Still open: switching rides by restart vs. in-app session switch (M3).

#### 3.2.2 Input Model: Keyboard, Mouse, Gamepad and Touch (planning, 2026-11-13, v2.54)

**Rule (decided by the user, 2026-11-13):** the **entire UI** – every menu page, the workshop scene (14 Phase 4, 4A), the character corner, dialogs, the console's menu-side functions, the HUD's interactive elements and later the start screen – is controllable with **gamepad and mouse, and touch where the device has a touchscreen**; the keyboard keeps working everywhere (3.2.1). No function may need one particular device (the console's text entry is the one exception: it needs a keyboard, physical or on-screen). The rest of 3.2.2 is a proposal.

**Platform facts (Bevy 0.20.1 / winit 0.30.13, as read in their sources 2026-11-13):**

| Input | Linux X11 | Linux Wayland | Windows | macOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keyboard, mouse, wheel | yes | yes | yes | yes | trackpad two-finger scroll arrives as `MouseWheel` (pixel deltas) |
