| Gamepad (gilrs 0.11) | yes (evdev) | yes | yes (XInput / WGI) | yes | hot-plug; `Gamepad::vendor_id()` / `product_id()` tell Xbox / PlayStation / Switch / generic apart for the glyphs |
| Touchscreen (`TouchInput`, `Touches`) | yes (XInput 2.2 touch; winit drops the emulated pointer events) | yes (`wl_touch`) | yes (winit does **not** filter the mouse events Windows synthesises from touch: we must) | **no touchscreens** (winit: touch unsupported) | multi-touch with ids; no built-in pinch on Linux / Windows – our recogniser computes it from the touches |
| Gestures (`PinchGesture`, `RotationGesture`, `DoubleTapGesture`, `PanGesture`) | – | – | – | pinch, rotation, double tap from the trackpad | `PanGesture` only on iOS; on macOS pan comes as scroll |
| Picking (`bevy_picking`) | mouse and touch are both *pointers* (`PointerId::Mouse`, `PointerId::Touch(id)`): UI and mesh picking (hotspots) work for both | | | | the menu rows already use `PointerClick` / `PointerOver` (`ocw-render::menu`), so taps reach them today (untested) |
| Focus (`bevy_input_focus`) | `InputFocus`, tab navigation, directional navigation (`AutoDirectionalNavigation` in `bevy_ui`) | | | | usable for the Bevy UI pages; the menu model keeps its own focus (3.2.1) and may adopt it |

Devices that have all of them: Windows tablets and touch laptops, Linux touch laptops, the Steam Deck (touchscreen + gamepad, Linux), a kiosk with a touch monitor. Browser (Phase 10): touch, pointer and Gamepad API all available; phones / tablets are touch-first. VR (Phase 11): the controller ray is one more pointer.

**Abstract actions (one layer for all devices):** today's menu actions (`Up`, `Down`, `Left`, `Right`, `Confirm`, `Back`, `TabNext`, `TabPrev`, 3.2.1) are extended by `Secondary` (context: compare, details), `Tertiary` (a page's extra action: buy, sort), `Orbit(Δ)`, `Zoom(Δ)`, `Pan(Δ)`, `Point(position)` and `Activate(position)` (click / tap at a point) and `Scroll(Δ)`. A pure mapper in `apps/desktop/src/input/` (Bevy-free, with the existing hold-repeat of `menu/controls.rs`) turns device events into actions; pages and scenes see only actions, so every page and scene can be tested once with actions and once per device.

| Action | Keyboard | Mouse / trackpad | Gamepad | Touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Move focus | arrows, Tab / Shift+Tab | hover (moves focus only while the pointer moves, 3.2.1) | D-pad, left stick (repeat) | – (no focus frame; tap acts directly) |
| Confirm | Enter, Space | left click | South (A / ✕) | tap |
| Back | Esc, Backspace | right click, mouse "back" button | East (B / ○) | the on-screen **Back** button (top left, always shown in touch mode), swipe from the left edge inward (not the OS edge: starts 16 px in) |
| Change a value | ← / → | drag the slider, wheel over it | D-pad / stick ← / →, LB / RB big steps | drag the slider, tap the ‹ › arrows |
| Switch tab / category | Q / E, PgUp / PgDn | click the tab | LB / RB | tap the tab, swipe horizontally on the tab bar |
| Secondary (compare, details) | C | middle click, or the card's button | North (Y / △) | long press (500 ms) |
| Tertiary (buy, sort…) | X | the card's button | West (X / □) | the card's button |
| Scroll a list | arrows, PgUp / PgDn | wheel, drag the scroll bar | right stick ↕, focus moves | one-finger drag (with inertia) |
| Orbit (3D scenes) | I / J / K / L, or Shift + arrows | left drag (in empty space), trackpad drag | right stick | one-finger drag |
| Zoom | + / − | wheel, trackpad pinch (macOS gesture) or two-finger scroll | RT zoom in, LT zoom out (analog) | pinch |
| Pan | Ctrl + arrows | middle drag, Shift + left drag | right stick click + right stick | two-finger drag |
| Reset view / focus | Home | double click | right stick click (R3) | double tap |
| Open / close menu | Esc | the ☰ button (top left in a ride, shown after a mouse move) | Start / Menu | tap ☰ |

**Last-used device and hints:** a resource `ActiveInput { Keyboard, Mouse, Gamepad(kind), Touch }` follows the device of the last meaningful input (a key, a click, a stick beyond the dead zone, a touch; mouse motion of less than 4 px is ignored, so a nudged table does not flip it). The **hint bar** at the bottom of every page and scene ("Ⓐ Select  Ⓑ Back  Ⓨ Compare  LB/RB Category") shows the glyphs of that device: keycaps, mouse icons, Xbox letters (also for generic pads), PlayStation shapes, Switch letters; touch shows short words ("Tap to select · Long press: compare"). The glyphs are our own drawings (Phase 8 Q11: no logos; button letters and shapes are not logos). **Confirm is the bottom face button on every pad** (positional, as today: Bevy's `South`), so on a Switch pad the hint shows "B" for Confirm – one rule for all pads; a per-pad swap is a later accessibility setting (M9).

**Focus frame vs. pointer:** with keyboard or gamepad active the focus frame is shown (ten-foot rule, 3.2.1); with mouse or touch active it is hidden and hover / press states show instead; the focus is kept and returns on the next key or button. Pointer and focus never fight: a click or tap also moves the focus there.

**Touch mode** (when `ActiveInput` is `Touch`, or the setting `controls.touch on|off|auto`, default `auto`):

- **Hit targets:** at least **9 mm** and at least **48 logical px** (whichever is larger; 44 px is the bare minimum) high and wide for every interactive element, 2 mm (≥ 8 px) apart. The ten-foot layout (text ≥ 3 % of the window height, rows of ≥ 6 %) already gives 43 px rows at 1280 × 720; in touch mode rows grow to the minimum where the window is smaller, and pages page earlier (3.2.1 paging) rather than shrink. Millimetres from the window's scale factor (1 logical px ≈ 0.19 mm at scale 1 on a 96 dpi panel; winit gives no physical screen size, so a setting `display.touch_scale` corrects odd panels).
- **Gesture recogniser** (`apps/desktop/src/input/gestures.rs`, pure, fed with `TouchInput` events and their times): tap (< 10 px movement, < 300 ms), double tap (< 300 ms apart, < 20 px), long press (500 ms without moving), drag (beyond 10 px), swipe (a drag faster than 0.5 px/ms, released), pinch (distance of two touches: zoom factor), two-finger drag (centroid: pan), two-finger tap (= Back in 3D scenes). A third touch cancels. On macOS the trackpad's `PinchGesture` / `RotationGesture` / `DoubleTapGesture` map onto the same actions.
- **Emulated mouse events:** Windows sends a synthesised mouse event for the primary touch; winit 0.30 passes it on. The mapper ignores mouse buttons and motion within **500 ms** of a touch event at the same place (X11 already filters them in winit), so one tap is never also a click. (To check on a real Windows touchscreen.)
- **Text:** text fields (names, titles) open the OS on-screen keyboard where the platform offers one through IME (Windows touch keyboard, GNOME / KDE on Wayland), else our own on-screen keyboard (the one planned for the gamepad, 3.2.1).
- **System gestures:** the OS edge swipes (Windows, GNOME, KDE) are left to the OS; our gestures start at least 16 px from the window edge.

**Mouse:** everything that has a focus has a pointer equivalent (no hover-only function, 3.2.1); right click = Back; the wheel scrolls lists and zooms 3D scenes; in a ride a mouse move shows the ☰ menu button and the clickable HUD elements for 3 s.

**Gamepad:** the full menu and every scene are reachable (D-pad / left stick focus, South / East / North / West, LB / RB, LT / RT analog, right stick for scenes and long lists, R3 reset, Start menu, Select = the voice mute of 2.4 in a ride); several pads: any pad drives the UI (the ride's steering rule stays: the largest deflection steers).

**During a ride (touch proposal):** riding is driven by the trainer; touch is for the HUD and the camera. A **touch overlay** (shown on the first touch, fades after 8 s without one; `controls.touch_overlay auto|on|off`):

- ☰ menu (top left), **autodrive** toggle, **U-turn** (asks with a second tap, as the key does not), ~~**lean ‹ ›** buttons at the lower left and right edges~~ (v3.78: replaced by **steering zones on the left / right half of the screen** – tap = one step, hold = as the held arrow key, for line and lean steering and the junction exit choice; 3.2.3), and at a junction the **exit arrows** of the junction overlay (2.2.1) become tap targets (tap = choose that exit).
- **Camera:** one-finger drag on the 3D view orbits (as the mouse), pinch changes the chase distance, double tap = camera reset (C), two-finger tap cycles the camera mode.
- **Tap HUD elements:** the voice indicator (mute the microphone / speaker, 2.4), the mini elevation profile (zoom 1.5 km ↔ 5 km), the bike computer (cycle its fields), the event panel (expand the standings), the damage widget (Phase 12: the part list), the REC dot (stop recording).
- **Virtual power** (no trainer, 2.9): + / − buttons beside the power field.
- The overlay is part of the HUD layer (hidden with `hud off`, drawn in captures only when shown).

**Workshop and other 3D scenes** (the workshop, the world preview / map later, Phase 13's view later): orbit, zoom and pan as in the table, with limits per scene (workshop: 0.8–4 m around the stand, pitch −10° … 70°), inertia after a flick (0.3 s), and the same camera state machine whatever the device (14 Phase 4, 4A).

**Settings → Controls** gains: *Touch mode* (auto / on / off), *Touch overlay* (auto / on / off), *Pointer speed* (orbit speed, existing), *Invert orbit*, *Stick dead zone* (existing), *Gamepad glyphs* (auto / Xbox / PlayStation / Switch). Rebinding stays M9 (Phase 7).

**Tests (spec 11.4: no step without tests):**

- **Mapper** (pure): every row of the table above, per device, → the expected action; hold repeat; dead zones; `ActiveInput` switching (and not switching on 1–3 px mouse jitter); emulated-mouse suppression after touches (a tap is one `Activate`, never two); glyph sets per gamepad vendor id.
- **Gesture recogniser** (pure, synthetic `TouchInput` sequences with times): tap / double tap / long press / drag / swipe thresholds, pinch factor, two-finger pan, cancellation, three-finger cancel.
- **Reachability on every page** (headless app with `MinimalPlugins` + `ConsoleCorePlugin` + the menu and workshop models, input injected as Bevy input messages `KeyboardInput`, `MouseButtonInput` / `CursorMoved`, `TouchInput`, gamepad events): for **every page of the menu tree and every workshop / character state**, every focusable item can be reached and activated with the keyboard alone, the gamepad alone, the mouse alone (click at the item's laid-out rectangle) and touch alone (tap at its rectangle); Back works with each; no page needs a second device.
- **Hit-target sizes:** in touch mode every interactive rectangle on every page is ≥ 48 logical px and ≥ 9 mm at 1280 × 720 and 800 × 600, scale factors 1, 1.5 and 2, with ≥ 8 px gaps (extends `every_menu_page_fits_a_16_9_window_with_its_text`).
- **3D scenes:** orbit / zoom / pan reach the same camera states with each device; limits hold.
- **Ride overlay:** taps on lean / autodrive / U-turn / exit arrows produce the same `ClientCore` inputs as the keys; overlay hidden with `hud off`.
- **Screenshots:** the hint bar for each device and the touch overlay, X11 + Wayland (scene harness).

#### 3.2.3 Touch Steering: tapping or holding the left / right side (planning, 2026-11-16, v3.78; built v4.23 and v5.15, see *Built*)

The user asked (2026-11-16): "when running on a touch capable device (e.g. iOS/Android, but not limited to that, check browser capabilities) we need a way to control the steering (left/right) by tapping on the screen on the left or right side." This section is a **proposal**. It refines the ride touch overlay of 3.2.2 (M10): the small *lean ‹ ›* buttons there are replaced by the two **halves of the screen**. The open decisions are in *Open questions* at the end.

**As found (2026-11-16, origin/main at v3.77):**

- **Riding has no touch input yet.** The browser page sets `touch-action: none` on the canvas (`apps/web/web/index.html`) and reports `coarse_pointer` in `window.ocwDeviceInfo`, but only for the quality preset (B7). Touches reach the menu rows through `bevy_picking` (`ocw_render::menu::MenuPointer`). The handover notes say: "phone HUD wraps, no touch riding controls (M10)". `controls.touch` / `controls.touch_overlay` (3.2.2) are not built.
- **Unicorn mode already has touch** (`ocw_ui::god::touch`, Phase 13B, shared since v3.39). It is pure and keeps a `Finger { id, pos, start, prev }` per touch. A finger on the left half is a stick, a finger on the right half looks around, two fingers pinch, a third cancels, and the + / − buttons come from a layout shared with the renderer (`ocw_render::inspect_hud::touch_buttons`). In the same frame a touch also suppresses the mouse look (Windows' emulated mouse). Ride touch reuses this pattern: a shared finger tracker, a pure mapping and a button layout shared with the HUD.
- **Ride steering keys are shared only in part.** `ocw_client::input` has the pure parts (`steer_direction`, `lean_ramp`, `LINE_KEY_RATE_MPS` = 2 m/s, `junction_key`, `KeyThrottle`). The Bevy systems that call them are still per app: `apps/desktop/src/input.rs::steer` and `apps/web/src/plugin.rs`. **Parity gap:** the browser's system has no junction exit keys (Q / E, the arrows at an active junction in autodrive), no U-turn and no rejoin, so a browser free ride cannot choose exits. Step TS1 closes this gap first, so touch steering is written once, in shared code.

**Detection: when touch steering is active and when its hints show**

- **Zones vs hints.** The two steering zones **always answer a real touch** in a ride, unless the setting is *off*: a touch is never ignored because detection guessed wrong. Detection decides only whether the **hints** (chevrons, the first-ride tip, the touch power buttons) are shown and whether the HUD uses touch-size targets. This is 3.2.2's `ActiveInput::Touch`.
- **Browser facts**, read once by the page and added to `window.ocwDeviceInfo`: `navigator.maxTouchPoints`, `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)')` (the primary pointer), `matchMedia('(any-pointer: coarse)')` (any touch screen), `matchMedia('(hover: none)')`, `'ontouchstart' in window`. Bevy's winit web backend turns Pointer Events with `pointerType == "touch"` into `TouchInput` (to verify in TS3; if it does not, a small page listener forwards them). Pen and mouse pointers stay pointers.
- **The rule** (pure: `ocw_client::input::touch::TouchPresence`, fed with input events, their times and the facts):
  1. **Shown at the start** on a touch-first device, where the primary pointer is coarse and `maxTouchPoints > 0`: phones, tablets, and an iPad that reports a Mac user agent (`MacIntel` with `maxTouchPoints > 1`, as `ocw-gpu.js` already tells them apart).
  2. **Shown once a real touch arrives** (a `TouchInput` start), on any device. This covers **hybrid laptops** and touch monitors: their primary pointer is fine, so `any-pointer: coarse` alone does not show the hints.
  3. **Hidden again** after another device is used: a key press, a mouse click or a mouse move of 4 px or more (3.2.2: jitter below that does not count), or a gamepad button or stick beyond its dead zone. Mouse events within 500 ms of a touch at the same place are the system's emulated mouse (Windows) and do not count. The next touch shows the hints again. An iPad with a keyboard starts shown and hides on the first key.
  4. **The setting overrides:** `controls.touch_steer auto|on|off` (default *auto*; Settings → Controls beside *Touch mode*; console `controls.touch_steer`). *on* always shows the hints. *off* turns the zones off as well, so taps reach only the HUD buttons, for riders who only want the camera on touch. In the browser, `?touch=on|off` sets it for the session (used by the tests).
- **Desktop app:** the same code reads Bevy's `TouchInput` on Linux X11 (XInput 2.2), Wayland (`wl_touch`) and Windows. Devices: touch laptops, tablets, the Steam Deck, a touch monitor. Windows' emulated mouse is filtered as in 3.2.2. macOS has no touch screens (winit), so it never shows the hints. The kiosk stays untested on real touch (Phase 4 Q5, postponed).

**The zones**

- The ride view is split into a **left** and a **right zone**. Both are computed per frame (pure: `TouchZones { view, safe_insets, top_band, dead_band, excluded: Vec<Rect> }`, `zone_at(pos) -> Option<Side>`).
- **Not part of a zone:**
  - a **dead band in the centre**: 12 % of the view width, at least 48 px (a touch there does not steer; Q7 has what it does instead);
  - a **top band**: 15 % of the view height, where the status line, the GPS / ride info and the ☰ button sit;
  - the **safe-area insets** (notch, home indicator; `env(safe-area-inset-*)` in the browser);
  - **16 px at every window edge** (3.2.2: OS edge swipes, Android's back gesture, the iOS home bar);
  - every **interactive HUD rectangle**: ☰, autodrive, U-turn, the junction fan's exit arrows, the power + / − buttons, the voice indicator, the elevation profile, the results panel. These rectangles come from the same layout functions the renderer draws with, as `touch_buttons` does today, so a tap on a button is never also a steer.
- **The zone follows the finger.** A finger counts for the zone it is in now, like a held key. Sliding it into the dead band pauses the steering; sliding across into the other half steers the other way. Lifting the finger, or a `TouchPhase::Canceled` (an incoming call, the OS taking the gesture), releases the side.
- **Not active** while the menu, a dialog, the console or the results panel is open (they take the taps), while the rider is down after a crash (14 Phase 12), or in Unicorn mode (`not_flying`, as the keys). A finger that is already down when the menu closes or the rider lands counts only after it is lifted, so nothing carries over.

**Tap vs press-and-hold** (proposal; Q1, Q2)

- **Steering starts on touch-down, with no wait.** A finger in a zone is the arrow key of that side held down: it goes through the same `steer_direction` → line or lean code as the keys, so a hold steers exactly like holding ← / →. The 300 ms tap delay is not an issue: the page has `touch-action: none` and no double-tap zoom.
- **A tap** is a touch lifted within **250 ms** that moved less than 10 px (the gesture recogniser's thresholds, 3.2.2). A tap gives a **guaranteed minimum step**. When the finger lifts, the steering it did is topped up to the step, at any frame rate:
  - **line steering (autodrive):** a tap moves the line by **0.5 m** (`TAP_LINE_STEP_M`, about one rider's width; the arrow key moves it 2 m/s × the hold). A hold of 1 s moves it 2 m, like the key. The edge limits stay as they are (5.2.1).
  - **lean steering (manual, wild mode):** a tap changes the lean by **0.1 rad** (about 6°, `TAP_LEAN_STEP_RAD`; what a 0.25 s key hold gives with `LEAN_KEY_RATE`). As with the keys the lean **stays** after the finger lifts (Q2). The upright stop of `lean_ramp` applies: a tap toward upright from a small lean stops at upright, and a second tap leans on to the other side.
- **Autodrive (Q3):** a touch does what an arrow key does. In autodrive it moves the line and does **not** switch autodrive off; the autodrive toggle switches it off. With autodrive off the zones lean.
- **Junction exit choice (2.2.1; Q5):** while a junction is **active** in autodrive, the zones choose the exit, as the arrows do (`junction_key` with the touch as the arrow press). Each touch-down is **one exit step** (Select ±1); holding does not repeat, and a second tap goes one exit further. The line does not move meanwhile. With manual steering the zones keep leaning, and the fan's exit arrows are tap targets (tap = choose that exit, 3.2.2): the touch form of Q / E. The overlay's lock point and the green locked arrow are unchanged; taps after the lock point apply to the next junction, as keys do.
- **Route rides:** route rides are the same as with the keys. In solo route rides the zones choose exits, and choosing another exit leaves the route (2.2.1). The HUD's "Off the route" line gets a **Rejoin** button. In group rides with "follow leader" the zones only move the line.
- **U-turn:** U-turn stays a **button** (in the overlay, lower centre, beside autodrive). It asks with a second tap, as in 3.2.2, since a stray U-turn on a phone is costly. It is rate-limited like the key and shown only in free ride. There is no zone gesture for it (Q4 lists one as an option).
- **Both sides at once (Q4):** the proposal is the key rule. ← and → together give `steer_direction` 0, so nothing steers while both are held, and a tap on the other side while one is held does nothing. Lifting one finger resumes the other side. Two fingers on the same side count as one.

**Visual feedback** (`ocw-render::touch_hud`, part of the HUD layer: hidden with `hud off`; in captures only when shown)

- **Chevrons** ‹ and › at the lower left and lower right, drawn at 40 % opacity while the hints are shown. They fade to 15 % after 8 s without a touch, the overlay rule of 3.2.2 (`OVERLAY_S`). In junction mode they become small exit arrows.
- **An edge glow** on the side being held: a soft gradient 24 px wide along that screen edge, at 25 % opacity in the HUD's accent colour (M9's colour-blind-safe palette). A tap flashes the chevron for 150 ms.
- **A first-ride tip:** "Tap or hold the left / right side to steer". It is shown once per device (setting `controls.touch_tip_seen`) and also listed on the help page.
- The glow and the chevrons are hints only. The steering itself shows in the rider and the line marker, as with the keys.

**Accessibility and size**

- **Handedness:** `controls.touch_hand right|left` (default right) mirrors the overlay buttons (☰ stays top left; autodrive, U-turn and the power buttons move to the other side). It **never swaps the steering**: the left side always steers left.
- **Zone size:** `controls.touch_zones full|lower` (default *full*: the whole height below the top band; *lower*: only the lower half, so the upper half is free for the camera on a tablet). The dead band's width is set with `controls.touch_dead_band` (5 – 30 %, default 12 %).
- **Tap-only mode:** `controls.touch_hold on|off` (default on). With *off* a touch-down does nothing until the finger lifts, and each touch is exactly one step, however long it is held. This is for riders who cannot hold a finger still on a moving handlebar mount.
- Hit targets and gaps of all overlay buttons follow 3.2.2 (≥ 9 mm and ≥ 48 px).

**Haptics:** a short vibration (10 ms) on a tap step, an exit change and the exit locking (20 ms), through `navigator.vibrate` where it exists (Chrome and Firefox on Android). iOS Safari has no Vibration API, and desktop browsers ignore it. `ocw_ui` sends a `HapticPulse` message; the browser app plays it (`apps/web/src/browser.rs`, guarded, so it never fails where there is no API), and the desktop app ignores it (winit has no API; gamepad rumble stays separate). Setting `controls.haptics on|off` (default on).

**Other touch needs it raises**

- **Menu:** the ☰ button (top left, inside the safe area) is **always shown** while the hints are shown, not only after a mouse move (3.2.2). The menu's Back button is shown in touch mode, as planned.
- **Power without a trainer:** this is the virtual trainer of the preview (B8a) on a phone, where ↑ / ↓ do not exist. Proposed: **+ / − / stop buttons** at the right edge above the right zone (left edge with `touch_hand left`). A tap on + is one 25 W step, a hold ramps the power, and *stop* brakes. These are ↑ held, ↑ pressed and ↓ fed into the shared `KeyThrottle` as `ThrottleKeys` from the touch buttons, so the rules are the keyboard's. They are shown only when no power device is connected. A trainer or power meter hides them.
- **Browser gestures must not move the page** (`apps/web/web/index.html`):
  - `touch-action: none` also on `html` and `body`, not only the canvas;
  - `overscroll-behavior: none` (no pull-to-refresh in Chrome Android, no rubber band in Safari);
  - `-webkit-user-select: none` and `-webkit-touch-callout: none` on the canvas (no selection or callout on a long press);
  - `contextmenu` prevented on the canvas (Android's long press);
  - Safari's proprietary `gesturestart` / `gesturechange` prevented (pinch zoom: iOS ignores `user-scalable=no` since iOS 10, but `touch-action: none` together with these stops the pinch on the canvas);
  - `touchmove` listened to with `{ passive: false }` and prevented on the canvas, for older Safari.
  - The 300 ms click delay does not apply (`width=device-width` and `touch-action`).
- **Safe areas:** the viewport gets `viewport-fit=cover`, so the canvas fills the whole screen behind the notch. The HUD and the zones then keep out of `env(safe-area-inset-*)`: the page passes the insets to the app in `window.ocwDeviceInfo` and on `resize`. Built in v5.15 (see *Built* below).
- **Full screen and staying awake:**
  - A *Full screen* entry in the menu and the first-ride tip, where the Fullscreen API exists (Android Chrome, iPad Safari). It needs a user gesture, and a tap counts.
  - The iPhone's Safari has no element full screen. There the page offers *Add to Home Screen*: a web app manifest with `display: fullscreen` (standalone on iOS) and an Apple touch icon.
  - `navigator.wakeLock.request('screen')` keeps the screen on while riding (Chrome, Safari 16.4+). It is requested again after `visibilitychange`.
- **Orientation:** landscape is preferred. `screen.orientation.lock('landscape')` is tried in full screen (Android; iOS has no lock). In portrait the ride still works, since the halves are halves either way and the HUD wraps (v3.68). A one-time tip says "turn your phone for a wider view".
- **Audio unlock:** the first tap both steers and unlocks the audio gate (`ocw_audio::unlock::AudioGate`, 14 Phase 10 B5). Nothing extra is needed.
- **Unicorn mode:** while flying, `ocw_ui::god::touch` owns the screen (left half = stick, right half = look). The ride zones and their hints are off and the god-mode + / − buttons show. Landing hands the screen back after all fingers have lifted. Both use one shared finger tracker (`ocw_ui::touch::Fingers`, moved out of `god::touch`), so ids, cancel and the emulated-mouse filter are handled once.

**Where the code goes (both apps, full parity)**

- `ocw_client::input::touch` (pure, wasm): `TouchZones`, `zone_at`, the per-frame `TouchSteer` state machine (fingers in → `TouchSide { left_held, right_held, left_tap, right_tap, left_down, right_down }`), the tap top-up (`TAP_LINE_STEP_M`, `TAP_LEAN_STEP_RAD`) and `TouchPresence`.
- `ocw_ui::ride_input` (new, Bevy): **one ride-steering system for both apps.** It takes keys, pads and touches, and calls `junction_key`, `steer_direction`, `lean_ramp`, `u_turn`, `rejoin_route`, autodrive and wild mode as `apps/desktop/src/input.rs::steer` does today. It replaces that system and the browser's copy, which closes the parity gap. `ocw_ui::touch` adds the finger tracker and `TouchInput` → `TouchSteer`.
- `ocw-render::touch_hud`: the chevrons, the glow, the overlay buttons and their shared layout (as `inspect_hud::touch_buttons`).
- `apps/web`: the page CSS / JS above, the device facts and the insets, `HapticPulse`, wake lock, full screen and the manifest. `apps/desktop`: nothing of its own beyond the plugin.

**Steps**

- **TS1:** the shared ride-steering system in `ocw_ui` (junction keys, U-turn and rejoin also in the browser).
- **TS2:** the pure zone, tap and presence logic, with its tests.
- **TS3:** the Bevy glue and the HUD (chevrons, glow, tip, ☰).
- **TS4:** the page: browser gestures, safe areas, wake lock, full screen, the manifest.
- **TS5:** the touch power buttons and Rejoin.
- **TS6:** haptics.
- **TS7:** the browser and screenshot tests.

TS1 – TS3 are what the user asked for; TS4 makes it usable on phones.

**Tests (spec 11.4: no step without tests)**

- **Pure (`ocw_client::input::touch`):**
  - `zone_at` for both halves; the dead band at 12 % and its 48 px minimum; the top band; the safe insets; the 16 px edges; an excluded HUD rectangle (a tap on autodrive is never a steer); `touch_hand left` mirrors the buttons but not the sides.
  - Tap vs hold at the thresholds (249 / 251 ms, 9 / 11 px).
  - A tap moves the line exactly 0.5 m and leans exactly 0.1 rad at dt 1/30, 1/60 and 1/144. A 1 s hold moves the line 2 m, like the key.
  - The upright stop on a tap toward upright.
  - At an active junction in autodrive: one exit per touch, no repeat on hold, the line kept.
  - Both sides at once give 0; one lifted resumes the other.
  - A finger sliding into the dead band and across.
  - `Canceled` releases; a finger down from before the menu closed is ignored.
  - Tap-only mode.
  - `TouchPresence`: coarse device shown at start; hybrid laptop hidden until a touch; a key, a click and a 4 px mouse move hide the hints; 3 px jitter and emulated mouse within 500 ms do not; gamepad beyond the dead zone hides them; *on* / *off* override; the iPad-as-Mac facts.
- **Shared UI, headless** (`ocw-ui` with `MinimalPlugins` over the in-memory `FrameServer`, as the god-mode tests):
  - Injected `TouchInput` sequences give the **same `ClientCore` state as the matching key presses**: line offset, lean, exit selection, U-turn through its button and confirmation, rejoin.
  - Touches do nothing while the menu is open or the rider is flying.
  - The touch power buttons drive `KeyThrottle` as ↑ / ↓ do.
  - Both apps' plugin tests run the same cases (parity).
- **Browser** (`scripts/test-web.py`, a new case `touch`; Chromium over the DevTools protocol with `Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled` and `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`; read through a new `window.ocw.steer()` JSON: line offset, lean, autodrive, zone state, hints shown):
  - a tap on the right half moves the line by +0.5 m;
  - a 1 s hold on the left moves it about −2 m;
  - a tap in the dead band and on the ☰ button does not steer;
  - a pinch does not zoom (`visualViewport.scale` stays 1) and a drag does not scroll (`scrollY` 0);
  - the hints show after the first touch and hide after a key press.
- **WebKit** (`scripts/test-web-webkit.py`, its `iphone` case: Playwright's iPhone 15 with `hasTouch`): `page.touchscreen.tap` on each half steers; the safe insets are passed in; the page throws nothing where `navigator.vibrate` is missing.
- **Screenshots** (scene harness, X11 + Wayland, and the browser cases):
  - the HUD with the chevrons, the glow on a held right side, junction mode with exit chevrons, the power buttons, the first-ride tip;
  - iPhone 15 landscape and portrait;
  - `hud off` hides everything.

**Open questions (for the user)**

- **Q1 – Tap vs hold: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): as proposed** – touch-down steers at once like a held arrow key, and a tap (< 250 ms) is topped up to one step (line 0.5 m, lean 0.1 rad).
- **Q2 – Lean steering on touch: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): as proposed** – as with the keys: the lean stays after the finger lifts and is straightened with the other side (it does not spring back to upright like the stick).
- **Q3 – Does a touch switch autodrive off? Decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): no, as proposed** – as with the arrow keys, in autodrive a touch moves the line, and only the autodrive button switches it off.
- **Q4 – Both sides at once: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): nothing, as proposed** – touching both halves at once does nothing (as holding ← and → together).
- **Q5 – Junction choice by the zones: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): the halves always steer; exits are chosen by tapping the fan** – the user: "halves stay steering, select road by clicking the fan". At a junction, in autodrive and with manual steering alike, the screen halves keep steering; the exit is chosen only by tapping its arrow in the junction fan.
- **Q6 – Desktop app too: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): yes, as proposed** – touch steering in the desktop app too (parity rule), on Windows / Linux touch screens with the same *auto* rule (hints after the first touch). The kiosk stays untested on touch (Phase 4 Q5).
- **Q7 – Camera drag vs steering: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): two fingers move the camera** – the user: "make the camera drag when dragging with two fingers". In a ride one finger only steers (the halves, no 250 ms wait); a **two-finger drag** anywhere orbits the camera and a pinch sets the chase distance (as planned in 3.2.2). The one-finger orbit of 3.2.2 stays outside a ride (menus, the workshop, god mode's look).
- **Q8 – Zone height: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): as proposed** – the steering zones cover the full height below the top band; *lower half only* is a setting.

**Built (2026-11-16, v4.23): TS2, TS3, TS7 and parts of TS4, in both apps (parity: one shared implementation).**

- **Pure core** `ocw_client::input::touch` (Bevy-free, wasm): `TouchZones` / `zone_at` (the halves without the dead band – 12 %, at least 48 px –, the top band of 15 %, 16 px edges, the safe-area insets and the HUD's tap targets; `ZoneHeight::Lower` starts the zones at half the height), `TouchSteer` (fed with `TouchEvent`s, steering a `Steerable` – the `ClientCore` or a test rider): a finger in a zone is the held arrow key of that side (line 2 m/s in autodrive, `lean_ramp` with its own upright pause otherwise); a finger lifted within 250 ms and moved < 10 px is a tap, topped up to 0.5 m / 0.1 rad from where it started (the upright stop of the lean included); both sides held steer nothing and a tap on the other side while one is held does nothing (Q4); the zone follows the finger; `Cancel` releases; fingers down while the zones were inactive are ignored until lifted (`suspend`); a touch never switches autodrive off (Q3). **Two fingers** are two steering fingers until their centre or their spread moved 12 px (`CAMERA_START_PX`); from then on they are the camera until lifted: the centre's move is the orbit drag, the spread's ratio the chase distance in wheel steps (Q7). `fan_hit`: a touch on the junction fan picks the exit whose arrow is nearest in direction (within half the gap to its neighbours, at most 45°, not at the pivot); the fan's rectangle is a tap target, so the halves never choose exits (Q5). `TouchPresence` with `TouchFacts` (`maxTouchPoints`, `pointer: coarse`, the iPad-as-Mac): shown at the start on touch-first devices, after the first touch elsewhere, hidden by a key, a gamepad, a click or a mouse move of 4 px; the emulated mouse within 500 ms and 32 px of a touch does not count; `controls.touch_steer on / off` override; the chevrons dim after 8 s.
- **Shared Bevy glue** `ocw_ui::touch::TouchSteerPlugin` (added by `apps/desktop/src/main.rs` and the browser's `WebUiPlugin`): Bevy's `Touches` → `TouchSteer` → the ride's client through `RideAccess` (line or lean; `choose_exit` for a fan tap, sent by the apps' existing turn message), `CameraOrbit::apply` for the two-finger camera, the presence from keys / mouse / pads, `TouchHud` for the renderer, the tip marked seen (`controls.touch_tip_seen`, saved) by the first touch steer, and `state_json` (the browser's `window.ocw.steer()`). Active only in the ride's input context, not in flight and not with *off*. The chase camera's mouse orbit (`ocw_render::camera`) ignores the mouse while a finger is down (Windows' emulated mouse; Q7: one finger never orbits in a ride).
- **Hints** `ocw_render::touch_hud` (part of the HUD: `hud off` hides them): the chevrons ‹ › at the lower left and right (two rotated bars each; 40 %, 15 % dimmed, 90 % while held or for 150 ms after a tap step), the edge glow of the held side (two strips of 12 px at 25 % and 10 % of the accent blue, from the zones' top), the first-ride tip "Tap or hold the left / right side to steer – two fingers move the camera". `ocw_render::junction::fan_geometry` is the fan's layout (window size and `UiScale`) used by the drawing and by the hit test.
- **Settings:** `controls.touch_steer auto|on|off` (default *auto*), `controls.touch_zones full|lower` (default *full*), `controls.touch_tip_seen`; on *Settings → Controls → Touch and unicorn* (the former *Unicorn mode* page, renamed: the Controls page was full; rows *Touch steering*, *Touch zones*, *Unicorn: invert Y*, *Unicorn: flight*). The browser's page option `?touch=auto|on|off` sets it for the visit (not saved).
- **Page** (`apps/web/web/index.html`): `window.ocwDeviceInfo` gets `max_touch_points` and `ipad_as_mac` (`DeviceInfo::touch_facts`); `overscroll-behavior: none` on `html` / `body`, no selection or callout on the canvas (`user-select`, `-webkit-touch-callout`). The touches reach Bevy through winit's touch pointers (no page listener needed).
- **Tests:** pure (`ocw_client::input::touch`): the zones (both halves, the dead band and its 48 px minimum, the top band, the edges, the insets, an excluded rectangle), *lower* frees the upper half; a tap = 0.5 m at 30 / 60 / 144 fps and holds of one frame, 0.1 s and 0.249 s; a 1 s hold = 2 m; steering starts on touch-down; tap vs hold at 249 / 251 ms and 9 / 11 px; a tap leans 0.1 rad at 30 / 60 / 144 fps and the lean stays; a tap toward upright stops there, the next leans on; both sides = nothing, a tap on the other side is nothing, one lifted resumes the other, two fingers on one side count as one; the zone follows the finger (dead band pauses, across reverses); `Cancel` and a finger from before the menu closed; autodrive stays on; two fingers moving together = camera drag and pinch (wheel steps), one lifted stays camera, one finger never the camera; the fan's hit test (three exits, between arrows, the pivot, outside, close arrows) and a fan tap chooses the exit and never steers while the halves keep steering; the presence (phone, iPad as Mac, hybrid laptop hidden until a touch, the emulated mouse, 3 px jitter vs 4 px, key, click, *on* / *off*, dimming); the page's touch facts. `ocw_render`: the fan geometry with the HUD scale, the chevrons' bars and opacities, the hints drawn and hidden headless. `ocw_ui` (headless over the in-memory `FrameServer`): `TouchInput` tap and hold move the line, a tap leans, *off* and a finger from the menu do nothing, two fingers orbit and pinch zoom without steering, a fan tap is taken by the fan. **Both apps** (`apps/web/src/plugin.rs`, `apps/desktop/src/input.rs`, the desktop on its local server): synthetic `TouchInput` gives the same line as the matching ← hold (0.8 m in 20 frames), a tap +0.5 m, autodrive kept, the key hides the hints; the browser's `?touch=`. **Browser** (`scripts/web_ui_test.py`, part of `make test-web`; CDP touch emulation and `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`, read through `window.ocw.steer()`): *on* shows the hints and the tip (screenshot `-touch-hints.jpg`), *auto* hides them on a desktop browser until the first touch, a tap on the right half +0.5 m, a held left side steers left (screenshot `-touch-hold.jpg` with the glow) by about 2 m/s, taps in the dead band and the top band do not steer, a two-finger pinch across both halves does not steer and the page neither zooms nor scrolls, a key hides the hints. The desktop's hints: an X11 screenshot with `controls.touch_steer on`.
- **Open (v4.23, partly done in v5.15 below):** TS1 – the shared ride-steering system (the free ride's keys – exits, U-turn, rejoin – are shared and in the browser since v5.21, 3.2.5; the fan tap chooses exits in both apps); the other HUD tap targets (☰, autodrive, U-turn, Rejoin, the touch power buttons of TS5) do not exist yet, so only the fan is excluded from the zones; handedness, the dead band's setting, tap-only mode; haptics (TS6; the iPhone has no `navigator.vibrate` anyway); the rider-down check (the keys do not have it either); screenshots with a held side on the desktop (a real touch screen; the kiosk stays untested on touch, Phase 4 Q5). Not yet tried on a real phone or touch screen.

**Built (2026-11-19, v5.15): the rest of TS4 – the phone page – and the WebKit iPhone case of TS7.**

- **Safe areas:** the viewport has `viewport-fit=cover`, so the canvas and the 3D view fill the whole screen behind the notch. The page (`window.ocwScreen`) measures `env(safe-area-inset-*)` with a hidden probe on load, on `resize` and after a turn (again 300 ms later: iOS updates them late), sets them as the CSS variables `--safe-top` … `--safe-left` (the Devices panel and its button, the sound hint, the GPU note, the status and loading screen, the preview's start page and its line keep clear of them) and passes them to the app (`window.ocwScreen.safeArea()`, followed every frame by `apps/web/src/screen.rs`; also `safe_insets` in `window.ocwDeviceInfo`). The page option `?safe-insets=T,R,B,L` (CSS px) stands in for them in tests and screenshots (desktop engines have no notch). In the app `ocw_render::safe_area::SafeArea`: while any inset is set, the UI is drawn by a camera of its own (`SafeUiCamera`: order 10, no clear, the world camera's MSAA, no tonemapping) whose viewport is the safe part of the window, so every HUD box, the menu and the touch hints are laid out inside it; the code that places UI by the window's size (the navigation map's and the workout panel's fit, the top panel's width, the photo preview) takes the safe area's size (`ui_area`), the name tags at a point of the 3D view (unicorn mode's names and pins) subtract its top left, the navigation map's box for the page stays in window coordinates, and the console stays on the world's camera. Insets that would leave less than a quarter of the window are ignored. Without insets (the desktop, phones without a notch, all other tests) there is no extra camera – nothing changes. The touch zones take the insets (`TouchZones::insets`, `Insets::from_json` in the pure core): a touch behind the notch or on the home bar never steers; the junction fan's hit test follows the HUD into the safe area; `window.ocw.steer()` reports `insets`.
- **Page gestures** (while riding, class `ocw-riding` on `html`): `touch-action: none` on `html` and `body` (not on the preview's start page, which must scroll); Safari's `gesturestart` / `gesturechange` / `gestureend` prevented; `contextmenu` (the long press's callout) prevented on the canvas; `touchmove` on the canvas listened to with `{ passive: false }` and prevented.
- **Staying awake:** `navigator.wakeLock.request('screen')` when the ride starts, again on `visibilitychange` to visible and on the next touch or key if it is not held (Safari may want a gesture); where the API is missing nothing is asked and nothing is thrown (`window.ocwScreen.state().wake_lock`: `unsupported` / `held` / `released` / `failed`).
- **Full screen:** *Menu → Captures → Full screen* (the browser's page of its own commands; command `fullscreen toggle|on|off|status`) and a *⛶ Full screen* button beside the first-ride tip, both where the Fullscreen API exists (Android's Chrome, the iPad's Safari; the button's tap is the gesture it needs); entering it tries `screen.orientation.lock('landscape')` (Android; iOS has no lock). On the iPhone, which has no element full screen, the tip and the command say *Share → Add to Home Screen*: the page has a web app manifest (`manifest.webmanifest`: `display: fullscreen`, `start_url` `./`, theme and background `#10141a`, the logo's PNGs 256 and 512 and the SVG), `ocw-256.png` as the Apple touch icon, `apple-mobile-web-app-capable`, `mobile-web-app-capable`, the title *OCW* and the translucent status bar; started from the home screen there is no tip. `scripts/build-web.sh` (`make web`, `make web-preview`) copies the manifest and the icons, `scripts/web-preview-site.py` puts them on the GitHub Pages site, `scripts/web-serve.py` serves `.webmanifest` as `application/manifest+json`.
- **Orientation:** a one-time tip "Turn your phone for a wider view" in portrait on a touch-first phone (8 s, or until turned; remembered in `localStorage`); the ride works in portrait too.
- **Tests:** pure – the page's insets read and checked (missing, broken, negative, capped), the zones keep off the notch and the home bar (iPhone 15 in landscape and portrait); `ocw_render::safe_area` – the viewport in both orientations at pixel ratio 3, no viewport without insets or with insets that leave too little, the camera spawned, moved on a turn and removed; `ocw_ui::touch` – with insets a touch behind the notch, on the other side and on the home bar does not steer, each half does, `insets` in the JSON; the web app – the page's insets become the safe area; the browser menu's Captures page has *Full screen*. **WebKit** (`scripts/test-web-webkit.py`, Playwright's iPhone 15 with `hasTouch`, portrait with insets 59 / 0 / 34 / 0 and landscape with 0 / 59 / 21 / 59, no element full screen as on the iPhone): the manifest served and valid with its icons, the Apple touch icon and the meta tags, `viewport-fit=cover`; the insets reach the app; `touch-action: none` on `body`; the hints and the tip with *Add to Home Screen*; `page.touchscreen.tap` on each half steers ±0.5 m, taps behind the notch and on the home bar do not; a held right side (touch pointers) steers and glows; the wake lock missing (tolerated) and present (held, asked again after `visibilitychange`); no page errors. Screenshots: `test-output/touch-ts4/`.
- **Still open for the iPhone:** a try on a real iPhone (the emulation has no real notch, no real home-screen start and no real wake lock); TS1, handedness / tap-only settings, haptics (none on iOS). TS5's power buttons: built in v5.17 (below).

**Built (2026-11-19, v5.17): TS5's touch power buttons, and the phone layout (3.2 *Phone layout*).**

- **The buttons** (`ocw_render::touch_hud`, as *Other touch needs it raises → Power without a trainer* planned): **stop**, **−** and **+**, 56 CSS px (about 9 mm on a phone, kept at any HUD scale) with 12 px between them, right-aligned with the right chevron's outer edge above the right zone – in landscape a row at the top right under the timestamp's column (+ nearest the thumb), in portrait a column along the right edge just above the chevron (+ at the top), so they stay off the road in the middle; below the top panel and the top-right column if those reach down to them (`power_buttons`, their boxes of the last frame) – a portrait column pushed down that way shrinks to stay above the chevron, to no less than 44 CSS px. Shown with the touch hints while the power is the virtual trainer's (`ClientCore::virtual_device`): a trainer or power meter hides them.
- **What they do** (`ocw_ui::touch::TouchPower`, read by both apps' power keys and joined with the keyboard's, `ThrottleKeys::or`): + is ↑ (a finger down = one 25 W step, held = the ramp), − takes 10 W (per tap; Page Down did that until v5.21, now it chooses the junction's exit, 3.2.5), stop is ↓ (no extra power, the brake on, the virtual trainer at 0 W); + after stop releases the brake. As with the keys the extra power is added to the virtual trainer's, so − does not go below it. The held button is drawn darker. A finger that starts on a button never steers (the buttons are left out of the zones, `TouchZones::excluded`).
- **Tests:** `touch_hud` (the layout at desktop and iPhone sizes: the size in CSS px, the gaps, above the chevron, the row / column, + at the right, off the middle, pushed below a panel in the way and not by one beside; the buttons shown and hidden with the hints); `ocw_ui::touch` (headless ride: no buttons with a power device, + pressed and held, − = Page Down, stop = ↓, none of them steers, the half beside them still does, nothing with the setting off); WebKit (both iPhone cases: + adds power without steering, − takes some away, stop gives 0 and the brake, + rides on; screenshots `-stopped`, `-riding`). `window.ocw.steer()` reports `power`, `power_held`, `power_buttons` (CSS px) and `key_power_w`.
- **Not built (TS5's rest):** the Rejoin button (needs TS1's shared rejoin in the browser) and `controls.touch_hand left` (mirrored buttons).

**Built (v5.64): the first ride's hints apart on a phone, portrait and landscape.** The first-ride tip, the page's screen tip (*Full screen: Share → Add to Home Screen* on the iPhone, *⛶ Full screen* on Android) and the power buttons covered each other (the v5.46 Loop screenshot in portrait; in landscape the tip lay over both chevrons and the screen tip over the riders). Now each has its own place, the safe areas included:
- **The first-ride tip** (`ocw_render::touch_hud::tip_place`, placed every frame): below the HUD's top boxes (the top panel, the top-right column) in a band of its own, centred over the rider – in portrait from the left edge to the power buttons' column, with a slot of 44 CSS px for the screen tip right above it; in landscape between the two chevrons and below the power buttons' row. Its box is measured (`HudBoxes::touch_tip`) and `window.ocw.hudLayout()` gives it with the screen tip's slot (`banner_slot`) and the chevrons.
- **The screen tip** is a small banner (12 px, one or two lines, the × a 36 px target; `apps/web/web/index.html`, `placeTip`): the page puts it at the first place that covers none of the app's boxes (panels, first-ride tip, chevrons, power buttons, the map) nor the Devices button – the app's slot (portrait), the bottom between the height profile and the Devices button (landscape), below the first-ride tip, the top; again on every tip check and after a turn.
- **The power buttons** keep their column (portrait) and row (landscape) of v5.17; nothing else enters them.
- **Tests:** `touch_hud::tests::the_first_ride_tip_keeps_clear_of_the_buttons_and_chevrons` (iPhone 15 and 360 × 640 sizes in both orientations: the band clear of the buttons, the chevrons and the top boxes, above the middle, the banner's slot above it in portrait); `scripts/test-web-webkit.py` cases `layout-iphone-390x844`, `layout-iphone-844x390` (with the notch's insets), `layout-android-360x640`, `layout-android-640x360`: no two of the first-ride tip, the screen tip, the power buttons, the chevrons, the HUD's boxes and the Devices button overlap, all inside the safe area, the first-ride tip in the upper half (above the rider).

#### 3.2.4 One local config file, and the start choice: a server or local (planning, 2026-11-17; built v5.02)

Asked by the user (2026-11-17): *"have a local config file in which all local settings are placed. when the desktop app starts, ask the user whether he would like to connect to a server or play local."*

**Today (found 2026-11-17):** the desktop app keeps its local state in several files in its config folder: `settings.toml` (the settings registry, 3.2.1), `riders.toml` (rider profiles), `devices.toml` (remembered trainers and sensors), `strava.toml` / `strava-token.toml` / `strava-sync.toml` (2.8.1), `workshop.toml` (the workshop's choices), `account.json` (the sign-in, 9.1) and `trusted-keys.json` (world package keys). The app starts straight into a local ride (or joins `--server ADDR`); the start screen of 3.2.1 is still "later".

**Planned – one local config file:**
- **One file, `ocw.toml`,** in the app's config folder (Linux `~/.config/ocw/`, Windows `%APPDATA%\ocw\`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/ocw/`), holds **every local setting** in sections: `[settings]` (today's registry, unchanged keys), `[devices]`, `[strava]`, `[workshop]`, `[servers]` (recent servers, the start choice), … – readable and editable by hand, comments kept when the app saves.
- **Local means this computer's settings,** not the rider's: with W5 (decided 2026-11-16) the account, the rider profile, inventory and hearts live on the server; the local file keeps only what belongs to the machine (display, audio devices, controls, trainer pairing, …) and, for local play, the local rider (Q4).
- **Migration:** on the first start of the new version the old files are read once, written into `ocw.toml`, and renamed to `*.migrated` (never deleted); a test covers every old file.
- **The browser** keeps its `localStorage` as the same sections (one key per section), so both apps share the code (`ocw_ui::settings` over `TextStore`).
- `--settings-file PATH` (today: the settings file) points at the whole config file; `--temp` settings stay session-only.

**Planned – the start choice (desktop app):**
- **When the app starts, it asks: *Connect to a server* or *Ride locally*** – a start screen in the shared menu model (3.2.1, all inputs: keys, gamepad, mouse, touch), over the world's backdrop.
  - *Ride locally:* today's behaviour – the in-process local server (6.1), the world and route chosen as now, no account needed.
  - *Connect to a server:* a server address (with recent servers from `ocw.toml`), sign-in where the server needs it (9.1, W5), then that server's welcome (rides, events, hosted rides).
- **Skipped when the command line already decides** (`--server ADDR`, `--world …`, `--free-ride`, `--screenshot`, `--capture`, kiosk / show mode), so automation, tests and the kiosks start as today.
- *Host a ride* (7.1, V2) stays in the Ride menu of a local session.

**Open questions (for the user):**
- **Q1 – The file's name and place: decided (2026-11-19, the user):** yes – `ocw.toml` in the platform's config folder. *Was asked:* today the desktop app keeps its local state spread over about ten files in its config folder (settings, rider profiles, remembered trainers, Strava, workshop, sign-in, trusted keys). The plan is one file that holds every setting of this computer and can be read and edited by hand. The question is what that file is called and where it lives. Options: (a) `ocw.toml` in the system's usual config folder – `~/.config/ocw/` on Linux, `%APPDATA%\ocw\` on Windows, `~/Library/Application Support/ocw/` on macOS; (b) the same folder, another name; (c) beside the app itself – a "portable" set-up, e.g. on a USB stick, where the settings travel with the program. Nothing built yet. Proposal: a – `ocw.toml` in the platform's config folder.
- **Q2 – Secrets in the same file?: decided (2026-11-18, dashboard): as proposed** – secrets (the Strava API application's client id and secret and its tokens, the sign-in session) stay **out of `ocw.toml`**, in a separate `secrets.toml` in the same folder, readable only by the user (mode 0600; the OS keychain later), so the config file can be shared or posted safely. Until `ocw.toml` is built, `strava.toml` / `strava-token.toml` stay as they are (v4.70: an example `strava.toml` is installed into the config folder by the kiosk deploy); with `ocw.toml` they move into `secrets.toml`.
- **Q3 – Ask at every start, or remember?: decided (2026-11-19, the user):** ask at every start with the last choice preselected (Enter takes it). *Was asked:* when the desktop app starts it will ask *Connect to a server* or *Ride locally* – unless the command line already decides (`--server`, `--world`, the kiosk, screenshots). A rider who always rides locally would then answer the same question every day. Nothing built yet. Options: (a) ask at every start with the last choice preselected, so Enter takes it, plus a tick box *Always do this* that skips the question from then on (changeable again in Settings → General); (b) always ask, with no way to skip; (c) ask only on the very first start and then always do the same. Proposal: a.
- **Q4 – The local rider in local play: decided (2026-11-19, the user):** *Ride locally* uses a **local rider kept in `ocw.toml`** (name, weight, height, FTP). Two modes: **Training mode** – all bikes and all gear are available; **Campaign mode** – the rider starts with only one bike, an old and rusty city bike, and earns the rest (as Phase 4 Q16 for new accounts). Campaign mode is **planned but postponed** – Training mode is built first. (The user: "In Training mode all bikes and gear available, In campain mode only one bike as start equipment: a old and rusty citi bike. plan for a campain mode, but postpone for later.") *Was asked:* once accounts exist (W5), a rider's profile, bikes, kit and hearts (the in-game currency earned by riding) live in the account on a server. *Ride locally* runs without a server or account, so it needs a rider of its own: the plan is a local rider in the local config file – name, weight, height, FTP (the rider's power benchmark) and looks, with no hearts and no shop. Open is what that rider rides and wears: (a) only the starter equipment a new account gets – the rusty city bike, sneakers, jeans and hoodie (Phase 4 Q16); (b) everything unlocked, every bike and part free to try; (c) a copy of the signed-in account's rider with its bikes and kit, kept for offline use (related: Phase 4 Q20). (See 4O *No local wallet*: without an account the rider rides the plain default bike and kit everywhere – possibly already answered in part.) The spec makes no firm proposal. Proposal: c for a rider who has signed in once, else a – a suggestion, not in the spec yet.
- **Q5 – What *Connect to a server* offers: decided (2026-11-18, dashboard): as proposed** – an address field plus the recent servers; a public server list comes with the hosting (Phase 5).
- **Q6 – The browser app: decided (2026-11-18, dashboard): as proposed** – the browser app is served by a server and always connects to that one: no start choice there; *Ride locally* in the browser stays the in-page local server it has today, chosen in its own start page.

**Built (v5.02):**
- **`ocw.toml`** (`apps/desktop/src/config.rs`): in the platform's config folder (Linux `~/.config/ocw/`, Windows `%APPDATA%\ocw\`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/ocw/`; `OCW_CONFIG_DIR` overrides it; `--settings-file PATH` names the whole file, `secrets.toml` beside it). Sections: `[settings]` (the registry, its groups as `[settings.audio]`, `[settings.display]`, …; keys unchanged), `[riders]` (the local riders, `[[riders.rider]]`), `[devices]` (`[[devices.device]]`; `--devices-file` still names a file of its own), `[servers]` (the recent servers of *Connect to a server*: `[[servers.recent]]` with `link` and `world`, newest first), `[start]` (`choice = "local" | "server"`), `[strava]` (`auto_upload`, not a secret). The file is edited in place (`toml_edit`): saving a section replaces only that section; the comments and order of the rest stay, and the comment above a replaced section and its tables too. Every write goes through a temporary file (`*.part`, then renamed). The console's `get` shows a saved value as *(saved)* (was *(settings.toml)*), and `get`, `riders.list` and `devices.list` name the place as `~/.config/ocw/ocw.toml [settings]` etc.
- **`secrets.toml`** (Q2): beside it, written with mode 0600 on Unix (also re-set on every save; on Windows the user's profile folder is private): `[strava]` (`client_id`, `client_secret`), `[strava_token]` (the tokens, refreshed by the Strava thread) and `[account]` (`session`: the sign-in session's JSON when no system keyring keeps it; `OCW_ACCOUNT_FILE` still names a file of its own). The environment variables `OCW_STRAVA_CLIENT_ID` / `OCW_STRAVA_CLIENT_SECRET` still win. `ocw.toml` never holds a secret: `config::SECRET_KEYS` (`client_id`, `client_secret`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `session`, `id_token`, `password`, `token`) are checked by a test on a migrated config. While Strava is not set up, the watch looks at `secrets.toml` and at an old `strava.toml` written by hand (it is migrated when it appears, 2.8.1 *uploaded later* keeps working). The kiosk deploy installs `packaging/secrets.example.toml` (values commented out) instead of the example `strava.toml`, and seeds the remembered devices only while `ocw.toml` has none.
- **Migration:** at every start (cheap: only files that are there) the old files of the config folder are read into their sections – `settings.toml` → `[settings]`, `riders.toml` → `[riders]`, `devices.toml` → `[devices]`, `joins.txt` → `[servers]`, `strava.toml` → the credentials to `secrets.toml [strava]` and the rest (`auto_upload`) to `ocw.toml [strava]`, `strava-token.toml` → `secrets.toml [strava_token]`, `account.json` → `secrets.toml [account]` – and **renamed to `*.bak`** (the plan's `*.migrated`; never deleted, a second backup becomes `*.bak.2`); each move is logged once (`config: moved ~/.config/ocw/settings.toml → ~/.config/ocw/ocw.toml [settings] (kept as settings.toml.bak)`, also in the console). Idempotent: the old files are gone afterwards, a second run changes nothing. A broken old file stays where it is (a warning). An old file that appears again later (by hand, an older script) **replaces its section** – it is the newer one – and `ocw.toml` / `secrets.toml` from before is kept as `*.bak`. A `--settings-file` in the old format (a top-level settings group such as `[audio]`) is converted in place the same way (kept as `PATH.bak`). Not moved: the workshop's garage and hearts ledger (`<data dir>/ocw/workshop.toml`, `hearts-ledger.jsonl`: game data in the data folder, not settings) and the trusted world keys (`trusted-keys.json`, `trusted-roots/`, kept by `ocw-worldstore`).
- **The public server first (v6.81, 11.5):** the start page lists **Ride on the public server (ocw-server.fly.dev)** above *Connect to a server* (while `net.public_server` names one); it runs `join public` and opens Ride → Join, which shows how far the join is. Kept as `[start] choice = "public"`, `--start-choice public`. *Ride locally* stays the choice marked before any other, so a plain start never goes online by itself.
- **The start choice** (Q3, Q5; `apps/desktop/src/start.rs`, rows `ocw_client::menu::start`): at every start that no option decides, the menu opens on the page *Open Cycling World* with **Connect to a server** and **Ride locally as NAME (Training mode)**, the last choice marked *last choice* and focused, so Enter takes it (keys, gamepad, mouse and touch as on every menu page). *Connect to a server* opens Ride → Join: the address / link field (typed, pasted), the fingerprint when needed, and the recent servers from `ocw.toml [servers]` (Q5; a public server list comes with the hosting, Phase 5); *Ride locally* closes the menu – the local ride, already running behind the page over the world's backdrop, goes on. The choice is saved in `ocw.toml [start] choice`; console `start.choose server|local`, `start.ask` (shows the page again). **Never asked** when an option decides: `--server`, `--join`, `--world`, `--route`, `--route-file`, `--route-gpx`, `--free-ride`, `--start`, `--workout`, `--screenshot`, `--capture`, the kiosk's show mode (`--no-hearts`, `scripts/kiosk-show.args`; a test reads that file), `--fetch-world`, `--list-worlds` and scripted runs (`--cmd`, `--exec`, `--at`) – so kiosks, smoke runs and tests never stop at the question; `--start-choice ask|local|server` decides explicitly (screenshots of the page use `ask`). The browser app keeps its own start page (Q6): the page is not on the browser's platform.
- **The local rider** (Q4): *Ride locally* rides the chosen local rider of `ocw.toml [riders]` – name, weight, height, FTP (and bike and looks), edited in Settings → Riders and the Workshop as before (the page's note says they are kept in `ocw.toml`). **Training mode** (`workshop::PlayMode::Training`, set by the desktop app; `Wallet::training`): every bike and all gear are available – the balance is unlimited, so nothing in the shop is locked, prices show as *free*, buying, building a bike and repairs book nothing, riding earns no hearts – in a garage of its own (`<data dir>/ocw/training/`), so what is tried there never mixes with a wallet of earned hearts. Tests keep the wallet's rules (`PlayMode::Hearts`, the default).
- **Campaign mode (planned, postponed – not built):** the second mode of *Ride locally*: a new local rider starts with **one bike only, an old and rusty city bike** (and the starter kit of Phase 4 Q16: sneakers, jeans, hoodie), and earns the rest with hearts by riding, as a new account does. *Plan:* (1) a city-bike profile and a "rusty" starter frame and paint in the catalogue (Phase 4, 4B / 4D; the profile's physics within the curated caps); (2) `LocalMode::Campaign` (`ocw_client::menu::start`, already there, `built()` false) becomes a choice on the start page (*Ride locally: Training / Campaign*, remembered in `[start] mode`); (3) Campaign mode uses `PlayMode::Hearts` and the wallet in `<data dir>/ocw/` (the hearts ledger of 4E) with a starter garage of that one bike instead of the six starter bikes (`Garage::starter`); (4) the hearts earned locally stay local until accounts (W5) decide whether they move to the server (related: Phase 4 Q20, offline riding). Open questions for it are asked when it is planned in detail.
- *Tests:* the migration of each old file into its section with its backup (unchanged content), idempotence (a second run changes nothing), an old file coming again (replaces, both backups kept), a broken old file (left where it is), an old `--settings-file` converted in place, a section saved with the rest of the file and its comments kept, secrets only in `secrets.toml` with mode 0600 (also after a later save) and no secret key in `ocw.toml`, the sign-in session in `secrets.toml [account]`, the Strava credentials picked up from an old `strava.toml` written while the app runs (the existing Strava tests), the environment winning, the start choice (the page, the last choice focused, Enter taking it, Down + Enter the other, the choice kept; skipped with deciding options, in captures and with the kiosk's arguments), the recent servers' round trip through `[[servers.recent]]`, the local rider's round trip through `ocw.toml [riders]`, and Training mode unlocking every frameset, the dearest parts and kit with no hearts booked or earned. Screenshots (X11, Wayland) and a listing of a migrated test config folder (made-up data): `test-output/local-config/`.

#### 3.2.5 Input mapping, and the junction's exits on Delete / Page Down (2026-11-21; built v5.21)

Asked by the user (2026-11-21): *"The cursor keys are double used, for steering and also for selecting which road to ride. Use del key to switch leftwards through the option, use page down to switch rightwards."* and *"Add an Input mapping entry in the settings menu, where the user can remap controls. Show the selected mapping for keyboard and gamepad. Allow remapping by selecting the entry. Save the mapping in the local config file."* Decided the same day: **Page Up / Page Down no longer change the keyboard power at all; the power stays on ↑ / ↓ only.**

**The junction's exits (decided, built v5.21):**
- **Delete** moves the next junction's exit choice **one exit to the left**, **Page Down one exit to the right** – in every steering mode, as soon as the junction is known (also before it is active: pre-selection). **Q / E stay** as second keys of the same two actions (they collide with nothing while riding; in the menu Q / E and Page Up / Page Down keep switching tabs – the menu reads its own keys, 3.2.1).
- **← / → only steer** (the line in autodrive, the lean otherwise): they never choose an exit, also not with autodrive near a junction (until v5.17 they did, 2.2.1 *Decided key bindings (v1.6)*).
- **Page Up / Page Down no longer change the keyboard power.** The two actions *Power +10 W* / *Power −10 W* are gone (settings `keys.power_up`, `keys.power_down`, `pad.power_up`, `pad.power_down` are dropped from a file that still has them, without a warning). The keyboard's power is ↑ (faster) / ↓ (stop); the touch power buttons keep their −10 W (3.2.3 TS5).
- **The gamepad is unchanged:** its D-pad left / right were already the exits only – the left stick steers, the D-pad never steered – so nothing was double used there.
- **Both apps:** the free ride's keys (U-turn, back to the route, the two exits) are one shared function `ocw_ui::controls::free_ride_keys`, so the browser now has them too (until v5.17 only the desktop had them; the browser could choose an exit only by tapping the fan, TS1 of 3.2.3).
- **Shown where the keys are told:** the HUD's key line ("up: faster, down: stop, left/right: steer, Del/Q PgDn/E: exit, …") and a hint just above the junction fan while the choice is open ("Del/Q  < exit >  PgDn/E"; not once the exit is locked, not while the touch hints show) – both from the mapping in effect, so a remapped key shows its own name; the README tables, the browser's start page and the help texts.

**Input mapping (decided, built v5.21):**
- **Where:** *Settings → Controls, input mapping → Input mapping* (the former *Keys and buttons* of M9, renamed; the Settings item is labelled *Controls, input mapping*, because Settings has seven items, the ten-foot maximum – see Q1). The page lists four groups – *Power and steering*, *Autodrive and junctions*, *Camera, video, app*, *Voice chat and map* (each a sub page of at most six actions: the ten-foot rule) – then *Pad Confirm button* and *Reset to defaults*. Every ride action is there: faster, stop, steer left / right; autodrive, wild mode, U-turn, back to the route, exit left / right; camera, video, fullscreen, restart, unicorn mode, the Strava recording (S); mute microphone, mute voices, the navigation map on / off and its zoom (desktop-only actions are not offered in the browser).
- **Each row shows the mapping for keyboard and gamepad:** "Delete / Q | D-pad left" – one or two keys (at most two, `MAX_KEYS`: a main key and a second one), then the gamepad button; "-" for none; "(!)" and the warning dot on a conflict.
- **Remapping by selecting the entry:** Enter (A) on a row starts the capture: the status line says *"Press a key or gamepad button for Junction: exit left... Esc / Start cancels"*; the next key (with Shift: the `Shift+X` binding when it is a choice) becomes the action's **only key**, or the next pad button its button. Esc or Start cancel (the status says *unchanged (cancelled)*). ← / → still step the (first) key through the list (no keyboard needed for a gamepad user).
- **Conflicts (decided: a swap, never a double binding):** a captured key or button that another action of this platform has **moves** to the row's action. The other action keeps its second key if it has one ("Q was taken: Junction: exit left keeps Delete"); left without any, it gets the row's old key or button – a **swap** ("W was taken: Wild mode now has A"); if the row had none, the other action is unbound and the status says so. Nothing is asked: the swap loses no binding and is undone by capturing again. A key on unicorn mode's flight keys for an action that also works in flight stays a marked conflict (as in M9). Double bindings can still be made with ← / → or `set keys.ID …` (scripts); they are marked as before and both actions fire. `bind ACTION KEY` (one key or button) follows the capture's rule; `bind ACTION KEY1,KEY2` and `bind ACTION none` set as given.
- **Not remappable (so the user can't lock themselves out):** the menu's keys and buttons keep their menu roles whatever the mapping says (Esc, Enter, Space, Backspace, the arrows and Tab, Q / E and Page Up / Down for tabs; the pad's Start, A / B and the D-pad) – the menu reads them directly, and a ride action bound to one of them works only while riding –; Esc, \` and F12 and the pad's Start can never be bound; the analog stick and triggers, the pad's god mode chords and unicorn mode's flight keys stay fixed (M9).
- **Saved in the local config file:** the bindings are the settings `keys.<id>` and `pad.<id>` in `[settings.keys]` and `[settings.pad]` of `ocw.toml` (3.2.4; written section-wise, comments and the other sections stay), **only those that differ from the default** – a capture back to the default and *Reset to defaults* remove the entries (and an emptied table). The browser keeps the same text in its settings store (`localStorage`). A value saved by an older version that equals the old default of the exits (`exit_left = "Q"`, `exit_right = "E"`: the old reset wrote every default) is read as not set, so the new default applies. Applied live: the ride's input, the camera key, the HUD's key line and the fan's hint follow at once.
- **Code:** `ocw_client::bindings` (pure: `Bindings::assign` – the capture's rule –, key lists `key_list` / `parse_keys` / `key_label`, `hud_lines`), the setting kind `Kind::Keys` and `Settings::unset` in `ocw_client::settings`, the Bevy side in `ocw_ui::bindings` (capture, `assign`, `reset`, the status line, `ocw_render::hud::RideKeys`), the rows in `ocw_client::menu::pages::binding_rows`; `ocw_client::input::junction_key` takes only the two exit actions.
- **Tests (11.4):** the default exit keys (Delete / Q, Page Down / E fire the exits; ←, →, Page Up do not; no action on Page Up, Page Down only the exit; the D-pad unchanged), the pure `junction_key` (never the arrows), no key changes the power by 10 W (the touch −10 W still does), the retired settings and the old exit defaults read from an old file, the key lists, the capture's rule (swap, second key kept, unbound, unchanged, back to the default leaves the file, the browser's actions, the flight-key conflict), the Bevy capture with the prompt, the swap and the status, a pad button, `bind` and `bind --reset` leaving no binding in the settings, the HUD lines following the mapping (and the HUD's defaults matching the default mapping), the menu pages (rows "keys | button", six rows each), the round trip through `ocw.toml` with only the changed bindings, other sections and comments kept, and reset removing the table; screenshots of the page, a capture prompt and a junction with the key hint (X11, Wayland, browser).

- **Q1 – Where the Input mapping entry sits: decided (2026-11-22, the user): (a) keep it so – a row of Settings → Controls, the Settings item reads *Controls, input mapping*** – Was asked: the user asked for "an Input mapping entry in the settings menu". The Settings page already has seven items (Account, Controls, Trainer, Audio, Display, Voice, Back) – the ten-foot maximum of 3.2.1 – so an eighth item cannot be added without moving another. Built: the page is the second row of *Settings → Controls* and the Settings item reads *Controls, input mapping*, so it is found from the Settings page in two steps. Options: (a) keep it so; (b) give *Input mapping* its own Settings item and move *Voice* into *Audio* (as an *Audio → Voice chat* sub page); (c) give it its own item and move *Account* to the Ride or Navi page. Proposal: a.

### 3.3 Audio

Two separate audio systems:

**Game audio** (own audio module, decided in M5): ambient sounds, bicycle sounds, wind, tyres, freewheel, gear shifting, UI and event cues; background music later.

**Implemented (M5):** `apps/desktop/src/audio/`, Bevy-free except its plugin (`mod.rs`). **Shared since Phase 10 B5 (v3.21):** the sounds, their parameters and the mixer are the crate `crates/ocw-audio` (pure, wasm) and what they hear of the ride is `ocw_client::audio::AudioFeed`; the desktop keeps the cpal engine, the recording and its plugin, the browser plays the same mixer through Web Audio (14 Phase 10 B5). Module names below are `ocw-audio`'s.

- *Options evaluated:* (a) `bevy_audio` (rodio) – plays only on the default device, no device list, no bus mixer: rejected (it is now disabled in the app). (b) `kira` 0.12 – a good game mixer (tracks, tweens, spatial), but it links **cpal 0.18** while Bevy 0.20 links cpal 0.17, so the app would carry two cpal copies (two ALSA bindings), and it is built around sample files we do not have; its device choice is no better than cpal's. (c) **cpal directly with an own small mixer** (chosen): cpal 0.17 is already in the lock file through Bevy (Apache-2.0, no new system library: `libasound` is linked anyway), it lists and opens devices by name on ALSA / WASAPI / CoreAudio, and since every sound is synthesised in code a sample-playing layer (rodio) is not needed – the mixer renders straight into the device buffer at the device's rate, channel count and sample format (f32, i16, u16, i32). If music files come later, rodio's decoders (or symphonia) can feed the music bus.
- *Engine:* an `OutputBackend` trait (list devices, default device, open by name, close, stream failed) with the cpal backend, a `NullBackend` (no sound) and a mock for tests. The engine runs on its own thread (cpal streams are not `Send` on every platform) and talks to the game through channels: commands (output, refresh) one way, a status (device list, default, playing device, fell back, message) the other; the mixer gets its input (ride parameters, cues, bus gains) through a bounded queue, read at the start of each device buffer (cues older than 0.4 s are dropped, so nothing stale plays after a device came back).
- *Device choice:* `audio.output` is a device name (cpal's device description, e.g. "USB Audio Device, USB Audio" on ALSA) or `default`; matching ignores case and surrounding spaces; several devices with one name (ALSA lists a card as `hw:`, `plughw:`, `sysdefault:`) are tried in order until one opens. A missing device falls back to the default device (shown as "NAME (gone)" on the Audio page). **Hot-plugging:** the device list is re-read every 3 s (cheap: cpal's ALSA listing does not open devices); a device that comes back is opened again, a stream that fails (unplugged: cpal's `DeviceNotAvailable`, `StreamInvalidated`, backend errors; underruns are ignored) is closed and the default opened. A failed open is retried after 15 s. Without any device (headless Xvfb / weston runs, CI) the app runs silently with one log line ("audio: no audio output: …"); `--no-audio` and frame capture (`--capture`, game time not real time) use the null backend (the mixer still runs for recordings, below).
- *Sound in videos (decided 2026-11-12, v2.30):* recorded videos carry the game mix (`audio::record`), muxed as AAC 192 kbit/s, 48 kHz stereo. **Live recording** (V, console `video`): while a device plays, the mixer copies every buffer it renders for the device to the recorder (a tap: exactly what the rider hears, in step with the real-time video); without a device (`--no-audio`, headless) the game thread renders the mixer itself, as many samples as game time has passed. The samples go to a hidden WAV beside the hidden H.264 file; after the stop ffmpeg muxes both into the final MP4 (`-c:v copy -c:a aac`), else the picture alone is kept. **Frame capture** (`--capture`): a capture source pulls exactly `frame × rate / fps` samples (integer accounting, no drift; 1920 per frame at 48 kHz and 25 fps) from the mixer per rendered frame – also during the warm-up, so the sound is settled, but only the captured frames are written to `DIR/audio.wav` – so picture and sound match whatever the render speed, with no audio device; the scripts mux it (`drive.sh`). Options considered: recording the system's output (PulseAudio monitor, WASAPI loopback: platform-specific, records other apps too, impossible headless), an offline backend behind the `OutputBackend` trait that opens like a device (the engine thread would drive it on its own clock, not the frame's), **pulling from the shared mixer in the game thread (chosen)** for capture and the tap for live. Voice (LiveKit) plays through its own path and is not in the recordings yet.
- *Buses:* master × music / effects / voice, and the other riders as a part of the effects (master × effects × others); each volume is 0–100 % on a squared curve (gain = (v/100)², 50 % ≈ -12 dB), the bus gain is master gain × bus gain, mute sets all to 0; gains are smoothed (60 ms) so changes do not click; a soft limiter (linear to 0.8, tanh knee) keeps the sum within ±1. Pure and unit-tested (`mix.rs`, `mixer.rs`).
