BC formats are supported by every desktop GPU we target (AMD, Apple Silicon, Windows drivers, Mesa lavapipe for the headless tests); Basis Universal (and a transcoder for the browser app, Phase 10) can replace them later without changing the manifest. Without BC support the app falls back to the flat colours.
- **Validator:** `ocw-assets materials validate [DIR]` and unit tests: every entry needs `license`, `source` (https), `author`, a SHA-256 per file and a roughness source; the licence rule of Phase 8A is shared by models and materials (`ocw_assets::licence`: CC0, public domain, own work, CC BY 4.0, DL-DE-BY/ZERO 2.0, OGD BY, Copernicus accepted; share-alike, non-commercial, no-derivatives and unknown rejected with the reason). Credits come from the manifest (`CREDITS.md`, console command `materials`).
- **Terrain (T2):** each land class is a fixed mix of the nine ground materials (e.g. farmland 55 % soil / 45 % meadow, forest 60 % needles / 40 % moss, residential meadow + gravel, water banks gravel + sand). Per tile the weights are stored at the **corners of the 5 m cells** (mean of the four cells around each corner, neighbour tiles included) in two RGBA8 textures of 201², sampled bilinearly: class borders blend over one cell, never show the 5 m grid, and neighbouring tiles agree on their shared edge. The fragment shader (`ground.wesl`; Rust twins `ground::blend_weights`, `rock_weight`) warps the lookup by ±2 m of noise (organic borders), sharpens the weights with a per-material noise ("height blend": a mix becomes patches, not a smear), turns slopes of 75–120 % into rock, less under forest (forests hold on steep slopes; the flat colour map used 60–100 %; with the limestone texture the steep alpine meadows of the 10 m grid read as bare cliffs) (**triplanar** on steep ground, no stretched texels on cliffs), samples every material at its real-world repeat size (`size_m`) and at a rotated macro scale ×7.3 that hides the tiling and takes over with distance, and fades between 90 and 350 m to the land-use colour map, whose class colours are now the materials' mean colours (so near and far agree; slopes turn to the rock colour as in the shader). Only the PBR input changes (albedo, roughness, normal); lighting, shadows and fog stay Bevy's, independent of the light setup (Phase 9).
- **Roads (T2):** the world builder keeps OSM `surface` (refined by `smoothness`, `tracktype` on tracks) as one byte per road strip in the new package section **`RSRF`** (only tiles where a strip differs from its category's default; older readers skip it, older packages get the category default: tracks and paths gravel, the rest asphalt). The road material (`road.wesl`) picks the layer per strip – asphalt, worn asphalt, gravel road, paving, dirt – with (across, along) texture coordinates in metres, fading to the material's mean colour far away; edge faces and the generated centre line (markings) stayed as they were until T5 (v2.60: markings, kerbs, sidewalks and the sloping road edge, Phase 8 T5). Physics still uses the three rolling-resistance classes (`RoadSurface::physics`).
- **Road damage (v4.75; asked by the user 2026-11-17: "add some cracks and potholes to the roads", and "look at the OSM flag for the quality of the tarmac"):** the carriageway shows its condition – drawn, and since v5.35 felt in the ride (*In the ride* below); the ridden height is not changed.
  - **Condition from OSM `smoothness` first** (`ocw_world::road_wear`, `ocw_world::road_condition`; package section `RCND`, 4.7): excellent → almost nothing (a crack every kilometre or so, no potholes); good → a few fine cracks; intermediate → cracks, sealed crack lines, repaired patches, the odd small pothole; bad → many cracks, alligator areas, potholes, broken edges and loose stones on the surface; very bad / horrible / very horrible / impassable → heavy damage, frequent potholes, much loose stone. The value maps to a **wear grade** 1 … 7 (excellent 1, good 2, intermediate 4, bad 5, very bad 6, worse 7). **Where `smoothness` is missing the grade is an estimate** (`estimate_grade`; **cleaner and plainer since v5.35, Phase 8 Q14 (b)**, so that mostly the tagged roads show damage): from `tracktype` on tracks (grade1 → 2, grade2 / grade3 → 3, grade4 / grade5 → 4), else from the road class (trunk, primary, secondary 1; tertiary, residential, cycleway, unclassified, service, path 2; track 3) and the surface (worn asphalt at least 3). Before v5.35: `tracktype` 4 / 5 / 5 / 6 / 7, trunk 1, primary and secondary 2, tertiary, residential, cycleway 3, unclassified, service, path 4, track 5, worn asphalt at least 5. **Measured share of the road length with `smoothness`** (`world-builder condition`, packages of 2026-11-17): Liechtenstein 229.9 of 993.6 km tagged (23.1 %; excellent 7.7 %, good 7.1 %, intermediate 4.8 %, bad 2.6 %, worse 0.9 %), Black Forest south 2,460 of 20,018 km (12.3 %; excellent 1.9 %, good 2.8 %, intermediate 3.4 %, bad 2.3 %, worse 1.9 %), Tenerife 189 of 9,129 km (2.1 %) – the rest (77 %, 88 %, 98 %) is estimated. The section adds 22 kB, 361 kB and 179 kB.
  - **Surface types:** asphalt (and chip seal, other paved values) takes every feature; **concrete** (`surface=concrete`, `concrete:lanes`, `concrete:plates`) a lighter grey with a sealed joint every 5 m and along the middle and half the random cracks; **paving stones, setts, cobblestones** no cracks, rarely sunken spots (potholes × 0.3) and loose stones; **unpaved** (compacted, gravel, dirt, grass) no cracks but two ruts (darker, compacted; loose material between them), loose stones on every unpaved road and potholes as hollows (× 1.5).
  - **Features** (`road.wesl`, per grade from `wear_density`, the placement's Rust twins in `road_wear`): transverse cracks (11 m cells) and longitudinal cracks beside the middle joint and in the edge zones (16 m cells; five slots since v5.74: the middle joint, the edge zones and the outer wheel tracks), block cracking (v5.74), a share of them **sealed** (dark glossy bitumen lines, more on the better roads); **alligator areas** in the outer wheel track (20 m cells; a Voronoi crack pattern of ~22 cm cells); **repaired patches** (darker rectangles, no cracks in them); **worn wheel tracks** (darker, polished, stronger on worn roads); **worn paint** (flecks, missing on patches of worn roads; cracks run through the paint, potholes take it away); **potholes and edge breaks** (7 m cells per side, 10 – 60 cm radius, outlines, depths and clusters of their own since v5.74 (*Variety* below), 35 % of them bite into the edge; within a zone from the edge that widens with the grade, on **main roads within 1.2 m of the edge whatever the grade**; on tracks in the wheel ruts) recessed by a parallax step (the far wall and the bottom seen through the rim, 1 – 8 cm deep since v5.74, before 3 – 5 cm), tilted normals, a darker coarse bottom and a lighter broken rim; **loose stones** (10 cm cells, 0.8 – 2.5 cm, from bad on; more at the edges and between the wheel tracks, swept out of the tracks). Everything is a hash of the cell in the strip frame (across, along in metres), so it is the same on every machine and in both apps, runs on over tile borders (the along coordinate does) and through a junction patch on the main road; the corner fans of town junctions (no strip frame) draw none.
  - **Variety (v5.74; asked by the user 2026-11-24: "the potholes look all the same. create more variety in the potholes and cracks"):** the shapes are part of the shared description (`road_wear`, the shader its twin), so the ride feels them (*In the ride*):
    - **Every road its own damage:** a seed of 64 values from the hash of the edge's length (`road_dress::road_seed`; every strip of an edge has it, so the damage runs on over tile borders) moves the road's damage cells along the hash sequence; it rides in bits 12 – 17 of the lines code (`MarkCode::seed`, the lines code < 2^18 stays exact in the interpolated vertex attribute). No package change. Patches are seeded too.
    - **Potholes:** radius 10 cm up to 25 + 35 × t cm (t the grade 0 … 1: intermediate ≤ 42 cm, horrible ≤ 60 cm, i.e. 0.2 – 1.2 m across); an outline of its own: an ellipse of aspect 1 – 1.45 at any angle, or (30 %) 1.5 – 2.4 long along the wheel's way (± 14°), its long half axis at most 0.8 m, its radius warped by value noise of 15 – 45 % at its own frequency and offset; **depth** 1 – 8 cm (0.01 + 0.07 × (0.3 t + 0.7 × random × (0.35 + 0.65 × size)): deeper on worse roads and for larger holes), drawn by the parallax step, a darker bottom and the wall's tilt; **edge breaks** (35 %) 1.4 – 2.6 long along the edge, biting in; **clusters** (5 + 30 × t %): one or two smaller holes (40 – 75 % of the radius, 7 – 30 cm) within 0.75 m, never nearer the middle, sometimes merging into one outline; **filled holes** (50 − 30 × t %, paved roads only): fresh tarmac, darker, finer and smoother, 12 % beyond the old outline with a thin cut seam, the paint gone – not felt; a **broken rim** (lighter chunks, some missing) and **loose grit** around open holes (up to 30 % more stones within 1.6 × the outline). Main roads keep their holes near the edge, tracks in the ruts (≤ 35 cm).
    - **Cracks:** transverse cracks across the whole width (35 %), round the middle (35 %) or in from one edge (30 %), 3 – 10 mm wide, of their own wander (6 – 26 cm at 1.2 – 2.4 rad/m), a share with a **branch** (10 + 60 × t %: 0.3 – 1.4 m at 26 – 60°, tapering); longitudinal cracks in five slots – the middle joint, both edge zones (15 – 75 cm in) and both outer wheel tracks – 2 – 15 m long, 3 – 9 mm wide, wandering 3 – 12 cm; in the edge zones a share are **edge cracks** (15 + 70 × t %) with short slanted cracks off to the edge every 0.7 m or so; **block cracking** (one chance per 30 m: 50 × (t − 0.25) %, from intermediate on) over one half or the whole width, 3 – 14 m long, blocks of 0.35 – 1.25 m (smaller on worse roads) in rows whose joints are offset like bricks; **alligator areas** 1 – 13 m long, 0.2 – 0.9 m half width, in the outer (60 %) or inner wheel track (25 %) or between them, cells of 12 – 30 cm; **sealed bands** 3 – 9 cm wide (more on better roads).
    - **Tests (11.4):** determinism; no two potholes of six roads' kilometre with the same shape parameters, two roads' holes in different places; the shares of elongated, clustered, filled holes and edge breaks, the sizes and depths, an irregular outline; the crack kinds per condition (excellent and good few and mostly sealed, no block cracking; intermediate block and edge cracks; bad and worse every kind, more branched, more blocks); every feature (with its rim, branch and noisy outline) in its cell; the noise the shader's; the feel: every open hole met along a line through it with its depth, nothing beside its drawn outline, nothing from a filled hole, block areas entered, two roads felt differently; the bump strengths by size, depth and width, the `dip` cue; the tables reaching the shader.
  - **Wet roads** (Phase 9 S4): water stands in the potholes first – from a well wet road on, up to the rim when the puddles fill (dark mirror, roughness 0.03); since v5.74 the deep holes first, a 1 cm hole holds only a film (fill × (0.3 + 12 × depth)); the cracks (roughness ≥ 0.55) and the alligator and block-cracked areas (≥ 0.42) stay rough on a wet road, so they do not vanish in the sky's mirror (before v5.74 a wet road hid its damage).
  - **Quality presets** (`ocw-render::quality`, `road_material::sync_damage`): High all features to 160 m, Medium 80 % of them to 110 m, Low 55 % to 60 m; fine features (cracks, the alligator pattern, loose stones) are skipped where the pixel is wider than they would show and no alligator crack pattern (the areas stay as tone). Same shader for Vulkan, WebGPU and WebGL 2 (uniform tables per grade, no textures).
  - **The ridden height is unchanged:** no geometry, `Track::surface_height` untouched; the road meshes' positions, normals and indices are the same for every grade (test).
  - **In the ride (v5.35, Phase 8 Q12 (c)):** riding over damage gives a **bump** and a bad surface **rolls harder**, server-authoritative (5.2, 6.1) from the same pure data the renderer draws, so what a rider sees is what they ride over. `ocw_world::road_feel::RoadFeelMap` holds the package's strips of grade 3 and worse (nothing on excellent and good roads; after Q14 that is the tagged intermediate and worse roads and the untagged tracks) with a 16 m segment index per tile; the road network carries it (`RoadNetwork::with_road_feel`, `Track::road_feel`; the home package, like the obstacles; the browser adds streamed tiles). The wheel's place (the path's centre line moved by the lateral offset) gives the strip and its frame (across from the drawn centre line, along the drawn arc length), and the features the wheel meets in a tick are the shader's (`road_wear`: potholes and edge breaks within 0.8 × their radius – since v5.74 inside 0.85 of their drawn outline –, open transverse cracks crossed – not sealed ones, not in a repaired patch –, the entry into an alligator area). `ocw_sim::road_feel` applies them in `ride::tick_in`, so the game server, the prediction and its extrapolation ride the same:
    - **Rolling resistance** per grade on paved roads: grades 1 – 2 + 0, 3 + 2 %, 4 (intermediate) + 6 %, 5 (bad) + 15 %, 6 (very bad) + 30 %, 7 (horrible and worse) + 50 % (Crr 0.004 → 0.006; gravel is 2.5 ×); on gravel and dirt half of it on top of their own factor. It goes through the shared additive hook `Environment::with_rolling_extra` (rolling = surface factor × weather factor + surface factor × the sum of the extras: the shares add up, none multiplies another; wet leaves, 4.6.2 Q6, add their share to the weather factor) and reaches the trainer in SIM.
    - **Bumps** (strength 0 … 1): a pothole 0.3 + 0.2 × size + 0.35 × depth (size 10 → 60 cm radius, depth 1 → 8 cm: 0.3 … 0.85; before v5.74 0.35 – 0.8 by the radius only), × 0.6 as a hollow on gravel or dirt or a sunken spot on paving, an edge break × 0.9, each hole of a cluster its own bump, a filled hole none; the wheel meets a hole where its way crosses the drawn outline (`Pothole::shape_q` < 0.85, sampled every 4 cm); an open crack 0.09 – 0.15 by its width (before 0.12); into an alligator area 0.18, into a block-cracked one 0.16 (v5.74). A bump costs 0.35 m/s × its strength, in full from 8 m/s (the largest, deepest hole about 1.1 km/h); only the speed changes, never the lateral place, so the prediction stays smooth (no sideways step, nothing to snap). A tick moving the wheel more than 2 m (a teleport) bumps nothing.
    - **On the client** (`ocw_client::road_bumps`, from the prediction, each feature once even when a reconciliation moves the prediction back over it): a **trainer kick** in SIM – the trainer's Crr × (1 + 4 × strength) for 0.6 s (the largest, deepest pothole × 4.4, a crack × 1.4 – 1.6; it reaches the trainer within its 0.5 s update interval; ERG holds its power); a small **camera shake** of 0.35 × the strength (a crash shakes with 1; off with `camera.shake off` / `display.camera_shake`, reduced motion, and in the kiosk's show mode); a **sound**, `pothole` (a hollow thump, front and rear wheel, a rattle), `dip` for a hole below strength 0.5 (a lighter, shorter knock in and out, no rattle; v5.74) or `crack` (a dull tick; also block cracking).
    - **Drawn in full:** the features a rider feels (potholes, transverse cracks, alligator areas) are drawn at their full amounts on every quality preset; the preset thins only the others (longitudinal cracks, patches, loose stones). The `road.damage` override stays visual only.
  - **Measured** (marge, AMD Radeon RX Vega, `scripts/measure-fps.sh`, 1280 × 720, no vsync, 40 s with 12 s warm-up, two interleaved runs each; before = the deployed main build on the packages without `RCND`, after = this build on the packages with it): no cost above the noise of the shared machine: 1280 × 720, ms per frame, round 1 / round 2 – Vaduz side street: before 5.44 / 5.02, this build with `road.damage off` 6.56 / 5.99, as tagged 6.62 / 3.60, all roads `horrible` 10.43 / 3.93; Freiburg street (intermediate): before 14.39 / 7.67, off 13.95 / 10.83, as tagged 12.10 / 9.65, horrible 9.26 / 10.75 (the same scene varied by a factor of two between runs while other builds ran on marge; the shader adds about 20 hashes per road pixel near the rider and skips what the pixel footprint would fade). **Measured again on a quiet machine (v4.87; 4.6.2 *Frame-rate cost* has the method and the table):** at 1920 × 1080 High road damage costs +0.03 ms in the Black Forest, +0.07 ms on a Vaduz street, +0.03 ms at Masca (Vaduz and Masca with the estimated grades: those packages had no `RCND` yet) and **+0.18 ms (+0.13 … +0.27 over three rounds) with every road `horrible`** at Puerto de la Cruz – Teide km 4 (210.6 → 202.7 fps); at Medium the same road +0.18 ms, at 1280 × 720 at most +0.07 ms. Well under the ~1 ms that would call for cutting features. **With the varied shapes (v5.74)**, leela, 1920 × 1080 High, before → after, damage on minus off: Black Forest km 7 +0.33 → +0.20 ms (noisy), Masca +0.06 → +0.04 ms, a Vaduz street +0.05 → +0.14 ms, every road `horrible` +0.17 → +0.26 ms.
  - **Tests:** the grade from each smoothness value (any class), the estimate from class and `tracktype`, smoothness over `tracktype`; densities grow with the grade and shrink with the preset's share; deterministic placement and the counts per smoothness (none on excellent, a few on good, more on each worse value), per estimated class, cracks and loose stones; potholes off the middle of main roads for every smoothness, minor roads' holes on their side, tracks' in the ruts; every feature inside its cell (the shader looks only there); the `RCND` round trip, an older reader skipping it, unknown codes; the world builder's condition by OSM way and on changed packages (geometric match); the mark code's wear, concrete and main-road bits; the uniform tables and the preset reaching the materials; the road geometry the same for every grade.
  - **Questions:** Phase 8 Q12 (the ride feel, built v5.35), Q13 (the densities, kept), Q14 (the estimate for untagged roads, built v5.35) – decided.
- **Bridges (4.8.6):** the deck surface is the road strip on it, so it already gets the asphalt / paving / gravel material of its OSM `surface`; the structure (parapets, piers, arches) keeps the flat colours of `bridges::bridge_colour` until its meshes get texture coordinates (T4/T5). Road strips, textured or flat, are flat overlays without shadows of their own (4.5).
- **Regional material sets (v2.46):** the manifest's `[[region]]` entries apply to packages whose time zone (section `TZID`) they list. A set fills the nine ground layer slots with other library materials (`layers`, e.g. `rock = "lava_rock"`) and gives land classes another slot mix (`classes`, e.g. `default = { meadow = 0.45, gravel = 0.55 }`); the client builds one pair of texture arrays per set and picks it per package, the far palette follows the set's means and mix. The first set, `volcanic` for `Atlantic/Canary` (Tenerife: the island rendered green before), draws rock as lava (Poly Haven Dark Rock), scree and gravel as volcanic ash / cinder (ambientCG Gravel 024), sand and beaches (`natural=beach` and `surface=sand` are the class bare) as black sand (Poly Haven Coast Sand 05) and forest floor as Canary pine needles (ambientCG Ground 077); ground without land use is half ash. Data-driven, so T3 can add regions, slot materials and mixes (and measure the mixes from imagery) without code.
- **Regional tint hook (T3):** `TerrainLook::material_tint` per ground material (near) and a per-class tint in `ground::class_palette` (far), neutral (1.0) without a measured look.
- **Region calibration (T3, v2.47):** packages calibrated with `world-builder calibrate` carry their measured look (4.7 "Look sections"). The client (`ocw-render::region_look`) tints each ground layer towards the measured median colour of the land class it stands for (meadow layer → meadow, farmland → farmland, forest floor → forest, rock / scree → rock / scree, sand → bare, wetland → wetland; snow and gravel stay neutral): 80 % of the way in chroma and 50 % in brightness (the aerial photo is taken in full sun from above), the forest floor only 35 % of that (the orthophoto shows the canopy, not the floor), within a factor 0.4 … 2.5. The season multiplies in: the class's median colour in the Sentinel-2 composites blended for the world date over its summer colour, mostly as brightness (25 % of the chroma, 50 % of the brightness change, within 0.6 … 1.6: a factor cannot turn green grass into snow – the first winter renders went pink), so the real seasonal colour comes from the far map. The far colour map's class colours get the tint that matches the near layers (their mix of tinted layer means), then the tile's seasonal satellite map is laid over them at 70 %; the date comes from the world clock (`ocw-sky`, Phase 9), in 4-day buckets, and the loaded tiles are rebuilt when the bucket changes (time machine). Buildings take their measured roof colour (an OSM `roof:colour` a quarter of the way to the default, so a named "red" reads as tiles).
- **Forests:** the forest floor is 60 % needle litter and 40 % moss, its albedo darkened under the canopy (`CANOPY_SHADE` 0.55 at full forest floor; the low-poly trees' own shadows leave the ground too bright), and forests keep 70 % of their ground on slopes that would otherwise turn to rock.
- **Orthophoto corridor (T7, v3.10):** where a package has the section `ORTC` (4.7), the ground near the roads takes its colour from the real place's orthophoto: fields, gardens, driveways, parking lots, lava flows. The photo never replaces the tiling materials; it gives the colour, the materials give the detail – the photo times the materials' brightness relative to the land-use colour they stand for (`ortho::apply`; a per-channel ratio gave purple lawns where a material's hue differs from its class colour). Up close the colour comes from the photo blurred to about 4 m (no magnified 0.5 m pixels beside the rider), between 15 and 120 m the sharp photo takes over, and where the materials have faded to the colour map (beyond 350 m) the ground is the photo itself; the corridor weight (alpha) and a view-distance fade (650 → 950 m) scale it all. The client builds one texture per tile for the tiles around the rider's (3 × 3, the fade ends before the next ring): the JPEG chunks decoded at 2,000² (0.5 m) or 1,000² (1 m), the weight in alpha, a mip chain averaged in linear light, BC3 – 5.3 MB per 0.5 m tile instead of 21 MB uncompressed – in the background; without the material library (no BC support) there is no corridor. Setting `display.orthophoto` on / off (default on; console `ortho`), off drops the textures.
- **Forest type and density (T3, v3.20):** where a package has the section `FRST` (4.7), the trees follow the Copernicus HRL: OSM's land use stays the outline of woods, fields and towns, the measured tree cover density sets the chance of each 8 m candidate inside it (forests: proportional to the cover, full at 80 %, at least 6 % of the class's chance in clearings; outside forests the class's chance or 0.6 × the cover where trees were measured – hedges, tree rows, gardens, unmapped copses; never trees on water, rock, scree, glacier, bare ground or vineyards), and each tree's leaf type is broadleaved with the cell's measured broadleaf share (decided by the tree's position, deterministic); the seasons (9I-S8) then colour and strip the broadleaves, conifers stay green, a share of the conifers are larches by the region's mix. The far terrain's canopy takes the same cover and leaf mix per sample. Without the section, or where no trees were measured, the regional fallback mix (`season::LeafMix`) decides.
- **Performance:** see Phase 8 T2 status (14) for the measured frame rates.

#### 4.6.1 Vegetation: species, crops and plantations (research 2026-11-15, v3.49)

The big plants and crops that define each landscape, the open data that places them and the rules where the data is thin. The species rules are **proposals** taken from the cited ecology; the code is `ocw_world::flora` (species, regional tables, tree line), `ocw_world::vegetation` / `plantings` (section `VEGE`, rows), `ocw-worldgen::vegetation` (the builder) and `ocw-render::flora` / `vegetation` (models, seasons, chunks; 14 Phase 8 T8).

**Table 1 – Liechtenstein / Alpine Rhine.** Forest 6,865 ha, 43 % of the country; LWI 2010: spruce 54 %, beech 11 % of the volume, conifers 77 % ([llv.li forest](https://www.llv.li/en/individuals/recreational-environmental-and-animal-management/forest-nature-landscape-climate/forest-and-wood); Landeswaldinventar 2010). Belts after the Amt für Umwelt's *Waldgesellschaften* ([B10](https://www.llv.li/serviceportal2/amtsstellen/amt-fuer-umwelt/publikationen/naturkindliche-forschung/b10-waldgesellschaften-2.pdf)):

| Belt | Altitude | Species (shares of the rule) | Shapes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Valley floor, Rhine | 430 – 600 m | ash and sycamore on wet soils, alder and willow on the banks (rule: beside water and in wetlands 50 % alder, 40 % willow); Scots pine and birch on dry ridges | ash open crown, willow silvery, alders narrow |
| Submontane | to 650 m | beech dominant with oaks, cherry, small-leaved lime; conifers spruce 50 %, Scots pine 35 %, fir 15 % | beech 20 – 25 m, dome |
| Montane | 650 – 1,150 m | beech, sycamore, ash; fir more important (conifers: spruce 55 %, fir 38 %, pine 7 %) | fir tiers flat, old firs flat-topped |
| Subalpine | 1,150 – 1,900 m | spruce, fir, sycamore (conifers: spruce 75 → 90 %, fir 25 → 0 %; larches by the seasons' mix, 5 – 20 %) | spruce narrow, drooping tiers, to 50 m |
| Tree line | 1,600 – 2,000 m (natural limit above 1,900 m) | mountain pine (krummholz, seed stands at Triesenberg/Malbun 1,600 – 2,000 m), green alder in a belt about 100 m wide above the closed forest on moist slopes (Malbun) ([LI seed list](https://www.llv.li/serviceportal2/amtsstellen/amt-fuer-umwelt/wald-natur-landschaft/landesforstbetrieb/preisliste_2024.pdf), [Ber. Bot.-Zool. Ges. LI 27](https://www.zobodat.at/pdf/Ber-Bot-Zool-Ges-Liechtenstein_27_0249-0284.pdf)) | trees shrink over the last 350 m below 1,950 m to 40 % above it (`flora::stature`) |

Crops (Amt für Statistik, Landwirtschaft 2023): 3,590 ha farmed, 2,260 ha (63 %) permanent grassland, 237 ha cereals; vineyards about 25 – 30 ha in Balzers, Eschen, Gamprin, Schaan, Schellenberg, Triesen and Vaduz (Herawingert about 4 ha). No open maize or orchard statistics: the crop mix for fields without a tag is a **proposal** – maize 38 %, cereals 30 %, temporary grass 18 %, vegetables 6 %, potatoes and rapeseed 4 % each; above 900 m 70 % grass. Lone trees in the valley's meadows: fruit trees 38 % (Streuobst), sycamore 18 %, ash 16 %, oak, lime, beech; above 900 m sycamore, ash, beech.

**Table 2 – Black Forest.** BWI 3 (2012), Schwarzwald growth area, share of the stocked area ([FVA](https://www.fva-bw.de/fileadmin/user_upload/Daten_und_Tools/Monitoring/BWI/Ergebnisse_BWI3/Wuchsgebiet_Schwarzwald.pdf), CC BY 4.0): spruce 42.8 %, fir 18.5 %, beech 15.3 %, Douglas fir 5.1 %, Scots pine 5.0 %, oak 3.1 %, larch 1.0 %, other broadleaves 9 %; spruce falling, beech rising since 1987. Baden-Württemberg BWI 4 (2022): spruce 31 %, conifers 51.5 %, beech 22.8 %, fir 9.0 %.

| Belt | Altitude | Rule (conifers / broadleaves) |
|---|---|---|
| Rhine plain, foothills | 200 – 500 m | spruce 40 %, fir 24 %, Douglas fir 16 %, Scots pine 20 % / beech 35 %, oak 30 %, ash, sycamore and sweet chestnut 10 % each, birch 5 % |
| Low and middle mountains | 500 – 900 m | spruce 55 %, fir 30 %, Douglas fir 9 %, pine 6 % / beech 70 %, sycamore 20 % |
| High montane | 900 – 1,250 m | spruce 60 %, fir 35 %, pine 5 % / beech 60 %, sycamore 35 %, birch (rowan) 5 % |
| Feldberg massif | above 1,250 m | spruce 92 %, mountain pine 8 % (moors); the summit is open pasture from historic grazing, not a natural tree line ([waldwissen.net](https://www.waldwissen.net/de/wald-und-mensch/forstgeschichte/suedschwarzwald-waldwandel-seit-1790)) – the rule shrinks the trees from 1,080 m to wind-shaped spruces above 1,430 m |

Crops: Baden's vineyards 15,142 ha in 2025 (Kaiserstuhl 4,079, Markgräflerland 3,250, Ortenau 2,530, Breisgau 1,513, Tuniberg 1,035 ha; [Statistisches Landesamt BW](https://www.statistik-bw.de/fileadmin/user_upload/Service/Veroeff/Statistisches_Monatsheft/PDF/Beitrag_26_08_03.pdf)), up to about 400 m (Durbach granite). In the Rhine plain maize is the main crop – EUCROPMAP 2022 samples: Bühl 32.6 % maize, 16.4 % wheat, 23.7 % grass of all pixels. The fields of the packages take their crops from EUCROPMAP (below); the fallback mix is maize 40 %, cereals 32 %, grass 10 %, vegetables 5 %, rapeseed 4 %, sunflower and fallow 3 % each, potato 2 %, beet 1 %.

**Table 3 – Tenerife** (north = windward, the trade-wind cloud belt; south = leeward; the sources differ by up to 200 m; [floracanaria.com](https://floracanaria.com/canary_islands_flora/ecosystems.html), [Jardín de Flora Canaria (ULL)](https://www.ull.es/centros/jardin-flora-canaria/cardonal-tabaibal/), del Arco et al. 2006):

| Belt | North | South | Species | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Succulent scrub (cardonal-tabaibal) | 0 – 300 m | 0 – 500 (700) m | cardón *Euphorbia canariensis*, tabaiba *E. balsamifera* (summer-deciduous), *Kleinia*, prickly pear, agave | scrub below 300 m (north) / 650 m (south): tabaiba 48 %, cardón 24 %, prickly pear 14 %, agave 8 %, date palm 6 % |
| Thermophilous woodland | coast – 350 (500) m | 500 – 900 m | dragon tree, Canary date palm (10 – 21 m), juniper, wild olive | lone trees and towns in the lowlands: date palm 34 %, other palms 14 %, laurel-like town trees 30 %, dragon tree 5 % |
| Laurel forest | 400 – 1,200 m (Anaga, Teno, Orotava) | absent | *Laurus*, *Persea indica*, *Ocotea*, *Apollonias*, *Ilex* | measured broadleaf forest in the north 450 – 950 m: laurel 75 %, faya-heath 22 %, eucalyptus 3 % |
| Fayal-brezal | 500 – 1,000 m, up to 1,700 m | patches | *Morella faya*, *Erica arborea* (after fire and logging) | 950 – 1,450 m: faya-heath 62 %, laurel 30 %; above: faya 80 %, pine 20 % |
| Canary pine | from 1,200 m | from 700 – 800 m | *Pinus canariensis* (to 50 m, long drooping needles), *Cistus* | every measured conifer; unmeasured forest outside the north's cloud belt |
| Summit scrub, Las Cañadas | above 1,800 – 2,000 m | | Teide broom *Spartocytisus supranubius* (to 2 m, dome, white-pink flowers late May – early June), codeso | scrub above 1,800 m: broom, shrinking towards 3,200 m |
| Summit cone | above 3,000 m | | Teide violet | nothing drawn above 3,050 m (thinning from 2,750 m, `flora::alive`) |

The windward side is the side north-west of the line through the Teide at a bearing of 60° (the Anaga – Teno ridge; `flora::windward`). Crops: the official Mapa de Cultivos 2021 (177,543 parcels): bananas 3,935 ha (0 – 300 m), vines 2,836 ha (+ 370 ha mixed; DO Valle de la Orotava 250 – 700 m, 83.6 % of it in the braided *cordón trenzado* on props 60 – 80 cm high; Tacoronte-Acentejo 50 – 1,000 m; Abona up to 1,700 m), potatoes 1,745 ha, avocado 802 ha, citrus 289 ha, cereals 532 ha, maize (*millo*) 258 ha, 2,808 ha under greenhouses or netting, 19,216 ha of 38,728 ha unused (abandoned terraces); chestnut groves about 1,374 ha in the Orotava valley and Acentejo. Rules without data: OSM orchards without a tag are bananas below 350 m, avocado / citrus to 900 m, fruit trees above; greenhouses below 400 m banana houses; vines on low trellises (1.1 m) in wider rows.

**Table 4 – Plantations and fields (rows, `plantings::row_spec`):** vineyards on wire trellises 2.0 m × 1.1 m (Tenerife 2.4 × 1.4 m, low), canopy wall 1.8 m (Tenerife 1.1 m), posts every 5 m; orchards of half-standard trees 7 × 5.5 m (Tenerife 6 × 5 m); bananas 2.5 × 2.2 m (about 1,800 plants per hectare); avocado / citrus 6 × 5 m; berry hedges 2.8 × 1.0 m. Rows run along a field's main axis (its long sides), vineyards steeper than 12 % down the fall line (the steep vineyards of Vaduz and the Ortenau); measured plantations outside OSM's fields along the contour (terraces). Large fields without a crop are cut into parcels across their main axis (55 × 220 m; Tenerife 30 × 70 m), one crop each. Maize, cereals, rapeseed, sunflowers, potatoes and beet stand as slabs over their cells, by the crop calendar (maize 2.5 m from June to the October harvest, cereals 0.9 m until the July harvest, rapeseed yellow in flower in late April and May).

**Table 5 – Phenology per species (`flora::timing`, factors on the degree-day thresholds of 14 9C, proposals):** birch spring × 0.8, willow × 0.75, sycamore × 0.95, lime × 0.95, alder × 0.9, fruit trees × 0.92 (blossom from 70 to 190 growing degree days: Vaduz about 10 – 25 April; the DWD's mean apple blossom 26 April), ash × 1.35 and oak × 1.25 (late), chestnut × 1.15, vines × 1.6 (late April); autumn: ash × 0.85 (early, dull yellow-green), lime × 0.9, birch × 0.95, alder and willow × 1.15 (late, alders green), oak × 1.15 (brown). Colours: beech copper to orange-brown, sycamore yellow to orange, larch gold then bare, birch, lime and willow yellow, fruit trees orange or red, vines yellow (red varieties – Vaduz's Blauburgunder – red) in October. Beech canopy leaf-out mean day 119 (one plot 2009 – 2025, [waldwissen.net](https://www.waldwissen.net/de/lebensraum-wald/klima-und-umwelt/phaenologische-untersuchungen-eines-rotbuchen-versuchsflaechenbestandes)). Tenerife: the broom flowers from day 128 to 178, the tabaibas drop their leaves in the summer drought.

**Table 6 – Andorra / eastern Pyrenees** (v6.51, 4.7 *Fifth world: Andorra*). Forest 18,227 ha, about 39 % of the country; the first national forest inventory (INF1, CTFC and Andorra Recerca + Innovació, measured in summer 2022, 194 plots, 9,137 trees; [carbon report, Zenodo 12519202](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.12519202)): mountain pine *Pinus uncinata* 51.7 % of the trees, Scots pine 32.3 %, silver fir 4.9 %, birch 3.0 %, holm oak 2.9 %, rowan 1.3 %, downy oak 1.3 %, ash, sallow, sessile oak, hazel and others under 1 % each – no spruce, no larch, no beech worth counting. Strata: mountain-pine forests 35.9 % (mesophile 23.1, xerophile and planted 12.8), Scots-pine forests 32.7 % (xerophile and planted 18.1, mesophile 14.6), protection forests 17.9 %, fir and fir-pine 3.5 %, mixed broadleaf, ash, birch and aspen woods 3.4 %, holm-oak woods (*carrascars*) 1.8 %, downy-oak woods 1.4 %, hazel 0.9 %, the rest under 1 %.

| Belt | Altitude | Rule (conifers / broadleaves) | Shapes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Valley floors, the south (Sant Julià, Andorra la Vella) | 840 – 1,400 m | Scots pine 88 %, fir 12 % / downy and sessile oak 38 %, holm oak 16 % (drawn with the evergreen laurel model), ash 14 %, birch 14 %, lime, willow and chestnut 6 % each; river banks alder 40 %, willow 40 %, ash 20 % | pines with tall bare trunks and flat umbrella crowns on the sunny slopes |
| Montane | 1,400 – 1,700 m | Scots pine 62 %, mountain pine 26 %, fir 12 % (north slopes, Ordino) / birch 50 %, sycamore 18 %, ash 12 %, willow 12 %, oak 8 % | |
| Subalpine | 1,700 – 2,000 m | mountain pine 62 %, Scots pine 28 %, fir 10 % / birch 65 %, sycamore 20 %, willow 15 % | the upright mountain pine (to 20 m, dark, conical) is drawn with the Scots pine model below 2,050 m – the library's mountain pine is the low *Pinus mugo* |
| Tree line | 2,000 – 2,400 m (closed forest to about 2,300 m) | mountain pine 95 – 100 % (drawn low, krummholz, from 2,050 m), lone trees to 2,500 m; scrub there: mountain pine, rhododendron and juniper / birch, willow, green alder | trees shrink over the last 350 m below 2,350 m (`flora::stature`) |
| Alpine | above 2,400 m | pasture, scree and granite; no trees | |

The leaf-type share where the package has no measured forest (`leaves::region_broadleaf`): 30 % below 1,300 m, 6 % above. Lone trees in the hay meadows: ash 40 % (pollarded along the field walls), fruit trees 25 %, birch, oak and willow below 1,500 m; birch, sycamore and willow above; town trees lime, sycamore, ash, birch and fruit trees; town and meadow conifers Scots pine 75 %, fir 25 %. Crops (no Andorran crop statistics found; proposal): fields without a crop tag are hay meadows 72 %, potatoes 10 %, vegetables 8 %, cereals 6 %, fallow 4 % (the tobacco plots of Sant Julià and La Massana stand as vegetables); no EUCROPMAP (Andorra is outside the EU). Phenology as table 5.

Open: the Black Forest's species shares from BWI 4 by growth area, Liechtenstein's 2022 inventory, maize and orchard statistics; the banana altitude limit per coast (intersect the crop map with the DEM); sources for the leaf-out order of ash, oak, birch (DWD phenology open data); the upper vineyard limits in the Markgräflerland and at Sasbachwalden.

- **Fixed (v5.44): the trees turned bald all of a sudden when coming closer** (the user's report of 2026-11-23, late November, Liechtenstein). **Cause:** the two models of a broadleaf (`ocw-render::flora`, near up to 230 – 310 m from a chunk's centre, far beyond, cross-faded) drew a bare or thinning crown differently since they were made (v3.42, 2026-11-15) – the far model a grey-brown crown of twigs (a solid blob), the near model only seven branches, so a forest that looked grey-brown from afar lost its crowns at the switch; with leaves between 12 and 50 % (late October) the far model was the same grey haze while the near one had a full, coloured crown. The season itself was the same for both (one `PlantLook` per tree, the far terrain's canopy by the same phenology) – it showed now because the world's date reached the bare weeks; no commit since v0.2.4 changed it. **Fix:** one crown per tree and day for both models (`flora::crown_form`): bare deciduous trees have a see-through crown of fine twigs around their branches (85 % of the crown's width, 45 % of its pixels drawn and 45 % of its shadow cast, an ordered dither by the vertex alpha in `see_through.wesl` and the tree material's shadow pass `see_through_prepass.wesl`), thinning crowns their reduced size and colour with an opacity from 51 % up to full at half the leaves, in leaf as before; only the mesh detail differs between near and far. Test (11.4): `near_and_far_models_have_the_same_leaves_every_season` (eleven broadleaf species, 10 May, 15 July, 28 October, 23 November, at 455 m and 1,300 m in Liechtenstein and 700 m in the northern Black Forest: the same crown form, opacity, height and colour near and far). Pictures: `scripts/tree-lod-shots.sh` (a wood in the Rhine valley approached from 600 m to 60 m in May, July, late October and late November, the Black Forest; before / after).

#### 4.6.2 Near-field ground detail (planned and built 2026-11-17, v4.72)

Asked by the user (2026-11-17: "graphic enhancement: add some dirt, dust, stones, rocks, parts of plants/vegetation"): the verges, shoulders and the ground next to the road looked clean and empty from the saddle. The renderer now scatters **small ground detail** there (`ocw-render::ground_detail`).

- **What:** 14 kinds – road-edge gravel and grit (within 0.25 m of the road's edge also on its surface), pebbles, a few larger rocks (0.2 – 0.9 m, lumpy, sunk a third into the ground), dirt and dust patches, moss, needle-litter and (since v5.08) leaf-litter patches (soft-edged, blended decals in their own mesh), fallen leaves, twigs, cones, grass tufts, dry stalks, ferns and small shrubs. Own low-poly models made in code (4 – 25 vertices a bit, ferns about 100, shrubs about 40; no third-party assets).
- **Where:** in a band from the road edge to **14 m** beyond it (beyond the sidewalk where there is one; 7 m until v4.98), along every road strip of a tile in 1 m steps of the road's own arc length (`dress.start_m`, so the steps run on across the tiles). Each kind has its own place across the band (gravel at the edge, pebbles mostly within 2 m, rocks and shrubs further out). **Spread wider, the same amount (Q4, v5.08):** the number of bits per metre of road is the one of the 7 m band; each kind lies evenly over its first part (to 7 m for rocks, moss, needles, tufts, ferns and shrubs; 5 – 5.5 m for dirt, stalks, twigs, cones and leaves; 3.5 m for pebbles) and thins out linearly over a tail as long again (to 14 m; 10 – 11 m; 6 m) – a trapezoid, so about a third of a kind's bits lie beyond its old end and the band's outer edge fades instead of stopping (`ground_detail::spread`). 14 m was chosen as twice the old band: wide enough that the verge no longer ends in a visible line from the saddle, still inside the 25 m chunks along the road (a chunk lies near a road when its centre is within the band + 2 m + half its diagonal) and well inside the ground the camera sees at 80 m. **On the road itself (Q4, Q5, v5.08), very few:** per metre of each side's half of the carriageway 0.035 grit and 0.012 small stones (× 0.6 on an excellent road up to × 2.1 on the worst, from the road damage's wear grade, `road_wear::wear_grade`; × 2 on gravel and dirt roads, × 0.5 on paving and in towns), in the woods 0.012 twigs (elsewhere 0.003), and leaves in autumn and winter (`road_mix`); on a 6 m tertiary road through a meadow in summer some 0.07 bits per metre of road – one every 15 m –, on a horrible road about twice that. They lie mostly near the edge and never where the wheels run: off the wheel tracks (the road damage's tracks, 0.8 m either side of each lane's middle, `road_wear::wheel_tracks`, where its loose stones are swept out too) and at least 0.45 m from a lane's middle (`road_spot_free`) – on a two-lane road in practice 0.25 – 0.4 m in from the edge (inside the edge gravel's 0.25 m) and beside the centre line, between the lanes' inner tracks; none in junctions, on bridge decks or under lying snow; only the smaller half of each kind's sizes (grit 1 – 2 cm, stones up to 5 cm).
- **On the drawn ground:** every bit takes its height from `TileGround` (the terrain mesh after the junctions lowered it) or from the road's shoulder where that lies higher, sinks into it on slopes and terrace edges, and is left out on road surfaces (other strips too), on bridge decks, in building footprints (with the camera's 0.5 m clearance), on water, wetland and glacier, and where the ground lies far off the road (more than 1.2 m + 0.6 × the distance from the edge: cuts, walls, embankments, tunnels).
- **Region-aware** (by `FloraRegion`, the land class at the place, the forest type of section `FRST` or the region's broadleaf share, the altitude): **Tenerife** dark basalt and red scoria grit, more lava rocks (pale pumice above 1,800 m), ochre dust and volcanic ash patches, few and dry tufts, more dry stalks and grey-green shrubs, no ferns or moss, needle litter and cones only under the Canary pine; **Black Forest** granite and gneiss, dark wet earth, in the woods needle litter, cones, moss, ferns and twigs, leaves under the beeches; **Liechtenstein** limestone gravel (more of it), dense meadow tufts, alpine rocks and dwarf shrubs above 1,200 m. Towns get a third of the plants and few rocks, farmland more dirt, rock / scree / bare land more stones, gravel and dirt roads more gravel.
- **Season** (Phase 9, `ocw_sky::season`): the grass colour (green, dormant, summer-dry) of the tufts; dry stalks grow with the summer drought and the dormant season; leaves lie from the leaf fall through the winter (coloured while fresh, brown later) and fade under the spring green – **a bit stronger since v5.08 (Q5):** a quarter more single leaves (7.5 instead of 6 per metre in a pure broadleaf wood, 0.65 instead of 0.5 in open land) and larger ones (8 – 15 cm instead of 6 – 12 cm), **leaf-litter patches** under the broadleaves (0.45 – 1.2 m, blended, the leaves' colours with 30 % soil between them; 0.5 per metre × the broadleaf share – at least 0.2 in any wood, since woods measured as mostly conifers still have beeches and maples by the roads – × the leaf fall, 0.02 in open land; none in summer) and **leaves on the road** (0.8 per metre of each half × the same broadleaf share × the leaf fall in woods, 0.06 in open land) – from the leaf fall through the winter; since v5.34 exactly the amount the physics of wet leaves rides over (Q6: the shared `ocw_world::leaves` map in 20 m cells and its amount; sidewalks no longer halve them); the climatological snow cover thins every small kind (rocks and shrubs stay, whitened by the trees' snow shading); lying snow of the weather (cover ≥ 0.5) hides all but rocks and shrubs. The tiles are built again when the season bucket changes, as before.
- **Deterministic:** no data in the package; a hash of each step's world position (quarter metres) draws the bits, so every client and every screenshot has the same ones (tested: the same tile twice, the chunks in any order against the whole tile, a road unchanged by a road elsewhere).
- **Cheap:** merged per 25 m chunk (40 × 40 a tile, only the chunks near roads get an entity) into one mesh in the trees' material (sway, snow) plus one blended mesh for the patches, no shadows of their own. Bevy's automatic instancing of the few models was not used: thousands of entities a tile cost more on the CPU than one merged mesh a chunk, which also keeps WebGL 2 simple. A chunk's meshes are built on the task pool only when a camera comes within the draw distance + 30 m (nearest first, at most 6 at a time) and dropped beyond the draw distance + 70 m (the chunks are looked at every 4th frame while nothing is being built); a tile keeps only its terrain vertices, footprints and chunk list (about 0.13 MB). Drawn up to the preset's distance from the chunk's centre and faded out (dithered) over its last quarter.
- **Quality presets** (`QualityPreset::ground_detail`, `ground_detail_m`): **High** all of it up to 80 m, **Medium** 60 % up to 55 m, **Low** (WebGL 2, phones; the browser's usual levels) 25 % up to 35 m; the share keeps the same deterministic draw. **VR** (Phase 11, Q2 decided): 50 % up to 50 m (`VR_LEVEL`, kept as it was in the code). **The setting `display.ground_detail` (Q1, v5.08):** `auto` (the default: the preset's share and distance), `off`, `low` (25 % up to 35 m, the Low preset's, whatever the preset) and `full` (all of it up to 80 m, the High preset's) – in both apps, on *Display → Graphics → World detail* (the Graphics page is full with six rows, so the sky moved there with it) and with the console `ground_detail auto|off|low|full` (User; `on` is still taken as `auto`), which reports the mode, share, distance, chunks built and bits.
- **Wet (Q3, v5.08):** while the road is wet (the weather's road wetness, Phase 9 S4) the bits darken and shine like the road: their two materials (the solid bits' and the blended patches') get a colour factor 1 − 0.38 × wetness (0.62 when soaked: between the wet road's asphalt 0.55 and unpaved 0.72) and a roughness 1 − 0.4 × wetness (0.6 when soaked; 0.38 made the thin grass blades mirror the bright overcast sky and look white), changed only when the quantized wetness changes (`wet_look`, `wet_ground_detail`) – leaves on a wet road shine with the road. No shadows of their own (Q3: no extra shadows).
- **Frame-rate cost, measured on a quiet machine (v4.87; replaces the noisy pairs of v4.72)** (marge, AMD Radeon RX Vega (RADV, Vulkan), release build of origin/main of 2026-11-18, `scripts/feature-fps-cost.sh` → `scripts/measure-fps.sh`: headless weston on the GPU, no vsync, riding at 250 W, no bots, 20 June 11:00 clear, the dynamic render distance off; all off, each feature alone and all on in 3 alternating rounds (off → all, then all → off), 25 s per run after a 15 s warm-up; marge checked quiet before every run (no build, under one core busy, a 1-minute load below 1.5 at the start of each scene) and a block that a release build disturbed measured again; marge's packages of 2026-11-15; the Tenerife and Liechtenstein ones have no `RCND`, so there `road.damage auto` draws the estimated grades). Cost per feature in ms of mean frame time against all off, mean of the three rounds (lowest … highest round); the last column is the change of the 95th-percentile frame time:

  | scene (1920 × 1080, High) | all off: fps; mean / p50 / p95 ms | ground detail | road damage | map | all on | all on, p95 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Black Forest, Baden-Baden – Mummelsee km 7 | 168.0; 5.95 / 3.70 / 13.26 | +0.04 (−0.07 … +0.11) | +0.03 (−0.12 … +0.22) | +0.02 (−0.16 … +0.14) | +0.22 (+0.12 … +0.35) | +0.69 |
  | Liechtenstein, Vaduz street (free ride) | 196.7; 5.08 / 3.44 / 10.70 | ±0.00 (−0.04 … +0.05) | +0.07 (+0.06 … +0.09) | +0.02 (−0.02 … +0.08) | +0.13 (+0.06 … +0.23) | +0.29 |
  | Tenerife, Masca km 9 | 227.2; 4.40 / 3.43 / 7.91 | +0.02 (+0.01 … +0.05) | +0.03 (−0.03 … +0.06) | +0.02 (−0.04 … +0.07) | +0.08 (+0.06 … +0.10) | +0.67 |
  | Tenerife, Puerto de la Cruz – Teide km 4, `road.damage horrible` | 210.6; 4.75 / 3.52 / 9.67 | +0.09 (+0.07 … +0.11) | +0.18 (+0.13 … +0.27) | +0.06 (+0.03 … +0.11) | +0.25 (+0.19 … +0.32) | +0.14 |

  The other presets and sizes (mean cost, the four scenes): **1920 × 1080 Medium** ground detail +0.02 … +0.05, road damage −0.01 … +0.18 (the most on the `horrible` road), map +0.04 … +0.09, all on +0.01 … +0.22 ms; **1280 × 720 High** ground detail −0.01 … +0.05, road damage +0.04 … +0.07, map +0.02 … +0.15, all on +0.07 … +0.14 ms; **1280 × 720 Medium** every feature within −0.06 … +0.04 ms, all on +0.03 … +0.08 ms. All off varied by up to 0.24 ms between rounds in the Black Forest (the forest's shadows) and by 0.01 – 0.11 ms elsewhere, so single costs below about 0.05 ms are at the noise. **No feature costs more than ~1 ms at 1080p High: the largest is road damage on a `horrible` road (+0.18 ms, about 4 %), all three together +0.08 … +0.25 ms (+0.14 … +0.69 ms at the 95th percentile); nothing needs to be cut.** Should a slower GPU ever need it, the order to trim would be road damage's fine features (cracks, the alligator pattern, loose stones) at Medium, then the ground detail's reach (80 m at High). The frame times are two-humped on this GPU (p50 about 3.5 ms, mean 4.4 – 6 ms): the features move both humps by about the same amount. The numbers are in `test-output/feature-fps-cost/` of the measuring branch (`results.tsv`, the run logs). A chunk's build takes a fraction of a millisecond on the task pool; with all resident tiles of a world set some 5,000 – 20,000 chunk entities exist (about 30 – 60 built near the rider, 4,000 – 7,500 bits; 71 chunks, 11,864 bits at Puerto de la Cruz – Teide km 4).
- **Pictures:** `scripts/ground-detail-shots.sh` renders each scene with the detail off and on, from the rider's view and a close orbit, on X11 and Wayland (Tenerife km 9 Masca, a Black Forest forest road, a Liechtenstein meadow road, an autumn and a snow scene). The answers of v5.08: `scripts/ground-detail-answers-shots.sh` (`OCW_BEFORE_APP` = the build before) – a Liechtenstein meadow verge from above before and after the spread, the bits on the road from in front of the rider, the same road wet and dry under an overcast sky, an autumn Black Forest road (2 November) with leaves and leaf patches beside and on it, dry and wet, and the menu row *Display → Graphics → World detail*, on X11 and Wayland. The total stays put: 7,245 bits before and 7,227 – 7,299 after in the same Liechtenstein scene (the console's count of the built chunks).
- **Frame-rate cost of the v5.08 changes** (marge, AMD Radeon RX Vega, 1920 × 1080 High, `scripts/feature-fps-cost.sh` with the new `OCW_FC_APP` / `OCW_FC_TAG` / `OCW_FC_CONFIGS`: the build before (`ground_detail on`) against this one (`auto` and `off`), 25 s after a 15 s warm-up, a quiet machine before every run, six rounds per scene – three with the old build first, three with the new one first; two rounds disturbed by other work (p50 doubled) left out): **Black Forest, Baden-Baden – Mummelsee km 7** before 6.43 ms (155.7 fps), after 6.60 ms (151.6 fps), after with the detail off 6.43 ms – **+0.17 ms** (+0.45 when the new build ran last, −0.05 when it ran first: the order moves it more than the change); **Liechtenstein, a Vaduz street (free ride)** before 4.96 ms (201.6 fps), after 5.02 ms (199.4 fps), off 4.96 ms – **+0.06 ms**. The 95th percentile: +0.9 ms in the forest (two-humped frame times, 13.2 – 16.5 ms over the rounds), +0.2 ms in Vaduz. The bits are as many as before (Black Forest 3,968 – 6,837 against 3,877 – 6,689 in the same runs, the few on the road included); the wider band puts them in about a quarter more 25 m chunks (34 – 49 built against 27 – 38), i.e. a few more draw calls. Well under the ~1 ms that would call for cuts. Numbers: `test-output/gd-answers-fps/` of the branch (`results.tsv`, `results2.tsv`, the run logs).

**Open questions (ground detail):**

- **Q1 – A setting for it: decided (2026-11-19, the user), built (v5.08):** a user switch – "make a user switch": `display.ground_detail` (off / low / full) on the Display page, next to the quality level. *Was asked:* since v4.72 the renderer scatters small ground detail beside the roads – gravel and grit at the edge, pebbles, rocks, dirt and moss patches, leaves, twigs, grass tufts, ferns and small shrubs – in a band up to 7 m from the road edge. Today the amount follows only the graphics quality preset (High: all of it up to 80 m away, Medium: 60 % up to 55 m, Low: 25 % up to 35 m); the only other control is the console command `ground_detail on|off`. It costs very little: about 0.1 ms per frame at most, measured. Options: (a) a rider setting on the Display page (`display.ground_detail`: off / low / full) next to the quality level; (b) keep it tied to the quality preset, with the console switch only. Proposal: b, since the measured cost is so small – a suggestion, the spec makes none. *Built (v5.08):* `display.ground_detail` auto / off / low / full with a fourth value **`auto` as the default** (the quality preset's share and distance, as before; low = the Low preset's 25 % to 35 m, full = the High preset's all to 80 m, whatever the preset), on *Display → Graphics → World detail* (Display and Graphics are full: six rows) and the console `ground_detail` – see *Quality presets* above.
- **Q2 – The VR amount: decided (2026-11-19, the user), built (v5.08):** (a) – "modest 50 % up to 50 m". *Was asked:* in a VR headset every frame is drawn twice (once per eye) at a steady 72 – 90 frames a second, so the ground detail costs more there. For the VR quality level (Phase 11) the code already holds a value: half of the bits (50 %) up to 50 m from the rider – between Medium (60 % to 55 m) and Low (25 % to 35 m). Options: (a) keep 50 % up to 50 m; (b) less, e.g. the Low amount, to protect the frame rate; (c) more, e.g. the High amount, since the ground is close to the eyes in VR. Proposal: a – 50 % up to 50 m, checked again after the first headset measurements. *Built:* already in the code as `VR_LEVEL` (0.5, 50 m) for the VR preset of Phase 11; now marked decided there and tested.
- **Q3 – Shadows and rain: decided (2026-11-19, the user), built (v5.08):** "yes, as you propose" – (b): the bits darken and shine when wet like the road; no extra shadows. *Was asked:* two things the ground detail does not do yet. Shadows: the rocks and shrubs cast none; giving them shadows means one more mesh per 25 m piece of ground on High. Rain: the road darkens and shines when it is wet, but the bits beside it keep their dry look, because the material they share with the trees has no wetness yet. Options: (a) both – shadows on High and wet darkening; (b) only the wet darkening; (c) only the shadows; (d) neither for now. Proposal: b, matching the wet road at almost no cost – a suggestion, the spec makes none. *Built (v5.08):* see *Wet* above – darker (× 0.62 when soaked) and shining (roughness 0.6), no shadows.
- **Q4 – Beyond the 7 m band: decided (2026-11-19, the user), built (v5.08):** "make it a bit more spread out, not more in overall quantity. add very few to the road, too." – the same number of bits spread over a wider band beyond the 7 m, and very few on the road itself. *Was asked:* the ground detail lies only in a band from the road edge to 7 m beyond it; further away – forest floors, meadows in view – the ground is the plain terrain. Options: (a) keep the 7 m band beside the roads; (b) spread detail over the visible ground away from the roads too, e.g. forest floors and meadows – this costs more and needs another way of placing it, since today it is placed along the road in 1 m steps. Proposal: a, until riding off the road of Phase 13 makes the ground away from roads part of the ride – a suggestion, the spec makes none. *Built (v5.08):* the band reaches 14 m – even to the old ends, thinning out linearly to twice them, the same number of bits – and very few bits on the road, off the wheel tracks and the lanes' middles (see *Where* above).
- **Q5 – Stronger autumn leaves: decided (2026-11-19, the user), built (v5.08):** "a bit stronger, and also on the road. wet leaves are slippery." – leaves a bit stronger (the proposal c: leaf-coloured patches under broadleaf trees, a few more single leaves) and some leaves on the road too; how wet leaves on the road affect the ride is asked in Q6. *Was asked:* from the leaf fall through the winter, fallen leaves lie beside the road – coloured while fresh, brown later. They are small (6 – 12 cm) and hard to see from the saddle, so autumn hardly shows on the ground. Options: (a) more of them; (b) larger ones; (c) leaf-coloured ground patches under the broadleaf trees, like the moss patches; (d) keep them as they are. Proposal: c, with a few more single leaves – a suggestion, the spec makes none. *Built (v5.08):* leaf-litter patches under the broadleaves, a quarter more single leaves and leaves on the road from the leaf fall through the winter, darker and shining when wet (see *Season* above); the ride is not changed (Q6).
- **Q6 – Wet leaves on the road and the ride: decided (2026-11-22, the user): (b) leaves on a wet road cost a little speed and add a small wobble when ridden over at speed; (c) a slide risk in a corner at speed only with damage on and never in group rides** – *Built (v5.34):* where leaves lie is a pure map of the package shared by the server and the renderer (`ocw_world::leaves`: 20 m cells, the land use's class and FRST's broadleaf share; 0.8 × max(broadleaf, 0.2) leaves a metre in a wood, 0.06 in open land, half in towns, × the season's leaf fall and (1 − snow)²); the slickness is the cover (per metre / 0.4, at most 1) × the road's wetness (from 0.1, full at 0.5). Wet leaves add 0.5 × slickness to the rolling factor (additive with the wet road's: −1 km/h at 200 W on a full cover; the Black Forest's mixed woods are 40 – 60 % slick when soaked), sway the bike sideways by up to 3 cm × slickness from 18 km/h (full at 36 km/h; seen on its lean, up to 4°), and with damage on, the full model, outside group rides and for client riders, a corner above 6 m/s and 0.15 g of sideways pull may end in a slide (0.1 × slickness × the excess pull in shares of 0.15 g per second, at most 0.5): the crash of Phase 12 (`ContactKind::Leaves`, "Wet leaves – slipped"), with its sound and damage; nothing on a dry road, outside the leaf season, under snow or with the weather physics off; the client predicts the cost and the sway (`ocw_sim::leaves`, see v5.34). Was asked: the user said wet leaves are slippery. Today nothing on the road changes the ride – the road damage and the ground detail are only drawn (the physics are unchanged; the same question is open for potholes, Phase 8 Q12). Since v5.08 leaves lie on the road from the leaf fall through the winter (in a pure broadleaf wood one or two per metre of road, in the Black Forest's mixed woods one every 2 – 4 m, few in open land) and shine when the road is wet. Leaves on a wet road could (a) only look slippery (shine, no effect); (b) cost a little speed and add a small wobble of the bike when ridden over at speed; (c) in a corner at speed with collisions and damage on, risk a slide (a crash like the others of Phase 12) – off in group rides by default; (d) only be a warning on the bike computer ("wet leaves"). Proposal: b, and c only with damage on and never in group rides.

#### 4.6.3 Fixed: water along its outlines, the far ground, the alpine ground and phantom pylons (v6.68); russet alpine grass and the evening glow of the far land (v6.76)

Reported by the user on 2026-11-26 with pictures (the Mummelsee from above, the hills towards the Rhine plain from the Hornisgrinde, the Port d'Envalira in October and January): "fix that but in a general way. for instance i noticed all lakes and rivers have that zig zag pattern. fix it for all similar cases". Four faults, each fixed for every world and every similar case.

**1. Water: the staircase shores, the slab and the flat grey surface.**

- *Cause:* the land use marks the terrain vertices inside the water and carves them 1 m below the level; the client draws a flat quad over every 10 m grid cell whose four corners have a level, and the shore is where the terrain rises through it. With one vertex in the water and its neighbour on land the drawn shore follows the grid's cells – every lake and river was a staircase. The vertices beside the water kept their natural height: where the DEM there lay below the lake's level (the lake's level is the median of the DEM under it; the Mummelsee's rim), the water stood over the land as a slab with stepped walls. Rivers drawn as lines (the Murg, the Valira, a river 12 m wide on the 10 m grid) had both shores in one cell: patches of water. The water was a plain glossy `StandardMaterial` with one vertex colour: grey, without depth, ripples or the sky in it.
- *Fix – shores (world builder, `ocw_worldgen::shore`, the stage `shorelines` of `package` and the command `world-builder shores` for built packages):* the terrain within 1.5 grid steps of the outline of every OSM water area (lakes, reservoirs, ponds, riverbanks, rivers drawn as areas; the sea of 4.6 *The sea*) follows its **signed distance** to the outline: height = level + k · d (d < 0 in the water, down to the water's depth of 1 m, the sea's 2 m, deeper along steep banks where the band needs it), with one bank slope k per water body: the median rise over distance of its land vertices in the band, between 0.1 and 0.5 (one slope keeps the distance field linear; the median keeps a lake in steep country from a cut-down terrace); no vertex moves more than 3 m (a cliff or a dam beside the water keeps its shape, land left below the water there gets no level). On every triangle across the shore the drawn terrain then crosses the water level where the outline is (a distance field interpolates linearly: exact along straight shores, within decimetres along curved ones). The band's vertices all get a water level (the nearest one, the sea 0 m), so the surface is drawn up to the outline and the land beside it stands above the water. Roads (their half width plus a grid step), junction surfaces and building sites keep their heights.
- *Fix – rivers (new section `WATR`, `ocw_world::water_lines`, optional and additive):* the OSM `waterway=river|stream|canal` lines (and drains at least 2 m wide) of at least 2 m are **ribbons along their course**, cut into the tiles: the wide ones (at least 8 m) at their level – the land use's levels along them, else the drawn ground, never rising downstream (the isotonic fit of 4.8.4) – over a channel carved 1 m below it with banks raised beside it, their grid water dropped; the streams draped on the drawn ground (8 cm above it). Left out inside lakes, riverbank areas and the sea (their surfaces are drawn there); a river ends one point into the lake it flows into. Older readers skip the section and draw the land use's water as before.
- *Fix – the material (`ocw-render::water`, `water.wesl`):* the standard PBR light on a rippled normal (four directional waves moving with the weather's wind and a noise layer; short waves fade out with the pixel's footprint, no shimmer far away), the water's own colour by depth and kind (shallow water shows its bed, deep water dark blue-green; rivers greener, the sea bluer), the sky reflected by Schlick's Fresnel term (the fog's horizon colour turning bluer towards the zenith), a broken band of foam on the shallowest water and the surface fading out at the shore (alpha by depth), so land and water meet softly. No textures: the same in WebGPU, WebGL 2 and on the Quest. The sea plane of the far terrain uses it too.
- *Numbers* (`world-builder shores` measures, every 5 m along every outline off the roads, the distance along its normal to where the drawn terrain crosses the water, at most 15 m; "wide water": outlines at least 3 grid steps across on average – lakes, reservoirs, the sea, wide riverbank areas; "narrow areas": rivers drawn as areas, where the river's ribbon replaces the grid's water): wide water, median / 90th percentile before → after – Liechtenstein 1.32 / 4.44 m → 0.00 / 0.86 m, Black Forest north 2.19 / 15 → 0.00 / 1.63 m, middle 2.78 / 15 → 0.00 / 2.25 m, south 2.68 / 15 → 0.03 / 2.77 m, Tenerife (mostly the sea's coast) 2.37 / 6.79 → 0.34 / 3.78 m, Andorra 2.35 / 7.37 → 0.15 / 1.89 m. What stays off: shores beside roads and buildings (kept: 10 – 25 % of the band), cliffs where the fit would move the ground more than 3 m (`shore::MAX_CHANGE_M`; the shore follows the grid there, under the slope), and outlines narrower than the grid. The rivers: 452 – 19,738 ribbon pieces per package (Liechtenstein 257 km, Tenerife 5,212 km of barrancos and streams draped, Black Forest south 4,423 km, Andorra 499 km). Lint: `water.river_step` 629 → 2 (Liechtenstein), 1,050 → 48 (north), 5,878 → 2 (Andorra); `water.river_uphill` 432 → 136 (north), 171 → 6 (middle); `water.level_step` falls everywhere but Tenerife (7,401 → 8,224, the sea's new band levels beside the barrancos' fitted levels; 3 new `water.lake_not_level` there); every road, junction, side and building key unchanged.

**2. The far terrain: sand dunes instead of forest.**

- *Cause:* beyond the streamed tiles the far terrain (100 m grid) tints the ground with the forest canopy by the measured cover. The conifers' canopy colour is shaded (their sides and the shadows between the crowns), but the deciduous and larch crowns took their **sunlit** leaf colour – in October the foothills' beech woods (100 % broadleaf in the Copernicus leaf type) came out light orange-tan, as bright as a sand dune, and flat (one colour per 100 m vertex, no texture). The seasonal satellite map, which the near colour maps lay over the class colours, was not used on the far tiles at all; and the near colour maps showed the forest floor (litter) wherever the trees were not drawn.
- *Fix:* the deciduous and larch canopy tones are shaded like the conifers' (`season::FAR_CROWN_SHADE`, 0.66); the far tiles lay the tile's seasonal Sentinel-2 map over their colours like the colour maps (70 %); the colour maps put 60 % of the canopy colour over forest cells (the ground beyond the trees' range is forest, not litter); the far terrain has its own material (`far.wesl`): its vertex colours with the forest's crowns (8 m) and stands (90 – 230 m) by the trees' cover and the stones of the alpine ground, faded out where a pixel is larger than the detail.
- *Left as it is:* looking west into the low sun (the user's Hornisgrinde picture, 18:15) the far hills still glow gold – that is the fog's light towards the sun (the directional fog colour of the sky model, 9), laid over whatever ground is there; at noon the same view shows the far forests green-grey (`test-output/water-ground/`, `wg-hornisgrinde-far` and `wg-hornisgrinde-far-noon`). Whether the evening haze should be weaker over the land is a question of the sky model, not of the ground. *Since v6.76 (item 6):* measured, the fog's colour was not the cause (the legacy fog has no glow towards the sun; a darker fog changed the far hills by 4 %) – the far terrain mirrored the low sun in every slope seen at a grazing angle.

**3. The sandy high slopes.**

- *Cause:* above the tree line the grass classes (no land use, meadows, `natural=grassland|heath`, parks, scrub) were drawn as lowland meadow, in the season's dormant straw – one sand-yellow sheet; the rock and scree layers were tinted towards the region's measured "rock" colour (Andorra: [120, 115, 81], the imagery's rock is lichen, turf and haze on it), which turned the grey limestone texture sand-yellow; the satellite's beige of the bare high ground then covered the far colours.
- *Fix (general, by the region's tree line, `FloraRegion::tree_line_m`):* from 400 m below the tree line (the open pastures above the forest's closed edge) to 100 m above it the grass classes turn to **alpine ground** – turf 50 %, scree 25 %, rock 15 %, gravel 10 % in the splat (the height blend makes patches of it), the stone's grey in the colour maps and the far terrain (`ground::alpine_weights`, `region_look::alpine_stone`); the rock and scree layers follow the measured colour's brightness but only 30 % of its hue (`region_look::ROCK_CHROMA`), their far colours keep half their chroma; above the tree line the satellite colour loses up to 70 % of its chroma and 50 % of its weight. The Feldberg (1 430 m), the Alps of Liechtenstein (1 950 m), Andorra (2 350 m) and Tenerife's high zone (2 250 m) all follow the same rule.

- *Result (pictures):* the alpine rule turns the far and colour-map ground of the high zone greyer and stony; near the road at the Port d'Envalira in October the slopes still read tan-ochre – the textured turf in the season's dormant straw under the measured palette's brightness, which is the imagery's real colour of dry alpine grass there. Darker, russet dormant alpine turf (its own season colour above the tree line) is the next step if that is still too light. *Done in v6.76 (item 5).*

**4. The obelisks beside the Envalira road: phantom pylons.**

- *What they were:* the towers (`power=tower`) of the 110 kV line *Liaison 110 kV n°1 Grau-Roig – L'Hospitalet* (OSM way 1479410052, tagged `disused:power=line` beside `power=line`; FEDA), and a second row 40 m beside it on a bare `power=line` without voltage, operator or name (way 174888964): 20 towers within 700 m of the pass. The link now runs as a 225 kV cable underground (way 1479410054); the overhead line was taken down – the locals see nothing there – but OSM keeps its towers. We drew every `power=tower` within the 62 m corridor of a road with the solid four-sided pyramid of the first prop export (`props/pylon-pyramid.glb`), 30 m by default (25.5 m: the height byte), so they stood as grey obelisks.
- *Fix (general, `ocw_worldgen::obstacles::dismantled_towers`; `package` and `obstacles` leave them out, `world-builder pylons` removes them from built packages):* towers of power lines that are out of service or gone (a lifecycle prefix `disused:` / `abandoned:` / `removed:` / `razed:` / `demolished:` on `power=line|minor_line`, or `disused` / `abandoned=yes`) are not built, nor the towers of a bare line (no voltage, operator, name, cables, circuits or ref) running alongside such a line (80 % of its towers within 150 m of its course: the same corridor mapped twice; at Envalira the two rows stand 100 – 140 m apart). Towers of working lines are drawn as an **open steel lattice** now (`props/pylon-lattice.glb`, `ocw_assets::pylon`: four legs, X-braced panels, two levels of cross arms with insulator strings, an earth-wire peak; about 1,400 triangles, `lod1` 250, within the props' budgets), its arms across the line (the direction to the neighbouring pylons, `obstacles::pylon_line_angle`), the collision proxy as before.
- *Numbers* (`world-builder pylons`): Andorra 43 power lines (5 dismantled), 23 towers left out of `OBST`, all at the pass (14 of the disused line, 9 of the bare row beside it; the towers in OSM beyond the roads' 62 m corridor were never drawn); Black Forest north 5 (8,593 lines, 360 dismantled), middle and south 0, Liechtenstein and Tenerife no dismantled line.

**Packages** (`scripts/water-build.sh` on marge from the J9 packages – `world-builder shores`, then `world-builder pylons` – into `data/water-build/`, with manifests, route files, build logs and the lint before and after; not installed): 

| Package | SHA-256 | Shores: band vertices (kept), new levels | River ribbons (wide / draped), km |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pilot/liechtenstein.ocwpkg` | `604b297268329fb14e851a751c0f4c13139b5b67605caaa8cceafe6e873910ff` | 32,662 (10,123), 3,632 | 11 / 448, 257.5 |
| `tenerife/tenerife.ocwpkg` | `945f21725ff1ed3f8a8019c95639fb98f20aa6f5afa938b47e6ab35e4b1be4c7` | 245,089 (58,171), 33,532 | 6 / 10,054, 5,211.7 |
