**Tests (11.4; each fails without its fix):** `ocw-worldgen` – `shore::tests::the_drawn_shoreline_follows_the_outline_not_the_grid` (a lake on the 10 m grid: before the fit the drawn shore lies up to metres off the outline, after it within 0.6 m at every sampled point, p90 0.3 m), `the_land_beside_the_water_stands_above_it` (no slab), `kept_vertices_stay_and_tile_borders_agree`, `the_sea_keeps_level_zero_along_its_fitted_coast`, `rivers_and_streams_are_ribbons_along_their_course` (levels never rising downstream, the channel below the surface, the inflow ending at the lake's shore, the stream draped, the river's grid water gone, the package round trip), `obstacles::tests::towers_of_dismantled_power_lines_are_left_out`; `ocw-world` – `water_lines::tests::lines_are_cut_into_tiles_and_round_trip`; `ocw-render` – `water::tests::a_wide_river_lies_flat_at_its_level_and_a_stream_on_the_ground`, `the_ripples_follow_the_wind`, `far_terrain::tests::far_forests_are_dark_like_the_satellite_sees_them`, `package::tests::bare_high_ground_is_turf_and_stone_not_sand` (no texel of an Andorra-like high slope reads as sand, `region_look::is_sand`; the meadow's splat has scree and rock up there, not in the valley; the rock tint stays grey), `season::tests::trees_by_season` (the shaded crowns), `obstacles::tests::pylons_are_lattice_towers_not_obelisks`, `a_pylon_faces_its_power_line`; `ocw-assets` – `pylon::tests::the_pylon_is_an_open_lattice` (from the front it covers under 25 % of its box; the pyramid covered half), `the_shipped_file_is_the_generator_s`.

Pictures (before: main's build on the J9 packages; after: this build on the new packages; the same views): `test-output/water-ground/` (index.md).

**5. Russet dormant and dry grass above the tree line (v6.76; approved by the user 2026-11-27: "yes, rust-brown dry grass").**

- *Cause:* the season model turned meadows dormant only after 700 – 1 100 cold degree days (`Phenology::grass_dormant_cdd`, calibrated on the lowland meadows of the Alpine Rhine valley), so the high pastures were still "green" in early October (the Port d'Envalira, 2 420 m, on 8 October: 690) and their colour was the measured palette's tan-ochre with the satellite's beige over it; where they were dormant they took the lowland meadow's olive straw. Las Cañadas never dried (the meadows' dryness starts at 19 °C daily mean, the high zone's August is 18 °C).
- *Fix – the season (`ocw_sky::season`, general):* `Grass::high_brown` – how brown a high pasture is besides the meadows' dormancy: dormant after the first frosts (`Phenology::high_dormant_cdd`, 250 – 600 CDD: Envalira brown from mid-September, all of it by early October) or dried in a dry summer at the high zone's lower temperatures (`high_dry_c`, 10 – 14.5 °C daily mean, by the climate's `summer_dry` / 0.6: the Canaries fully, Andorra's short dryness a little, the Alps and the Black Forest not); the shader gets it as an altitude ramp (`SeasonRamps::high_brown`). The cycle restarts at the coldest day, so spring's green-up (GDD) is as before.
- *Fix – the colour (`ocw-render::season`):* around the region's tree line (from 300 m below to 50 m above it, `russet_share`; the Feldberg 1 430 m, Liechtenstein's Alps 1 950 m, Tenerife's high zone 2 250 m, Andorra 2 350 m) brown grass (the larger of dormant, summer-dry and `high_brown`) is retinted to **russet**: between a rust (sRGB 0.36, 0.20, 0.12) and a darker brown (0.28, 0.18, 0.12) by noise at 23 m and 5 m, 90 % of the way, keeping only 10 % of the layer's own brightness (`alpine_grass`; the meadows keep 65 %). The terrain shader applies it after the regional tint (the measured palette's tan does not turn it back), also on the orthophoto corridor; the colour maps and the far terrain take the same colour (`ground_colour(…, tree_line_m)`); the satellite colour weighs 80 % less over russet grass (`region_look::RUSSET_SATELLITE_LESS`); the ground detail's tufts and stalks above the tree line are russet too. Green where the climate says so: Envalira in July, the Alps in summer, the valleys unchanged.
- *Result (pictures, the same views, mean sRGB of the slopes):* the Port d'Envalira from above in October (`wg-envalira-pass`) 176 / 163 / 128 → 176 / 148 / 122, the road at the pass (`readme-andorra-envalira`) 166 / 154 / 118 → 166 / 137 / 114, the Feldberg in late October 149 / 134 / 108 → 149 / 126 / 104, Las Cañadas in August 166 / 148 / 135 → 158 / 142 / 130: rust-brown instead of tan, a little darker – the alpine ground is half scree, rock and gravel (item 3), whose grey keeps its brightness; Envalira in July unchanged (176 / 171 / 139 → 177 / 170 / 139).

**6. The evening glow of the far land (v6.76; approved by the user 2026-11-27: "weaker evening haze").**

- *Cause (measured):* looking into a low sun the far hills (the far terrain's 100 m grid) glowed gold-white on every slope seen at a grazing angle, whatever their colour – also with the far terrain painted magenta, and also with the simple sky. It was the PBR material's specular reflection: the far material had the default reflectance (0.5, a smooth dielectric), whose Fresnel term goes to 1 at a grazing angle, so the sun was mirrored in the far slopes. A darker fog over the land changed the far hills by 4 % only, a darker far canopy not at all.
- *Fix – the far terrain (`far_terrain::FAR_REFLECTANCE`, `far.wesl`):* no specular reflection on the far terrain (a forest, a meadow and a field are rough at the 100 m grid's scale; Bevy's Fresnel goes to the reflectance's f90, 0 now). Far forests lose up to 60 % of their colour looking into a low sun (`backlit_canopy`, `FAR_BACKLIGHT`: the shaded side of the crowns faces the eye; by the trees' cover, the square of the cosine between the view and the sun on the ground, below 8° of sun elevation and none from 25°; `far.backlight K [OPEN]` for comparisons).
- *Fix – the haze over the land (`ocw_sky::light::land_fog_srgb`, `land_aerial_m`; `ocw-render::sky`):* at a low sun (from −1° to 8°, easing off to none at 20° and below −4°) the distance fog over the land is 85 % of the way to a colour 45 % as bright as the sky's horizon and bluer (the horizon colour × 0.80 / 0.92 / 1.15), and the atmosphere's own haze (its aerial perspective) is integrated over 12 km instead of Bevy's 32 km; the sky, the clouds' haze and the clear colour keep the horizon colour. Only in a clear, unlimited view (`land_haze_share`): a limited view (Medium, Low – the land must still fade into the sky, 10G), the weather's fog and rain (visibility below 8 km; all of it from 20 km), an overcast sky and `sky.haze 0` keep the fog as before. The same in WebGPU and WebGL 2 (the simple sky uses the same fog).
- *Result (pictures, the same views; mean sRGB of the far land band, the sky above the horizon unchanged):* the unicorn over the Hornisgrinde at sunset (`unicorn-hornisgrinde-sunset`) 164 / 127 / 121 → 138 / 113 / 116 (its brightest 0.5 %: 163 → 145), `wg-hornisgrinde-far` (18:15) 175 / 156 / 149 → 152 / 144 / 145, the simple sky (the WebGL 2 path) 145 / 132 / 121 → 112 / 108 / 104, the morning into the sun (08:45) 159 / 152 / 149 → 113 / 127 / 142 (the sand dunes are blue-grey hills now), noon 148 / 169 / 192 → 140 / 165 / 191, Medium 175 / 156 / 149 → 156 / 147 / 147 (the specular fix only); the dawn mist at Encamp, the rain on the Schauinsland, Tenerife's sunset and Liechtenstein's sunrise look as before. The far hills stand as darker, bluer layers under a golden sky.

**Tests (11.4; each fails without its fix):** `ocw-sky` – `season::tests::high_pastures_turn_brown_in_autumn_and_dry_summers` (Envalira brown on 8 October, green in July; Las Cañadas dry in August; the shader ramp matches); `ocw-render` – `season::tests::dormant_alpine_grass_is_russet_and_darker` (Andorra in October and December, Liechtenstein's Alps, the Feldberg, Las Cañadas: hue 8 – 35°, red over green above 1.3, under 60 % of the old brightness over the tan; the valley unchanged; July green), `uniforms` (the tree line and the ramp in the terrain uniform), `region_look::tests::the_satellite_does_not_pull_russet_grass_back_to_beige`, `ground_detail::tests::alpine_tufts_and_stalks_are_russet_when_dormant`, `package::tests::bare_high_ground_is_turf_and_stone_not_sand` (russet is not sand), `far_terrain::tests::far_forests_look_dark_looking_into_a_low_sun` (at most 45 % into a 0.5 – 6° sun, unchanged at noon, across the sun, away from it and on open ground; no reflectance), `sky::tests::far_land_at_sunset_is_darker_and_bluer_than_the_sky` (the fully fogged far land at most 55 % of the horizon's brightness and bluer, −1 – 8°, both skies; a half-fogged forest darker than before and under half the sky's brightness; day, night, Medium, mist, rain, overcast and `sky.haze 0` unchanged; the aerial perspective 12 km at a low sun, 32 km otherwise).

### 4.7 Data Packages

Regions are stored as self-contained data packages.

Example:

```
worlds/europe/germany/berlin/
```

Contents:

- Geographic source data (the extracted road graph and attributes, 13).
- Terrain data.
- Road meshes.
- Building meshes.
- Vegetation.
- Materials, splat maps and color maps.
- Routes.
- Metadata, including source attributions.
- Version information.

**Package format (v1.6):** the binary package (`.ocwpkg`) holds the 1 km tiles (terrain heights, road strips) and, from format version 2 (`OCWPKG02`), tagged sections after the tiles that readers skip when they do not know them. The first section is the **road graph** (`GRPH`: vertices, edges with stable ID, class, name, width, one-way, bridge / tunnel / boundary / dead-end flags, centreline and smoothed elevation profile), so the client and the server can ride free on it (2.2.1). Packages without a graph are still written as version 1, and clients read both.

**Look sections (Phase 8 T3, v2.47):** `PALT` holds the imagery sources of the package (id, name, licence, notice, URL, date, resolution) and the **regional palette**: the median colour per land class (interior land-use cells only – all four neighbours of the same class, away from roads and buildings), of the paved and of the unpaved roads (every 2 m along the graph's centre lines, no tunnels or bridges) and of all roofs, with the number of pixels and the source; classes the orthophoto does not cover come from the Sentinel-2 summer composite. `ROOF` holds one colour per building (r, g, b and its origin: orthophoto or OSM) in the order of the `BLDG` section: the per-channel median of the orthophoto pixels inside the footprint eroded by 1 m (fewer than 6 pixels: the whole footprint), OSM `roof:colour` / `roof:color` (CSS names, `#rgb`, `#rrggbb`) wins. `SEAS` holds the seasonal tint maps: per season its date window and centre day, the number of scenes and the median colour per land class; per tile one map per season of 50 × 50 cells (20 m; `--season-cells 100` for 10 m), each stored as YCoCg with chroma at half resolution, LOCO-I predicted and deflated (lossless within a few levels), gaps (cloud all season) filled from the summer composite, tiles outside the composites left out. Readers that do not know the sections skip them (tested); a skeleton reads only `PALT` (credits). Package sizes before → after: Liechtenstein 30.2 → 35.0 MB (`SEAS` 4.8 MB for 510 tiles, `ROOF` 0.07 MB for 17,897 buildings), Black Forest south 258.5 → 284.5 MB (`SEAS` 24.8 MB for 2,800 tiles, `ROOF` 1.25 MB for 306,478 buildings), Tenerife 238.5 → 261.6 MB (`SEAS` 22.6 MB for 2,690 tiles, `ROOF` 0.48 MB for 116,479 buildings); `PALT` is a few hundred bytes. The tint maps cost about 9 KB per tile and season set at 20 m (4 × 50²); at 10 m they would be about four times as large, which is why 20 m is the default.

**Orthophoto corridor (Phase 8 T7, v3.10):** `ORTC` (optional, only added; `ocw_world::ortho`) holds the orthophoto along the package's roads: layout version, pixel size, corridor half width, chunks per tile side (8: 125 m chunks), weight cells per tile side (250: 4 m), the encoding (1 = baseline JPEG, sRGB, rows along +z), the indices of its sources in `PALT` (their notices are the credits), then per tile its **corridor weights** at the cell corners (0 … 255; LOCO-I predicted and deflated like the tint maps) and its stored chunks (column, row, JPEG bytes). Only chunks the corridor touches are stored; pixels outside it are the local ground colour. The weight is 1 up to 30 m beside the nearest road edge (the strips of the tile and its neighbours) and fades to 0 at 50 m (`corridor_weight`); it is 0 in forests (the photo shows the canopy from above, not the floor under our trees; this also halved the Black Forest's corridor) and on building footprints, rising from 1.5 to 4 m around them (roofs lean in the photo and would be painted on the ground beside the 3D houses). Readers that do not know the section skip it, a newer layout is skipped too, a skeleton leaves it out, and streaming clients (B2) do not fetch it with the base (`STREAM_SKIPPED_SECTIONS`; tested).

**Obstacles section (Phase 12 K3, v3.14):** `OBST` (optional, only added; `ocw_world::obstacles`) holds the static obstacles a rider can hit that the package has nowhere else: after a layout byte and the tree cells per tile side (125: 8 m), per tile its **points** (kind, flags, x / z in package metres as `f32`, the way's direction in 256 steps of π, the width a gate spans in dm, the height in dm) – OSM `barrier=*` nodes (bollard, gate, lift gate, block, cycle barrier / stile / kissing gate, any other barrier; entrances, cattle grids, kerbs and height restrictors are left out), `barrier=post`, posts (`power=pole`, `man_made=utility_pole`, guide posts) and pylons (`power=tower`), and since v5.43 the street lamps mapped in OSM (`highway=street_lamp`, kind 10: where they are mapped, OSM's `height` or 0; never road barriers; the apps place each beside its road, world look *Street lamps*; older readers leave the kind out) –, its **lines** (kind, flags, height in dm, points as `f32`) – barrier ways: fence (also railing, handrail), wall (also city / retaining wall, jersey barrier), hedge, guard rail, kerb, gate – and its **tree cells** (deflated; one byte per 8 m cell, 0 or the tree's land class + 1: the cells the shared tree placement `ocw_world::trees` fills, so the server rebuilds the same trunks the client draws without land use or terrain). The **2 m corridor rule**: only what lies within wild mode's reach (60 m beside a road centre line) plus 2 m is written; a point barrier within 2 m of a carriageway is a *road barrier* (flag 1; on the carriageway also flag 2) – drawn only with `display.road_barriers`, never solid (Q7); the parts of barrier lines on a carriageway are cut out (a fence ends at the road it meets; kerbs are kept). Buildings (`BLDG`), bridge railings (`BRDG`: the parapet's or rail's line at the deck edge, with the deck's height) and tunnel walls (the graph's tunnel edges, 1 m beside the road edge as the drawn tube, with the profile's height) are not repeated: `WorldObstacles::from_package` takes them from their sections (so packages without `OBST` have them too). Older readers skip the section, a newer layout is skipped, skeletons and streamed bases keep it (it is small, like `LITR`). Sizes (the main checkout's packages of v3.10 with `world-builder obstacles`, marge): Liechtenstein 0.16 MB (173 bollards, 154 posts, 87 gates, 45 pylons, 195 fences, 263 walls, 639 hedges …; 201 road barriers, 134 of them on a carriageway; 186 k trees in 168 tiles), Black Forest south 4.08 MB (+0.7 %; 8.48 M trees, 12,748 posts, 6,207 fences, 2,505 gates, 2,136 road barriers; 34 s, 3.1 GB peak), middle 3.24 MB (7.56 M trees), north 2.86 MB (6.47 M trees), Tenerife 2.10 MB (1.84 M trees, 15,680 walls – the terraces –, 3,997 pylons). The lint counts `obstacle.on_road.KIND` and `obstacle.on_through_road.KIND` (a gate across a through road: a data error, noted, never solid; 12H).

**Forest section (Phase 8 T3, v3.20):** `FRST` (optional, only added; `ocw_world::forest`) holds the measured forest: layout version (1), cells per tile side (50: 20 m), the sources (id, name, licence, notice, URL, date, resolution – the credits), then per tile two `cells²` planes, row-major along +z – the **tree cover density** (0 … 100 %, 255 no data) and the **broadleaf share** of the measured tree pixels (0 … 100 %, 255 no trees) – LOCO-I predicted and deflated together; tiles without data are left out. The world builder resamples the HRL rasters (10 m, LAEA Europe) with 4 × 4 points per cell through the tile's affine fit. Read only with the full package (not by skeletons, so not by the server, which keeps the trees it needs in `OBST`), streamed with the base; older readers skip it, a newer layout is skipped, packages without it keep the fallback leaf mix and the land use's tree chances. `OBST`'s tree cells are computed from the same placement, so they are renewed when `FRST` is added.

**Vegetation section (Phase 8 T8, v3.49):** `VEGE` (optional, only added; `ocw_world::vegetation`) holds what grows on the fields and plantations and the mapped trees: layout version (u32, 1), cells per tile side (u32, 100: 10 m), the sources beyond OSM (id, name, licence, notice, URL, date, resolution – as `FRST`; empty while only OSM is used), then per tile its x / z, the **planes** (u32 length + deflated bytes, 0 = no fields in the tile): `cells²` crop codes (`FieldCrop`: 0 none, 1 cereal, 2 maize, 3 rapeseed, 4 sunflower, 5 potato, 6 beet, 7 grass, 8 vegetables, 9 vineyard, 10 orchard, 11 banana, 12 berries, 13 fallow, 14 greenhouse, 15 avocado / citrus; only add codes) followed by `cells²` row directions (`× π / 256` from +x towards +z, 255 no rows), row-major along +z like the land use; and the **mapped trees** (u32 count; per tree x, z as `f32` package metres, the species code (`ocw_world::flora::Species`, 0 unknown: the rules decide; 32 codes, only add), the mapped height in dm (u16, 0 none) and the source (1 `natural=tree`, 2 a tree of a `natural=tree_row`). A row's plants stand on global lines (`dot(p, n) = k · spacing`), so rows run on across cells and tiles (`ocw_world::plantings`). Read only with the full package, streamed with the base; older readers skip the tag, a newer layout is skipped, unknown species read as unknown; packages without it keep the seasons' noise patches for the crops, orchards on the 8 m tree grid and no mapped trees. `OBST` follows the same placement: the tree grid leaves the plantations' cells and the 8 m cells of mapped trees empty, and the solid planted trees (orchard rows, mapped trees) are point obstacles of the new kind 9 `PlantedTree` (width = trunk diameter, height in dm; solid as a tree; older readers leave unknown kinds out), so `world-builder vegetation` renews `OBST`'s trees.

**Road condition section (v4.75, 4.6 *Road damage*):** `RCND` (optional, only added; `ocw_world::road_condition`) holds what OSM says about each road strip's surface condition, like `LITR`: per tile with a known strip its key, the strip count and two bytes per strip in the tile's strip order – `smoothness` (0 unknown, 1 excellent … 8 impassable) + 16 × `tracktype` (0 none, 1 … 5), and the `surface` value (0 unknown, asphalt, concrete, concrete plates, chip seal, paving stones, sett, cobblestone, compacted, fine gravel, gravel, dirt, grass, other paved). Packages without it, older readers and unknown codes give unknown (the renderer estimates the condition). `world-builder package` writes it; `world-builder condition --world PKG --pbf …` adds it to an existing package (strips matched to their edges by geometry where the package changed since it was built) and prints the road length per smoothness value.

**Places section (v4.77; 14 Phase 16 16A *Map labels*):** `PLCE` (optional, only added; `ocw_world::places`) holds the named places of OSM for the map labels: `place=city | town | village | hamlet | suburb` (also `quarter`) `| neighbourhood | locality | isolated_dwelling` with a `name`, from nodes and – where a place is mapped only as an area (a closed way, a multipolygon or boundary relation) – at the area's centroid (an area with a node of the same name inside it is left out: the node is the label's place); only places on the package's tiles are kept. Layout: version (u8, 1), count (u32), then per place a record length (u16; readers skip unknown bytes at a record's end, so fields can be added), the kind (u8: 0 city, 1 town, 2 village, 3 hamlet, 4 suburb, 5 neighbourhood, 6 locality, 7 isolated dwelling; only add codes, unknown ones read as unknown), the **rank** (u8, 0 most important: city 0, town 1, village 2, hamlet and suburb 3, neighbourhood 4, locality and isolated dwelling 5; the capital of a country or state – `capital=yes` or an admin level ≤ 4 – one higher, a town or village of 100,000 or more inhabitants 0), flags (bit 0 area; bits 1–2 the OSM element: node, way, relation), the capital's admin level (0 none), x / z (`f32` package metres), `population` (u32, `u32::MAX` not tagged; "12,345" and "12 345" read), the OSM id (i64), `name` (u16 length + UTF-8) and the `name:en | de | es | fr | it | rm` that differ from it (u8 count; language, name). Stored most important first (rank, population, name, OSM element – deterministic). It is small, so it is read by skeletons and streamed bases too; older readers skip the tag, a newer layout is skipped, packages without it load with no places. `world-builder package` writes it (three passes over the extract: place relations, ways, nodes); `world-builder places --world PKG --pbf PBF… [--out NEW]` adds it to a built package and leaves every other section byte for byte as it was. Sizes and counts (marge's packages with `world-builder places`, 2026-11-18; every other section and the tiles byte for byte identical, checked per section with SHA-256): Liechtenstein 88.00 → 88.00 MB (+4.0 KB; 107 places: 2 towns – Vaduz rank 0 as the capital –, 19 villages, 12 hamlets, 3 neighbourhoods, 63 localities, 8 isolated dwellings; 13 with population; 1 s), Black Forest north 435.98 → 436.03 MB (+56 KB; 1,418: 11 towns, 137 villages, 170 hamlets, 24 suburbs, 93 neighbourhoods, 808 localities, 175 isolated dwellings, 80 of them areas; 17 s), middle 471.07 → 471.15 MB (+80 KB; 1,994: 17 towns, 123 villages, 263 hamlets, 22 suburbs, 69 neighbourhoods, 324 localities, 1,176 isolated dwellings, 105 areas), south 578.01 → 578.10 MB (+89 KB; 2,209: 1 city – Freiburg –, 16 towns, 185 villages, 319 hamlets, 43 suburbs, 168 neighbourhoods, 602 localities, 875 isolated dwellings, 90 areas), Tenerife 499.99 → 500.06 MB (+76 KB; 1,823: 1 city – Santa Cruz –, 21 towns, 56 villages, 444 hamlets, 189 suburbs, 288 neighbourhoods, 727 localities, 97 isolated dwellings, 45 areas, 570 with population; 10 s).

**Landmarks section (v5.03; 2.11 Q4, 3.2 Q8):** `LMRK` (optional, only added; `ocw_world::landmarks`, pure and wasm-safe) holds the **peaks, mountain passes and viewpoints** of OSM for the photographer's view score and the maps: named `natural=peak` and `natural=volcano` (the Teide is one), `mountain_pass=yes` (named or not) and named `natural=saddle`, and `tourism=viewpoint` (named or not; nodes, and ways at their centroid), only those on the package's tiles. It travels with the places (`Places::landmarks`; a separate section, so a reader without it keeps `PLCE` as it was and never sees peaks as places of an unknown kind or nameless viewpoints as empty labels). Layout: version (u8, 1), count (u32), then per landmark a record length (u16; readers skip unknown bytes at a record's end), the kind (u8: 0 peak, 1 pass, 2 viewpoint; only add codes, records of unknown kinds are skipped), flags (bit 0 elevation known, bit 1 the elevation is the terrain's – the element has no `ele` –, bit 2 direction known, bits 3–4 the OSM element: node, way), x / z (`f32` package metres), the elevation (`f32` m; OSM `ele` – "3715", "3715 m", "1234,5", feet converted – else the package terrain's height there), a viewpoint's `direction` (u16 centre in degrees clockwise from north, u16 width: degrees "135", compass points "SE" / "NNW", ranges "90-180" / "W-NE" clockwise, "all" / "360"; a single direction is 90° wide), the OSM id (i64), `name` (u16 length + UTF-8, empty for none) and the `name:*` of `PLCE`'s languages that differ (u8 count; language, name). Stored peaks first, then passes, then viewpoints, higher first (then name, element, id – deterministic). Small, so read by skeletons and streamed bases too; older readers skip the tag, a newer layout is skipped, packages without it have none. `world-builder package` writes it with `PLCE` (the same three passes over the extract); `world-builder places --world PKG --pbf PBF… [--out NEW]` adds both to a built package, every other section byte for byte as it was, and prints the counts and the highest of each kind. **Marge's packages with it (2026-11-19, `world-builder places` on the `data/places-build/` copies into `data/landmarks-build/`, not deployed; the originals untouched):** Liechtenstein +3.8 KB (55 peaks – Vorder Grauspitz 2599 m, Naafkopf 2571 m –, 15 passes – Ijesfürggli 2348 m, Bettlerjoch 2108 m, Sareiserjoch 1992 m –, 24 viewpoints, 5 named, 6 with a direction; 1 s), Tenerife +47 KB (557 peaks, 547 with `ele` – Teide 3715 m, Pico Viejo 3129 m, Montaña Blanca 2748 m, Guajara 2718 m –, 34 passes, 24 with `ele` – Degollada de Ucanca, Col del Teide 2294 m, Puerto de Izaña 2223 m –, 480 viewpoints, 173 named, 28 with a direction – Mirador de La Fortaleza 3555 m –; 8 s), Black Forest north +29 KB (260 peaks – Hornisgrinde 1164 m –, 17 passes – Alexanderschanze 973 m, Ruhestein 915 m –, 453 viewpoints, 174 named, 156 with a direction; 14 s), middle +33 KB (320 peaks, 12 passes – Yacher Höhe 1109 m –, 539 viewpoints, 146 named, 209 with a direction), south +42 KB (393 peaks – Belchen 1414 m –, 44 passes – Feldbergpass 1231 m, Kandel –, 668 viewpoints, 212 named, 150 with a direction).

**Junction sections (v5.14; 4.8.8 J2, `JMRB` J3):** three optional, additive sections (`ocw_world::junction::section`, pure and wasm-safe); older readers skip the tags, a newer layout is skipped, and a section made for another road graph (its `GRPH` fingerprint differs) is ignored – the junctions are then computed from the graph as in J1, with the same result. **`JNCT`** – the junction rules and patch outlines, so the loader searches nothing: version (u8, 5 since J9 – clusters that no star-shaped outline holds are one patch with a simple outline, and an arm whose edge's far end has no junction surface takes the room it leaves, 4.8.8 *Built (J9)*; 4 since J8 – a junction's arm runs on past a plain way split and the mouths lie out for their corners' radius, 4.8.8 *Built (J8)*; 3 since J7 – paths along a road take no part in the junctions; 2 since J3 – the side roads' corners of 4.8.8 Q6 (d) change the drawn surface; an older layout is ignored and the junctions computed; 1 before), flags (u8; bit 0: the profiles are reconciled with the junction surfaces and the terrain is settled under them in the package – the renderer then leaves the terrain as it is), the graph fingerprint (u64), the vertex count (u32), then per rule, by growing vertex, a record length (u16; readers skip unknown bytes at a record's end), the vertex (u32), the kind (u8: 0 patch, 1 mitre, 2 cluster patch, 3 cluster member – J3; records of unknown kinds are skipped) and for a patch its arms by polar angle (u8 count; per arm the edge u32, flags u8 – bit 0 its `from` end is here –, the mouth's distance from its vertex f64 and the strip's along coordinate there f64) and its outline (u16 count; per point the offset from the patch's centre – the vertex, a cluster's centroid – dx / dz `f32` and the arm whose mouth it lies on, u8, 255 none); a cluster patch (at its first vertex) then its members (u8 count, u32 each, growing; J8: a junction whose arms run on past way splits first, then those splits) and the edges inside it (u8 count, u32 each), then (layout 4) the members that are such way splits (u8 count, u32 each; the patch's centre is the centroid of the other members); a cluster member the first member (u32), whose patch it shares. A vertex without a record has no junction surface. The computed outline is rounded the same way (offsets in `f32`), so a stored patch and a computed one are equal to the bit – test `stored_rules_are_the_computed_ones`; the renderer's `PackageJunctions` takes the stored rules (`JunctionSet::with_index`), the server and the client's prediction may compute them. **`RDGE`** – the edge of every road strip: version (u8, 1), the graph fingerprint (u64), the tile count (u32), per tile its x / z (i32), the strip count (u32) and per strip in the tile's order its edge index (u32, `u32::MAX` none); it replaces the renderer's geometric matching, a tile whose strip count differs is matched by geometry. **`JMRB`** (v5.36, J3) – the mini-roundabouts: version (u8, 1), the graph's vertex count (u32), then the vertices OSM tags `highway=mini_roundabout` (u32 count, u32 each, growing; `world-builder junctions --pbf EXTRACT`, matched to the junction vertex within 3 m); the renderer paints a disc on their junction surface. All three are read with the full package (not by skeletons); a streaming client leaves only `JNCT` out of its base. `world-builder package` writes them (flag set when it cleans); `world-builder junctions --world PKG [--out NEW]` bakes the junctions into a built package (4.8.8 *Built (J2)*), every other section as it was.

**Land use and buildings sections (Phase 3):** `LUSE` holds the splat map of every tile (layout version, cells per side, then per tile the classes run-length coded row by row and the water levels as (terrain vertex index, level) pairs); `BLDG` holds the buildings per tile (kind, roof shape and height, base and eave height, outline and courtyard rings in tile-local metres). Both are optional: older clients skip them as unknown sections (tested), newer clients without them fall back to plain grass. The pilot package grows from about 26 MB to about 30 MB with them.

**Building tags section (Phase 8 T4, v2.57):** `BTAG` holds, per tile and only for buildings OSM says something about, the facts the houses are styled by (`ocw_world::buildings::BuildingTags`): the finer use (chalet, farmhouse, barn, garage, shed, church, chapel, greenhouse, canopy, hut, hotel, retail, terrace), the tagged roof shape, a roof height from `roof:height`, `roof:angle` or `roof:levels`, `building:levels`, `roof:levels`, `min_height` / `building:min_level`, the wall material (`building:material`, `building:facade:material`), `building:colour`, `roof:material` and `roof:colour`. Layout: version, tiles, per record the building's index in the tile's `BLDG` list, a record length and a flag word, then only the flagged fields – readers skip flags and bytes they do not know, so fields can be added without a new layout; an unknown layout version is skipped, not fatal. `BLDG` itself is unchanged: pitched roofs keep their four-point rectangle and `Roof::Gabled` height, with the corners rotated so that the first edge carries the ridge (`roof:orientation=across`, `roof:direction`) or, for a skillion, the low eave – an old reader draws a gable along the right axis. A pyramid on a polygon (towers, spires; `roof:shape` pyramidal, cone, dome, onion on a convex footprint up to 600 m²) is `Roof::Flat` in `BLDG` and its height is in `BTAG`. Cost: `BTAG` is 0.02 MB in Liechtenstein (2,105 of 17,897 buildings with facts, 660 with a roof shape; +0.06 % of the package), 0.51 MB in the Black Forest south (51,729 of 306,478; 17,039 shapes; +0.18 %) and 0.53 MB in Tenerife (63,588 of 116,479; 949 shapes; +0.2 %).

**Building parts section (Phase 8 T4, v3.26):** `BPRT` (optional, only added; `ocw_world::buildings::write_building_parts`) holds the buildings' parts (OSM `building:part`: church towers and spires, wings of other heights): layout version (1), per tile and only for buildings with parts the building's index in the tile's `BLDG` list, a flag byte (bit 0: the parts cover the outline – at least 85 % of it, sampled; they are drawn instead of it, else on top of it), the part count and per part its length (u32) and the part as a `BLDG` building (kind, roof, base and eave height, rings) followed by its tags as a `BTAG` record – readers skip what follows a part's tags, and an unknown layout is skipped, not fatal. Readers that do not know the section draw the outline building as before. `BTAG` gained field 10 (v3.26), the **skeleton roof height**: a footprint that is not nearly rectangular but wants a pitched roof is `Roof::Flat` in `BLDG` (old readers draw it flat) and carries the height of its roof over the polygon (straight skeleton, 14 Phase 8 T4) here. Cost: Liechtenstein 2,734 pitched roofs over polygons and 49 buildings with parts (203 parts, 41 covered), `BPRT` 0.02 MB, the package +0.05 MB (+0.05 %); Black Forest south 36,934 / 1,042 buildings (2,949 parts, 694 covered), `BPRT` 0.25 MB, +0.64 MB (+0.11 %), middle 29,765 / 158 (466), north 23,901 / 700 (1,425), +0.36 and +0.35 MB; Tenerife 33,991 / 22,640 buildings (65,103 parts – the cadastre import maps most blocks as parts by storeys –, 18,350 covered), `BPRT` 5.29 MB, +5.5 MB (+1.1 %).

**Road dress section (Phase 8 T5, v2.60):** `RDRS` holds, after a layout version byte, per tile with a strip that differs from its class default and per road strip of the tile (in strip order): the arc length of the strip's first point along its road edge and the edge's length (f32 each), lanes forward / backward (a nibble each), the centre line and the edge / lane line flags, the cycle lanes left / right, the kerb height (cm), the sidewalk widths left / right and the junction zones at the edge's start and end (dm), and the transverse markings (count, then per marking its position along the strip (f32), kind and half). Older readers skip the section, an unknown layout version is skipped, packages without it draw their roads with the class defaults (`RoadDress::of_class`). Cost: about 13–19 bytes per strip: +0.18 MB in Liechtenstein (+0.5 %), +2.9 MB in the Black Forest south (+1.0 %), +1.5 MB in Tenerife (+0.5 %).

**Region section (decided):** `REGN` holds the region the package was cut to: the latitude / longitude box and the polygon rings (outer and holes) of the `.poly` file, if any (layout version, four `f64`, then the rings as (lat, lon) `f64` pairs). It is what neighbouring packages are matched and drawn by (2.2.2); `world-builder package --bbox S,W,N,E` narrows the `--poly` region to a box (cutting a region into neighbours), `--origin LAT,LON` sets the projection origin of the local metres (default: the box centre). Packages without it still load but cannot have neighbours. The manifest repeats the box as `bounds` (taken from the section when the package file is added), so clients find neighbours without reading every package.

**Routes section (decided):** `ROUT` holds the package's routes on the road graph (2.7): per route its name, a loop flag and the steps (stable edge ID with from / to metres as `f64`, or a U-turn). A package with only routes and no graph is still version 2. `world-builder gpx` and `route --world` add routes; readers that do not know the section skip it.

**Route files (v1.9, interim):** a plain-text `ocw-route 1` file holds one route with its elevation and the terrain grid around it (`name`, `origin` lat/lon of the local metres, `width`, `points` x y z every 5 m, optional `surface FROM TO NAME` stretches that are not asphalt, `grid`). It is written by `world-builder route` and ridden with `--route-file`, optionally together with a world package (`--world`) for the surroundings. Routes as part of packages (above) replace it; it keeps working until the last users are moved to package routes.

**Second world: the Black Forest (decided 2026-11-12, v2.24).** After the Liechtenstein pilot (about 160 km², 30 MB) the second package is the **southern Black Forest** (Schwarzwald, Germany), id `europe/germany/black-forest`, file `blackforest.ocwpkg`.

- **Sources (first build; since v2.36 both Regierungsbezirke and LGL DGM1, below):** the Geofabrik extract of the Regierungsbezirk Freiburg (Baden-Württemberg, 160 MB PBF; it holds the southern and central Black Forest, the northern part lies in the Regierungsbezirk Karlsruhe) and the SRTM tiles N47E007, N47E008, N48E007, N48E008; `scripts/fetch-pilot.sh blackforest` downloads them into `data/blackforest/` with a licence table (`SOURCES.md`; OSM ODbL 1.0, SRTM public domain). `scripts/build-blackforest.sh` builds the package and the routes.
- **Extent:** the box 47.72–48.12 N, 7.62–8.30 E (`--bbox`, 44 × 51 km, about 2,260 km² or 14 times the pilot), projection origin 47.92 N 7.96 E (`--origin`, fixed so that later neighbour parts share its metres and tile grid). It reaches from the Rhine plain west of Freiburg to Neustadt and from Waldkirch / the Kandel to St. Blasien: Freiburg, Schauinsland, Feldberg, Titisee, Belchen, Blauen, Schluchsee, Todtnau.
- **Measurements** (build machine `marge`, release build, one package each; client = `ocw-desktop` free ride on software Vulkan, whose RSS includes what a GPU would hold as VRAM):

| Extent | Area | Tiles | Edges | Package | Build | Builder RSS | Client peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Liechtenstein pilot | 160 km² | – | – | 30 MB | – | – | 0.68 GB |
| Core: Freiburg – Schauinsland – Feldberg – Titisee (47.84–48.08 N, 7.70–8.20 E) | 1,000 km² | 1,344 | 66,340 | 124 MB | 53 s | 2.9 GB | 0.99 GB |
| **South (chosen)** | 2,260 km² | 2,800 | 141,245 | 260 MB | 101–131 s | 3.2 GB | 1.76 GB |
| Large: Rhine to Baar, Waldshut to Elz (47.58–48.30 N, 7.55–8.45 E) | 5,370 km² | 6,192 | 300,190 | 564 MB | 251 s | 3.9 GB | 3.31 GB |

- **Why this extent:** building is cheap at every size (minutes, under 4 GB), so the client decides. It decodes the whole package into memory (tiles, graph, land use, buildings; about 5.5 MB of RAM per MB of package on top of 0.65 GB), so the large extent breaks the memory budget of 15 (≤ 2 GB) and is above the 200–500 MB disk target, while the south extent stays within both and holds every iconic climb of the southern Black Forest. More of the Black Forest (north of the Elz, the Karlsruhe part, the Baar) comes as **neighbour packages** (2.2.2): the same `--poly` extract or the Karlsruhe one, their own `--bbox`, the same `--origin`; only their tiles near the rider are loaded. Loading tiles from a package on demand instead of decoding all of it would allow larger single packages later.
- **Routes:** `Freiburg - Schauinsland` (19.9 km, 1,055 m climbing: Bertoldsbrunnen 281 m – Günterstal – Schauinslandstraße – road end below the summit at 1,267 m) and `Titisee - Feldberg` (13.5 km, 500 m climbing: Titisee 857 m – B317 via Bärental – Feldberg pass, about 1,280 m), both as package routes (`ROUT`; the first is ridden by `--world` alone) and as route files (`freiburg-schauinsland.route`, `titisee-feldberg.route`). `world-builder route` takes `--bbox` / `--origin` like `package`, so a route file is in the package's metres with its road heights (the context profiles of the part).
- **Check:** 0.003 % of the road samples lie under the terrain (8,818 of 333 million, worst 4.7 m on a track at the western border of the box), below the 0.1 % of the pilot test; land use 55 % forest, 20 % meadow, 10 % farmland, 5 % residential; 306,476 buildings.

**The whole Black Forest in three packages (decided 2026-11-13, v2.36).** The southern package gets two neighbours to the north, so that free ride runs from Freiburg to Baden-Baden; all three are built from the same day's Geofabrik extracts of both Regierungsbezirke, Freiburg and Karlsruhe (`--pbf` and `--poly` twice: Ortenau with Sasbachwalden and the Mummelsee lies in Freiburg, Baden-Baden, Bühl and Freudenstadt in Karlsruhe), with the LGL DGM1 terrain (4.3), the projection origin 47.92 N 7.96 E of the south and cut with `--bbox` on two shared border lines:

| Package (id `europe/germany/…`) | Box | Area | Tiles | Edges | Buildings | Package | Build | Builder RSS | Under terrain | Client alone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `black-forest` (south, rebuilt) | 47.72–48.12 N, 7.62–8.30 E | 2,260 km² | 2,800 | 141,244 | 306,478 | 259.9 MB | 206 s | 7.6 GB | 0.002 % | 2.02 GB |
| `black-forest-middle`: Elzach, Triberg, Hornberg, Wolfach, Schramberg, Offenburg's east | 48.12–48.45 N, 7.70–8.40 E | 1,900 km² | 2,337 | 104,359 | 238,882 | 213.9 MB | 178 s | 7.0 GB | 0.001 % | 1.78 GB |
| `black-forest-north`: Baden-Baden, Schwarzwaldhochstraße (B500), Mummelsee, Hornisgrinde, Sasbachwalden, Allerheiligen, Ruhestein, Bühlerhöhe, Kniebis, Achern, Bühl, Freudenstadt | 48.45–48.80 N, 7.85–8.45 E | 1,720 km² | 2,200 | 96,973 | 219,529 | 194.4 MB | 151 s | 6.5 GB | 0.001 % | 1.74 GB |

- **Cut lines from the measurements:** a package of about 2,300 km² is the most the client holds within 15 (it decodes the whole home package; 2.0 GB for the south at 2560 × 1440, 1.76 GB at 1280 × 720), so the region north of the south package (Elz valley to Baden-Baden, 75 km) needs two more: the line **48.12 N** (the south's border, Waldkirch / Kandel south of it, Elzach north) and **48.45 N** (between Hausach / Wolfach and Oppenau / Kniebis), which leaves the Schwarzwaldhochstraße with all its places (Kniebis 48.47 N to Baden-Baden 48.76 N) in one package. West and east edges follow the Rhine plain (the Rhine is the state border; France is not in the extracts) and the Kinzig / Murg uplands; 163 roads cross 48.12 N, 155 cross 48.45 N.
- **Riding them as one world:** the neighbour search follows joined neighbours (2.2.2), so any of the three loads the other two (as skeletons). Measured client peak (free ride, release build, software rendering at 2560 × 1440, 4 bots): south with both neighbours 2.62 GB, north with both 2.50 GB, middle with both 3.45 GB (its neighbours' tiles come near on both sides) – above the 2 GB budget of 15 for the middle; loading tiles of the home package on demand (streaming from the file, 3.5 / 4.5) is the fix, not smaller packages. Joining needed 80 s at first (the edge at each boundary vertex was looked up by a scan per vertex pair); with a one-pass index the start takes 25 s like a single package.
- **Projection:** one origin keeps the tile grids and metres identical across the seams (no frame needed), at the price of the local projection's scale error far from the origin: x is about 1.4 % long at the Mummelsee (cos 48.6° / cos 47.92°). The same error appears in any joined world ridden from the south; own origins per package would only help a package ridden alone.
- **Routes** (package routes and route files): `Baden-Baden - Mummelsee` (27.3 km, 914 m climbing: Lichtentaler Straße – Geroldsau – Malschbach – Schwarzwaldhochstraße via Hundseck and Unterstmatt to the lake, 1,032 m), `Sasbachwalden - Mummelsee` (12.3 km, 780 m: Brandmatt), `Bühl - Bühlerhöhe` (9.3 km, 446 m: Bühlertal), `Hornberg - Triberg` (middle, 11.0 km, 352 m: B33 / Gutach valley); the south's routes on DGM1: `Freiburg - Schauinsland` 19.9 km, 995 m, `Titisee - Feldberg` 12.7 km, 449 m.
- **Releases** (`scripts/prepare-world-release.sh`, nothing uploaded): per package `ocw-world-<file>-v<N>.zip` (package, manifest, route files, `LICENSE-DATA.md` with every source's attribution from the manifest, `README.md`) and per region `<region>-osm-source.zip` (the extracts and `.poly` files with `SOURCES.md`: the ODbL offer of the road graphs).
- **Showcase:** scenes `showcase-*` in `scripts/scenes.toml` (Mummelsee, Hornisgrinde, Schwarzwaldhochstraße, Baden-Baden, Sasbachwalden, Feldberg, Titisee, Schauinsland, Freiburg, Schluchsee, Belchen, and the before/after viewpoints Malbun, Schauinsland, Feldberg pass); reference photos to compare with in `docs/reference/black-forest.md` (Phase 8D).

**Fourth world: Tenerife (decided 2026-11-13, v2.42).** The first island and the first region outside Central Europe: `europe/spain/tenerife`, file `tenerife.ocwpkg`, the **whole island in one package**.

- **Sources:** the Geofabrik extract of the Canary Islands (`africa/canary-islands`: Geofabrik files the islands under Africa, there is no `europe/spain/canarias`; 60 MB, 2026-11-12) with its `.poly`, the IGN MDT05 (4.3) and the SRTM tiles N28W017 and N27W017 (the sea beyond the DTM); `scripts/fetch-pilot.sh tenerife` downloads them into `data/tenerife/` with `SOURCES.md`, `scripts/build-tenerife.sh` builds the package and the routes.
- **Builder options:** `--tiles-near-roads` (or `--land-tiles`) and `--no-clean` combine freely; the sea's frame is the region's box plus 5 km, the sea is kept out of the bridge water test (one area over the whole region) and passed to the land use beside the other areas.
- **Extent:** the box 27.98–28.61 N, 16.94–16.10 W around the island (the other islands lie outside it), projection origin 28.29 N 16.52 W, time zone `Atlantic/Canary` (WET / WEST, from the origin: the region table of `ocw_sky::zone` has the Canary Islands now; spec 14 Phase 9I). Islands are built with **`--land-tiles`** (v2.56, see *Tile cover* below): the tiles within the margin (2 km) of a tile with a road plus every tile with land, not the whole box of the roads, which was 64 % open sea. Until v2.55 it was `--tiles-near-roads` alone, which left out the Teide's summit (3.3 km from the nearest road, the cable car's base station) and Pico Viejo: the mountain was missing.
- **One package or two, from the measurements** (marge, release build; client = `ocw-desktop` free ride in Las Cañadas, software Vulkan at 2560 × 1440, 4 bots, as for the Black Forest):

| Build | Tiles | Edges | Buildings | Package | Build | Builder RSS | Under terrain | Client peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whole box (first build) | 5,460 | 69,103 | 116,479 | 577 MB | 68 s | 3.2 GB | 0.005 % | – |
| Tiles near roads, before the world cleaning (4.8) | 2,690 | 69,103 | 116,479 | 239 MB | 66 s | 1.8 GB | 0.005 %, worst 0.6 m | 1.42 GB (1.35 GB at 1280 × 720) |
| Tiles near roads, with the world cleaning (v2.42–2.55) | 2,690 | 69,103 | 116,479 | 238 MB | 80 s | 2.3 GB | 291 samples (0.000 %), worst 0.36 m | – (same tiles) |
| **Tiles near roads and on land, with the world cleaning (chosen, v2.56)** | 2,744 | 69,103 | 116,479 | 244 MB | 87 s | 2.3 GB | 291 samples (0.000 %), worst 0.36 m | – |

  About 2,034 km² of land with 9,088 km of roads give a package the size of the southern Black Forest, within the disk target and the client's memory budget of 15, so the island stays **one package**: every signature climb (Teide from the north and from the south, Masca, Anaga) is in it and a cut through the Teide would only add a seam. The 3,700 m of relief cost nothing extra (the same 10 m grid).
- **Lint** (`world-builder lint --pbf`, with cleaning, 4.8.1): 9,038 km of roads (+ 36 km bridges: 516 tagged, 15 from outlines, 4 over water, 179 over gaps); floating untagged roads 0.8–1.5 m 2.4 %, 1.5–3 m 1.0 %, 3–6 m 0.3 %, > 6 m 0.04 %; 1,629 samples over the class grade limit (8.1 km, mostly paths), 43 kinks, 1 step, 1 near-miss end; 0.64 % of the road samples over untagged water (coastal roads where the OSM coastline runs on or beside them, and the irrigation ponds), 7,401 water level steps and 132 river steps (the barrancos: steep dry riverbeds the river rule levels downhill), 27,585 half-buried buildings on the steep slopes. The water cleaning levels 5,467 lakes and 2 river chains and keeps the sea at 0 m (a river mouth does not lift it).
- **Routes** (package routes and route files; gradients from the road profiles, with cleaning): `Puerto de la Cruz - Teide` (42.0 km, 2,349 m climbing: Puerto de la Cruz at the sea – La Orotava – TF-21 via Aguamansa and El Portillo – the cable car base station at 2,356 m; steepest 20 % on a short stretch of the Carretera de las Medianías above La Orotava, a shortcut the router takes off the TF-21), `Los Cristianos - Teide` (48.6 km, 2,509 m: Arona – TF-51 Vilaflor – TF-21 Boca de Tauce – Parador – cable car; steepest 14 %), `Masca - Santiago del Teide` (5.1 km, 426 m: the TF-436 hairpins to the Cherfe pass; steepest 15 %), `Buenavista - Masca - Santiago del Teide` (21.9 km, 1,230 m: the whole TF-436), `La Laguna - Anaga` (10.9 km, 449 m: Las Mercedes – TF-12 through the laurel forest – Cruz del Carmen – the TF-114 junction below the Pico del Inglés; steepest 8 %). The road and terrain cleaning in progress (bridges, steep spikes) may change these numbers.
- **Land use** (existing classes, no new ones): the lava fields and the Teide's slopes are `natural=bare_rock` / `scree` → rock / scree, the retama scrub of Las Cañadas and the coastal tabaibal `natural=scrub` → scrub, the Canary pine forest and the laurel forest of Anaga `natural=wood` / `landuse=forest` → forest, banana plantations (`landuse=orchard`, `trees=banana_plants`, 3,007 areas) → orchard, greenhouses (`landuse=greenhouse_horticulture`, 3,088) → farmland, terraces `landuse=farmland`, vineyards, the black-sand beaches `natural=beach` / `sand` → bare, the ports (`landuse=port` / `harbour`) → industrial; 15,659 small `natural=water` and 7,136 `landuse=reservoir` are the irrigation ponds (water). Shares: default 28 %, sea 26 %, forest 18 %, scrub 14 %, rock 3 %, residential 3 %, farmland 3 %, orchard 2 %. Missing for Phase 8 (the materials work of another branch, nothing added here): lava rock (black / red-brown, blocky), volcanic ash and pumice (the ochre caldera floor), black sand, Canary pines (long needles, open forest) and laurel forest as their own tree types, banana terraces and net houses, flat-roofed whitewashed houses.
- **Tile cover (v2.56, bug 2026-11-13 "the Teide's summit is missing").** Which 1 km tiles a package has (`ocw_worldgen::package::TileCover`): `Box` (default, inland regions) – the box of all roads plus `--margin-tiles` (2); `NearRoads` (`--tiles-near-roads`) – only tiles within the margin of a tile with a road; **`NearRoadsAndLand` (`--land-tiles`, islands)** – `NearRoads` plus every tile of the box that has **land**: its natural ground (the DEM, before the roads shape it) rises above 1 m at any point of a 21 × 21 test grid (50 m), so islets count and the open sea (0 m in MDT05 and SRTM) does not. Mountains far from roads – the Teide, Pico Viejo, the ridges of Teno and Anaga – are then in the package as terrain-only tiles. They keep the package's one grid (the format has one `samples` per package; a coarser grid for terrain-only tiles would need a format change and saves little, they are few); the far terrain (4.5) draws them at distance. Tenerife: 2,690 → 2,744 tiles (+54: the summit area of the Teide and Pico Viejo and the inner Las Cañadas, the rest of the land was already within 2 km of a road), 238.5 → 244.3 MB, build 89 → 87 s (2.3 GB builder RSS, unchanged). `world-builder check --peak LAT,LON,M` fails unless the highest terrain within 150 m of the point is within 50 m of M; `build-tenerife.sh` checks the Teide (28.2724 N, 16.6424 W, 3,715 m): terrain 3,712 m at x −11,980 z 1,920 (missing before: no tile). Unit tests (`ocw-worldgen`): a cone far from two coast roads is in the package with its summit height and the sea tiles are not (`land_cover_keeps_a_mountain_far_from_roads_and_drops_the_sea`), the land test sees a 60 m islet.
