**Built (J3, 2026-11-22; with Q6 (d)).** `ocw_world::junction` (the renderer, the server and the prediction) and `ocw_worldgen::junctions` (the world builder):

- **Side roads with too little room (Q6 (d)).** At a through road (Q1) a side road's own surface now starts where its centre line leaves the main road's carriageway – its **edge point**, at the main road's edge (3.75 m out from a 7.5 m road at a right angle, 7.5 m at 30°, against the 10 – 14 m of J2's mouths at narrow angles) – at the main road's surface there; from there it goes on at **its own grade** (a crease at the main road's edge, no longer the main road's slope along it). Its mouth row (where its strip begins, still at the farther corner tangent point: the corner arcs need the room) lies at its own height and grade, without a blend beyond. Between the main road's edge and the mouth **the corner slopes**: the patch's height field is the main road's own surface on its carriageway (exactly as in J2: the main road's carriageway is unchanged) and beyond its edges an inverse-square blend of the main road's surface (by the distance from its carriageway) and each side road's own surface in its corner (by the distance from its centre line there or from its mouth row): C1 at the main road's edge and at the mouths; it slopes over the fillets and beside the side road from the one to the other. In the world builder the side road's profile gets the blend from the edge point (`L = clamp(|Δh| / 0.01, 5 m, 30 m)` from the main road's surface there, starting at its own grade, up to one sample before the next junction's fixed stretch – its edge point, for a side road with a corner there too); the grade re-limiting of J2b keeps the samples on the main road's carriageway and the edge point fixed, the corner and everything beyond free, the edge point a crease (no curvature limit carried on from it, no kink rounded there), so a side road's missed height is spread from the main road's edge. A side arm whose mouth lies at the main road's edge (no room for a corner) keeps J2's blend; in a cluster a side road leaving from a vertex off the main road's carriageway follows its own profile from there. The patch mesh has two more rings 0.4 and 1 m inside its outline (the corners curve there; the mesh meets the strips with their slope).
- **Clusters (dual carriageways, offset T junctions, small roundabouts).** Junction vertices (three or more roads) joined by edges of at most 12 m on the ground (`CLUSTER_EDGE_M`) that do not both get a patch alone, or whose patches alone nearly meet on that edge (their mouths together cover 85 % of it), are one cluster (at most 6 vertices, 8 arms): one patch round their centroid, its arms the other edges of all of them (mouths measured from their own vertex), the short edges inside it (no strip; their own profile is a node of the height field along their centre lines, a through road's of its class part of its carriageway). Between two arms of different vertices (two carriageways side by side, a roundabout's entries) the outline runs round the centroid from mouth to mouth (outside the edges inside); the rest is a patch's (corner arcs, mouths, Q6 corners). Every member vertex has the cluster's patch; it is drawn, measured and stored once, at its first member. A small roundabout (its ring split at the entries into arcs of at most 12 m) becomes one patch – its island paved (a hole in the patch is open, see below).
- **Forks below 15°**: corners down to 4° (`MIN_CORNER_DEG`); the arms of a corner below 15° (`FORK_DEG`) may have their mouths up to 40 m out (`FORK_MAX_MOUTH_M`, at most 45 % of the edge), where their carriageways separate.
- **Mini-roundabouts:** the nodes OSM tags `highway=mini_roundabout` matched to the junction vertex within 3 m (`ocw_worldgen::mini_roundabouts`; `world-builder junctions --pbf EXTRACT`), section `JMRB` (4.7); the renderer paints a white disc on the junction surface (an overlay at the patch's drawn heights, `road.wesl`'s crossing kind 3 with half code 3: radius 0.3 × the narrowest road there, 1 – 2 m).
- **Tried and left out:** (1) outlines that are not star-shaped from the vertex (arms that curve within the junction: their mouth row lies off the straight edge line the corner follows) made star-shaped by dropping the outline points that turn back – Liechtenstein got 655 more junction surfaces, but 460 more kinks and 124 more seams (poor surfaces where the arms curve); those junctions keep the overlapping strips. (2) A blended patch's arm extensions only up to the vertex (no grade carried through the junction onto the other arms): slightly more kinks (Black Forest north 6,164 → 6,441 inside blended patches).
- **Section `JNCT` layout 2** (4.7: clusters, the drawn surface changed), **`JMRB`**; **lint** `road.vertical.kink.{crease, junction, other}` (4.8.1).

Tests (11.4): `ocw_world::junction` – the T junction's side road leaves the main road's edge (3.75 m) at its own grade, its mouth row at its own height, the corner rising steadily (`a_t_junction_keeps_the_main_road_and_the_side_road_starts_at_its_edge`); a side road at 30° off a 10 % road falling at 15 %: its edge point 7.5 m out at the main road's surface, the mouth row at its own height, the main road's carriageway its own plane, the corner falling steadily between the two (`a_narrow_side_road_leaves_at_the_main_road_edge_at_its_own_grade`); a dual carriageway T as one cluster patch (both vertices, the edge across inside it, no strip, its own profile; the other strips end at the mouths: `junctions_a_few_metres_apart_share_one_patch`); a small roundabout as one patch (`a_small_roundabout_is_one_patch`); a 10° fork with mouths beyond 25 m, a 3° fork without (`forks_get_a_patch_unless_too_narrow`); the stored rules (layout 2, clusters, members) the computed ones to the bit. `ocw_worldgen` – `narrow_side_roads_leave_steep_roads_at_their_edge` (the J2b `junction_room` case: a 33 m track off a 12 % road at 30°: within 25 %, the main roads unchanged, the drawn surface, lint clean), `clusters_are_one_junction_surface` (counted, reconciled and measured once), the T junctions' side roads at their own grade from the edge, `mini_roundabouts::nodes_mark_the_junction_vertex_next_to_them`. `ocw-render` – `mini_roundabouts_get_a_painted_disc` (the overlay at the patch's drawn heights, its radius); `wheel_contact::tyres_touch_the_junction_surfaces` now holds the path to the drawn surface within 4 mm (3 mm before: the corners curve, the path's points lie 0.5 m apart) and, on the T junction as the world builder shapes it, the tyres of a rider 1.6 m beside the centre turning in within 12 mm (5 mm before: the crease where the side road leaves the main road's edge at its own grade lies under the wheelbase; 11 mm; on a side road the builder has not shaped, climbing from the vertex, 25 mm, printed only); the terrain lowered at load beside a side road's corner on an older package.

What the numbers say: **Q6 (d) does what it was chosen for** – `junction_room` falls by 57 – 71 %, `junction` by 56 – 68 %, the steps by 58 – 87 % (Liechtenstein 53 → 7), and the seams by 14 – 49 %: the side roads too short for their blend (`short_side_road`, 75 – 1,592 per package) are gone, because a side road no longer climbs from the main road's surface at its mouth. What is left of `junction_room` is where even leaving the main road's edge at its own grade cannot reach the next fixed height within the limit (Liechtenstein's worst: Valünastrasse's track at a bridge end, 81 %). **Kinks do not fall back to the live packages' level:** the live packages' profiles did not follow the drawn junction surfaces (J1 drew them on top, riders rode them all the same), so their lint did not see the junctions' kinks; since J2 it does. Of the J3 kinks 27 – 57 % are the **creases** Q6 (d) asks for – a side road leaving the main road's edge at its own grade, the main road's slope along it differing by more than 8 points (`kink.crease`) –, most of the rest lie inside **blended junction surfaces** (no clear through road: equal crossings, Y junctions and forks of tracks, Q1: an arm's grade changes within the patch where the other arms climb or fall differently; Black Forest north 6,164 of 9,142 in a Q6-only build), and the new fork surfaces add some (Liechtenstein's 65 forks: +144 kinks between builds with and without them). Q7 asks how to go on. **Overlaps** grow by 10 – 83 (clusters and forks: arms that curve over their neighbour inside a longer patch). The fixed point of the reconciliation holds less tightly in the Black Forest (371 – 483 samples more than 1 cm off the drawn surface, at most 0.19 m; J2b 14 – 36) – where a cluster's or a fork's long patch meets a side road's corner.

Scenes `junction-*` before (the J2b packages, main's build – the deployed 04ffd3f) and after (the J3 packages, this branch), on Wayland and X11: `test-output/junctions-j3/` (index.md); new scenes `junction-bf-narrow-*` (Black Forest north, the J2b `junction_room` case of a track 88 % steep between junction surfaces), `junction-fork-*`, `junction-dual-*` (a dual carriageway cluster) and `junction-mini-*` (a mini-roundabout's disc), Liechtenstein.

**Built (J4 / Q7, 2026-11-23; Q7 (d), the light terrain smoothing of v5.52, the first part of the Rule on the sides).** The user on the Q6 / crease pictures: "the crease fix of making the road longer and more equal is good. make sure the side road does not stick out of the main road. better smoothen the whole terrain a bit without losing too much precision." `ocw_worldgen::junctions`, `ocw_world::junction` (the renderer, the server and the prediction), `ocw_worldgen::terrain_smooth`, `ocw-render::junction_mesh` / `road_mesh`:

- **Creases rounded (Q7 (b)).** A side road with its corner (Q6 (d)) still leaves the main road's carriageway at its edge point, but now with the main road's slope along it there (its own surface's, outward), turning to its own grade (its mean over the next 10 m) along a parabola of `crease_curve_m` = |change of grade| / 1.5 % per metre, 5 – 10 m (`round_creases`, in the re-limiting of J2b, always at a side road with a corner). The height the curve leaves behind is spread over the road beyond, fading in and out smoothly over at least three times the curve (at most 1.5 times its mean extra grade): the road gets there "longer and more equal". **Never steeper:** where that would make the stretch up to the next fixed height (another junction, a bridge) steeper than its class grade or than it already was, the curve shortens to 5 m, and where even that would, the crease of Q6 (d) stays – so `junction_room` never grows (a follow-up of the first J4 build, which let it grow by up to 46 %). A change of grade up to 15 points leaves no kink in 5 m stretches, larger ones half. With a fixed point within the curve a cubic Hermite curve to it, under the same rule. The drawn corner follows the profile as in J3.
- **Never above the main road.** (1) The patch's triangles near the through road's carriageway edge are halved twice where they cross it (`refine_at_main_edge`: the edge of a cluster's carriageways, a union of strips, bends inside a triangle) and then cut at it (`cut_at_main_edge`: the crossing of each triangle side a shared vertex at the field's height, the main road's surface) – before, the star mesh's triangles across the edge carried a corner's slope onto the main road (0.2 – 0.4 m at steep side roads and clusters; 319 junctions in Liechtenstein as main drew the J3 package). The drawn height is looked up by the mesh's sectors (`Patch::sectors`). (2) A side road's mouth row corner on the main road's carriageway lies on the main road's surface (paths drawn along a main road). (3) A side road's strip rows within 1 m of the main road's carriageway, on the patch or beside its arms up to 40 m past their mouths (their edges' centre lines, so also where the main road curves; `Patch::main_road_height`), lie 3 cm under the main road's surface, whole rows; wherever a strip comes that near, it gets a row every 0.5 m. Lint `junction.mouth.above_main` (4.8.1).
- **Blended junctions on one plane (Q7 (c)).** At a junction without a through road (Q1; not clusters) the world builder fits a plane to its roads (least squares over each road's own profile at its mouth and 5 m on, the gradient at most the steepest class grade) and lays every road's profile from the vertex to the first sample past its mouth on it; from there each road turns to its own height and grade along a cubic Hermite curve of 10 – 20 m (`blended_planes`, first round of the reconciliation). A junction where one road would get steeper than its class grade or than it was keeps the surface of J3 (no `junction_room` gained). The patch's field takes it: each arm's extension carries the cross slope of the plane through the arms' mouths (`Arm::cross`, `blend_plane`, at most 12 %), flat across at its mouth and fading in over a quarter of the mouth's distance – so arms on one plane make that plane.
- **Light terrain smoothing** off the roads (4.8.3 *Terrain smoothing*, `world-builder smooth-terrain`, `package`).
- **The sides at a junction's corner (Rule, first part):** the verge round a corner (the patch outline's shoulder) keeps the narrow width of the arms' junction zones along the whole corner, and an arm's strip that meets a junction surface narrows its verge to that width at the mouth and widens it again over 6 m (`SIDE_FADE_M`, the mouth's along coordinate passed to `road_mesh` as a negative `junction_m`): the verge band meets its neighbour without the step and the hole the user found at Letzanaweg ("do you see that little hole on the right side?"), and follows the corner as one even band. Lint `side.gap`, `side.step`, `side.kink`, `side.corner` (4.8.1, `junctions::side_faults`): the outline chains between the mouths and the arms' strip edges, measured as drawn.
- `world-builder junctions` prints the planes; `scripts/j4-build.sh` builds the set: `condition` (RCND) → `junctions` (Q7, mini-roundabouts) → `smooth-terrain` → `street-lamps` (the OSM lamps of `data/lamps-build`), lint of the new package and of the J3 one; `scripts/j4-lint.sh` lints again, `scripts/j4-shots.sh` the pictures.

Tests (11.4): `ocw_worldgen` – `creases_are_rounded_into_a_vertical_curve`, `round_creases_shapes_the_curve_and_keeps_its_ends`, `creases_never_make_a_short_road_steeper` (a 22 m side road at 18 % to a fixed height: never steeper than the limit or before), `side_roads_stay_below_the_main_road_surface` (T junctions up and down, at 90°, 30° and 45°, a dual carriageway cluster), `a_path_along_a_curving_main_road_stays_below_it`, `a_cluster_vertex_beside_the_main_road_does_not_lift_it`, `blended_junctions_lie_on_one_plane`, `smoothing_keeps_the_roads_and_its_bounds`, `smoothing_keeps_water_and_building_sites`, `the_kernel_keeps_quadratic_surfaces`; the J2b / J3 tests adapted; `ocw_world` – `side_roads_never_stand_above_the_main_road`; `ocw-render` – `the_corner_verge_meets_the_arms_verge_without_a_hole` (the ground under the roads: the verge's outer edge 0.4 m out on the patch and on the strip at every mouth corner, every patch shoulder vertex there one of the strip's).

(The J3 packages linted again with this lint: their junction surfaces drawn with J4's mesh, so their seams and `above_main` here are those of J4's renderer; their profiles are J3's, so the kinks, steps and grades are those of *Built (J3)*.)

What the numbers say: **kinks fall by 33 – 44 %** – the creases by 52 – 64 %, the kinks near junctions by 22 – 36 % (the blended junctions on their plane; most of the rest in forks, whose arms run side by side over 25 – 40 m, and clusters, which keep their J3 surface) – the **steps by 17 – 57 %**, and **`junction_room` falls in every package (9 – 33 %)**: a crease is rounded only where the road has the room, so the curves give up some of the kinks the first build removed (it had 36 – 48 % fewer kinks, but 13 – 46 % more `junction_room` in three packages). **A side road above the main road** is gone in Liechtenstein; 1 – 4 junctions per package remain elsewhere, 2 – 12 cm above (a strip whose quads reach onto a curving main road beyond 1 m of its rows; one junction surface in Tenerife at a cluster). The **terrain** moves by 0.8 – 1.9 cm on average, at most 0.5 m. **The sides (Rule):** the gap at Letzanaweg's corner is closed (the corner verges as wide as the arms' at the mouths; `side.gap` 0 – 1); `side.step`, `side.kink` and `side.corner` measure the outline chains as the junction surfaces have them since J1 – a corner's outline jumping to a side road's mouth row at its own height a fraction of a metre from the main road's mouth (Liechtenstein's worst 0.72 m, a path's mouth 0.85 m from a primary road's), corner bands rising at up to 90 points where a track's corner climbs between two roads, outline chains folding back on themselves at arms that curve – the Rule's work list, not yet at 0.

Pictures (Wayland on marge, the same build for all three packages – so the live and J3 packages are drawn with J4's mesh here; the pictures of main's renderer are those of the Q6 / crease investigation): `test-output/j4-q7/` (index.md): the charts of the three examples (A Letzanaweg / Bergstrasse, Triesen; B Waldistrasse / Amiseschaweg fork; C Rofenbergstrasse, Schaan) with live / J3 / J4, their shots, Letzanaweg's corner before / after the verge fix, and the terrain before (J3) / after (J4) at a forest edge and a meadow in low sun.

**Built (J5 / the Rule, 2026-11-23; v5.61).** The user's picture at Letzanaweg leaving Bergstrasse (Triesen): the side road's verge started with a square-cut end above the corner's surface and the main road's verge dropped like a wall to the grass. `ocw_world::junction` (`sides`, the renderer, the server and the prediction), `ocw_worldgen::junctions` (the lint), `ocw-render::junction_mesh` / `road_mesh`:

- **In plan: the sides follow the real edge lines.** Between two mouths the outline runs along each road's edge line – the offset of its curving centre line, a mitre on the inner side of a bend and a round join on the outer – from each mouth corner inward and turns from the one into the other along a curve tangent to both (a cubic Bézier of a circular arc's handles, the corner radius of Q4; each tangent length as far as its arm leaves room, so a corner squeezed on one side reaches farther along the other), its bends sampled every 8° at most; where the edge lines do not meet, a smooth join (the outer side of a bend round the vertex, a width change as one taper along the narrower road over 4 × the change, two roads of a cluster round the centre). Every outline leaves its mouth corners square to the mouth row, as the strip's edge goes on (where the mouth lies on a bend of the centre line a curve from the corner into the edge line coming in), and the remaining bends above 8° are rounded over up to 2 m. Before (J1 – J4) the corners ran along the straight first 8 m of each arm and met mouths on curving or bending arms at an angle or folded back over them. A chain that would not keep the outline star-shaped (the mesh is a star from the vertex) keeps J4's straight-line chain, smoothed at its ends where that stays star-shaped; a junction whose J4 outline is not star-shaped keeps its overlapping strips as before (the J5 outline would give 460 more junctions a surface in Liechtenstein, but with 59 more seams and 199 more road kinks – J3's finding again).
- **In height: the sides lean with the road and are smoothed along the outline.** A side road with a corner (Q6 (d)) leans at its mouth with the main road's slope across it at its edge point, an arm of a blended junction with the plane through all its arms (Q7 (c); before, the plane was faded out to flat over a quarter of the mouth's distance inside the patch) – at most 20 % (`MAX_WARP`), the mouth row's corners at the arm's height ± the cross slope times the half width; its strip turns flat over `sqrt(150 × rise)` m past the mouth (3 – 20 m, within the room before the next junction; the strip's edge bends by at most 4 points per metre; `JunctionSet::lean_at`, rows every metre, both ends of a short road summed): the corner between a steep main road and a side road no longer twists by the main road's grade times the side road's half width within a few metres. Along each chain between two mouths the outline's heights follow a cubic curve (C1 with the field's slope along the chain) between fixed points – the mouth corners, the points on the through road's carriageway (the main road keeps its surface) and, where the curve would leave the field by more than 15 cm, the farthest point until it does not (`side_lift`): the field's S-shaped blends between two roads' surfaces become even slopes; the drawn surface follows the lift inward over 1.5 m (`Patch::surface`), never on the main road's carriageway.
- **The verges.** The verge round a corner is as wide as the ground's drop asks, as the arms' verges are at their mouths (J4 kept it at its narrowest, 0.4 m: a wall where the ground lies low), at most 0.8 of the corner's radius where the corner turns towards it (its outer edge would fold) and smoothed along the corner, its two ends as they are – so it ends on the arm's verge's outer point; the arms' strips no longer narrow their verges at the mouth (J4's 6 m fade). A strip keeps no point of its own within 1 m past a mouth and no row whose corner lies behind the row before it (rows square to two pieces of a bent centre line crossed: the strip's edge and verge folded back over the mouth).
- **The lint** (`side.*`, 4.8.1) measures the sides against the drawn surface's slope (a side turning on a sloping surface changes its grade by the turn alone), the joint of the outline with its arm's strip edge too, and bends over pieces of at least 0.3 m however finely a curve is cut – the J4 packages linted again with it below.
- `scripts/j5-build.sh` builds the set as `j4-build.sh` (condition → junctions → smooth-terrain → street-lamps, lint of the J5 and the J4 package); `scripts/j5-shots.sh` with `scripts/j5-views.txt` the pictures (the J4 packages shot with J4's build, the J5 ones with this one); `examples/side_pick` picks corners with a fault of the sides per kind of junction, `examples/side_dump` dumps a package's sides with their faults (JSON lines) for looking at the causes.

Tests (11.4; the first four fail on the J4 code): `ocw_worldgen` – `junction_sides_follow_a_bending_side_road` (a side road bending 20° / −15° at its mouth: J4 `side.corner` 1), `junction_sides_stay_smooth_beside_a_steep_main_road` (15 % and 12 % main roads at 90° and 60°: J4 a kink), `a_narrowing_road_tapers_smoothly` (7.5 m to 4 m at a 20° way split: J4 a corner); `ocw-render` – `the_corner_verge_meets_the_arms_verge_without_a_hole` (the corner's verge ends on the arm's verge's outer point and is as wide as the drop asks: J4 0.4 m); the J1 – J4 tests adapted to the leaning mouth rows and the lifted surface (`check_mouths`, the side road's corner, the tyres beside the centre 13 mm, limit 15 mm).

What the numbers say: **the corners in plan halve** (−49 to −54 %), **the kinks of the sides fall by 7 – 10 %**, the steps stay at a few dozen per package (15 – 74, of tens of thousands of junctions), no new gap; the seams and overlaps fall a little (2 – 7 %), the road profiles keep J4's gains (kinks +1 – 2 %, Tenerife +6 %: the leaning mouths change the drawn surface beside the creases; steps and grades within 2 %). **The Rule is not at 0** – the remainder, by cause (from `examples/side_dump` on Liechtenstein, typical of the others): (1) **corners squeezed by short arms** – a corner whose edge lines cross less than a metre from a mouth capped at 45 % of a short road between two junctions: its curve has a radius under 0.7 m (a third of the corner faults); rounding it would need the strip beyond the mouth to bend, or the two junctions joined into one surface (J3's clusters, today only for roads up to 12 m whose surfaces would meet); (2) **chains J5 cannot draw star-shaped** – arms that curve strongly within the junction, forks, clusters' round-the-centre chains: they keep J4's straight-line chain (about half the corner faults; a mesh that is not a star from the vertex, or J3's non-star junctions given a surface, is the work list); (3) **kinks of steep junctions** – two roads leaving at grades 20 – 35 % points apart within a corner of 3 – 4 m (a path at 35 % beside a track at 24 %): no curve that short can turn the grade within 8 points per metre; the lift keeps within 15 cm of the field, so they stay; (4) **side roads above the main road** – the 1 – 4 per package of J4 (2 – 12 cm, strips over a main road bending away beyond 1 m of the rows), untouched; (5) **steps** at paths drawn along a main road (their strip rows lie 3 cm under the main road's surface, their mouth row at their own height: lowering the mouth row moved the step into the corner, so it was left). At Letzanaweg the square-cut end and the wall are gone; the verge's toe line still has a V where the side road's verge meets the corner's (close-up).

**Built (J6 / the Rule, 2026-11-24; v5.65).** The user's spot at Letzanaweg after J5: the corner rounded, no wall – but the verge's outer edge with a V where Letzanaweg's verge met the corner's. `ocw-render::road_mesh` (the verges), `ocw_world::junction` (`plane_mesh`, the never-above rules, the outlines' choice), `ocw_worldgen` (tests, `examples/above_probe`, `side_dump`):

- **The V at Letzanaweg: the verges' outer edges run on smoothly.** Its cause (plan view, `junction_verges_dump` + `scripts/verge-plot.py`): Letzanaweg's strip bends right just past its mouth; its verge, 3 m wide there (the ground drops away), went out along the strip's rows – square to the centre line before the bend, askew to the edge after it – and on the inner side of the bend its outer points zig-zagged back over the corner's verge; the corner's verge itself was cut to 0.8 of a small corner's radius in its middle (J5), a notch where a corner is tight. Now (1) a strip's verge goes out square to its edge line (the end rows keep the row's direction: the corner's verge and the next tile's strip go on from them) and widens by at most 0.3 m per metre (`VERGE_WIDEN`; where the ground asks for more it slopes steeper for a few metres); (2) the outer edge of every verge – a junction corner's and a strip's – is its own curve (`corner_outer`): the widths smoothed along it, the offset line's loops cut out where the edge turns tighter than the verge is wide, the stretches that still bend more than a curve of 1.5 m would over 0.3 m replaced by a cubic tangent to the line on both sides (reaching farther along it until it bends little enough), its ends kept where the arms' verges end and leaving them along the arms' edges, never nearer the edge than 0.4 m; (3) where two arms' verges cross beyond short mouths (a verge wider than the corner leaves room for) the corner's verge runs straight from the one's outer end to the other's, under them. At Letzanaweg the outer edge is one smooth curve from Bergstrasse's verge into Letzanaweg's.
- **A side road never above the main road** (`junction.mouth.above_main` 0 in all five packages; the user's requirement). The 1 – 4 per package were side roads starting on the main road and running along it (a service road climbing beside a secondary road, paths and tracks, a residential road leaving at 28° where the main road curves towards it): their mouth row leaned from the main road's surface up to their own height across the main road's edge, their strip past the mouth was already put under the main road, and between the two the strip's triangles rose 2 – 13 cm above it. Now a side road whose mouth has a corner on the main road and stands above it there – on its straight carriageway as the patch draws it, or on its real, curving one (the centre line's offsets), and within 1 m where the side road leaves at under 35° (`ALONG_DEG`) – starts on the main road: it is blended onto the main road's surface as a side road whose mouth lies at the main road's edge (J2: the mouth row on the main road's surface, the strip turning to its own profile over 5 – 30 m past it, the patch's surface there the main road's; lowering only the mouth row, tried first, left steps of up to 1.1 m to the patch's surface – `side.step` +15 in Tenerife); and the strip's triangles between two rows are sampled over the main road's real carriageway and the rows go down until they lie 3 cm under it (the mouth row stays, the row after it goes down by its share; at most 0.5 m a round).
- **Outlines that are not star-shaped; each corner the chain that bends least.** A corner's chain along the real edge lines (J5) may be taken wherever the outline stays a simple polygon – no longer only where it stays star-shaped from the vertex – and of a corner's chains (J5's sides, J4's line smoothed, J4's line) it takes the one that bends least as the side lint measures it (the strips' edges on at both ends; J5's sides first within a degree); where pieces of the outline would cross, the corners involved take their next. Such a patch is meshed by a constrained Delaunay triangulation (`spade`, pure Rust, wasm-clean) of the outline with inner points – two rows 0.4 m and 1 m inside each outline point and a grid 2.5 m apart – at the surface's heights (the field with the sides' lift, the lift from the outline's nearest piece), cut at the through road's carriageway edge as the star mesh, its triangles looked up by 1 m cells (`junction/plane_mesh.rs`, `Patch::is_star`). Clusters keep J5's star-shaped choice (their chains round the centre between two carriageways left seams of 6 cm with the strips beside a median when drawn otherwise). The junctions J1 – J5 leave without a surface (their J4 outline not star-shaped) keep their overlapping strips (J3's and J5's finding: more seams and kinks when given one).
- **Steep junctions: a gentler corner was tried and dropped.** A corner radius long enough to turn the side's grade by at most 6 (3) points per metre (a path at 30 % off a level road: 1.5 m → 3.2 (6.4) m, the mouths moved out with it) lowered the kink only from 41 to 18 points: the mouth moves up the slope with the larger corner, and the side's height follows the patch's field, level on the main road and climbing near the mouth (`side_lift` keeps within 15 cm of it). Left as it was.

What the numbers say: **the user's requirement holds – no side road above the main road** in any package (4 / 1 / 3 / 3 → 0), and **the V at Letzanaweg is gone** (the verges are not in the lint: plan views and pictures). **The corners in plan fall by 17 – 22 %** (515 → 428 in Liechtenstein, 6,995 → 5,615 in the Black Forest south), **the kinks of the sides by 2 – 4 %**, the steps stay at a dozen to 75 per package (−1 to +7: corners now taking J4's line where it bends less), no new gap (the Black Forest north's one stays); **the seams fall by 3 – 7 %, the overlaps by 2 – 5 %**, the road profiles stay within 1 – 3 % (kinks −1 % in Tenerife, +3 % in Liechtenstein: 6 more, at junctions whose outline changed; steps and grades within 2 %). **The Rule is still not at 0** – the remainder by cause (`examples/side_dump` and the J6 classification on Liechtenstein, the others alike), each with a plan view in `test-output/j6-sides/`: (1) **clusters** – 183 of Liechtenstein's 428 `side.corner` (166 at a joint), 50 of its 261 `side.kink`, 8 of its 14 `side.step`: mostly paths and cycleways drawn along both roads of a crossing and joined to it into one surface, the outline between a path's mouth and the road's turning back by 130 – 140° (`case-cluster9.png`); their outlines keep J5's star-shaped choice (drawn otherwise they left seams of 6 cm beside a median) – they need the path drawn as part of its road's side, not as a road of its own; (2) **corners squeezed by short arms** – 152 corners, 97 kinks, 3 steps (`case-short57.png`, `case-short100.png`: town centres with edges of 10 – 20 m between junctions, their mouths at 45 % of the edge, no room for a radius): merging junctions closer than two corner radii makes them clusters (cause 1's outlines), so it was not done; bending the strip past the mouth was not tried; (3) **steep junctions** – 73 kinks (`case-steep720.png`): the corner's side follows the patch's field, level on the main road and climbing near the mouth; a larger corner moves the mouth up the slope (tried: 41 → 18 points at a 30 % path, not below 8 – dropped); (4) **forks and island tips** – 93 corners, 41 kinks where two roads leave side by side and the tip between them has no room for a radius (`case-other291.png`); (5) **steps** at paths along a main road – 14 (Liechtenstein) and 32 (Tenerife), mostly clusters. One view got worse: the Black Forest path view's cycleway (`bf-path-*`, `plan-bfpath-*`) – its corner's J5 chain bends less by the lint's measure than J5's smoothed J4 line, but turns at the cycleway's mouth where J5's line ran round.

**Built (J7 / the Rule, 2026-11-24; v5.67).** J6 left the Rule not at 0 – most of it at crossings whose sidewalks OSM draws as ways of their own along both streets – and one view worse: the Black Forest path view's cycleway, whose corner verge ended in a sharp tip where J5's was round. `ocw_world::junction` (`alongside`, `sides`, the clusters; the renderer, the server and the prediction), `ocw-render::junction_mesh` / `road_mesh`, `ocw_worldgen::junctions` (the reconciliation, the lint):

- **The Black Forest path view: a corner cut short turns round again.** The cycleway leaves Güterstraße at 57° and turns north 1.3 m before its mouth, beside the street's short arm (12.7 m to the next junction): both tangents of the corner's arc are cut short, and the edge line coming in already bends there, so the curve drawn with the uncut circle's handles turned 158° at once – a hook at the cycleway's mouth corner (`side.corner` 58°), its verge a sharp tip (J5's outline had run round over the cycleway's first metres). Now, where a corner's arc bends more than 20° over 0.3 m pieces (as the lint measures, the strips' edges on at both ends), its tangent lengths and handles are searched – Bézier curves of several handles and a biarc (two circular arcs, an even bend where one cubic cannot follow a U-turn) – for the one that bends least while staying off both carriageways: the island between the cycleway and the street ends in a round nose (27° over 0.3 m pieces – 1.6 m wide, it has room for no rounder one), its verge round it (`zoom-bfpath-j7.png`, `bf-path-j7.jpg`).
- **Cause (1): paths along a road are drawn as a band of its side.** A path or cycleway whose every point – its first and last 5 m left out, where it turns to its crossing – lies within 3 m of a road's edge (or over it by up to 0.5 m), alongside it within 20° and at its level (within 0.5 m) is a side path (`junction::alongside`; from the graph's geometry alone, so the world builder, the renderer, the server and the prediction agree – the package has no OSM tags per edge; OSM `footway=sidewalk` / `cycleway=track` ways are such paths). It stays in the road graph – routable and rideable as before – but takes no part in the junctions: no mouth of its own, no arm of a patch; a vertex where it crosses a street beside a junction stays a member of that junction's cluster (the street's arm goes on from it). The renderer draws no strip for it: the road's sidewalk reaches the path's far edge there (its own kerb, or 8 cm), and round the junction's corner the corner's sidewalk runs from the one street's band to the other's – one band (`case-cluster9-j7.jpg`). The world builder puts its profile at the band's height (the road's beside it, the kerb, the sidewalk's fall) and its ends on the junction surfaces they lie on (blended over 5 – 30 m), so a rider on it rides on the band and comes off it onto the street without a step (J6 profiles lay 11 cm under the band at the median in Liechtenstein, from −30 to +10 cm at the 10th / 90th percentile). The seam and overlap lint leaves such paths out (not drawn as carriageways). Liechtenstein: 205 of its 898 paths.
- **Clusters: corners between arms of different members.** Where a cluster's arm leaves from another member than its neighbour's (a street through the cluster's short inner edge to the main road – typically where a sidewalk way crossed it), their edge lines meet behind the one arm, straight on through the cluster: that corner is now drawn as at one vertex – a rounded corner of the corner radius, the mouths moved out for it – instead of J3 – J6's curve round the centroid that met the main road's mouth at 85° (`case-cluster9`: 134° → none). Where that outline cannot be made each member keeps its own rule (tried: falling back to J6's cluster outline left 57 more `side.corner` in Liechtenstein).
- **Section `JNCT` layout 3**: a layout 2 section has the side paths' mouths, so it is ignored (the junctions computed as without a section, J3's rule).
- **Cause (2), corners squeezed by short arms – tried and dropped:** most such arms end at a plain way split (OSM ways split at a bridge or a tag change), so an arm whose edge ends at one (two edges of the same width, bending less than the mitre limit, no patch there) was allowed 85 % of its edge for its mouth instead of 45 %: Liechtenstein `side.corner` +6, `side.kink` +6, road kinks +17 (longer side-road blends cut short) – left out. Bending the strip past the mouth would need the next edge's strip trimmed with it (an arm over two edges); not done.

Liechtenstein's junction surfaces 3,925 → 3,901 (the paths' own junctions gone, clusters that cannot take J7's corners split into their members' rules), the other packages gain about 330 – 510. **The Rule is still not at 0.** What remains in Liechtenstein by cause (`examples/side_dump`, `scripts/side-classify.py`; the others alike): (1) **clusters** – 60 corners, 18 kinks, 1 step (J6: 183 / 50 / 8): 27 corners where a path that is not along a road (a crossing footpath, a path leaving at an angle) is still an arm, 33 in clusters without paths (dual carriageways, offset T junctions); (2) **corners squeezed by short arms** – 166 corners, 120 kinks, 3 steps (J6: 152 / 97 / 3; some of cause (1)'s now count here – a junction no longer a cluster has its short arms): mostly arms ending at a way split 3 – 15 m away; the larger mouth share was tried and dropped (see above); (3) **steep junctions** – the kinks of 'other' (90) and part of (2); (4) **forks and island tips** – 7 corners, 13 kinks, 3 steps where a path leaves its road at a narrow angle, and the 58 'other' corners (island tips of forks, roundabout entries). The side paths' profiles lie on their bands (Liechtenstein, 2,582 samples: the 10th – 90th percentile within 1 cm; J6: −30 to +10 cm, median −11 cm).

**Built (J8 / the Rule, 2026-11-24; v5.78).** J7 left the Rule not at 0 in four causes (Liechtenstein: corners squeezed by short arms 166 corners / 120 kinks, steep junctions ~90 kinks, clusters 60 corners, island tips and roundabout entries 58 corners); the user chose (2026-11-24) to improve the junctions first, in order of count. `ocw_world::junction` (the renderer, the server and the prediction), `ocw_worldgen::junctions` (the reconciliation):

- **Cause (2): an arm runs on past a plain way split.** Where an arm's edge ends at a plain way split (OSM splits a way at a bridge, a tag change: one other edge goes on, of the same class and width, bending at most 20°, no side path, bridge, tunnel or region border there) less than 15 m from the junction, and the junction's patch alone squeezes that arm (its mouth at its share of the edge, 45 %, or no patch at all), the split is no junction for drawing: the arm runs on past it – the short edge lies inside the patch (no strip of its own, the patch's surface all along, as an edge inside a J3 cluster), the arm is the edge beyond, its mouth on it where the corners need it (`JunctionSet::runs_on`, `Patch::run_on`). The corners' edge lines follow the real centre line through the split (`Arm::lead`). A split between two junctions that both want it stays as it is (it belongs to neither); a junction in a cluster keeps its rule. The road graph and the routing are unchanged; the world builder puts the short edge's profile on the patch's surface (up to the split, where the edge beyond keeps its mouth's profile), blended junctions their plane over it. Liechtenstein: 36 more junctions with a surface (2,867 → 2,903; "a straight way split" without a surface 443 → 413, "an acute corner beyond the mouth limits" 459 → 424).
- **Cause (2): mouths out for their corners' radius along the real edge lines.** The corner arcs place the mouths by straight lines from the vertex to a point 8 m out (J1); where an arm curves near the junction (or runs on past a split) its real edge line meets the other road's elsewhere and J5 – J7's corner was cut short at the mouth (a hook). Now each mouth moves out by what its corner's tangent lacks along the real edge lines (`sides::corner_deficit`, up to three rounds, within the arm's share of the edge) – on arms at most 6 % steep at their mouth: on steeper ones the mouth farther out left their blend less room (tried on all arms: Tenerife's road kinks 2,892 → 3,095, +7 %, 300 of the new ones at plain patches). A junction's patch alone, from which the clusters and the way splits run on past are decided, keeps J7's mouths (with the new ones a few clusters grew past what can be made and two Tenerife junctions lost their surface), and where the patch with its mouths moved out cannot be made, or its sides would bend more than before (as the lint measures them), it is drawn as before – so is a junction whose arms would run on past a split (with them the Black Forest path view's island got a sharper nose than J7's round one).
- **Section `JNCT` layout 4**: the patches of junctions whose arms run on past way splits are stored as a cluster patch (kind 2) with the junction first, then the splits, and the list of those splits (the patch's centre is the junction's vertex); a layout 3 section has J7's squeezed mouths and is ignored.
- **Tried and dropped – an arm reaching past its share where the far end leaves room:** an arm squeezed by an edge whose other end's junction (alone) takes little of it (or has no surface: a bridge, a dead end) was allowed its mouth up to 1 m (3 m) before that junction's reach, the far junction kept at its mouth alone: Liechtenstein `side.corner` 266 → 252, `side.kink` 236 → 229, 38 more surfaces – but road kinks 247 → 258 (J7: 240, +7.5 %: the side roads' blends cut short and the new surfaces' roads; with 3 m: corners 268, road kinks 259); left out (road kinks were to stay within a few % of J7's).
- **Not done – causes (3), (4) and (1):** spreading a steep junction's grade change over the corner and the first metres of both arms' side bands (a side band's own vertical curve – each strip edge past the mouth would need its own height offset, fading out), round island noses where a fork's island is narrower than 1.4 m (a nose that narrow bends more than 25° over 0.3 m pieces whatever its shape: its mouths would have to move out where the arms leave no room), roundabout entry flares tangent to the ring (the strip past the mouth widened along the corner's circle: needs room past the mouth the far end's junction takes on short ring arcs) and the crossing footpaths / dual carriageways of the clusters were not built in this stage (counts below).

What the numbers say: **`side.corner` falls by another 5 – 9 %** (291 → 266 in Liechtenstein, 4,351 → 4,064 in the Black Forest south), `side.kink` stays within −2 to +1 %, `side.step` within ±3, no new gap, no side road above the main road, no lamp in a road; **no junction loses its surface** and 141 – 1,840 more vertices per package lie under one (the way splits run on past, junctions J7 left without one: Liechtenstein's surfaces 2,867 → 2,903); the road profiles nearly as before – kinks +1 to +3 % (240 → 242 … 7,730 → 7,886), steps −1 to +17, grades over the limit +0.3 to +2 % (Liechtenstein 35 → 37), seams −10 to +1 %, overlaps ±3. **The Rule is still not at 0.** What remains in Liechtenstein by cause (`scripts/side-classify.py` on `examples/side_dump`, J7 → J8; the others alike): (2) **corners squeezed by short arms** – 166 → 147 corners, 120 → 117 kinks, 3 steps: now mostly short arms between two junctions that both need the edge (or ending at a bridge, a class or width change), where neither running on nor a longer share has room – a cluster or a strip widened past the mouth along the corner's circle would be next; (3) **steep junctions** – the 89 kinks of 'other' (not built in this stage: the grade change spread over the corner and the first metres of both arms' side bands); (1) **clusters** – 60 corners, 18 kinks, 1 step, unchanged (27 at crossing footpaths that are not along a road, 33 dual carriageways / offset T junctions; not built); (4) **forks, island tips and roundabout entries** – 7 corners, 13 kinks, 3 steps at paths leaving at a narrow angle and 58 → 52 'other' corners (not built: a nose narrower than 1.4 m bends more than 25° over 0.3 m pieces whatever its shape, and a roundabout's entry flare needs room past the mouth that its short ring arcs do not leave).

**Built (J9 / the Rule, 2026-11-25; v5.91).** J8 left in Liechtenstein: (2) corners squeezed by short arms 147 corners / 117 kinks, (4) island tips and roundabout entries 52 corners, (1) clusters 60 corners, (3) steep junctions ~89 kinks, (4b) paths at a narrow angle 7 corners / 13 kinks. The round had a time box of about 5 hours before a release; it took the short arms first (by count), measured each step on Liechtenstein (`scripts/j9-iter.sh`: the road condition once, then this checkout's junctions, the lint and the findings by cause) and left the rest analysed. `ocw_world::junction` (the renderer, the server and the prediction):

- **Cause (2): two junctions on a short edge share one patch.** Where the two junctions' patches alone meet on the short edge between them (J3's cluster rule: an edge of at most 12 m whose mouths cover 85 % of it) but no star-shaped outline holds both, J3 – J8 gave each its own patch, both arms on the edge squeezed to their share (45 %). Liechtenstein had 62 corner findings at such junctions (`examples/side_dump` now writes why a cluster was not made). Now the cluster takes a simple outline (as a junction's own patch since J6, meshed by `plane_mesh`) – where its sides bend no more than the lint allows (25°) or than the members' own patches, and all its arms are at most 6 % steep at their mouths (the plane over both members kinks steeper roads: without that limit Liechtenstein's road kinks rose 242 → 267, +10 %; without the bend limit `side.corner` rose 266 → 323). Liechtenstein: `side.corner` 266 → 255, road kinks 242 → 244.
- **Cause (2): an arm takes the room its edge's far end leaves.** An arm whose edge ends at a vertex without a junction surface – a bridge or tunnel, a dead end, the region border, a way split drawn as a mitre (not one an arm runs on past) – was held at its share of the edge like any other. Now its mouth may lie out to 1 m before what that end takes (a mitre's shift + 0.3 m, else nothing; `JunctionSet::far_room`), the J8 rounds moving it out where the corners need it – on arms at most 6 % steep there, and only where the junction's sides then bend less than with the mouths at their shares (no new surfaces). J8 tried a longer share towards far *junctions* (+7.5 % road kinks) and dropped it; towards ends without a surface and on flat arms the road kinks stay as they were. Liechtenstein: `side.corner` 255 → 232, `side.kink` 237 → 229, seams 96 → 89, road kinks 244 → 242 (with a margin of 0.5 m the same; up to 9 % steep: 231 corners but road kinks 246).
- **A painted crossing stays where OSM has it.** A crossing inside a junction surface is drawn at its mouth (the renderer moves it there), so a shared patch or a longer mouth moved some zebras away from their OSM place (Liechtenstein: a zebra on a side street 8.4 m out was drawn 4.5 m farther out at the shared patch's mouth; the first J9 packages swallowed 8 – 35 more crossings per package than J8's). The world builder now reads the painted crossings of the package's strips onto the edges (`junctions::keep_crossings`) and every junction set it bakes knows them (`JunctionSet::with_crossings`): a shared patch and an arm taking the room its far end leaves are used only where they swallow no more crossings than the junctions' own patches. Liechtenstein: crossings swallowed 320 (J8) → 328 (J9 without it) → 321, `side.corner` 232 → 234. `examples/crossing_near` counts the crossings junction surfaces swallow and lists those near a point.
- **Section `JNCT` layout 5** (a layout 4 section has the members' own patches and the mouths at their shares and is ignored).
- **Analysed, not built – what remains** (Liechtenstein after J9, `scripts/side-short.py`, `side-other.py`, `side-kinks.py` on `examples/side_dump`): *steep junctions* – of the 229 `side.kink`, 135 lie where a corner's band meets an arm's strip edge, 82 of them at an arm whose cross slope (its mouth leaning with the main road, J5) turns flat in the few metres its edge leaves before the next junction: the strip's edge climbs 10 – 20 % in its first metre while the band arrives at the main road's grade (Liechtenstein vertex 26: an 18 m side street, its cross slope of 13.8 % turned flat over ~2.5 m); spreading that over the corner needs the strip's warp, which depends on the far end's patch, known when the band's heights are made – a band lifted towards the strip's grade over its last metres, computed after both ends' patches, is the next step. Others are forks whose two branches part in height across a narrow island (vertex 1303: two tracks 1.1 m apart in height over a 1.7 m nose – 67 %), which no smoothing of the band can hide. *Dual carriageways* – 45 corners lie between two carriageways of a cluster leaving side by side (a median): the chain goes round the cluster's centre from mouth to mouth; a U-turn round the median's nose (a biarc leaving the one mouth inward along its arm, reaching the other outward) would bend under 25° wherever the median is at least 1.4 m wide – tried where it bends less than the way round the centre: Liechtenstein `side.corner` 232 → 229 only and road kinks 242 → 244 (most of those clusters keep their star-shaped outline, which such a U-turn would leave), dropped for now; with the clusters' outlines free (J9's first step) for these too, it is the next try. *Island noses under 1.4 m* (9 corners) and *roundabout entries* need the island's outline or the strip past the mouth moved (the renderer's strips), not built. *Short arms between two junctions* that both need the edge and are not one cluster (29 corners: edges of 12 – 20 m, or mouths that do not meet) – a longer share towards a far junction was J8's dropped try.

**Open after J3:**
- **Outlines not star-shaped** (636 – 9,321 per package, the largest group without a surface): arms that curve within the junction. Dropping the outline points that turn back gave them a surface, but a poor one (Liechtenstein: +655 surfaces, +460 kinks, +124 seams), so it was left out; they need outlines that follow the curving arms (the mouth rows on the edges' own lines, not the 8 m chords).
- **Acute corners beyond the mouth limits** (465 – 4,203): mostly short arms (< 8 m) ending at a way split or a dead end, not at another junction (no cluster), or clusters that cannot be made (more than 6 vertices, 8 arms).
- **Roundabouts:** small rings become one patch with the island paved (a hole in the patch: open); rings with arcs longer than 12 m keep a T patch per entry and the J1 rules at their split vertices.
- **Kinks** (Q7: built with J4, see above) and the **overlaps** of clusters and forks.
- The renderer's analysis test `junction_seams` was not rerun on the J3 packages; the lint measures the same surfaces.

**Open questions:**

- **Q1 – Who keeps the height at a junction: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): as proposed** – where there is a clear through road, the **main road keeps its own surface**, and the side roads adapt to it over 5–30 m, as real roads are built. A blended surface only at equal crossings, forks and multi-way junctions (no hump or dip on the main road at steep side roads).
- **Q2 – The main road's centre line through a junction: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): per world, from real images** – the user: "look at real images and extract the variants. add this workflow to the world builder spec. junctions might look different at different places in the world, so for each world look at the local data." The lines through a junction are no single global rule: each world takes them from its region's real junctions, with the workflow of 4.8.9. The former proposal (the main road's centre line **continues** across the junction, the edge lines break at the side roads' mouths, the side roads' lines end at the mouth) stays the fallback for a world without its table yet.
- **Q3 – Give-way lines without OSM tags: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): as proposed** – give-way and stop lines **only where OSM tags them** (`highway=stop|give_way`, as now); no line is invented on untagged side roads.
- **Q4 – Kerb radii of the corners: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): per world, from real images** – the user: "Not all roads have kerbs, e.g. outside of cities there are no curbs. Look at images." Whether a junction corner has a kerb at all, and its radius, come from the region's images with the workflow of 4.8.9 (by road class and setting: town or open country). Without a kerb the carriageway edge is still rounded, as the verge or shoulder. The former proposal's radii by the smaller road's class (8 m primary / secondary / trunk, 6 m tertiary / unclassified / residential, 3 m service / track, 1.5 m cycleway / path) stay the fallback for a world without its table, with kerbs only where the road already has them (towns, T5).
- **Q5 – Package rebuild for J2: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): as proposed** – all packages (Liechtenstein, the three Black Forest packages, Tenerife) are rebuilt and deployed once J2 is checked; until then J1 runs on the current packages.
- **Q6 – Side roads with too little room between the main road's surface and the next junction: decided (2026-11-22, the user): (d), built with J3 (v5.36, *Built (J3)*)** – the side road's mouth goes to the main road's edge at narrow angles and its blend starts at its own grade; where it is still too steep, the corner between the two roads slopes from the main road's edge to the side road (the main road's carriageway stays as it is). Was asked: since J2 a side road's first metres lie on the main road's surface, flat across it (Q1: the main road keeps its surface). Where the side road leaves a steep main road at a narrow angle its mouth is 10 – 14 m from the junction's centre, and the main road's surface there lies up to 3 – 4 m above or below where the side road would be. When the side road's next junction (or a bridge) is only 20 – 35 m away, no profile in between can stay within its class gradient: in the Black Forest north a 33 m track has to fall 8.5 m over 10 m (88 %) between its two junction surfaces; in the packages built with J2b 101 (Liechtenstein) to 6,402 (Black Forest south) 5 m intervals are steeper than their class limit for this reason (`grade_over_limit.junction_room`), shown as short walls and steps of the road. A smaller case: a side road leaving with the main road's slope in the opposite direction keeps a short stretch steeper than its limit inside the blend (8 – 496 intervals per package). Options: (a) leave it (the walls stay until J3 looks at clusters of junctions); (b) at such junctions no road keeps its surface: the junction is blended between all its roads (the main road gets a small hump or dip, as at equal crossings); (c) the side road's mouth is put at the main road's edge instead of further out at narrow angles, so it leaves the main road's surface sooner, and the blend starts at the side road's own grade instead of the main road's slope along it; (d) as (c), and where it is still too steep the corner between the two roads slopes from the main road's edge to the side road (the main road's carriageway stays as it is). Proposal: d, built with J3.
- **Q7 – Kinks at junctions after J3: decided (2026-11-23, the user): (d), built with J4 (v5.56, *Built (J4 / Q7)*)** – the creases are rounded (the side road leaves the main road's edge with the main road's slope along it and turns to its own grade over 5 – 10 m) and never stand above the main road's surface; the blended junctions get the smoother surface of (c); plus a light smoothing of the terrain off the roads (see the v5.52 row). The question was: since J2 the road profiles follow the drawn junction surfaces, so the lint counts the kinks riders feel at junctions – a change of grade of more than 8 points between two 5 m stretches: 344 (Liechtenstein) to 12,667 (Black Forest south) per package after J3, against 6 – 43 in the live packages, whose profiles did not follow the junction surfaces riders already rode on them. Two causes make up nearly all of them. (1) **Creases** where a side road leaves the main road's edge at its own grade (Q6 (d)): 131 – 3,686 per package – for example a side road climbing at 15 % off a main road whose slope along it is 0 %: the rider feels the change of 15 points at the main road's edge, as at a real driveway. (2) **Inside blended junctions** (no clear through road – equal crossings, Y junctions and forks of tracks, Q1): a road's grade changes within the 10 – 30 m of the junction surface where the other roads climb or fall differently – most of the 207 – 9,129 kinks per package near a junction (in the Black Forest the larger share: tracks meeting tracks). Options: (a) leave them: they are the shape of the junctions, and the lint lists them by cause (`kink.crease`, `kink.junction`); (b) round the creases into short vertical curves: the side road leaves the main road's edge with the main road's slope along it and turns to its own grade over 5 – 10 m – fewer kinks, but a little of what Q6 (d) gained on `junction_room` is lost; (c) a smoother surface for blended junctions: the change of grade spread over the whole junction surface and 10 – 20 m of each road (the junction surfaces change shape, the packages are rebuilt); (d) both (b) and (c). Proposal: c – keep the creases, which Q6 (d) chose, and smooth the blended junctions.


#### 4.8.9 Junction variants per region (decided 2026-11-16, 4.8.8 Q2)

How a junction is marked differs from place to place: whether the main road's centre line runs through, how the edge lines meet the side roads' mouths, what the side road's lines do, how give-way and stop lines look, and whether a junction is painted at all (narrow rural roads often are not). The world builder therefore takes these from **each world's own region**, not from one global rule. The workflow, for every world before its junction markings are built (4.8.8 J1d / J2) and for every new world:

1. **Sample:** list the world's junctions by kind (T, crossing, fork, roundabout, way split) and by the road classes that meet, and pick a sample of each kind spread over the area (about 10 per kind and class pair where the world has them). A world-builder command lists them with their coordinates (to be built with J1d).
2. **Look at real images** of each sampled junction, **openly licensed only** (4.6): the orthophotos the world already uses (Orthophoto Liechtenstein / SWISSIMAGE, LGL DOP20, PNOA – at 10–20 cm per pixel the markings are visible) and, where useful, openly licensed street-level photos (for example Mapillary, CC BY-SA 4.0, with attribution). Never Google, Bing, Esri or Mapbox imagery.
3. **Extract the variants** per region and junction kind, each with its share in the sample: the main road's centre line (continues, dashed, breaks, absent), the edge lines at the mouths (continue, dashed, break), the side road's lines (end at the mouth, stop line, none), the form of give-way and stop lines where OSM tags them (4.8.8 Q3), pedestrian crossings at the junction, and whether it is painted at all. The corners too (4.8.8 Q4): **whether there is a kerb at all** (often none outside towns) and the corner radius of the kerb or of the plain carriageway edge, by road class and setting (town, village, open country).
4. **Record** them as a table per region in this section (like the vegetation tables of 4.6.1), with a reference board of orthophoto crops and their attribution in `docs/reference/`. The world builder reads the table as the region's junction rules, next to its other regional look data (house styles, material sets).
5. **Check** each world with the `junction-*` scenes (4.8.8), side by side with the orthophoto crops of the same junctions.

OSM tags win over the table where they exist (`highway=give_way|stop`, `crossing=*`, lane markings). A world without a table yet gets the fallback of 4.8.8 Q2.

**Tables:** none yet – Liechtenstein, the Black Forest (south, middle, north) and Tenerife are the first to be sampled.

## 5. Bicycle Physics and Training Simulation

### 5.1 Physics Module

Bicycle physics is a standalone Rust crate, `ocw-sim`, with no Bevy dependency. It contains physics, rider state, drafting and session logic, and is used by the client (prediction), the server (authority) and offline mode (6.1).

**Inputs:** power in watts, cadence, rider weight, bicycle weight (from the physics profile, 2.5), gradient, speed, wind, rolling resistance, air resistance, drafting position.

**Outputs:** speed, acceleration, position, energy expenditure, resistance, riding state.

Fundamental resistive forces:

- Gravitational force.
- Rolling resistance.
- Aerodynamic drag.
- Inertial (acceleration) resistance.

**Low speed and steep ramps (decided):** the drive force is P/v. Below 1 m/s it is taken at the speed at the end of the tick (implicit in that term, `m·(v₁ − v₀)/dt = P/v₁ − R`, one positive root): finite from standstill, stable however slow, and its fixed point is the exact steady speed P = R·v. So a rider with positive power never stays at 0 km/h: on a ramp too steep for the power they crawl at that steady speed (33 % at 200 W and 83 kg: ~2.6 km/h) instead of stalling; speed is never negative (no rolling back; at 0 W the rider stops). The rider's measured power is evidence that the cranks turn, so the bike moves (a real rider would get off and walk at a few km/h – the crawl stands in for it). With the brake key held, the drive force is taken as if riding at 1 m/s (the old floor), so the brake still holds a moderately pedalling rider at standstill. Server and client prediction share the function (`ocw-sim::physics::step`).

### 5.2 Simulation Model

- **Riders move in 1D along their path:** state = `distance_along_route: f64`, `lateral_offset: f32`, `speed: f64`. The 3D position is derived from the road geometry only for rendering. This makes the physics cheap, robust and easy to synchronize.
- In free ride the path is an **edge list that is extended on the fly** by each junction decision (2.2.1). The lateral offset is blended across junctions so the avatar follows a smooth curve, not the raw graph corner.
- **Free-ride path (v1.6):** a list of steps – (part of) an edge with its riding direction, or a U-turn loop (2.2.2). It is extended automatically where the road just continues (up to 2 km ahead), with a U-turn at dead ends and at the region border, and at the **lock point** (20 m before the next junction) with the chosen exit. Corners at junctions are rounded (a curve starting at most 10 m before the junction, so it is never under the rider at the lock point); the height along the curve follows the road by arc length, never bunched into the apex: in a window of up to 20 m of road before and after the curve, the path position maps linearly onto the road position (2t + 2X metres of road onto L + 2X of path) and takes the road's height there. The curve is shorter than the road it replaces but climbs as much; spread over the window, a hairpin on a 10 % road is ~12 % (the curve alone would be ~2×). The geometry is a pure function of the step list, so the server, the client's prediction and the client's copy of other riders' paths agree; steps more than 600 m behind the rider are dropped, step indices keep counting. Route files and test loops keep their fixed route; physics and rendering use either through the same interface (`Track`).
- **Routes on the graph** use the same path: it may follow a route plan, which decides the steps the free ride would otherwise take by default (2.2.1 route rides). Whether each step is on the route is a function of the steps, so the path stays the one source of truth for server and clients.
- Riders on different paths are compared where their paths share a road in the same direction (drafting, 5.2).
- **Sharp turns** and U-turns: the slow-down is a speed limit along the path – 15 km/h through turns sharper than 120°, 10 km/h through the U-turn loop – reached with ~2 m/s² before it. Junction turns sharper than 60° are taken with at most 4.5 m/s² sideways in the rounded corner (~22 km/h), so nobody turns off a descent at 60 km/h.
- **Fixed timestep:** physics at **50 Hz** (20 ms) on client and server, independent of frame rate.
- **No strict bit-level determinism:** `f64` is used. The client predicts, receives authoritative state, and corrects small errors by smoothing (blending over ~0.5 s); it snaps only above a threshold (e.g. > 5 m). This avoids the cost of fixed-point math.
- **Drafting** (reduced CdA behind other riders) is computed server-side because it depends on other riders. The client predicts it from the interpolated positions of nearby riders.
- **Sharp turns** (> 120°): an automatic short slow-down is applied (the rider can't brake on a trainer), so the avatar does not take a hairpin at 40 km/h.

#### 5.2.1 Lateral Steering and Surfaces

- Besides `lateral_offset`, a rider has a **heading relative to the road** and rides a curve of its own; the road's curves turn the road under the rider. Lateral offset changes with `v · sin(heading)`; the distance along the road with `v · cos(heading)`. The avatar leans by `atan(v² κ / g)` for the curvature κ it rides.
- **Autodrive** (default; bots always): an autopilot leans the rider to hold a line (the middle of the road, or where the rider moved it), through the road's curves. **Manual:** the rider leans (keys ramp the lean and it stays; held through upright, the opposite key pauses there for ~0.3 s, then leans on to the other side; a gamepad stick sets it), κ = g·tan(lean)/v²; the road's bends have to be steered, or the rider drifts to the edge. Near the largest angle to the road (~17°, wild ~70°) the turn fades out, so the rider settles at it smoothly.
- **Road edge:** the rider stops at the edge (0.6 m inside); while still steering (or carried by a bend) into it, the rider scrapes along it with an extra deceleration. Rolling straight along the edge or steering away from it does not scrape. **Wild mode:** no edge; the rider may leave the road (up to 60 m either side, at up to ~70° to it) and rides on the terrain. Switching wild mode on also switches autodrive off (upright, manual lean steering; one steering intent carries both), since autodrive would hold the rider on its line on the road; switching it off keeps the steering mode (autodrive can be switched on again at any time). Within the band the gradients are still the road's; in a free ride a wild rider who reaches the band's edge rides on into the terrain in free 2D (14 Phase 13, 13A, v5.53), as after a unicorn landing away from a road.
- **Surfaces:** asphalt, gravel (OSM tracks and paths; the `surface` tag later), grass (anything beside the road). Each has a factor on the rolling resistance coefficient (1, 2.5, 6), applied in the physics and sent to the trainer in SIM mode (Crr), so gravel and meadows are harder to ride. The bike's physics profile (2.5) scales the part above asphalt: factor = 1 + (surface factor − 1) × off-road share, so a gravel bike (0.5) rolls on gravel at 1.75 × its asphalt Crr and a mountain bike (0.3) at 1.45 ×; asphalt stays 1 for every bike. The world package has no per-edge surface yet (only the road class: tracks and paths are gravel); the OSM `surface` tag (paved / unpaved / compacted / …) in the road graph comes later and feeds the same three surfaces.
- Steering is an intent like the junction choice (6.1): the server applies it, the client predicts it with the same rule; heading and ridden curvature are part of the rider state in snapshots.
- **U-turns** (2.2.2): slow-down to ~10 km/h, turn, continue in the opposite direction.
- **Touch steering** (planned v3.78, built v4.23, 3.2.3): the left / right half of a touch screen is the ← / → key held (line steering in autodrive, lean in manual); a tap is one step (0.5 m line, 0.1 rad lean).

Training data is stored independently of rendering.

### 5.3 Trainer Control

Trainer control translates the virtual road into resistance for compatible smart trainers via the FTMS control point:

- *Set Indoor Bike Simulation Parameters* (grade, wind speed, Crr, Cw) for **SIM mode**.
- *Set Target Power* for **ERG mode** (workouts, 2.8).
- *Set Target Resistance Level* as a fallback.
- *Spin-down calibration* where supported.

**Grade sent to the trainer:**

- **Trainer difficulty** slider from 0–100 %, default 50 %, which scales the grade.
- Separate downhill handling (e.g. negative grades capped or scaled further).
- Rate limit (e.g. at most 1 %/s change) and a short look-ahead to avoid jolts.
- Updates sent at 1–2 Hz; most trainers do not handle faster updates well.

**ERG mode:** smoothing, and a "catch-up" on sudden cadence drops.

**ERG and SIM during a workout (decided):** while a workout runs it owns the trainer mode. Steps with a target put the trainer into ERG with that target (ramps update continuously; the ERG controller ramps steps at 50 W/s, updates at most 1 Hz and eases off on low cadence); *free* steps return to the mode from before the workout (normally SIM, the road's gradient); when the workout ends or is stopped, that mode is restored and the workout no longer touches the trainer. Manual `trainer.mode` / `erg.target` commands during a workout are overridden by its next update. Without a controllable trainer the targets are shown as guidance only. The virtual trainer acts as an ideal ERG trainer: it reports the target while its set power is above 0.

## 6. Real-Time Multiplayer Architecture

### 6.1 Roles: Client, Remote Server, Local Server

| Role | What it is | Where it runs | Physics responsibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Client** | The desktop app (`apps/desktop`): rendering, sensors, UI, audio | The user's PC | Runs `ocw-sim` for its **own rider only** as a *prediction*, so the bike reacts instantly to pedaling |
| **Remote server** | Our game server (`services/server`) | Our Linux hosts (Docker) | Runs `ocw-sim` for **all riders in a session**; its result is the truth (positions, drafting, race results) |
| **Local server** | The same server logic, linked into the desktop app | Inside the client process | Single-player / offline rides: it is the authority, no network involved |

The application uses a **server-authoritative** model. There is only one code path: single-player runs the same server logic in-process, and the desktop app talks to it through the protocol from Phase 1.

The trainer and sensors are always connected to the client only. The server never talks to hardware; it receives the measured values from the client.

**The client transmits** only inputs: timestamped power, cadence and heart-rate samples with sequence numbers, device information, steering inputs (6.5) and riding state requests.

**The server computes:** rider state, position, speed, drafting, race state, rankings, group membership and events. It then distributes updated states to the participants.

**End of a route (decided):** on a route that is not a loop (route files, routes that end) riders stop at its end: the distance stays at the route's length and the speed at 0 (`ocw-sim::ride::stop_at_finish`, used by the server's physics and the client's prediction alike), so HUD, avatar, gradient and profile stay consistent. Before, the distance ran on past the end (the HUD counted on to 18 km of a 14 km route while the avatar, GPS position and gradient stayed at the last point and the profile was empty). The dev command `teleport KM` likewise moves a rider past the end to the end, and before the start to the start, and its reply says so (`teleported to 14.023 km, the end of the route …`); on a loop any distance is taken (that many laps on). Regression tests: `teleport_and_riding_stop_at_the_end_of_a_route` (`ocw-sim`), `teleport_past_the_end_of_a_route_goes_to_its_end` (`ocw-server`).

**Start point and test riders (v1.9):** a session starts all riders together at a configured distance (`ServerConfig::start_m`); the desktop app picks a random point by default (on a route that ends, at least 1 km before the end; off for screenshot and capture runs, which must be reproducible). Riders start in a formation: rows of up to three across the lane, 1.2 m apart and always 0.3 m inside the lateral limit (fewer per row on narrow roads), rows 3 m apart behind the start point; the front row's centre is kept for the client rider (bots fill the other places in order, so the formation is deterministic). The formation never starts before the road begins: on a route it is moved forward until its last row is at 0 m, in free ride every rider's path starts at their place on the start edge (moved forward if the edge behind is too short). Server-side test riders (bots, 10 by default) ride at twelve different strengths (85–280 W, easy and strong interleaved) so a field spreads out, each on its own bike and kit (the bike types in turn, colours from the palette, never the local rider's pink – also the bots a local event brings, which used to be the default pink rider on the standard road bike), push harder uphill (at least the power for 10 km/h on the current gradient, so easy bots do not crawl) and steer with autodrive.

### 6.2 Network Protocol

- **Tokio** as the asynchronous runtime.
- **Quinn** for QUIC-based communication (TLS 1.3).
- **Protobuf** via `prost` for all structured messages.
  - Schemas live in `proto/` and are versioned (`ocw.v1`). Changes follow protobuf compatibility rules: add fields, never reuse field numbers.
  - Position datagrams use compact quantized fields: distance in cm (`uint32`), speed in mm/s (`uint32`), lateral offset in cm (`sint32`), animation state (`uint32` enum).
  - A protocol version is exchanged during the handshake; incompatible clients are rejected with an update prompt.
- **Unreliable datagrams** for position updates; **reliable streams** for login, session management, steering intents and important events.
- The protocol is transport-independent: the browser app joins over a WebTransport endpoint next to the native one (3.5, 14 Phase 10 B3; below).

**Join links (v3.73).** A server is named in one line to share: `ocw://HOST[:PORT]?cert=SHA256HEX[&world=ID[@VERSION]][&route=NAME][&name=TEXT]` – the native QUIC endpoint (port default 47800), the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint (64 hex digits; `:` allowed), optionally the world package (`id@version`, or a manifest URL to fetch it from), the route and a name for lists. `https://HOST[:PORT][/ocw/1]?cert-hash=HEX` is the WebTransport form (port default 47801; the browser joins only these). Parsed by `ocw_protocol::join::JoinLink` (pure, wasm-safe), which also takes a bare `HOST[:PORT]` (IPv6 in brackets) with the fingerprint given separately and a pasted `ocw-desktop --server HOST:PORT --server-cert HEX` line; errors say what is wrong in words. A link without a fingerprint is accepted only for this machine (`localhost`, 127.0.0.0/8, `::1`), like `--insecure-dev`. `ocw-server` prints its link(s) – with the machine's LAN addresses for an unspecified bind (the source address towards the internet, nothing sent) and its world and route – above the `Clients connect with` line; the kiosk keeps them in `server-connect.txt`. A join (3.2.1 *Shared rides from the menu*) sends the rider's hello **without** the world, so the server answers with its `Welcome` whatever it rides (the course: free ride / route, the package's name and graph fingerprint); the client loads that course and rides on the same connection (the server ignores a second hello).

**QUIC transport (decided, Phase 5 groundwork).** `ocw-server::net` carries the unchanged encoded `ClientMessage` / `ServerMessage` bytes; `GameServer` stays transport-independent and the desktop's `ClientCore` runs on the same channel interface as with the local server.

- **Port:** UDP **47800** by default (`ocw-server --listen [ADDR]`, `ocw-desktop --server HOST[:PORT]`); no TCP port. ALPN `ocw/1`.
- **Threads:** the game loop stays one synchronous thread at 50 Hz. `NetServer` owns a small Tokio runtime (two workers) with one task per connection; each tick the loop calls `pump` (connection events and received messages → `GameServer::connect` / `handle` / `disconnect`, replies to the sender) and `broadcast` (the tick's output to every joined client). The client's `NetClient` has its own one-worker runtime; the Bevy side only sends and drains channels.
- **Streams and datagrams:** one bidirectional stream per connection, opened by the client, with every reliable message as a length-prefixed frame (4-byte little-endian length, at most 1 MiB): Hello / Welcome / Reject, steering, turn and U-turn intents, rejoins, dev commands, path updates. **Snapshots** (server → client) and **sensor samples** (client → server) – both superseded by the next one and sequence-numbered – go as unreliable QUIC datagrams. A message larger than the connection's datagram limit (a big field's snapshot exceeds ~1.2 kB; 6.3 interest management will shrink it) or a peer that accepts no datagrams falls back to the stream. The client sends samples on the stream until the server has answered its Hello, so no sample overtakes it. Datagrams may be reordered: the client drops a snapshot whose `server_tick` is not newer than the last one. Considered and not chosen: everything on one stream (simple, but a lost packet stalls all later snapshots – head-of-line blocking); a new unidirectional stream per snapshot (no head-of-line blocking, but per-stream overhead at 10 Hz × riders and still retransmits stale data).
- **Flow control:** each connection has a queue of 256 messages; when it is full, snapshots are dropped and a client that cannot take reliable messages any more is disconnected ("too slow") instead of growing memory.
- **Liveness:** keep-alive every 4 s, idle timeout 15 s; a vanished client's rider is removed after it. The client extrapolates snapshots by half the measured round trip when reconciling its prediction. The 2-minute session hold for reconnects (6.3) is not implemented yet: a reconnect is a new join.
- **Shutdown:** `ocw-server` stops on Ctrl+C / SIGTERM, closes every connection with "server shutting down" and waits up to 1 s for acknowledgements; the desktop shows "Disconnected: …" in the HUD and keeps running.
- **Course check:** the client rides its own course data; besides the world package check (6.5) it refuses a Welcome whose route (or free-ride mode) differs from its own. `ocw-server --route-file` rides a route file (as `ocw-desktop --route-file`; both build the route with `RouteFile::to_route`).
