- **Fixed (v4.30): "the other participant is never reported".** Found while testing V1: the two-rider tests saw no `ParticipantJoined` from the LiveKit Rust backend (SDK 0.10.1) on `livekit-server` 1.13.10 although the server listed both riders. *Not* an SDK ↔ server mismatch: the SDK asks for signal protocol 18, the server answers 17 and both work with 17 (no negotiated data channels; single peer connection over `/rtc/v1`); the server's debug log shows it sending each rider the other's `ParticipantUpdate` (JOINED, ACTIVE), and the SDK turns them into `ParticipantConnected`. *Root cause – the tests:* their `wait_for` drained the backend with `poll()` (which empties its queue) and returned at the first matching event, dropping the rest of that batch. `ocw_voice::livekit` reports `Connected` together with the riders already in the room (`remote_participants()` after the microphone is published, and the `ParticipantConnected` events queued meanwhile), so every wait for `Connected` threw the joins away – reliably when both joined at about the same time. The app's `VoiceController` handles every polled event in order and was never affected (shown by the new controller test). *Fix:* one shared `crates/ocw-voice/tests/support::wait_for` that keeps every polled event, used by `livekit_two_participants` and `bundled_voice_server`; the backend, `livekit` 0.10.1 and the pinned server 1.13.10 stay. *Regression tests:* `tests/backend_events.rs` (the batch case, without network) and, against a real `livekit-server` on marge, both directions of seeing and hearing in both LiveKit tests plus two desktop `VoiceController`s (above, *Integration test* in 7).
- **Kiosk and the live test (v4.36).** `scripts/deploy-test.sh` runs `fetch-livekit-server.sh` on the kiosk machine and installs `livekit-server` (and `livekit-server.LICENSE.txt`) next to `ocw-server` in the deploy directory before the binaries that restart the kiosk; the kiosk's game server (`ocw-kiosk.sh`, `--listen 0.0.0.0:47800`, no new options) finds it there and starts it, so riders who join a kiosk talk to each other; a failed fetch leaves the kiosk without voice and the deploy goes on. `ocw-kiosk.sh status` prints the server's `voice chat on …` / `off: …` line. `make test-voice-live` covers the one path the other voice tests do not: the real desktop app (debug build with `voice`, headless on Xvfb through `drive.sh`, fresh `--settings-file`, `voice.mute-mic off` since riders join muted) joining an `ocw-server` with its bundled voice server as a *rider*; an `ocw-bot` makes the session shared, the echo participant joins as the Echo rider with this start's keys (read from the child's environment); passes when the app reports `voice: connected`, LiveKit's room service lists it active with an unmuted microphone track and the echo participant reports hearing it.
- **Open.** ~~*Host a ride* in the app, the ports page and UPnP~~ (built in V2, v4.31, 7.1.9); ~~Block and the per-rider volume~~ (built v4.48, 7.1.10); ~~join muted and the X mouth (Q7), the server-side grants and range (Q6, Q8, Q10; V3 / V4)~~ (built v4.51, 7.1.11); packaging into the four release packages with licences (V6); the browser bridge (V5); a Windows and a macOS run (the Windows job object is build-checked only; the macOS source build not run yet); the HUD showing why voice is off; LiveKit's STUN start takes ~6 s behind NAT (inside the 10 s limit, but close on slow lines); `make test-web-livekit` runs `livekit-server --dev` with LiveKit's default RTC ports (7881 TCP), which collide with a bundled voice server already running on the same machine (the kiosk) – the test should get its own ports.


#### 7.1.10 Built: Block and a volume per rider (v4.48, 7.1.7 Q9)

- **Menu (both apps, `ocw_client::menu::voice`).** Settings → Voice → *Participants* ("3, 1 blocked") lists the riders in the voice room with their state (blocked, muted by you, microphone off, heard at %, too far away; the own volume if not 100 %); each opens its page (`Page::VoiceRider`): the name and state, *Mute for me* (this ride, as before), *Volume (%)* (← / → in 10 % steps, 0 – 200 %, Confirm back to 100 %) and *Block* (on / off). The list ends with *Blocked riders* (`Page::VoiceBlocked`): every blocked rider, here or not, by name; Confirm unblocks. The Voice page keeps its six rows (ten-foot rule).
- **Console (both apps, `ocw_client::voice`).** `voice.volume WHO PERCENT` and `voice.block WHO [on|off|toggle]` (default toggle); WHO is a rider id, voice identity or name in the room, or a remembered rider's key or name (unblock someone who is not here). `voice.status` shows "blocked" / "volume N %" per participant and the blocked list. The browser's `window.ocw.voice()` has `blocked`, `volume`, the blocked list and `apart`.
- **Remembered** in the settings file / `localStorage`, section `[voice_riders]` (not registered settings; no "unknown key" warning), one table per rider key with `name`, `volume`, `blocked`; an entry back at 100 % and not blocked is removed. Keys (`ocw_voice::riders`): `acct:ID` for a signed-in rider (9.1; the same on every server) – the snapshots carry `RiderUpdate.account_id` once a second (every 50th tick), the client keeps it while the rider is there – else `name:HOST/NAME`, the name on that server; HOST is the host the app joined (lower case, no scheme, port or path, so the desktop app's `HOST:47800` and the browser's `https://HOST:47801/…` share it; `local` for the app's own servers: solo, Host a ride). The account's entry wins over the name's; a block under either holds.
- **Volume.** The gain a voice plays at is spatial gain (distance, Q6 / Q10) × the voice volume (`voice.volume`, 0 – 200 %) × the rider's own volume (`ocw_voice::riders::gain`), in the desktop mixer and the browser's gain node alike (the `SetPlacement` gain). 0 % keeps the rider subscribed at silence.
- **Block, both ways.** The client sends its blocks for this server (`VoiceBlocks`: every blocked account id, the names blocked on this HOST; the whole list at the join if not empty and on every change). The game server (`ocw_server::voice_block`, pure) keeps, per rider, the riders it is *apart* from – those it blocked and those who blocked it (by account if signed in, by display name always, never oneself) – and sends each rider only its own set when it changes (`VoiceApart`, directed: `GameServer::take_directed`, delivered by `NetServer::send_directed`, the local and hosting threads and the stepped servers; never in a broadcast), at once for a rider who joins after the block and again when one leaves. It never says who blocked whom: the blocked rider gets exactly what the blocker gets. Each client (`VoiceController`) then (1) does not subscribe to a rider it blocked or is apart from, and (2) allows its microphone only to the other participants (LiveKit's track subscription permissions, an allow list – `SetSubscribers`: `set_track_subscription_permissions` in the Rust SDK, `setTrackSubscriptionPermissions` in `livekit-client`; everybody again when nothing is blocked; a new call starts open, the backends keep the list across reconnects). The voice server enforces (2): a modified client of the blocked rider that asks for the blocker's track itself gets nothing.
- **Private.** The blocked rider is not told: no message, no menu entry (its list shows the other as heard or not, like a rider out of range); only the effect – **except the headphones sign (7.1.7 Q18, decided 2026-11-22, built v5.33; this overrides the rule for the sign):** the blocker shows headphones to the rider it blocked ("cannot hear you", like a *Mute for me*), worked out by the game server from the blocks and sent to that rider alone in its `NotHearingYou`; the blocker sees no headphones on the blocked rider (unless blocked back), nobody else sees anything, and the block lists still never leave the server. A rider's volume at 0 % shows headphones to that rider too (`RiderStatus.silenced`).
- **Tests.** Unit: the keys, scopes, the volume grid and the gain maths (`riders.rs`); the controller – the volume on top of spatial gain and voice volume (with and without spatial), a block unsubscribes and allows the microphone to the others only, a newcomer allowed at once, unblock restores, `VoiceApart` without an own block, a new call starts open; the settings round trip (`[voice_riders]`, defaults forgotten, broken entries skipped); the menu rows (participants, a rider's page with the steps and their ends, the blocked list); the console commands in both apps (remembered, unblocked by key, saved in `localStorage` and back after a reload); the server's rules with three riders (A blocks B: A and B told, C not; the same set for the blocked as for the blocker; repeats send nothing; unblock; nothing in the broadcasts; newcomers; leaving; by account, the account in every 50th tick's snapshot only); the protocol round trip (`VoiceBlocks`, `VoiceApart`, `account_id`); three clients with the shared driver on one in-memory game server (console block → server → both apart, C with both; unblock). On marge against a real `livekit-server` 1.13.10: `make test-voice-livekit` (three desktop controllers, the apart sets from an in-memory game server), `make test-voice-bundled` (three riders over QUIC on `ocw-server --listen` with its bundled voice server; Ada blocks Bea over the game connection, only the two are told) and `make test-web-livekit` (three browser pages: Ada blocks Bea from the console) – with A blocking B neither hears the other, C hears both and both hear C, B's own request for A's voice is refused, and unblocking restores it (the browser test).
- **Open.** The voice server enforces a block through the *publishers'* permissions, so it holds as long as one of the two clients is unmodified (each denies the other); two modified clients could still exchange voice – LiveKit's server API has no per-subscriber permissions (only `UpdateSubscriptions`, which a client can undo), so a stricter rule would need the server-side grants of V3 / V4 or the own SFU of 7.1.1 (b). A modified client also learns that it is apart from a rider (the effect it would notice anyway). Q18 (the signs): built v5.33, see *Private*. *V3 / V4 (v4.51, 7.1.11)*: the game server now leaves blocked pairs out of both riders' `VoiceHearing` too, so an unmodified client of either side never subscribes nor allows; the enforcement by the voice server is still the publishers' permissions (see 7.1.11 *Open*).

#### 7.1.11 Built: voice by range and audience, V3 and V4 (v4.51, 7.1.7 Q6, Q7, Q8, Q10; range of Q20 v4.66)

- **Hearing range (Q6, Q10, Q20; v4.66).** `ocw_voice::spatial`: gain 1 up to **5 m**, then 5 m / distance times a smoothstep taper that reaches **zero at 10 m** (no floor; 1/3 at 7.5 m, ~0.22 at 8 m, < 10⁻³ at 9.9 m, 0 from 10 m). The curve's shape is the one of v4.51 (full to 10 m, zero at 300 m), only its distances follow Q20 ("start fading around 5 m, not audible beyond 10 m"): continuous at 5 m, smooth into zero at 10 m. **Selected riders are always audible (Q20):** a rider listening to *Voice room: Selected riders* hears the selected riders at **full volume** (gain 1, panned beside like anyone) **at any distance** – also before their place is known; with *Voice room: Everybody* a rider on the selection list (for *Who hears me*, Q19) is heard by range like anyone. A voice already heard counts 1 m nearer in the cap's ranking (15 m before). Distances as before: the gap along the route (the shorter way round a loop), the straight line in free ride. `voice.spatial off`: the same volume within the 10 m range, the selected riders at any distance (Q21's built semantics, with the new range). **The Echo rider** (7 *Echo bot*) keeps the curve of v4.51 (`SpatialConfig::echo`: full to 10 m, zero at 300 m) and its server range (310 m / 340 m): it is a test tool standing 20 m ahead, and with the riders' 10 m range its echo would be silent where it stands.
- **The server sends voice only to riders who can hear it (Q6, Q20).** `ocw_server::voice_hearing` (pure) decides per pair: listener L receives speaker S when they are within **10.5 m** (a grant then holds up to **12 m**, so riders side by side at the edge do not flicker in and out – the voice is silent beyond 10 m anyway; v4.66, before 310 m / 340 m) – or at any distance when L listens to *Voice room: Selected riders* with S among them (Q20) –, S's *Who hears me* allows L, L's *Voice room* includes S, and no block keeps them apart (a block always wins, also over a selection). With the Echo rider on either side the range is its own 310 m / 340 m. The game server recomputes it with every snapshot (10 Hz) and on every change of an audience, a block, a join or a leave, and sends each rider **alone** (directed, like `VoiceApart`) only when it changes: `VoiceHearing { may_hear, heard_by }` – whose voice it may receive, who may receive its own. Only servers with voice compute it. The Echo rider (no connection) listens to everybody and is heard by all nearby; the speaker's *Who hears me* still decides whether it hears them.
- **The clients follow it.** `VoiceController` (both apps): in the session and event rooms it subscribes only to riders in `may_hear` (nobody before the first answer) and, with *Voice room: Selected riders*, only to selected ones; it allows its microphone (LiveKit's track subscription permissions, the allow list of v4.48) only to `heard_by` minus blocked and apart riders – nobody with *Who hears me: No one* or before the server said, the selected ones only with *Selected riders*. The list is sent **before** the connect (the backends apply it when the microphone is published), so a new call never starts open. The voice server enforces it: a client that asks for a voice it is not allowed gets nothing. Group rooms are not limited by the range (everybody in the group is heard, blocks still hold). Riders the server allows whose place is not known yet are heard quietly (0.15) until placed.
- **The cap (7.1.2).** At most `voice.max_voices` (default **24**, 1–32) voices: riders who talk now or did in the last 5 s first (LiveKit's active speakers, so a pause between sentences keeps the place), then the nearest; a voice already heard counts 1 m nearer (15 m before v4.66).
- **Joined muted (Q7).** Both apps start with the microphone muted, and every call that ends (a ride switch, leaving, voice off) mutes the next; M unmutes for the ride. The microphone is not remembered: `voice.mute-mic` no longer saves `voice.mic_muted` (the setting now applies `voice.mute-mic` – muted now), and applying the other voice settings no longer touches the microphone (regression test: before, any `set voice.*` unmuted it again from the saved value). The X mouth is the status sign of a muted microphone in the call (2.6, wired to the controller's switch since v4.34) – so every rider shows it after joining.
- **Who hears me (Q8)** – `voice.heard_by` = `no_one` (default) | `nearby` | `selected`; **Voice room** (7.1.3) – `voice.room` = `everybody` (default) | `selected`. The client sends both with its selection to the game server (`VoiceAudience`: the setting values, the selected accounts and the names selected on this server – a blocked rider never; at the join if not the default and on every change).
- **Selected riders (V4).** `voice.select WHO [on|off|toggle]` (a rider id, voice identity or name in the room, or a remembered key or name); remembered like a block in `[voice_riders]` (`selected = true`, by account if signed in, else by name per server). One list serves *Voice room* and *Who hears me* (Q19). `voice.status` lists the room, who hears the rider, the server's sets and the selected riders.
- **Menu (both apps, `ocw_client::menu::voice`).** *(Replaced in v5.26 by the rows of 7.1.12.)* Settings → Voice: *Microphone* (as it is now), *Speaker*, **Voice room** ("hear all, heard by no one"), *Participants*, *Devices and options* (now also the voice volume), *Voice chat* – six rows. Voice → **Voice room** (`Page::VoiceRoom`): *Voice room* (Everybody / Selected riders), *Who hears me* (No one / All nearby / Selected riders), *Choose riders* ("2 selected (1 here)"). → **Choose riders** (`Page::VoiceSelect`): the riders in the call by name with "[x]" / "[ ]", the distance and "talking"; then *Not here now* and the selected riders not here; Confirm toggles. Participants' states: "not selected" (listening to the selection), "private" (near, but not letting the rider hear them), "too far away".
- **HUD.** The voice indicator's second line gets the room: "ROOM: everybody - heard by: no one", "ROOM: 3 selected (2 here) - …", "ROOM: group NAME - …"; talking selected riders are named first. **The first call's notice** (7.1.2, adapted to Q7 / Q8 – the planned "Your microphone is on" no longer holds): "Voice: you join muted - M unmutes. Who hears you: no one (Settings > Voice > Voice room)." for 8 s at the first call, then `voice.first_call_notice` is turned off (remembered).
- **Headphones (Q12, built from its proposal).** A rider listening to *Selected riders* shows headphones to the riders in the call who are not selected (the proposal's "they listen to Selected riders without you"); distance and *Who hears me* still do not count (Q12); blocks and 0 % volume count since v5.33 (Q18, 7.1.10 *Private*).
- **Browser.** The same controller, menu and commands; `window.ocw.voice()` has `voice_room`, `heard_by`, `selected`, `hearing`, `hud_room`, `notice` and per participant `selected`, `may_hear`, `distance_m`.
- **Test hooks.** `ocw-server --dev-commands` (hidden: accepts the clients' teleports, for the range tests; never on a public server; its welcome says so – `Welcome.dev_commands`, a field added – and both apps then allow their dev console commands for it, as for their own local server) and `ocw-bot --voice-nearby` (the bots let all nearby hear them).
- **Tests.** Unit: the gain curve (v4.66: 1 at 0 and 5 m, 1/3 at 7.5 m, 0 at 10 and 11 m, monotone, smooth; the Echo rider's curve), the selected riders at any distance, the cap with talking riders first; the server's rules (`voice_hearing.rs`: distances on a loop and in free ride, range in and out with the margin – 20 m out, in within 10.5 m, kept to 12 m –, a selected rider sent at 1 km, *No one* and a block over that selection, the three *Who hears me*, the room, by account and by name, a block over a selection, the Echo rider, the wire); the controller (nothing before the server's answer, a far rider unsubscribed, groups open, *Who hears me* to the permissions – before the connect –, the room, the cap's talking priority, joined muted); the selection keys and lists; the settings round trip; three clients with the shared driver on one in-memory game server (far and back, *Selected riders* and *No one*, the room, the headphones, a block over a selection); the menu rows (the Voice page, Voice room, Choose riders, the participants' states) and the commands in both apps (the regression above, the settings saved, `voice.select` with a block, the page's storage after a reload). On marge against a real `livekit-server` 1.13.10: `make test-voice-livekit` (three desktop controllers with an in-memory game server placing the riders, the near ones within 5 m: far (20 m since v4.66, 1.5 km before) – the near two hear each other, the far one hears nobody and nobody hears her, her own request for Ada's voice is refused; selected 1 km away (v4.66) – Cleo with *Voice room: Selected riders* (Ada) hears Ada and nobody else, nobody hears her; near (3 m) with Ada's *Who hears me: Selected riders* (Bea) – Bea hears Ada, Cleo does not and is refused; a block over the selection), `make test-voice-bundled` (the same over QUIC on `ocw-server --listen --dev-commands` with its bundled voice server, `VoiceHearing` over the game connection; the block test with the server's hearing), `make test-web-livekit` (three pages: joined muted and heard by no one; the pages stop (`sim.power 0`) and stand together; far (20 m) / near by teleports, the far rider refused, a selected rider 1.1 km away played; *Who hears me: Selected riders* and *Voice room: Selected riders*).
- **Open.** The voice server enforces who hears whom through the **publishers'** permissions (set by the speaker's client from the server's `heard_by`), so a modified speaker client could open its own microphone to everybody, and two modified clients could exchange voice; LiveKit's server API has no per-subscriber permissions (only `UpdateSubscriptions`, which a client can undo) – a stricter rule needs the own SFU of 7.1.1 (b). Distances in free ride are straight lines. Q19–Q22.

#### 7.1.12 Built: the Voice page's two rows, *My voice* and *I hear* (v5.26, 7.1.7 Q16)

- **Two separate settings** (Q16: "muting voice (who can hear me) is a complete separate setting to muting audio of other players (who do I choose to hear)"): *My voice* says who hears the rider, *I hear* whom the rider hears; neither changes the other.
- **My voice: on / off · Everybody / Selected.** The on / off is the microphone (`voice.mute-mic`, M, gamepad Select, Confirm on the row); every ride starts off (Q7 – joined muted, never remembered). The audience is the setting `voice.my_voice` (`everybody`, the default, or `selected`; ← / → on the row), kept while the voice is off. Mapping (`ocw_voice::audience::MyVoice`, sent as `VoiceAudience.heard_by`):

  | My voice | microphone | sign | server is told | who receives the voice |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | off (any audience) | muted | X mouth (Q11) | `NO_ONE` | nobody (grants and the voice server's permissions) |
  | on · Everybody | on | – | `NEARBY` | everybody within the 10 m range (Q20; riders who selected the rider at any distance) – v4.51's *All nearby* |
  | on · Selected | on | – | `SELECTED` | the selected riders (Choose riders, Q19) – v4.51's *Selected riders* |

  The other way, for old settings: *No one* → off (every ride starts so) with the audience Everybody, *All nearby* → Everybody, *Selected riders* → Selected. Turning My voice on asks the server for the new audience; the microphone is allowed to the listeners when its answer comes (one snapshot, ≤ 0.1 s).
- **I hear: everybody / selected / nobody** (`voice.i_hear`, default everybody; v4.51's *Voice room* plus *nobody*). Everybody: everybody within range; selected: only the selected riders, at any distance (Q20); **nobody**: no voice is subscribed (in the session, event and group rooms), the game server sends the rider nobody's voice (`VoiceListen.NOBODY`, a value added) and others may still hear the rider. The headphones (Q12, Q17): a rider who hears nobody shows headphones to **every** rider in the call – the client says so in `RiderStatus.hears_nobody` and the server also takes it from the rider's audience (`ocw_server::headphones::cannot_hear`), so the sign does not wait for the status; an older server reads *nobody* as everybody, the client still subscribes to nobody and sends `hears_nobody`. *My voice* never shows headphones (it is the other direction; the X mouth says it).
- **The old voice off** (*Voice chat* row, `voice.enabled off`) is **both rows off**: My voice off and I hear nobody. The rider stays in the call (others see the X mouth and the headphones). There is no single voice-off setting any more; `voice.off` (console, both apps) turns both off at once, each row turns on again by itself.
- **Old settings migrated** (`Settings::parse`, so `ocw.toml` and the browser's `localStorage` alike): `voice.heard_by` → `voice.my_voice` (as above), `voice.room` → `voice.i_hear`, `voice.enabled = off` → `voice.i_hear = nobody` (it wins over the room); a new key already in the file wins; the old keys are dropped (no "unknown setting" warning) and the next save writes only the new ones; the selection (`[voice_riders]`, `selected = true`) is not touched.
- **Menu (both apps, `ocw_client::menu::voice`).** Settings → Voice, six rows: *My voice* ("off (everybody)", "on, selected"), *I hear* (Everybody / Selected / Nobody), *Choose riders* ("2 selected (1 here)", the list of 7.1.11, now opened from here), *Speaker (voices)*, *Participants* (the call's state, "connected (3), 1 blocked" – before on the *Voice chat* row), *Devices and options*. The *Voice chat* row and the *Voice room* page are gone. A participant's state is "you hear nobody" with *I hear: nobody*.
- **HUD and notice.** The voice indicator's second line: "MY VOICE: off (everybody) - I HEAR: everybody", "MY VOICE: on, selected - I HEAR: 3 selected (2 here)", "… - I HEAR: nobody", "… - I HEAR: group NAME". The first call's notice (8 s): "Voice: My voice is off - M turns it on for everybody nearby. I hear: everybody (Settings > Voice)." (with Selected: "for the selected riders"). `voice.mute-mic` answers "my voice on: microphone on, heard by everybody" / "my voice off: microphone muted, nobody hears you"; `voice.status` shows "my voice: off (everybody), I hear: everybody". **Nobody hears you (Q22 (b), v5.33):** when My voice is turned on in the call (M, the menu, the console) and nobody can hear it by the rider's own settings – *on · Selected* with no selected rider in the call who is not blocked or apart, or *on · Everybody* with other riders in the session but every one in the call blocked or apart (`ocw_client::voice::nobody_hears_you`) – the voice notice line shows "Voice: nobody hears you - Settings > Voice" for 5 s, once per turn-on (it wins over the first call's notice; muting again ends it; distance is no reason).
- **Browser.** The same controller, page and commands; `window.ocw.voice()` has `my_voice`, `my_voice_on`, `i_hear` and `heard_by` (what the server is told: `no_one` while My voice is off) instead of `voice_room`.
- **Tests (11.4).** The mapping both ways (`audience`), the migration of every old value (and a new key winning, the selection kept), the controller (My voice off allows nobody before the connect and again after M; on · Everybody / Selected; *I hear: nobody* unsubscribes everyone, also in a group room, while others are still allowed), the server (*I hear: nobody* receives no voice; headphones for every viewer from the audience alone), three clients on one in-memory server (My voice off: the X mouth, heard by nobody, no headphones; I hear nobody: headphones seen by both others), `voice.off` = both off (saved), the HUD and notice texts, the Voice page's six rows, the settings in both apps; `make test-web-livekit` gets an *I hear: nobody* step. v5.33: the notice (*Selected* with none, the selected one blocked, every rider blocked, the normal cases without it, a few seconds and once per turn-on, gone when muted) and the headphones of Q18 (unit: each of the three reasons per viewer, a block one way, never on the own rider; the server with four riders: 0 % and a block each told only to that viewer, no list in any snapshot; three clients with the shared driver: Mute for me, 0 % and back, a block and unblock).

## 8. Bicycle and Character Assets

### 8.1 Asset Pipeline

3D format: **glTF 2.0**. Models are created, for example, with Blender. Phase 15 (planned v3.48) moves the shipped models to `artwork/3dmodels/` and every fixed-shape object from code into such files; Phase 16 adds the editor (OCW Studio).

Import process:

1. Create model.
2. Define materials.
3. Create skeleton and animations.
4. Export glTF.
5. Validate assets (`cargo run -p ocw-assets -- validate [DIR]`, including licence metadata, 13): the manifest `manifest.toml` next to the models has an entry with `license`, `source` and `author` for every `.glb` / `.gltf` (files without an entry are rejected), licences from the allowed list (2.5), no physics keys, bikes name a known physics profile; every model reads as glTF 2.0, uses only paint slots as materials, has the nodes the app animates (bike: wheels, crank, pedals, handlebar, grip and saddle anchors, `lod1`; rider: the rig of 2.6, head wear and kit nodes), plausible rig dimensions and stays within the triangle budget (bike 15 000, rider 8 000, far LOD 4 000). The validator is a subcommand of the asset crate instead of a separate `tools/asset-validator` (one crate shares the reader with the app; low). Textures (the material library, 4.6) have their own manifest `assets/materials.toml` and validator (`ocw-assets materials validate`) with the same licence rule (`ocw_assets::licence`, Phase 8A) plus a SHA-256 pin per source file.
6. Import into Bevy.
7. Register components.

### 8.2 Bicycle Components

Bicycles consist of modular parts: frame, fork, handlebars, wheels, tires, saddle, pedals, drivetrain, accessories.

Each component has a unique ID, a configuration, a visual part and an optional physics profile reference (2.5).

The catalogue of parts is `assets/parts.toml` (planned v2.53: generic unbranded names, tier, price in hearts from researched real prices in `assets/parts-sources.toml`, real weight, compatible bike types, physics classes, model reference; 14 Phase 4, 4H–4I). Every bike model has a hotspot anchor `hs_<slot>` per part slot for the workshop scene (4B).

### 8.3 Characters

Characters use a shared rig. Body, clothing and accessories are loaded modularly. Animations are driven by the riding state.

## 9. Backend and Infrastructure

The desktop application is the actual simulation client. Server services handle only tasks that must be centrally managed or synchronized between participants.

| Area | Technology |
|---|---|
| Language | Rust |
| Async runtime | Tokio |
| HTTP API | Axum |
| Web companion | Leptos (SSR on Axum) |
| Real-time networking | Quinn / QUIC |
| Data format | Protobuf (`prost`) |
| Database | PostgreSQL |
| Cache | Redis (optional) |
| Voice | LiveKit (self-hosted) |
| Authentication | OIDC towards the apps; **sign-in with Google (OIDC) and Strava (OAuth2) brokered by our own backend** – no separate identity server for now (decided 2026-11-14, v3.33, 9.1) |
| Telemetry | OpenTelemetry |
| Containers | Docker |
| Deployment | Linux servers, hosted in the EU |

### 9.1 Sign-in (decided by the user 2026-11-14, v3.33)

- **Providers:** **Google** (OpenID Connect) and **Strava** (OAuth2: athlete id and name, no e-mail) – for now the only ways to sign in. Anonymous riding stays (Phase 10 Q5). No separate identity server for now; Keycloak (recommended) or Authentik can replace the broker later without changing the apps.
- **Our backend is the only token issuer for the apps:** it runs the provider redirects (authorization code + PKCE, state, nonce), creates or links an **OCW account** (one account can link both providers, keyed by the provider's subject / athlete id), and issues its own short-lived **access tokens** (signed JWT, keys published as JWKS) and rotating **refresh tokens** (revocable). Endpoints are shaped like an OIDC provider (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`, `authorize`, `token`, `jwks`, `device_authorization`, `revoke`, `userinfo`), so the apps speak plain OIDC and a later identity server is a drop-in.
- **Flows per app:** desktop – system browser + loopback redirect (RFC 8252, PKCE); browser app – redirect with PKCE; kiosk and VR headset – **device authorization flow** (RFC 8628: a short code confirmed on the phone). The game server accepts the access token in the QUIC / WebTransport hello and checks it against the JWKS.
- **Strava upload:** the Strava sign-in may also ask for `activity:write` (optional consent) so the later Strava upload (2.8) needs no second authorization; Strava tokens are stored encrypted, server-side only.
- **Registrations and secrets:** the Google OAuth client (Google Cloud Console, consent screen) and the Strava API application are registered by the user; client ids and secrets live in a git-ignored server config, never in the repository or the apps. Real sign-ins need a public HTTPS domain (registered redirect URIs); development and tests run on `localhost` and against **fake providers** (in-process OIDC / OAuth2 test servers).

#### 9.1.1 Build (v3.46)

**What exists.** The pure crate **`ocw-auth`** (wasm-safe: no clock, randomness or I/O) holds what every side shares: compact JWS with **EdDSA** (Ed25519; one algorithm, `typ: at+jwt` for access tokens, RFC 9068), the claims, the JWKS, PKCE S256, the wire types (discovery, token and error responses, device authorization, userinfo, link ticket) and the apps' side of the flows (`client`: authorization URL, loopback redirect check, token / refresh / device / revocation forms, the kept `Session`), and `Verifier` – the game server's check (signature against the JWKS, issuer, audience, type, expiry with 30 s leeway; an unknown key id marks the key set stale). The backend **`services/accounts`** (`ocw-accounts`, native) is the Authentication and User service of the monolith: `AuthService` (transport-free) and its Axum router, run by the `ocw-server` binary (feature `backend`, default on; the apps embed the game server without it).

| Endpoint | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /.well-known/openid-configuration`, `GET /jwks` | Discovery (with `ocw_providers`, `ocw_account_endpoint`) and the published keys |
| `GET /authorize` | An app's request: exact redirect URI (loopback on any port for `ocw-desktop`, RFC 8252 7.3; the configured page for `ocw-web`), PKCE S256 required, `state` required, `nonce`, `provider=google\|strava` (without it a choice page), `link_ticket`; then the provider's sign-in with our own `state`, `nonce` and PKCE |
| `GET /callback/{google,strava}` | Code exchange at the provider (Google: discovery, ID-token signature, issuer, audience and nonce through `openidconnect`; Strava: the athlete from the token response through `oauth2`, the granted scope), the OCW account found or created, a one-time code (60 s, bound to client, redirect URI and challenge) back to the app with `iss` (RFC 9207) |
| `POST /token` | `authorization_code` (+ verifier), `refresh_token` (rotation; a reused one revokes its whole family; idle 30 days, at most 180), the device code grant (pending, `slow_down` +5 s, denied, expired); a reused code revokes what it gave |
| `POST /device_authorization`, `GET /device`, `POST /device/confirm` | RFC 8628: an 8-letter code (`BCDF-GHJK`, no vowels), 10 minutes, 5 s interval; the page shows the device's name and the code, its buttons post with a CSRF token (`SameSite=Strict` cookie against the form field, `__Host-` on HTTPS) and an `Origin` check |
| `POST /revoke` | RFC 7009, ends the sign-in (no oracle: always 200) |
| `GET /userinfo` | `sub`, name, the linked providers (Strava: upload granted), Google's e-mail |
| `POST /account/link`, `DELETE /account/providers/{p}` | A link ticket (5 min, single use) bound to the app's PKCE challenge of the sign-in that follows; the link is committed only when the app redeems the code. Unlinking never removes the last sign-in |
| `GET /account/export`, `DELETE /account` | 12: the account, its identities and every module's data (`AccountHooks`); deletion wants a sign-in at most 15 minutes old, deletes identities, refresh tokens and the Strava tokens and tells the modules |

Access tokens live 10 minutes (`aud: ocw`), ID tokens 10 minutes. Signing keys rotate every 30 days; a retired key stays in the JWKS until its tokens have expired. Strava's tokens are kept **encrypted** (ChaCha20-Poly1305, a 256-bit key file, the account and provider as associated data) for the later upload (2.8; `activity:write` is asked at sign-in, the athlete may untick it). Rate limits per client address (30 per minute on token, device, authorize and the device page; `X-Forwarded-For` only from the trusted proxy); Strava's budget (200 per 15 minutes, 2,000 per day) is counted and kept in step with its `X-RateLimit-*` headers. No token, code or secret is logged or printed (`Debug` redacts them).

**Game server.** `Hello.access_token` (optional), `Welcome.account` (`Account`: id, display name, providers), `Reject.auth` (the token was refused: sign in again). `ServerConfig.auth` holds the `Verifier`; a signed-in rider rides under the account's name; a bad, expired or foreign token is refused; no token stays anonymous unless `--auth-required`; the local servers have no sign-in and ignore tokens. `ocw-server --auth-config FILE` runs the backend in the same process (its keys go to the verifier every minute), `--auth-issuer URL` checks a separate backend's tokens (JWKS fetched every 5 minutes and soon after an unknown key), `--auth-dev [ADDR]` runs the backend with **fake Google and Strava** for development (`--auth-dev-web PAGE` allows the browser app's page, `--auth-info-file` writes the URLs).

**Apps.** Settings → **Account** (`ocw_client::account`, rows from the shared `AccountMenu`): signed out *Sign in with Google*, *Sign in with Strava* and on the desktop *Sign in with a code (kiosk)*; while waiting the status and *Cancel*; signed in the name and providers, *Link* the other, *Unlink* (only when two are linked), *Sign out*; on the desktop also *Rider profiles*. The `account` command (status, signin [google|strava|--code], link, unlink, signout, cancel, export, delete --yes). The **desktop** opens the system browser (`OCW_OPEN_URL` overrides) and waits on a loopback listener; a kiosk uses the code (client `ocw-kiosk`), shown with the URL on the page; the session goes into the OS keyring (`keyring`: Secret Service, Keychain, Credential Manager), else into a private file, and is refreshed in the background; the access token goes into the hello of a shared ride (`--server`). The backend comes from `--account-server URL` or `OCW_ACCOUNT_SERVER` (none: sign-in off). The **browser** goes to the backend and comes back with the code (the pending login and the page's query in `sessionStorage`; the code leaves the address bar at once), exchanges it with `fetch()` (CORS for the configured origin); page option `auth=URL`.

**Tests** (no network beyond the loopback): `services/accounts/tests/flows.rs` – discovery; Google with PKCE, state and nonce; state / nonce mismatch, a cancelled sign-in; unregistered or inexact redirect URIs (an error page, never a redirect), missing or plain PKCE, repeated parameters; single-use codes bound to the verifier, a replayed code revoking its tokens, expiry; refresh rotation, reuse detection, revocation, idle expiry, another client; Strava with the athlete, the optional upload consent and its rate limits; linking with tickets bound to PKCE (single use, another challenge refused, an identity of another account refused), unlinking never the last; the device flow (pending, slow down, CSRF refused, approved, used up, denied, expired, a client without it); JWKS rotation; export and deletion (recent sign-in); rate limits; bearer checks. Unit tests in each module (JWT tampering and algorithms, PKCE RFC 7636 vector, key rotation and persistence, encryption bound to the account, store linking rules and the private file). The game server: good token (the account's name), expired, another issuer or audience, forged, an ID token, garbage, anonymous allowed or required, a server without sign-in. The desktop: sign in, link, refresh, unlink, export, revoke against the backend and the fakes in-process; the kiosk's code; a forged redirect ignored, cancel; the console and the Account page end to end. The browser's redirect state (the original query back, a forged state ignored), the `auth=` option; **`make test-web-account`**: headless Chromium signs in with the fake Google through the redirect (the code leaves the address bar, the ride's options come back), links Strava (link ticket over CORS), signs out (`localStorage` keeps no access token). Screenshots: `scripts/test-account-pages.sh` (the desktop's Account page signed out, signed in, the kiosk's code; the backend's code page in Chromium).

**Proposals (v3.46, the agent's choices; open to change):**

- **Storage:** a `Store` trait with `MemStore` – in memory, or opened on a path a JSON snapshot written after every change (atomically, mode 0600) – enough for development and one small instance. Short-lived state (pending sign-ins, codes, device codes, link tickets) stays in memory (a restart only means signing in again). **PostgreSQL** (`sqlx` with migrations, the account schema of 12) is the next step for the hosted backend; marge has no PostgreSQL server, so it is not built yet. The trait is synchronous; the PostgreSQL store may make it async.
- **Tokens:** EdDSA (Ed25519, already in the tree for package signatures) rather than ES256; 10-minute access tokens; refresh tokens idle 30 days, at most 180 days after the sign-in; deletion wants a sign-in at most 15 minutes old.
- **Browser:** the access token in memory (for a remote ride also in `sessionStorage`, this tab), the **refresh token in `localStorage`** (rotating, reuse detection, idle expiry): an HttpOnly cookie needs the backend on the page's own site, which waits for B8 hosting.
- **Desktop:** the OS keyring through `keyring` 3, falling back to a private file (a kiosk without a Secret Service). The earlier desktop-side Strava upload (`strava.*`, the user's own API app) stays until the backend's upload replaces it (2.8).
- **Menu:** Settings is at the ten-foot limit, so *Account* took the place of *Riders*, and the rider profiles moved onto the Account page (and stay in the Workshop).
- **Linking:** a link ticket from `POST /account/link` bound to the app's PKCE challenge, committed when the app redeems the code (a stolen ticket cannot link another identity). One identity per provider: linking another Google account replaces the old one; an identity that belongs to another OCW account is refused (no automatic merge).
- **Kiosk:** the device flow uses its own client (`ocw-kiosk`); the desktop app offers it as *Sign in with a code*.

**To go live** (the user): register the Google OAuth client (web application; redirect URI `https://<domain>/callback/google`) and the Strava API application (callback domain `<domain>`), a public HTTPS domain with a TLS proxy in front of `listen`, `config/accounts.toml` from `services/accounts/accounts.example.toml`, and the apps pointed at it (`--account-server`, the browser's `auth=` and its page in `[[clients]]`). Steps: README, *Accounts and sign-in*.

Backend modules:

- Authentication Service.
- User Service.
- Profile Service (incl. the workshop: hearts ledger, inventory and bikes, purchases; 14 Phase 4, 4E).
- Device Service.
- Multiplayer Session Service (game server).
- Race Management.
- Friends and Groups.
- World Metadata Service.
- Asset and World Distribution.
- Training History.
- Strava Integration.
- Voice Room Management (LiveKit tokens).
- Web Companion (route group).

The first version is a **modular backend monolith** (`services/server`). A split into microservices only makes sense once there is an actual scaling need. LiveKit runs as a separate service.

## 10. Cargo Workspace and Repository Structure

The workspace starts with about 8 crates; crates are split only when they grow.

**Dependency rule:** only `ocw-render`, the apps `apps/desktop` and `apps/web`, and `ocw-client` (the shared client logic, which uses `ocw-render`'s view types but no Bevy systems) depend on Bevy. `ocw-core`, `ocw-sim`, `ocw-protocol` and `ocw-world` must also build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (3.5).

```
open-cycling-world/
├── Cargo.toml
├── Cargo.lock
├── rust-toolchain.toml
├── apps/
│   ├── desktop/          # Bevy app, wires all plugins together
│   ├── web/              # the same client in the browser: wasm32 + WebGPU, local server in the frame loop (14 Phase 10)
│   ├── bot/              # ocw-bot: headless remote riders over QUIC, multiplayer test verdict (no Bevy, 11.4.1)
│   ├── world-builder/    # CLI: OSM + DEM → world packages, route editor
│   └── web-companion/    # browser app without riding (Leptos)
├── services/
│   └── server/           # modular monolith: Axum API + QUIC game server
├── crates/
│   ├── ocw-core/         # shared types, units, IDs, config
│   ├── ocw-sim/          # physics, rider state, drafting, session logic (no Bevy)
│   ├── ocw-protocol/     # prost-generated messages + framing (no Bevy)
│   ├── ocw-devices/      # DeviceBackend trait, BLE/FTMS backend (no Bevy)
│   ├── ocw-world/        # package format, tiles, road graph, routes, map matching (no Bevy)
│   ├── ocw-worldgen/     # OSM/DEM import, smoothing, meshing (used by world-builder)
│   ├── ocw-worldstore/   # package files, keys, trusted roots, cache, download (not wasm)
│   ├── ocw-render/       # Bevy plugins: terrain, roads, avatars, bikes, HUD, console
│   ├── ocw-client/       # client logic shared by desktop and web: ClientCore, events, god state, keys, sky (wasm-safe)
│   ├── ocw-assets/       # bike/rider glTF generator and reader, asset validator, pose, animation states (no Bevy)
│   ├── ocw-fit/          # FIT activity writer (no dependencies, wasm-safe)
│   └── ocw-voice/        # LiveKit integration behind a trait (feature "voice")
├── proto/                # .proto schemas
├── artwork/              # original artwork: logos/ (app icon), 3dmodels/ (model files, Phase 15)
├── packaging/            # desktop entry (Linux), later installers
├── scripts/              # build machines, deploy, kiosk, AppImage, Windows build server setup, multiplayer test
├── config/               # build machine config (only examples in git)
├── assets/
│   ├── bicycles/
│   ├── characters/
│   ├── animations/
│   ├── materials/
│   ├── sounds/
│   └── shaders/
├── worlds/
├── tools/
│   ├── asset-validator/
│   ├── osm-converter/
│   └── performance-test/
├── infrastructure/
│   ├── docker/
│   └── deployment/
└── .github/
    └── workflows/
```

Mapping from the original (v1.0) layout:

| Original crate(s) | New crate |
|---|---|
| `cycling-protocol`, `multiplayer` (protocol part) | `ocw-protocol` |
| `cycling-physics`, `simulation`, `training` (sim part) | `ocw-sim` |
| `device-manager`, `bluetooth-ftms` | `ocw-devices` |
| `osm-import`, `terrain`, `road-generator` | `ocw-worldgen` |
| `world` | `ocw-world` |
| `renderer`, `avatar`, `bicycle`, `*-editor` | `ocw-render` and `apps/desktop`; models, pose and animation logic in `ocw-assets` (Bevy-free) |
| `voice` | `ocw-voice` |
| `core`, `platform`, `telemetry` | `ocw-core` (split out when needed) |
| `api`, `game-server`, `account-service`, `world-distribution` | `services/server` (modules) |
| `ant-plus` | deferred; later a second backend in `ocw-devices` |
