## 11. Cross-Platform Build System

Target platforms:

- Linux x86_64.
- Windows x86_64.
- macOS Apple Silicon.
- Optional: Linux ARM64, macOS Intel.

Each platform gets a native CI runner.

### 11.1 Platform Rollout Order

Platforms are implemented one after another, not in parallel:

| Order | Platform | Graphics backend | Bluetooth stack | Packaging |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Linux** x86_64 | Vulkan | BlueZ (D-Bus) | AppImage, Flatpak |
| 2 | **Windows** x86_64 | Direct3D 12 (Vulkan as fallback) | WinRT BLE | EXE/MSI installer, code signing |
| 3 | **macOS** Apple Silicon | Metal | CoreBluetooth | App bundle, DMG, code signing, notarization |

- **Linux is the primary development and test platform** from Phase 1 on. All features are first implemented, tested and released on Linux.
- **Windows** follows once the single-player core runs on Linux (end of Phase 3: real trainer + OSM world).
- **macOS** follows after Windows, before the release-ready milestone (Phase 7).
- Optional targets (Linux ARM64, macOS Intel) come after their main platform.
- The **web companion** is developed alongside, starting in Phase 5 (2.10).
- **Future development (not scheduled):** full web client and native mobile apps (1.3).
- **Portability from day one:** platform-specific code stays behind traits (`ocw-devices`, `ocw-core`). From Phase 1, CI also runs a build-only check (`cargo check` / `cargo clippy`) for Windows and macOS, and a `wasm32-unknown-unknown` build of the core crates.

### 11.2 Build Process

1. Install Rust toolchain.
2. Resolve dependencies.
3. Format code.
4. Run Clippy.
5. Run unit tests.
6. Run integration tests.
7. Create release build.
8. Package assets.
9. Create installers.
10. Publish artifacts.

**Build machines (v1.9):** all building and testing runs on remote machines described in `config/machines.toml` (git-ignored; keys in `config/ssh/`): a Linux machine with a real GPU and Bluetooth (development, tests, smoke screenshots and videos on X11 and Wayland, trainer tests, a kiosk that shows the latest build on its screen), a macOS Apple Silicon machine, and a Windows machine set up with `scripts/setup-windows-buildserver.ps1` (OpenSSH server and a local, non-admin build user). `scripts/remote.sh MACHINE run CMD` copies the working tree (git-tracked and untracked, not ignored) and runs the command; other branches get their own checkout and fewer parallel build jobs, so parallel work does not collide. `scripts/deploy-test.sh` installs a release build for the kiosk.

**Build infrastructure overview (v3.32; README *Build infrastructure* is the how-to).** The pieces and how they fit together:

- **Coordinator and build machines.** The coordinator (deb) holds the main checkout, the agents' git worktrees, `config/` and the build dashboard; it never builds or tests (decided by the user, 2026-11-13). Machine roles (user, 2026-11-13 / 2026-11-14):

  | Machine | System | Role |
  |---|---|---|
  | marge | Debian, 12 cores, AMD GPU, Bluetooth with the Wahoo KICKR, kiosk screen | Main Linux machine: full checks of every merge (fmt, clippy plain and with voice, `cargo test --workspace`, `make test-wasm`), X11 / Wayland screenshots, videos and scene renders, world packages, the kiosk, BLE hardware tests, release AppImages, the multiplayer test's server |
  | leela | Fedora, 16 cores, AMD GPUs, second kiosk screen | **No new jobs since v4.35** (the user, 2026-11-16 evening: "do not put new jobs on leela"; disabled in the build dashboard, running jobs finished, the kiosk (Tenerife) stays). Before: building again v4.00 – v4.35 (heavy Linux work in parallel with marge), excluded 2026-11-13 – 2026-11-16 |
  | macos | Mac M1, 8 cores, 16 GB | macOS builds and checks, the touched crates of a merge, smaller tasks (a crate's tests, clippy, the wasm check) |
  | Win11Builder | Windows 11, 6 cores, 8 GB | **Used normally since v4.26** (user 2026-11-16; before: v4.00 all work but Windows first and only work that can wait, before that Windows-related builds only): any build or test, merge checks included; the Windows checks and release zips run here; `OCW_REMOTE_JOBS=2` (MSVC linker memory) |
  | Weela | Windows, 16 logical cores, data disk D: | **Windows VR machine (v4.35, added by the user 2026-11-16)**: a Meta Quest on USB (Meta Quest Link as the OpenXR runtime) for the Windows VR runs of Phase 11 / 14; otherwise Windows builds and tests. Set up with `scripts/setup-windows-buildserver.ps1 -VR` (SSH, build user, Git with LFS, VS Build Tools, rustup, the OpenXR check) |

- **Configuration** (all git-ignored; a git worktree uses the main checkout's `config/`): `config/machines.toml` (hand-edited copy of the documented `config/machines.example.toml`: `name`, `os`, `host`, `user`, `identity_file`, `shell`, `repo_path`, optional `port`, `slots`, `jobs`, `sccache_size`, `connect_timeout_s`), `config/ssh/` (keys and `known_hosts`, strict host key checking), `config/build-machines.toml` (the dashboard's machine settings, the source of truth for which machines may build), `config/dashboard-token` (the dashboard's write token). `config/` is never copied to a machine; its contents are never printed, logged or committed.
- **`scripts/remote.sh MACHINE ACTION`:** `run CMD` (snapshot, slot, sync, run; `Cargo.lock` copied back; the command's exit code), `sync`, `ssh [CMD]`, `fetch REMOTE_PATH LOCAL_DIR`, `put LOCAL_FILE… REMOTE_DIR` (also git-ignored files, e.g. world data, into the checkout), `field KEY` (a machine setting for scripts), `enabled` (exit 0 / 3) and `slots` (both without ssh). `main` builds in `repo_path`, every other branch in `<repo_path>-<branch>` with its own `target/` (`OCW_REMOTE_DIR` overrides); branch checkouts build with 4 cargo jobs, the main checkout with all cores, a machine's `jobs` caps both, `OCW_REMOTE_JOBS` overrides per call. `data/` and `target/` are never synced: world data is built on the machine or copied with `put`. Further switches: `OCW_REMOTE_SLOTS`, `OCW_SCCACHE=0`, `OCW_BUILD_LOG=0`, `OCW_PROFILE_SWEEP=0`, `OCW_REMOTE_DEPLOY=1`, `OCW_WIN_HANDSHAKE=1`, `OCW_SEED=1`, `OCW_CARGO_SPLIT=1` (the last two off, see below).
- **Task markers:** every `run` keeps a JSON file `/tmp/ocw-tasks/PID-START.json` (Windows: `%TEMP%\ocw-tasks\`) while it runs – checkout, branch, command (one line, ≤ 200 characters), start time (the machine's clock), the remote shell's PID, state (`waiting`, or `running` in slot N) and since when, the machine's slot count – and removes it on exit (EXIT trap / `finally`). The dashboard's jobs and queue come from them, and the cleanup tools check them before touching a checkout. A marker whose PID is gone or was reused is stale: ignored by the dashboard, swept by the next run. Markers hold no hosts, users or keys.
- **Build slot locks:** Linux `flock -n` on `/tmp/ocw-build-slot-N.lock` (fd 9 of the run's shell); macOS (no flock) an atomic `mkdir /tmp/ocw-build-slot-N.d` holding the owner's PID, taken over when that PID is gone (under a second `mkdir` lock); Windows `%TEMP%\ocw-tasks\slot-N.lock` opened with `FileShare.None`. The OS frees each when the run dies; a waiting run gives up when its ssh session ends (Linux, macOS). Order of arrival and slot counts: below.
- **Kiosks and deploys:** `scripts/deploy-test.sh MACHINE` (`make deploy-test`) builds `ocw-desktop` in release (with voice where clang 21 is installed) through `remote.sh run` with `OCW_REMOTE_DEPLOY=1` and installs it into `/var/tmp/ocw` with `ocw-kiosk.sh`, the material library, the world packages built on that machine (manifests and route files beside them) and `ocw-desktop.args` (`scripts/kiosk.args` with the kiosk's world and route, plus the show mode of `scripts/kiosk-show.args`: virtual trainer at 500 W, collisions, hearts and camera shake off); every file copy-then-rename, the binary last, so the kiosk restarts once. Each kiosk keeps its world across deploys (marge: Black Forest north, leela: Tenerife, Puerto de la Cruz – Teide); `OCW_KIOSK_WORLD`, `OCW_KIOSK_ROUTE`, `OCW_KIOSK_ARGS`, `OCW_DEPLOY_WORLD=0|rebuild`, `OCW_WORLD_DATA`, `OCW_DEPLOY_DIR` change it. The kiosk itself is `ocw-kiosk.sh install [--monitor SPEC]`, run once by the desktop user (XDG autostart; restarts the app on every deploy and after crashes, logs in `~/.local/state/ocw/`). Deploys follow user-visible changes. World packages are built on marge only and copied to leela unchanged (`remote.sh marge fetch`, `remote.sh leela put` from the main checkout), with their SHA-256 compared on both machines before the deploy; there is no script for this yet. **The kiosk's game server (user, 2026-11-15, v3.72):** the deploy installs `ocw-server` too; `ocw-kiosk.sh` starts it before the app – the app's world and route from `ocw-desktop.args`, 10 bots (`OCW_KIOSK_BOTS`), UDP `OCW_KIOSK_LISTEN` (default 0.0.0.0:47800), a certificate kept in `~/.local/state/ocw/server-tls` (the fingerprint survives deploys) – waits for its ready line (at most 180 s, then the app rides alone) and runs the app as its client (`--server 127.0.0.1:PORT --insecure-dev`), so other riders can join the kiosk's ride; the join line is in `~/.local/state/ocw/server-connect.txt` (`ocw-kiosk.sh status`); a new build or a crash of either restarts both; `OCW_KIOSK_SERVER=0` turns it off, `OCW_KIOSK_SERVER_ARGS` adds options. *Planned (v4.01, 7.1.1):* the kiosk's `ocw-server` starts the bundled voice server too (nothing to configure), so riders who join the kiosk's ride talk with it. A game server already running on the machine (the UDP port in use, e.g. started by hand) is joined instead of starting another; `OCW_KIOSK_SERVER=join` always joins (waiting up to 180 s for it). A deploy that replaces `ocw-kiosk.sh` makes the running kiosk restart itself with the new script (exec), so kiosk changes need no login on the machine. Tested by `scripts/test-kiosk.sh` with a fake server (the course and options it gets, the app as its client, the join line, the status, both restarted after a server crash, off with `OCW_KIOSK_SERVER=0`).
- **Kiosks joining a remote server (v6.69; asked by the user, 2026-11-26: "have the kiosks connect to the new fly.io server").** `OCW_KIOSK_SERVER=remote` makes `ocw-kiosk.sh` join the server whose join info (11.5 *Join info*) `OCW_KIOSK_REMOTE` names, default `https://ocw-server.fly.dev/join.json`. **At every start of the app** it fetches the info (`curl`, `OCW_KIOSK_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_S` 10 s, at most 64 KB; the values are checked before use: a link of URL characters only, hex hashes, a package id) – never a hash baked in, since the server's certificates change at renewal and on a new volume – and takes the link `join` (`ocw://IPV4?cert=…&world=ID@VERSION`, native QUIC on UDP 47800), or, from a server without that key, the WebTransport link built from `webtransport` and the first (current) of `cert_hashes` (`https://IPV4:47801?cert-hash=…&world=…`; the desktop joins `https://` links too). The server's world is found among the packages of the kiosk dir by `world_sha256` (hashes cached by mtime, inode and size), without a hash by the manifest's id and version. The app then starts with `--join LINK` and `OCW_ARGS_FILE=~/.local/state/ocw/remote.args`: `ocw-desktop.args` without its course and server options (`--world`, `--route`, `--bots`, …) plus `--world PACKAGE` and `--bots 0`; **no local `ocw-server`, no bots** – the riders are the server's (the Fly server runs `--bots 0 --echo-bot`: no bots, the Echo rider; bots there would be `OCW_SERVER_ARGS` in `fly.toml`, unchanged). Voice comes with the server's grants (`wss://ocw-server.fly.dev`); the kiosk app is built with `voice`. **Reconnecting:** the kiosk reads the app log; `joined HOST: …` is logged once, `Disconnected: …` or `join failed: …` restarts the app with freshly fetched join info (after 5 s; after a failed join 5, 10, 20 s). **Fallback (decided here: keep a ride on the screen rather than wait):** a world that is not installed or differs falls back at once; join info that cannot be fetched and joins that fail fall back after `OCW_KIOSK_REMOTE_TRIES` (3) attempts in a row (`OCW_KIOSK_REMOTE_DELAY_S` 5 s, doubled); the fallback is the local mode (`OCW_KIOSK_SERVER=1`: the kiosk's own `ocw-server` with bots, or the app alone), the kiosk log says why, and every `OCW_KIOSK_REMOTE_RETRY_S` (60 s) the join info is fetched again: once it can join, the kiosk switches back (one failure then falls back at once again). **Settings files:** `OCW_KIOSK_DIR/kiosk.env` (from `scripts/kiosk.env`, written by every deploy: `OCW_KIOSK_SERVER=remote`, `OCW_KIOSK_REMOTE=https://ocw-server.fly.dev/join.json`) and `kiosk-local.env` (machine-local, never written by a deploy, read first) hold `OCW_KIOSK_*=VALUE` lines, read at every kiosk start (not sourced); a variable set in the environment wins; a deploy that changes one restarts a running kiosk on it (as with a new `ocw-kiosk.sh`). Nothing here starts a kiosk: they stay stopped until the user starts one (`ocw-kiosk.sh install` or `run` on the desktop), and then it joins Fly. `ocw-kiosk.sh dry-run` prints the mode, the join link, the matched package, the arguments file and the app's command without starting anything; `status` shows the last join. **The Windows VR kiosk** (`ocw-kiosk.ps1`, 11I) has the same mode as an option – `OCW_KIOSK_SERVER=remote` in `kiosk-local.env` / `kiosk.env` of its folder or the task's environment (no deploy writes them), the package searched in `worlds\`, the app's `--vr` and window options kept, `ocw-kiosk.ps1 dry-run` – and keeps the app's local server by default (Phase 11 Q14 / Q15). Tests: `scripts/test-kiosk.sh` with a fake join info server (the settings files and the environment winning, the dry run, the link and arguments, no local server, a dropped connection re-fetching a new certificate, two failed joins falling back and switching back, a world mismatch falling back and switching once the world matches, the WebTransport link of a server without `join`, a fetch failure retried then falling back); `ocw-kiosk.ps1 selftest` (`make test-kiosk-windows`) for the PowerShell side.
- **Profiling and measuring:** `scripts/build-profile.sh` / `.ps1` (below), `scripts/world-profile.sh` (world packages with the builder's stage profile, byte-for-byte against reference packages, 4.7), `scripts/world-clean-compare.sh li|bf` (with and without the world cleaning, 4.8), `scripts/measure-fps.sh` (the render rate of a binary on a headless weston with the GPU, builds compared interleaved, 15), `scripts/measure.py` (wall time and peak memory of a command).
- **Test and media harness (11.4):** the `make test-*` targets run on the build machines; the run-ocw skill's `drive.sh` (`shot`, `shot-wayland`, `video`, `video-wayland`) archives every screenshot and video in `test-output/YYYY-MM-DD/` with commit and mode in the name and a row in `test-output/index.md` (the build history); `scripts/render-scenes.sh` renders `scripts/scenes.toml` (`--remote`, `--pick` into `test-output/build-history/`); `scripts/collect-test-output.sh` merges the agents' worktrees' media into the main checkout's `test-output/` (never overwriting); `scripts/test-remote.sh`, `test-kiosk.sh` and `test-release-version.sh` test the infrastructure scripts without a machine; `scripts/test-multiplayer.sh` (11.4.1) and the `scripts/test-web*.py` runs (Phase 10) the network and browser paths. Nothing in `test-output/` is deleted: the art project ([OCW-ART](https://github.com/newkit/OCW-ART), its own repository since v3.50) uses all of it.
- **Releases and world builds:** 11.3 (versions, `make release-*`, `scripts/build-appimage.sh`, `scripts/build-macos-app.sh`, the Windows zip, `scripts/prepare-world-release.sh`) and 4.7 (`scripts/fetch-pilot.sh`, `fetch-imagery.sh`, `fetch-forest.sh`, `build-liechtenstein.sh`, `build-blackforest.sh`, `build-tenerife.sh`, run on marge in its main checkout, where `data/` lives).
- **Build log (for the art project):** `test-output/build-log/DAY/` of the main checkout: `runs.jsonl` and `HHMMSS-MACHINE-PID.log` per `remote.sh run` (below), `servers.jsonl` (the dashboard's masked status once a minute), `machines.jsonl` (machine settings) and `janitor.jsonl` (every deletion); `test-output/answers/` for the dashboard's answers.
- **Security:** keys and hosts stay in `config/`; `remote.sh` replaces host, `user@host` and the key path by the machine name in every log it keeps, the dashboard masks addresses, `user@host`, home directories and MAC addresses in everything it stores or serves, the multiplayer test replaces addresses by `<ip>` / `<server>`; scripts read hosts only through `field` and never print them; the dashboard's write actions need its token (11.2.1).

**Build id:** every desktop build carries a build id: the workspace version, the short git commit, `-dirty` for uncommitted changes to tracked files and ` (debug)` for debug builds (e.g. `0.1.0-63910f2-dirty`). It is shown small in the HUD's lower right corner, by `ocw-desktop --version` and in the startup log. Remote builds get no `.git`, so `scripts/remote.sh` passes the commit as `OCW_BUILD_ID` (`scripts/build-id.sh`); otherwise the build script asks `git`.

**Build profile and speed-up (decided 2026-11-13, v2.59).** `scripts/build-profile.sh` (Linux, macOS; `scripts/build-profile.ps1` on Windows; `make build-profile MACHINE=…`) times clean, no-op, touched-file and edited-file builds of `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-run`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, the voice release build of `ocw-desktop` and the wasm check, with cargo's `--timings` reports, into `test-output/build-profile/LABEL/` (`results.jsonl`, `summary.md` with the slowest crates, `scripts/build_profile.py compare A B` for before/after tables). Measured on 2026-11-13 (marge: 12 cores, shared with other builds; macOS: M1, 8 cores; Windows: 2 jobs):

| Machine | Command | before: clean / edit one file (full debug info) | after: clean / edit (v2.59 profile) | `target/` after clean | sccache, same checkout path | sccache, a second checkout (other path) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| marge | `build --workspace` | 646 s / 5.3–7.8 s | 464 s (−28 %) / 3.7–6.7 s | 16.2 → 4.2 GB | – | 380 s cold → 322 s (−15 %, 87 % hits) |
| marge | `test --workspace --no-run` | 613 s / 4.5–16.8 s | 457 s (−25 %) / 2.3–5.6 s | 24.0 → 5.3 GB | 173 s (−62 %) | 173 s |
| marge | `clippy --all-targets` | 99 s / 1.4–2.6 s (touch) | – | 1.3 GB | – | 125 s cold → 95 s (−24 %) |
| marge | release, voice | 276 s / 11–27 s (touch) | unchanged profile | 3.9 GB | – | 429 s cold → 309 s (−28 %) |
| Mac | `build --workspace` | 642 s / 2.0–4.6 s (touch) | 496 s (−23 %) / 2.0–4.5 s | 4.3 GB | 119–125 s (−76 %) | 508 s cold → 437 s (−14 %, 81 % hits) |
| Mac | `test --workspace --no-run` | 690 s / 2.0–6.6 s (touch) | – | 4.6 GB | 142–145 s (−79 %) | 360 s → 357 s |
| Mac | `clippy --all-targets` | 151 s / 1.3–2.4 s (touch) | – | 1.2 GB | 111–120 s | – |
| Mac | release, voice | 456 s / 15–34 s (touch) | unchanged profile | 4.8 GB | – | 471 s cold |
| Win11Builder (2 jobs) | `build --workspace` | 3,673 s / 158 s (touch and edit) | 2,564 s (−30 %) / 34–37 s (−78 %); no-op 9.2 → 5.1 s | 18.0 → 5.6 GB | – | not measured yet: sccache is installed and used by `remote.sh`, but the single Windows slot stayed taken by other builds for over an hour (`scripts/build-profile.ps1` in two checkouts, as on the Mac) |

No-op builds take 0.3–0.8 s everywhere; the wasm check is cached by cargo like any other build. The machines were shared with other agents' builds during the measurements (load 3–28 on marge's 12 cores), so single numbers vary by ±20 %; before/after pairs were run back to back. Within a cold run sccache already hit 30–50 % (the same crate built for build, test and clippy). Across checkouts it hits 80–87 % of the compile requests but saves only 14–28 % of the time: the misses are the big crates (Bevy, wgpu, naga, x11rb, …), whose inputs name the checkout path (the `OUT_DIR` of build scripts ends up in the metadata of every crate built on them), and binaries, proc macros and build-script runs are never cached. `SCCACHE_BASEDIRS` (set by `remote.sh`, client-side hashing) did not change that for Rust (Mac: 437 s → 477 s at higher load), and `--remap-path-prefix` with the checkout path made every Rust key unique (0 % hits). The full win needs the same path: a checkout rebuilt after `make remote-gc` or `cargo clean` takes Bevy from the cache (−62 to −79 %).

Decisions:

- **Debug info:** `[profile.dev]` `debug = "line-tables-only"` for the workspace crates (backtraces keep file and line), `debug = false` for the dependencies. Full debug info made each checkout's `target/` 30–80 GB on marge (148 GB in the main checkout) and is what the links of the many Bevy test binaries spent their time on.
- **Build caching across agent checkouts, without interference.** Every agent worktree keeps its own remote checkout and its own `target/` – a `target/` is never shared (cargo locks it for a whole build, so the two slots would run one after the other, and different feature sets and checkouts would overwrite each other's artefacts and binaries). What was built and measured:
  - **Compiler cache:** `sccache` on the machine's local disk, content-addressed (a hit needs the same compiler, arguments, environment and sources, so parallel checkouts cannot hand each other a wrong artefact), shared by all checkouts there. Pinned release, SHA-256 checked: `make deps-sccache` (Linux x86_64, macOS arm64; `~/.local/bin/sccache`), `make deps-sccache-windows MACHINE=…` (MSVC build, `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\sccache.exe`, `scripts/install-sccache.ps1`); installed on marge, the Mac and Win11Builder. `scripts/remote.sh` sets `RUSTC_WRAPPER` on all three whenever it is installed (`OCW_SCCACHE=0` turns it off; cache size `sccache_size` in `machines.toml`, default 30 GB). Most dependency compile requests hit across checkouts (80–87 %), the big crates do not (see above); workspace crates of debug builds are incremental and compiled as before; binaries, proc macros and build-script runs are never cached.
  - **Seeding:** a new checkout (no `target/` yet) on Linux or macOS starts with a copy-on-write clone of the main checkout's `target/debug`, `target/release` and `target/build-voice` (`cp --reflink=always` on Btrfs/XFS, `cp -c` – clonefile – on APFS), so cargo finds the dependencies built; the clone shares disk blocks until a file is rewritten. A probe file tells whether the file system clones; where it does not (marge: ext4, Windows: NTFS) nothing is copied and sccache does the work. Skipped while a build runs in the main checkout (no half-written artefacts). **Opt-in** (`OCW_SEED=1`): on the Mac the clone took 46 s and no extra disk, but cargo still rebuilt 358 of 529 crates (899 s, slower than a clean build under the same load), because the main checkout's `target/` came from another dependency and profile state; so seeding stays off until a seed from the same dependency state is measured to beat sccache alone.
  - **One build directory per feature set (measured, opt-in):** the premise was that alternating plain and voice clippy runs in one `target/` rebuilt each other's dependencies. `scripts/cargo-shim/cargo`, first on `PATH` with `OCW_CARGO_SPLIT=1` (the Makefile keeps it first via `OCW_CARGO_SHIM`), gives a cargo call naming the voice feature `CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR={workspace-root}/target/build-voice` (cargo's `build.build-dir`; the binaries still land in `target/debug` and `target/release`). Measured on marge: without the split, plain / voice / plain / voice clippy took 199 / 153 / 0.7 / 0.5 s (with `CC=clang-21` only on the voice calls, as `make` and `deploy-test.sh` do; 98 / 81 / 0.3 / 0.4 s with the same environment) – cargo 1.99 keeps both feature sets' artefacts side by side and nothing is rebuilt; with the split 153 / 216 / 0.7 / 0.7 s and 2.3 GB more, because the voice build compiles the shared dependencies again. So the split stays off; the commands users type are unchanged either way.
- **Disk:** `make remote-gc` (`scripts/remote-gc.sh`) lists the `target/` of every remote agent checkout whose branch is gone, or merged into main with its worktree removed (a new agent's branch looks merged: it has no commits yet), with its size per machine; `GC=1` deletes them. The main checkout, the sccache cache, the checkouts themselves and checkouts with a running or waiting task are kept. On 2026-11-13 it found 394 GB on marge, 77 GB on the Mac and 12 GB on Win11Builder.
- **Cleanup on merge (v2.63):** `scripts/remote-gc.sh --branch <branch>` (`make remote-gc-branch BRANCH=…`, `--dry-run` lists only) deletes the `target/` of that branch's checkout on every reachable machine (unreachable ones are skipped); the coordinator runs it after merging or abandoning an agent branch. A checkout with a live task marker (running or waiting) is never touched – the machine checks again right before deleting, and `target/` is renamed before it is removed, so a run starting meanwhile never sees half of it. Deletions are logged like the janitor's.
- **Disk watcher and janitor (v2.63, `tools/build-dashboard/janitor.py`):** the dashboard's poll reports per machine the disk of the home directory and, if another, the one holding the checkouts (Windows: the checkouts' drive and C:, which holds the user profile), as df's use (used / (used + free)). When the checkouts' disk is above a threshold, the janitor frees space, one machine per pass and at most one pass every 10 minutes (the fullest machine first):
  - **> 75 %:** the `target/` of agent checkouts whose branch is merged into main (worktree removed) or gone, unused for 2 h (last use: `.ocw-last-run`, which `remote.sh` touches on every run, else the newest of `target/*/deps`, `.fingerprint`, `incremental`); and in the main checkout's `target/` the build units unused for 3 days that a newer unit of the same crate and kind replaced – a unit is cargo's `<crate>-<hash>` (fingerprint, `deps/` files with that hash, build-script output), its age the later of access and modification time of its files (marge mounts with `noatime`), the kind (lib, bin, test, build script, its run) from the fingerprint's file names – plus incremental session directories unused for 3 days (like cargo-sweep; a unit still in use is at worst rebuilt from sccache);
  - **> 85 %:** also the `target/` of the least recently used agent checkouts idle for more than 24 h (sources kept), oldest first, until the disk is estimated below 85 %;
  - **> 92 %:** a red banner on the dashboard and a log line (no other notice).
  Never deleted: the sources of any checkout, checkouts with a running or waiting task, the sccache cache, `data/` (world data), `test-output/` (the art project keeps everything: its size on the coordinator is only shown), anything not ending in `<checkout>/target` or inside the main checkout's units. Every deletion (and every planned one in dry-run mode, once per plan) is a JSON line in `test-output/build-log/DAY/janitor.jsonl` (machine, path relative to the checkouts' directory, size, reason, threshold) for the art project. `--janitor off|dry-run|on` (default on); `--janitor-plan` / `make janitor-plan` prints what each threshold would delete on every reachable machine now. The decisions are pure and unit-tested (`test_janitor.py`, also the sweep against a scratch `target/`).
- **Dev profile change (v2.63):** `remote.sh` keeps a hash of Cargo.toml's `[profile.dev*]` / `[profile.test*]` sections in `.ocw-profile-hash` next to `target/`; when it changes, `target/debug` is removed once before the build (cargo would rebuild everything anyway and keep the old artefacts beside the new ones), unless another run of the checkout is building; logged to `janitor.jsonl`. `OCW_PROFILE_SWEEP=0` turns it off.
- **Fixed limits:** the sccache cache stays at 30 GB per machine (`SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE`, the machine's `sccache_size`). On Windows the toolchain and the cache move off C: (the system drive, which also holds the user profile) to the build drive: `scripts/windows-move-toolchain.ps1` (`make windows-move-toolchain MACHINE=…`, a dry run with the sizes on C: by default; `APPLY=1` copies with robocopy, checks file count and bytes, sets the user variables `CARGO_HOME`, `RUSTUP_HOME`, `SCCACHE_DIR` and `PATH`, verifies `cargo --version` and `rustc --version` from the new place, restores the old variables on failure, and only then removes the old directories); `remote.sh` puts `%CARGO_HOME%\bin` first on `PATH`.
- **Tree copy (v2.63):** `remote.sh run` / `sync` take a **snapshot** of the working tree (tracked and untracked, not ignored, without `config/`) into a temporary directory the moment they are called; a run syncs that snapshot only once it holds its build slot: the remote side prints `@@ocw-sync PID` after taking the slot and waits for a line on stdin, `remote.sh` syncs and answers `go` (or `fail`), then closes stdin (Linux, macOS; on Windows opt-in with `OCW_WIN_HANDSHAKE=1`, because in its first runs the PowerShell side stayed waiting after the sync and it could not be tested further – by default Windows syncs the snapshot right away, before waiting for its slot). Before, a run waiting for a slot could build a tree it was not called with (a half-merged main checkout, or a later run's sync). **No source mtimes:** rsync and tar kept the files' original mtimes, so a file replaced by an older version (a revert, a branch switch) looked older than the build that had compiled the newer one, and cargo kept the stale artefact. Now rsync compares by content (`--checksum`, no `-t`): unchanged files are not touched, changed ones get the time of the copy. Windows (tar): a manifest in the checkout (`.ocw-sync/manifest.tsv`: SHA-1, size and mtime of each file as written) tells which files are unchanged there; only the others are sent, unpacked with `tar -m`. Nothing relies on the remote mtime being older: a changed file is always written at the time of the copy, so it is newer than any earlier build there – also after the remote files were touched into the future to force a rebuild and newer content then arrived with an older local (merge-time) mtime, which left stale artefacts on Win11Builder on 2026-11-13 (regression test in `scripts/test-remote.sh`); a file touched on the machine no longer matches its manifest entry and is re-sent. **New checkouts (v2.95):** the manifest diff used awk's `NR == FNR`, which is also true for the second file when the first (the machine's list of unchanged files) is empty – so a new agent checkout on Win11Builder got "sending 0 changed of 397 files", only `.ocw-sync/` and an empty manifest, and cargo failed without `rust-toolchain.toml`. Now: the list is read with `getline`; a file is only skipped when it exists there with the manifest's size and mtime and the manifest's header names this checkout (`# ocw-sync v2<TAB>REPO`; a copied or older manifest counts as none, so existing checkouts get one full send); the manifest is only written when `tar.exe` succeeded; and when files of the snapshot are missing there after the sync, the whole tree is sent once more (still missing = failed sync). `scripts/test-remote.sh` tests the snapshot, the mtimes, the handshake, the manifest diff, the Windows sync against a simulated machine (new checkout, re-sync, files deleted there, stale manifests, failed extraction, the safety net) and the profile check.
- **Stale files (v6.48):** a file removed or moved away here (`git mv`) is deleted in the machine's checkout too. Before, the sync only knew the current file list (rsync `--delete-missing-args` deletes only listed paths that are missing; the macOS openrsync and Windows tar paths send only present files), so old copies stayed and broke builds there ("module found at both workshop.rs and workshop/mod.rs"). Each sync now leaves the list of the files it sent in the checkout (`.ocw-sync/synced.txt`; Windows: the paths of `.ocw-sync/manifest.tsv`) and, **before** copying, deletes there exactly the files of the previous list that are not in the new one (before, so a case-only rename on macOS / Windows deletes the old name and the new file is then sent). Only files an earlier sync sent: build outputs, git-ignored and other files of the machine stay, and nothing under `config/`, `target/`, `data/`, `test-output/`, `.git/` or `.ocw-sync/` is ever deleted; absolute paths, paths with `..` (Windows also drive letters and backslashes) and files reached through a symlinked directory (Windows: a junction) leading out of the checkout are refused and reported; only files and symlinks are removed, plus the directories they leave empty up to the checkout. A checkout without a list (its first sync since) deletes nothing and says so in one line. No extra ssh call: Linux / macOS run it in the `mkdir` call before rsync (the new list on stdin), Windows reads the old list with the manifest and deletes in the call that already removed the files deleted here (in chunks of 100 paths). `remote.sh` prints the number and first names of the deleted files. `scripts/test-remote.sh` runs the Linux and macOS sync end to end against a scratch machine (a fake `ssh` running bash, rsync locally) and the Windows one against its simulated machine: a moved file and its emptied directory disappear, build outputs, git-ignored files, `config/` and never-sent files stay, `..`, absolute and symlinked-directory paths are refused, the first sync deletes nothing.
- **Open questions in the dashboard (v2.63):** `tools/build-dashboard/spec_questions.py` reads every `- **Q<n> – …**` bullet of this spec (mostly the *Open questions (for the user)* subsections of 14): phase, section, id ("Phase 12 Q1"), title, text, the proposal ("Proposal: …", "(proposal)", "(recommended)"), and the status – decided when the bold label says *decided* or *postponed*. Milestones that name an open question are listed as blocked work. The spec stays the single source; the dashboard re-reads the main checkout's file when its mtime changes and shows the questions by phase (decided ones behind a toggle), in `--once` and in `/api/status`. **Answering on the dashboard:** each open question has an answer box and quick buttons ("Accept proposal", the options it lists); an answer is appended to `test-output/answers/answers.jsonl` of the main checkout (git-ignored, for the art project too; ISO time, question id, the exact question text from the spec, answer; a later answer supersedes an earlier one) and as one line to `test-output/answers/inbox.log`, which the coordinator watches (also `GET /api/answers?since=<ts>`) to record the decision in this spec; until then the question shows "answered – waiting for the coordinator", afterwards the parser shows it decided. Writing needs the random token in the git-ignored `config/dashboard-token` (created on first start, 0600; entered once on the page, kept in the browser, sent as a header; 403 without it); reading stays open; the token is never logged. Mobile, keyboard and touch usable; all text HTML-escaped (tested in `test_answers.py`, also the round trip, superseding and the 403).
- **Machines enabled/disabled and their slots (v2.66):** each machine card of the build dashboard has an Enabled/Disabled toggle (disabling asks for an optional reason), a build slots stepper (1–8; 0 = no limit only by hand or with `OCW_REMOTE_SLOTS=0`) and a short note; changes need the dashboard token (403 without it; machine names only from `machines.toml`, slots a JSON integer, text without control characters, at most 200 characters, HTML-escaped on the page). They are stored in `config/build-machines.toml` of the main checkout (git-ignored, the `[[machine]]` format of `machines.toml`, which stays the user's hand-edited file; `tools/build-dashboard/build_machines.py list|set` from a shell) and logged as JSON lines in `test-output/build-log/DAY/machines.jsonl` (who, when, old and new values). `scripts/remote.sh` reads it: `run` and `sync` on a disabled machine fail at once with the reason and exit code 3; `ssh`, `field`, `fetch`, `put` stay allowed, and deploys too (`deploy-test.sh` sets `OCW_REMOTE_DEPLOY=1`, so a kiosk on a disabled machine still gets new builds); `remote.sh MACHINE enabled` / `slots` answer without ssh (the multiplayer test skips disabled bot machines). Slot count: `OCW_REMOTE_SLOTS` (one call) > the dashboard's > `machines.toml` > OS default; a changed count applies to runs started afterwards, a running run keeps its slot (also one above a lowered count) and finishes normally. The dashboard's poll and the janitor still probe disabled machines (read-only, and the janitor's `target/` cleanup); disabled machines' slots are left out of the overview's total. Initial state (2026-11-13): leela disabled ("excluded by the user", kiosk only), Win11Builder enabled with 1 slot for Windows-related builds only, marge (2) and the Mac (1) enabled. Tested in `test_build_machines.py` (parsing, defaults, the endpoint, escaped cards) and `scripts/test-remote.sh` (refusal, deploy exception, slot precedence, a lowered count with a run still in a higher slot).
- **Build slots in order of arrival:** a waiting run leaves a free slot to an older waiting run (Linux/macOS; before, the first poll won and a run waited 28 min while later ones went ahead; the Windows path still takes the first free slot). `scripts/test-remote.sh` (`make test-remote`) tests the rule and the choice of `remote-gc`.
- **Build log:** each run in `test-output/build-log/*/runs.jsonl` also records `sync_s` (copying the tree: 341 files, 7.7 MB, about 1 s – not worth optimising), cargo's own `Finished … in` time (`cargo_s`), the crates compiled (`compiled`) and the build-slot wait (`wait_s`); the art journal (OCW-ART's `diary.py`) shows compile hours, crates and waiting hours per machine.
- **Rejected:** a faster linker on Linux (Rust 1.99 links x86_64 Linux with `rust-lld` already; the incremental builds are 2–13 s); `lld-link` on Windows (the MSVC CRT setup of the voice backend, `+crt-static`, would need its own verification, and Windows builds are rare); Bevy feature trimming (UI, picking, audio, glTF, gamepads are used; `bevy_ui_render` pulls in `bevy_sprite_render`; it would need a screenshot check for each feature for a gain of a few percent of a clean build); a shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` or build directory per machine (see above); seeding by a full copy or hard links where the file system cannot clone (a copy of 30+ GB takes minutes; hard links are unsafe because cargo rewrites fingerprint files in place); incremental release builds (shipped binaries stay as they are); limiting the wasm check to changed crates (a no-op check takes under a second).

**CI resilience (v1.9):** the Linux job's package installation retries with short timeouts and a step timeout, so an unreachable distribution mirror fails within minutes instead of holding a runner for hours.

#### 11.2.1 Build dashboard

The **build dashboard** (`tools/build-dashboard/`, details in its `README.md`) is the one place to see and steer the build infrastructure; it was asked for by the user on 2026-11-12 and grown since. Requirements:

- **What it is:** a small web page and JSON API (`/api/status`), Python 3 standard library only, running on the coordinator (deb) as the systemd user service `ocw-build-dashboard` on port 8765 (`make dashboard-install`; `systemctl --user restart ocw-build-dashboard`); `--once` prints the status as text, `--once --json` as JSON. It reads the main checkout's `config/` and never shows host names, users, addresses or keys (everything goes through the same masker as the build log).
- **Start and install (documented v3.32):** `make dashboard-install` writes `tools/build-dashboard/ocw-build-dashboard.service` with the checkout's path into `~/.config/systemd/user/`, reloads systemd and enables and starts it (`dashboard.py --port 8765`, all addresses; starts at every login, `Restart=on-failure` after 10 s; `sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER` once to start at boot without a login; logs with `journalctl --user -u ocw-build-dashboard`; `make dashboard-uninstall` removes it). By hand: `python3 tools/build-dashboard/dashboard.py [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port N]`; `--janitor-plan` (`make janitor-plan`, with `--no-record`) prints the janitor's dry run for every reachable machine and exits; `--no-answers` / `--no-machine-settings` make the page read-only; `--no-context` describes jobs from their commands only. It is opened at `http://<coordinator>:8765/` from any device on the LAN, a phone included.
- **Page layout:** a red banner for disks above 92 % and the coordinator's red alerts, an amber one for its softer alerts; the overview (machines online, running, waiting, slots used of the total of enabled machines, open questions); the coordinator card and the Claude tasks side by side (v3.54); one card per machine (state and error kind, CPU, load, memory, swap, disks, uptime; the build settings; slots and their holders; the queue; the running tasks with their purpose sentence and per-process CPU / memory; the kiosk); the open questions with answer boxes and the blocked work; the janitor (mode, last pass per machine, recent log, the size of `test-output/`). The page refreshes every 5 s.
- **Machines:** every machine of `config/machines.toml` polled every 5 s over one SSH call (read-only snippet, shared control socket): online / unreachable with the error kind, CPU, load, memory, swap, disks (home and checkout volumes; Windows: the checkout drive and C:), uptime; the kiosk state where `/var/tmp/ocw` exists (app running, deployed build, connected Bluetooth devices by name).
- **Jobs:** the running `remote.sh` runs (from their task markers) with checkout, command, running time, slot and the CPU / memory per process kind; the queue of runs waiting for a build slot (oldest first); the slots in use per machine. **Each job is described in one sentence by what it tries to achieve** (decided 2026-11-13, replacing the user's prompt): built by fixed rules from the command (checks, tests, wasm, release builds, deploys, world builds, renders, profiling …) and its context (the agent's task, or the latest commit / merge of the main checkout), at most 140 characters, the full breakdown as a tooltip (`--show-prompts` still puts the prompt into the JSON).
- **The coordinator (deb)** (v3.54; asked 2026-11-15 after deb ran out of memory at 00:39 that night): a card for the machine the dashboard runs on, read locally and cheaply (standard library, `/proc` and `/sys`, one `/proc/PID/stat` read per process; `du`, `journalctl` and `systemctl` throttled and time-limited) and without root. **Memory:** total, available, used, swap; the top 5 processes by RSS with name and RSS only (no command lines, no environment: they can hold secrets and paths); group sums for Claude Code (`claude`, its versioned binary), cargo/rustc (they should not run there), ffmpeg, python, QEMU VMs, browsers. **OOM kills:** systemd's unit OOM messages from the user journal (the unit, e.g. `ocw-build-dashboard.service`; checked every 5 min and at once when `/proc/vmstat`'s `oom_kill` grows), the kernel's "Killed process N (name)" when the kernel log or `dmesg` can be read (group `adm` / `systemd-journal`, or `kernel.dmesg_restrict=0`; otherwise marked "not readable"). **CPU:** load against the cores, PSI of cpu, memory and io. **Disks:** `/`, `/home`, `/home/claude`, `/tmp`, each only when it is its own mount, deduplicated by device (tmpfs marked "in RAM"); the sizes of OCW's `target/`, `test-output/`, `.claude/worktrees/`, OCW-ART's `build-history/` and `.git` with its LFS objects (niced `du -sx`, every 10 min, at most 60 s each). **Activity:** Claude Code sessions (claude processes without a claude parent) and their RSS, OCW's worktrees, ffmpeg and QEMU processes, the art timer (`systemctl --user show ocw-art-collect.timer`: state, next run), the dashboard's memory (its cgroup when it runs as the unit) against `MemoryMax`. **Alerts** (thresholds in one place, `coordinator.THRESHOLDS`, amber / red): memory available below 25 % or 4 GiB / below 15 % or 2 GiB; swap used above 50 % / 80 %; a disk above 85 % / 90 %; an OOM kill in the last 7 days / 24 h; memory pressure (some, 1 min) above 10 % / 30 %; load per core above 1.5 / 3; the dashboard above 75 % / 90 % of its `MemoryMax`; any cargo/rustc process (amber). **History:** a sample a minute as one JSON line in `test-output/build-log/DAY/deb.jsonl` (time, memory, load, PSI, disks, group sums, top processes by name, counts, alert kinds; `--record` / `--no-record` like `servers.jsonl`, which leaves the card out), 24 h in memory and read back on start; the page draws sparklines of the last 6 h (memory available, load, root disk free; inline SVG). `--no-coordinator` turns the card and the Claude tasks off.
- **Claude tasks** (v3.54; asked 2026-11-15 before the move of the coordinator to another user): a section next to the coordinator card (`claude_tasks` in the status, a block in `--once`). The tasks come from the coordinator's agent log `test-output/build-log/DAY/agents.jsonl` (OCW-ART's `diary.py agent-event`, masked; today and the two days before): the last event decides – started / resumed = running (with branch, start, running time, last event), interrupted listed with them, reported / merged / abandoned in the last 24 h behind a toggle. **Liveness** only from the mtime and size of Claude Code's task file `/tmp/claude-*/<project>/<session>/tasks/<task id>.output` (matched by task id; the glob also finds another user's): growing / active, "idle / waiting" when unchanged for over 20 min, "unknown" without a file; the files are full transcripts and are never opened, and session ids are never shown. **Worktrees** of OCW's main checkout and of OCW-ART (`git worktree list --porcelain`, `for-each-ref`, `branch --merged`, every 2 min; commit counts cached): last commit (short hash, subject, age), commits not in `main`, merged into `main`, pushed (against `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`, never fetched); linked to tasks by branch (or `worktree-agent-<id>`); listed: main, unmerged branches with commits and those of a task, the rest as counts. **Cutover check** at the top: "Cutover OK: no running tasks, no remote runs", or the list of running tasks and remote runs (the job queue of the machines), with the number of Claude Code sessions on the coordinator.
- **Machines enabled / disabled and build slots** (v2.66): a toggle and a slot stepper (1–8) per machine card, with an optional reason and note; stored in `config/build-machines.toml`; `scripts/remote.sh` refuses `run` / `sync` on a disabled machine (deploys stay allowed) and takes the slot count from it.
- **Agents on the coordinator** (v4.20; asked 2026-11-16): how many agents may run on deb at once, chosen by the user on the Coordinator card (− N +, 1–16, default 5; the dashboard token), stored as `[coordinator] max_agents` in `config/build-machines.toml` (before the machines; `remote.sh`'s lookup skips it) and in `/api/status` (`agents`: limit, running, free, level, available memory). The card and the Claude tasks header show "agents N of M" – N the running tasks of `agents.jsonl` (last event started / resumed) – amber at the limit, red above it. `scripts/agent-slots.sh` gives a session the same numbers without the dashboard (exit 0 when a slot is free, 3 when not); sessions check it before spawning an agent and wait while it is full.
- **Disk janitor** (v2.63): disk use per machine, automatic cleanup of build output above 75 % / 85 %, a red banner above 92 %; never sources, data, test output, the sccache cache or busy checkouts; every deletion logged. Snippets for POSIX machines run under `/bin/sh`, never the login shell (the Mac's is zsh, where an unmatched glob aborts the command; fixed v3.28).
- **Open questions and answers** (v2.63): every question for the user in this spec, grouped by phase with its proposal and options, decided ones hidden; **answerable on the page** (text box, "Accept proposal", option buttons) with the token from `config/dashboard-token`; answers go to `test-output/answers/answers.jsonl` and `inbox.log`, which the coordinator watches and records in this spec (the question then shows as decided). Blocked milestones are listed.
- **Build log and art project:** every `remote.sh run` is recorded in `test-output/build-log/DAY/` (`runs.jsonl` with machine, command, times, exit code, sync / cargo / slot-wait seconds, and the run's output; `machines.jsonl` and `janitor.jsonl` for machine and janitor changes); the dashboard adds its masked status once a minute as `servers.jsonl` (`--record-interval`, `--no-record`) – material for the OCW Build Diary (OCW-ART's `ART-PROJECT.md`). The page itself does not show the build log.
- **Security:** reading is open on the LAN (`--host 127.0.0.1` keeps it to the coordinator); the token is entered once per browser and kept in its localStorage, never logged, served or written to the answer files; every change (answers, machine settings) needs the token (header `X-OCW-Token`, 403 without it); all text shown is HTML-escaped; inputs are validated (machine names only from `machines.toml`, slots 1–8).
- **Phone friendly:** the page works at phone width and with touch, keyboard and mouse.
- **Tests:** `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/build-dashboard -p "test_*.py"` (run on a build machine via `remote.sh`), no network needed; the coordinator's and the tasks' tests use fixture text, a fake `/proc` and fake task files in a temp directory (never the real `/proc`), and check that no command line, environment or transcript content reaches the status.

### 11.3 Packaging

**Linux:** AppImage, Flatpak, optionally native packages.

**Windows:** EXE/MSI, code signing, installer.

**macOS:** app bundle, code signing, Apple notarization, DMG.

Build and release pipelines are automated for all three operating systems, introduced in the rollout order (11.1).

**Implemented so far (v1.9):**

- **App icon and desktop integration:** the logo (`artwork/logos/`, a unicorn riding a bike over a rainbow) is the window icon (X11, Windows); the window's app id `ocw-desktop` matches the desktop entry (`packaging/linux/ocw-desktop.desktop`), which Wayland compositors, docks and menus use. On Linux the app installs its desktop entry and hicolor icons into the user's data directory at start (only changed files).
- **Windows icon and version info (v4.64):** `ocw-desktop.exe`, `ocw-server.exe` and `ocw-studio.exe` carry the logo as their icon (Explorer, taskbar, shortcuts such as the VR kiosk's *OCW VR Kiosk – Start / Stop*) and a version block (product *Open Cycling World*, file description, file and product version = the workspace version). Each app's `build.rs` calls `ocw_winres::embed` (`crates/ocw-winres`, no dependencies but `png`): it builds the icon from the PNGs of `artwork/logos/` at build time – 16, 24 (the 48 px PNG halved), 32, 48, 64, 128 px as 32-bit DIBs, 256 px as PNG; licence as the logo's, no binary `.ico` in git – writes `ocw.ico` and, on Windows MSVC targets only, a compiled resource file (`<app>.res`: `RT_ICON` 1–7, icon group 1, `RT_VERSION`) that the linker takes directly (`cargo:rustc-link-arg-bins`; no `rc.exe` needed). Other targets (Linux, macOS, wasm32, Windows GNU with a warning) get no resource. At run time the desktop app sets the small window icon from the logo and, on Windows, the big (taskbar, Alt+Tab) one from the exe's icon resource. `ocw-studio.exe` carries the studio's own logo since v4.68 (`ocw_winres::embed_logo(…, &OCW_STUDIO)`, see the next point).
- **OCW Studio's icon (v4.66):** the studio has its own logo, `artwork/logos/ocw-studio.svg` (a horn-gold pencil drawing the rainbow on drafting paper; same tile, sky, rainbow and clouds as the game's logo, so the two read as siblings) with a simplified `ocw-studio-small.svg` for 16 and 32 px; `scripts/render-logos.sh` renders both logos' PNGs (16 … 512 px, rsvg-convert). The icon code is shared: `ocw_ui::app_icon` (native only) holds an app's logo and desktop entry (`app_icon!("ocw-studio", "ocw-studio")`) and sets the window icon (X11, Windows title bar), the big taskbar / Alt+Tab icon from the exe's resource (Windows), and installs `packaging/linux/<app id>.desktop` with the hicolor icons into the user's data directory (Linux; not for screenshot runs). The studio's window app id is `ocw-studio` (was `org.opencyclingworld.Studio`). macOS: `OCW_APP=studio scripts/build-macos-app.sh` builds `OCW Studio.app` (bundle id `org.opencyclingworld.studio`, `ocw-studio.icns`); macOS has no window icons, and an unbundled `ocw-studio` (like an unbundled `ocw-desktop`) shows the default Dock icon – setting it at run time needs an `unsafe` AppKit call, which the workspace forbids. The AppImage and the release tarball hold only the game so far; the studio installs its desktop entry and icons itself when it starts.
- **AppImage:** `scripts/build-appimage.sh` assembles the AppDir (binary, desktop entry, icons, `.DirIcon`) and packs it with `appimagetool` when installed.
- **Windows zip (documented v3.32):** built on Win11Builder with the same release `cargo build` as Linux (`-p ocw-desktop -p ocw-server -p world-builder --features ocw-desktop/voice`; the C runtime linked statically by `.cargo/config.toml`, so no Visual C++ redistributable is needed), then the three `.exe` files zipped as `OpenCyclingWorld-<version>-<sha>-windows-x86_64.zip` – by hand so far, no script. The world packages' release zips come from `scripts/prepare-world-release.sh` (4.7).
- **macOS app bundle:** `scripts/build-macos-app.sh` (`make macos-app`, runs on macOS) builds `Open Cycling World.app` (bundle id `org.opencyclingworld.desktop`; stripped binary; `Info.plist` with version + commit, minimum macOS read from the binary, `NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription`, without which macOS ends the app when it uses CoreBluetooth; `ocw.icns` from `artwork/logos/`), signs it ad hoc and packs a DMG (with an Applications link) and a zip. Started from Finder, the app logs to `~/Library/Logs/OCW/ocw-desktop.log` (stderr has no terminal there). CI builds and uploads both on pushes to `main`. Still open: Developer ID signing with the hardened runtime and notarisation (`CODESIGN_IDENTITY` already signs with a given identity), a 1024 px icon render for the 512@2x slot.
- **Versions (decided 2026-11-13, changed in v2.49):** every GitHub release increments the **patch** (last) version of the workspace (`[workspace.package] version` in `Cargo.toml`, inherited by every crate; 0.2.0 → 0.2.1 → 0.2.2 …), and the tag is `vX.Y.Z`. (Until v2.49 the minor version was incremented: 0.1.0 → 0.2.0.) All of it is in the Makefile: `make release-check` (current, latest released and next version), `make release-prepare` (on a clean, pushed `main`: bump with `make version-bump`, commit "Release X.Y.Z", push; the release binaries are built from that commit, so `--version` reads `X.Y.Z-<commit>`), `make release-publish DIR=… NOTES=…` (refuses unless the version is above every existing release; tags, pushes the tag, creates the pre-release with `SHA256SUMS`). Minor / major bumps only by hand (`make version-bump PART=minor|major`). Tested by `make test-release-version`. Older releases were tagged `v0.1.0-<commit>`.
- **Releases:** binaries and world packages are published as **GitHub Releases** (pre-releases while in development), never committed to git (decided 2026-11-12; the history was rewritten to remove the former `release/<version>-<commit>/<platform>/` binaries, the commit map of that rewrite, `release/commit-map.txt`, is in the git history since the folder was removed on 2026-11-16). Release binaries are built with voice (`--features ocw-desktop/voice`, Windows with the static C runtime). *Planned (v4.01, 7.1.1):* every package also carries LiveKit's `livekit-server` (pinned, ~20 MB compressed, 57 MB unpacked; macOS built from source) with its licences. Each release carries the AppImage and a tarball of the stripped Linux binaries, a Windows zip, the macOS DMG, the world package with its manifest and data licence (ODbL, 13), the OSM extract it was built from (the ODbL "offer the data" duty) and `SHA256SUMS`. Each GitHub release's notes are its build notes (the folder `release/` was removed on 2026-11-16, asked by the user). Screenshots and videos made during development are not in the repository (removed from the history on 2026-11-12): they are published by the art project as one zip per day (`ocw-build-history-YYYY-MM-DD.zip`) on the release `build-history` of [OCW-ART](https://github.com/newkit/OCW-ART) (days 1–4 also still on OCW's own release `build-history`, which keeps the README's images). The local archive is the `build-history/` of the OCW-ART checkout next to this one (v3.50; until then `art/build-history/` here, until 2026-11-14 `artwork/build-history/`). Only its masked text files are tracked, in OCW-ART: `index.md`, `SHA256SUMS`, and per day `journal.md`, `journal.json`, `tokens.json`, `incidents.md`. The hourly art collector keeps them up to date (OCW-ART's `ART-PROJECT.md` 2.5, 5.1; v3.35). New test runs land in the git-ignored `test-output/` (with its `index.md`); the ones worth keeping go into that day's zip.
- **Q1 – The art files in OCW's git history: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): remove them** – the user: "remove the ART history from OCW, make sure the binary images are not kept in the history of OCW." `art/` (the art project's code and masked journals, 93 text files in 35 commits, 3.4 MB) is removed from every commit with `git filter-repo --path art --invert-paths`; the commit ids change from the first art commit on, branches and the release tags `v0.2.0`–`v0.2.2` are rewritten and force-pushed, and a commit map (old ids → new ones) is attached to the GitHub release notes of the rewrite (the folder `release/` with the map of 2026-11-12 was removed on 2026-11-16). Binary images: checked 2026-11-16 – none left in OCW's history but the seven app logos of `artwork/logos/` (in use); the media were removed on 2026-11-12. OCW-ART keeps the art history. **To do** once the user gives the go-ahead (every clone and worktree has to be re-cloned or rebased; no session may commit meanwhile).
- **Q2 (open) – Turning the kiosks on again:** both Linux kiosk screens (marge: Black Forest north, leela: Tenerife, Puerto de la Cruz – Teide) are stopped since 2026-11-18 and start only when asked (11.2 *Kiosks and deploys*). Since v6.69 a started kiosk joins the public Fly server (`OCW_KIOSK_SERVER=remote`): it rides **Liechtenstein** there (the server's only world, v11) next to the Echo rider and anyone joining from the live page, with voice, and falls back to its own local server and bots when the join fails. leela's `kiosk-local.env` could keep it local on Tenerife instead (`OCW_KIOSK_SERVER=1`). Each running kiosk draws a full GPU at 500 W show mode all day (marge's fans are audible) and shows up on the status page as a rider. Options: (a) both stay off (as now); (b) marge on, joining Fly – one public rider always on the road, leela off; (c) marge on, joining Fly, and leela on, local on Tenerife (two worlds on two screens); (d) both on, both joining Fly (two kiosk riders together in Liechtenstein). Proposal: (c) – the Fly server always has a rider, and leela keeps showing a second world; it can be stopped any time with `ocw-kiosk.sh uninstall`.
