- **W6 – Repairs (v3.17, with Phase 12 K4):** the garage keeps each bike's damage (per damage part, per mille) and the rider's injury with its time (healing 10 % an hour of real time); the repair price is `ceil(price × (1 − condition) × 0.3)` ♥, exact in per mille (`ocw_sim::damage::repair_price`), from the **price paid** for the item on the part's slot (wheels → `wheels`, tyres → `tyres`, drivetrain → `groupset`, handlebar → `cockpit`, frame → `frame`; wheels and tyres are pairs: half each, rounded up); a **base part** is priced at the **cheapest paid part of the slot that fits the bike** (frames: of its profile) – decided here: a repair is worth what a new entry part costs, so the starter bikes are not free to wreck – or 20 ♥ if the catalogue has none; a frame or wheel below 10 % is **beyond repair** and replaced at the full price. In the workshop the stand bike's **hotspots** take the worst damaged part's status colour and their labels the condition and price ("● rear wheel 40 % – repair 51 ♥"); the slot's equipped row opens a dialog with *Repair the rear wheel for 51 ♥* and *Repair all for 90 ♥* (only when the balance covers it); the **condition card** (bottom left in the room and stand views) lists the bike's condition, the damaged parts worst first with their prices and *Repair all*; the **mirror** shows the rider's injury and the time to heal ("Heals in 4 h 30 min – or 1 % a minute of easy riding"). Console `workshop.repair PART|all [--bike ID]` (ledger reason `repair`), `workshop.damage PART|rider PCT` (dev: tests, screenshots). Scenes `k4-workshop-repair`, `k4-workshop-repair-card`, `k4-workshop-injury`.
- **Leftovers built (v3.23):**
  - *The bench catalogue (4D):* framesets as new bikes on new hooks, complete builds, the shelf, selling a bike – see 4D *Built*.
  - *Fitted lights drive the ride's bike lights (Phase 9 Q3):* a light set's catalogue entry says its lamps (`light = { front_lm, rear_lm, front_colour, rear_colour }`, validated: only light sets, not dark, at most 3,000 / 200 lm; `lights.set` 300 lm neutral white `#FFF6E8`, 15 lm red `#FF2614` – a typical StVZO set, proposal); in the ride the **lenses of the fitted set on the bike model** glow while the lights are on (`riders::BikeLens`, the material swapped; the Phase 9 placeholder – two glowing boxes at fixed spots on every avatar – is gone), the far glow beyond 40 m and the local rider's beam sit at the lenses (`riders::LampAnchors`, from the bike model's `light_front` / `light_rear` parts); brightness and colour come from the part (`sky::lamp_look`, pure: the glow grows with the square root of the flux, the beam's power with the flux – 40 Bevy lm per lamp lm, tuned so the set gives the earlier look, 12,000 lm, 45 m –, its reach with the square root, 15–90 m; proposal); a bike without a set has no lamps at all. **Changed in v5.05 (Phase 9 Q3):** every bike has small default lamps (the base part *Basic lights*, `light` 60 / 4 lm, on every exported bike model); the set is the upgrade.
  - *The trainer's SIM parameters from the build:* done since Phase 10 B4 (v3.09: `TrainerControl::follow` sets the server's build in force – `ClientCore::effective_profile` – before every update; the S6 wind and folded gradient build on it); now tested per race mode through the trainer protocol state machine with a mock FTMS and a mock Wahoo trainer (`the_trainer_gets_the_build_in_force_per_race_mode`): in free ride (Open) the build's Crr, cw (½ ρ CdA at the air's density) and – Wahoo SIM mode – mass; in a Profile race the profile's; in an Equal race `road`'s with the rider's weight (FTMS has no mass field).
  - *Idle animation:* `ocw_assets::pose::idle` (pure) stands the rider at ease at the mirror – the arms hanging beside the body with soft elbows (not the rest pose's straight arms held out), the weight shifting slowly from foot to foot (hips 1.8 cm, a little hip roll), breathing, the head looking about, the feet planted by two-bone IK and flat on the floor; incommensurate periods so it never visibly loops. Tested: ankles within 2 mm, feet flat, hands below the shoulders beside the hips, elbows bent, smooth at 60 fps, moving.
  - *Kit colours:* the free colours of shorts, socks, shoes and gloves (Phase 8 T6, the *Kit colours* page) are also a **colour row in the shorts, socks, shoes and gloves pickers** (← / → on a draft shown live in the mirror, Confirm applies a `kit.design` line; the other rows buy / wear as before), and they are kept **with the garage in `workshop.toml`** (`kit_colours`), applied at the start – so the default rider without a rider profile keeps them too (before only riders.toml kept them; proposal: the kit's colours belong to the wardrobe). Looks only: tested that the build and the ids the server counts stay the same.
- **Still open:** W5 (backend ledger; with accounts the server checks that the parts are owned; with it the backend keeps the damage); touch on a real screen (Q5 postponed); from W4: a global graphics-quality setting (the mirror's reflection is its own switch); the far LOD shows the base look and the default height; further light sets (brighter, dynamo) need their price research (4H) – the catalogue and the renderer take them as data; the browser app's workshop (UI parity, Phase 10).

**Result:** Individually customizable riders.

#### 4N – Character editor refined: name, body type, age, hair, facial hair, build (planning, 2026-11-16, v3.77; first step built, v4.37; second step built, v4.51)

**Asked by the user (2026-11-16):** "refine character editor in workshop. the user can give himself a name, chose his sex, age, haircut, hair color, mustache, body shape etc." This section plans it; the **open questions are Q6 – Q15 below** (they continue Phase 4's Q1 – Q5 of 4L, so "Phase 4 Q7" is unambiguous). Everything not marked *decided* is a proposal.

**What exists (W4 v3.07, T6 v3.12, 4M):**
- *Name:* the rider profile's `name` in `riders.toml` (`ocw_client::riders`: at most 32 characters, not empty, no leading / trailing spaces, no quotes or control characters) is the display name sent as `Hello.display_name` (`--name` overrides it for a session). The server takes the hello's name as it is – it applies no rules of its own – and a **signed-in rider rides under the account's name** (9.1.1: the provider's name, for Google usually the person's real full name). The name shows on the name tag over the rider, in the rider list, the standings and the entrant lists.
- *Character* (`ocw_core::Character`, free, `character` line per profile): height (the profile's `height_cm`, drawn 150–205 cm), build slim / medium / strong (per-node girth, `rider::girth`), 12 skin tones, 4 faces (classic, beard, moustache, stubble – **face and facial hair are one choice today**), 6 hair styles (short, buzz cut, long, ponytail, bun, bald), 8 hair colours (the wire's `hair_rgb` is already a free colour), 3 glasses. **One base body** for everyone, no age, no eye colour or eyebrows. Rigid parts, no skinning (2.6). The far LOD shows the base look at the default height (4M, still open).
- *The editor:* the mirror in the changing corner, five hotspots, LB / RB through 13 slots, a picker per slot, *Try on the bike*; the kit colours and the jersey designer edit a draft live. Its Bevy-free model lives in `apps/desktop/src/workshop/` – **the browser app has no workshop yet** (4M; Phase 10 Q5: customization only for signed-in riders).

**Principles (decided rules applied, not new decisions):**
- **Looks never change the physics** (2.5, 4G, 4C): nothing in this section enters `physics_profile`; the physics takes only the rider profile's **weight** (and the curated bike profile with parts and kit). Body type, age, height as drawn and build are rendering only. A property test checks it (N13).
- **Who someone is never costs anything** (Phase 4 Q4): every choice here is free, for every rider, from the start.
- **Inclusive by construction:** the body choice is a choice of **base body shape**, not a sex or gender field; nothing else depends on it – every hair style, beard, moustache, colour, glasses and kit item is offered on every body; no pronoun or gender is stored or sent (proposal; Q7). Defaults never follow the body choice.
- **One implementation in both apps** (3.2.2 rule, B6): the editor's model moves with the workshop's into the shared crates (N10); desktop and browser get the same pages, rows and keys.

**N1 – Name.**
- *What it is:* the rider's **display name** – the name tag over the rider, the rider list, standings, entrant lists and results, the voice participant's name (7) and a **name card on the locker** in the changing corner (like the bikes' name cards on the hooks). It stays the rider profile's `name` (renaming a profile also moves `active`); a profile keeps one name for all its rides.
- *Rules (proposal; one pure function `ocw_core::name::check`, used by the editor, the `riders.toml` loader and the server):* 2–20 characters as seen (grapheme clusters), at most 64 bytes of UTF-8; Unicode NFC; letters of any script, digits, space and `- ' . _`; spaces trimmed and collapsed; **no** control or format characters (bidi overrides, zero-width characters outside a grapheme), no emoji (the name tag's font, Q11), not only digits or punctuation. Reserved names are refused: "Echo" (the echo bot), "Host", "Server", "OCW", "Rider" followed only by digits (the fallback below) and the bots' name pattern. Profiles whose name breaks the new rules still load; the editor asks for a new name before the next shared ride (the old 32-character limit becomes 20 for new names only).
- *The server checks too* (today it does not): an invalid name from a hello is replaced by `Rider NNNN` (from the rider id) and the client is told in `Welcome` (a new optional `name_note`), so an old or modified client cannot put a 500-character or invisible name on everyone's screen.
- *Duplicates (proposal; Q8):* names are not unique worldwide. Within a session the server keeps them distinct: a second "Ada Rider" is shown as "Ada Rider (2)" (the rider id is the identity, the suffix only the label); the own client shows the suffix too.
- *Offensive names (proposal; Q9):* a small deny-list per language in `assets/names-deny.toml` (normalized: case folded, accents stripped, look-alike letters and digit substitutions folded), checked by `name::check`; the editor says "this name is not allowed" and offers the dice; on a shared server a listed name becomes `Rider NNNN`. Reporting and muting a rider belong to Phase 5's moderation, not here. The list ships as data so it can grow without a release.
- *Account (proposal; Q10):* a signed-in rider has a **rider name** of their own in the OCW account (chosen in this editor, stored by the backend with the account, 9.1.1 `AccountHooks`; the first sign-in proposes the profile's name, never the provider's full name). The server then uses the account's rider name instead of the provider's name, so a real name is never shown to others unless the rider typed it. Anonymous riders (browser, Phase 10 Q5) keep the default `Rider NNNN`.
- *Entering it:* a keyboard text field (desktop and browser); with a pad an **on-screen keyboard** (a letter grid in `ocw-ui`, ten-foot sized, shared by every text field a pad can reach); on touch the system keyboard (the browser through a hidden `<input>`). A **dice** proposes a made-up name from two word lists (an adjective and a riding word: "Swift Climber", "Calm Descender") – never a real person's name.

**N2 – Body type ("sex" in the request).**
- *Proposal (Q6, Q7):* **three base bodies** with the same rig, node names and anchors: **A** – broader shoulders, narrower hips, flatter chest; **B** – narrower shoulders, wider hips, a chest; **C** – in between. They differ in the torso, pelvis and thigh meshes and in shoulder and hip width (the rig's joint offsets), not in limb lengths, so the pose code (`ocw_assets::pose`, IK from the rig's lengths) and `BodyFit` work unchanged. The head and face come from N6 / N7, not from the body.
- *Shown as* three pictures of the bodies with neutral captions ("Body A / B / C"; whether the words "masculine / feminine / neutral" appear is Q7). No pronoun field (Q7).
- *Existing characters* keep body A (today's model is closest to it); for a new rider profile the editor asks for the body in its first-run step (no silent default).
- *Never physics:* the weight is the profile's (3.2.1), the height is the profile's (N4).

**N3 – Age (appearance only).**
- *What it is:* an **appearance age** in six steps (20s, 30s, 40s, 50s, 60s, 70+); not a birth date, not a number of years, never shown as text to others, never physics or animation tempo.
- *What it changes (proposal; Q12):* **hair greying** (from the 40s, a per-rider seeded grey share that grows with the step; *Keep my hair colour* turns it off); the **face** – subtle lines at the eyes and mouth and a slightly softer jaw as a head morph target (N8), the skin a touch less saturated in the 70+ step; the **posture** – in the workshop's idle pose only, the shoulders 1–2° rounder from the 60s (on the bike the pose comes from the IK and does not change).

**N4 – Body shape (height and build).**
- *Height:* the slider writes the **rider profile's height** (`height_cm`; one value, the same as in *Rider profiles*), 5 cm steps, drawn 150–205 cm (the profile allows 100–250 cm; values outside are drawn clamped, as today). It changes how the rider looks and where the saddle sits (`BodyFit`), not the physics (the physics has no height).
- *Build:* the three steps become a **slider 0–100** (lean … strong; today's slim / medium / strong map to 15 / 50 / 85), interpolating the per-node girth on each base body. A second slider **muscle** (0–100: thighs, calves, shoulders) is an extra (Q14).
- *Relation to the weight (proposal; Q13):* the visible build is **free**. The editor shows a small marker on the build slider where the profile's weight and height would put it (from the body-mass index: 18 → 10, 22 → 45, 27 → 75, 32+ → 95) and a *Match my weight* button; a new character starts at the marker. Others never learn the weight from it, and the physics keeps the profile's weight whatever the slider says. (Alternatives for Q13: bounded to a band around the marker, or always derived.)

**N5 – Hair.**
- *Catalogue (proposal, 18 styles; each free, on every body):* bald, shaved, buzz cut, crew cut, short textured, side part, short curly, afro (compressed under a helmet), pixie, mid-length, long straight, long curly, low ponytail, single braid, two braids, low bun, locs tied back, cornrows. Today's six stay with their indices.
- *Under every helmet (rule):* each style has two shapes – `hair` (no helmet: the workshop, the cap) and `hair_helmet` (only what shows below the shell's rim: sideburns, nape, and **long hair, ponytails and braids leaving through the gap between the shell's rear and the retention band**). A geometry test checks every style under every helmet (road, lightweight, aero road, TT) and the cap: no hair vertex outside the shell except in that exit zone, and the tail clear of the jersey's collar in the riding poses.
- *Movement (proposal):* ponytail and braids as a chain of 2–3 rigid segments on a damped spring driven by the speed, the pedal rhythm and the rocking (`ocw_assets::anim`, pure); close LOD only (N9).
- *Colour:* a **natural palette** of 12 (black, dark brown, brown, light brown, auburn, red, copper, strawberry blond, blond, platinum, grey, white) plus **Custom…** – the free colour picker of the kit colours (hue, saturation, value; hex on a keyboard), so dyed colours work. **Roots** (proposal): an optional second colour near the scalp with a soft gradient along the hair (a vertex attribute, no texture). **Greying** follows the age (N3) unless turned off; with a custom colour the grey blends into it.
- *Eyebrows* follow the hair colour (greying too) unless set in N7.

**N6 – Facial hair (moustache, beard, stubble).**
- *Split from the face:* today's face presets 1–3 become face 0 plus a facial-hair choice (migration in N11). Two independent rows, on every body:
  - **moustache:** none, classic, chevron, handlebar, horseshoe, pencil;
  - **beard:** none, stubble, short stubble beard, short boxed, full, goatee, chin strap, long.
- *Colour:* **follows the hair** (default, greying included) or its own colour (palette and Custom…, as N5).
- *Helmet straps:* the straps run over the beard (the beard meshes leave room under the strap line); a test checks the strap against every beard.

**N7 – Face, skin and the "etc."**
- *Face shape:* 6 shapes (jaw, cheekbones, nose, brow) as **head morph targets** (N8), mixed with the age (N3).
- *Skin:* the 12 tones stay; *proposal:* 18 (six depths × warm / neutral / cool undertone), the old indices kept.
- *Eyes:* colour – brown, dark brown, hazel, green, blue, grey, amber. *Eyebrows:* thin, medium, thick, arched (colour from the hair or own). *Freckles:* none, few, many (vertex colour on the face and forearms).
- *Glasses (exist: none, sport wrap, round):* proposal +2 frames (half rim, shield) and a lens tint (clear, smoke, mirror blue, orange). Free, as decided.
- *Extras (proposals only, Q14):* earrings / studs; a few tattoo designs on arms and calves (decals through the gear shader, near only); a **prosthetic lower leg or forearm** (a rigid part replacing the shin or forearm mesh – the rig makes this easy, the pose is unchanged).

**N8 – Models (Phase 15) and budget.**
- *Files* (`artwork/3dmodels/`, glTF `.glb`; the generators stay the exporters, with `.blend` sources, Phase 15 Q1): `riders/rider-a.glb`, `rider-b.glb`, `rider-c.glb` (the three bodies; today's `rider.glb` becomes `rider-a.glb`, the old name kept as an alias for one release) and `riders/rider-low.glb` (far); `hair/<id>.glb` with the nodes `hair`, `hair_helmet` and `tail_0 … tail_2` on `anchor_head`; `face/moustache-<id>.glb` and `face/beard-<id>.glb` on a new anchor `anchor_face` (the front of the head); glasses stay in `wear/`. New paint slots: `hair`, `hair_root` (the gradient), `facial_hair`, `brow`, `eye`; `skin` exists.
- *Morph targets:* only on the **head** (`face_0 … face_5`, `age`) – rigid parts can carry morph targets without a skin. They are **baked once per look change** on the CPU into the rider's head mesh (a cache keyed by the look's hash), so a ride has no per-frame morph cost; the body build stays a per-node scale (Phase 15's proposal).
- *Licence (8A):* own work, or an attribution-only base mesh (Phase 15 Q3) reworked into the low-poly style; every file in the manifest.
- *Budget (15B: a rider ≤ 8,000 near / 4,000 far triangles in total):* hair ≤ 1,200, beard ≤ 400, moustache ≤ 150, the head with its morphs ≤ 900; at most +3 draw calls per near rider (hair, facial hair, eyes merged per material); the baked-mesh cache ≤ 150 KB per distinct look. Measured with `scripts/measure-fps.sh` (a group of 30 bots with varied characters): at most +0.3 ms per frame on marge and in the browser (WebGL 2).

**N9 – LOD (8, 2.6 far LOD).**
- *Close (< 6 m: the mirror, the chase camera):* everything – eyes, eyebrows, freckles, face lines, roots, swinging hair.
- *Near (< 40 m, the near model):* body type, build, height, face shape, hair style and colour (greyed), facial hair, glasses; no eye colour, freckles or tail motion.
- *Far (≥ 40 m, the bike file's `lod1` rider):* proposal, closing the 4M gap – the far rider takes the rider's **height** (scaled, the saddle moved) and the **skin and hair colour** (a hair cap shape; long hair as one tail block), the helmet and jersey as today; one far body for all three base bodies.

**N10 – The editor's flow in the mirror (both apps).**
- *Categories* (LB / RB, Q / E or the tabs; ↑ / ↓ the rows; ← / → change; Confirm opens a picker or the keyboard): **Name** · **Body** (body type, height, build) · **Face** (shape, skin, eyes, eyebrows, freckles, age) · **Hair** (style, colour, roots, greying) · **Facial hair** (moustache, beard, colour) · **Extras** (glasses, …) · **Kit** (today's kit slots, the jersey designer, the kit colours) · *Try on the bike*. The hotspots stay (head → Hair, Face; torso → Body, Kit; hands, legs, feet → Kit). At most the ten-foot row limit per page (3.2.1).
- *Live preview on a draft* (as the kit colours do): every change shows at once on the rider and in the mirror; **Confirm** saves one `character` line, **Back** with changes asks *Keep / Discard*. The camera frames the category: the head close in Face, Hair and Facial hair (the mirror's reflection at full resolution while it fills the view), the whole rider in Body. **Helmet on / off** (Y, H) shows the hair with and without each helmet and the cap.
- **Randomise** (X, R, the dice): a random character from a seeded generator (`ocw_core::character::random(seed, locks)`), **per category or all**; a lock per category keeps it; the name only with the Name category's own dice. **Reset:** to the saved character (per category or all) and *Default*. **Presets:** about 8 made-up example characters to start from (varied bodies, ages, hair, skin), plus **saved looks** – up to 5 per rider profile (proposal). **Undo** of the last 20 draft changes (Ctrl+Z; a pad's Select + LB).
- *Input (3.2.2):* keyboard; mouse (hotspots, drag to turn, wheel to zoom, sliders dragged); gamepad (as above; the sticks turn and zoom); touch (tap the tabs and rows, swipe to turn, pinch to zoom, the system keyboard). Console: `character body b`, `character age 50s`, `character hair braid`, `character hair-colour #6B4426`, `character beard full`, `character random [SEED]`, `character reset`, `rider rename "Ada Rider"`.
- *Both apps:* the Bevy-free workshop model (`apps/desktop/src/workshop/`: model, nav, picker, designer, input) moves to **`ocw_client::workshop`** and its scene glue to **`ocw-ui::workshop`**, the way B6 shared the menus; the browser opens the workshop for signed-in riders (Phase 10 Q5), the mirror's reflection following the quality preset (`ocw-ui::quality`; low: the direct front view).

**N11 – Storage and migration.**
- *File:* the rider's table in `riders.toml` gets `character_version = 2` and readable ids instead of indices: `body = "a"`, `age = "30s"`, `build = 50`, `muscle = 50`, `face = 0`, `skin = 3`, `eyes = "brown"`, `eyebrows = "medium"`, `freckles = "none"`, `hair = "ponytail"`, `hair_color`, `hair_root_color`, `greying = true`, `moustache = "none"`, `beard = "stubble"`, `facial_hair_color` (absent: follows the hair), `glasses`, `glasses_tint`, and `[[rider.look]]` tables for saved looks. Unknown values are warned about and take the default (as today).
- *Migration v1 → v2* (on load, written on the next save; tested both ways): face 1 → face 0 + beard full, 2 → moustache classic, 3 → beard stubble; `body_build` slim / medium / strong → build 15 / 50 / 85; hair index → id; body A; age 30s; greying on. An older app reading a v2 file warns about the unknown keys and shows the defaults for them.
- *Signed in (proposal):* the character and the rider name are also kept in the OCW account (with W5 / Phase 5), so the browser and another computer show the same rider; the local file is the cache, the newer change wins.

**N12 – Network (6.2; fields only added).**
- `RiderLook` gets the optional fields `body_type` (22), `appearance_age` (23), `moustache` (24), `beard` (25), `facial_hair_rgb` (26, absent: follows the hair), `hair_root_rgb` (27), `greying` (28), `eyebrows` (29), `eye_colour` (30), `freckles` (31), `build_pct` (32; `body_build` (6) is still sent as the nearest of the three for older apps), `muscle_pct` (33), `glasses_tint` (34). `face` (8) keeps the shape, `hair` (9) the style index (new styles after the old six; an older app draws its default). They travel as the character does today: in `Hello`, `BikeChange` and once per change in `RiderBuild.look`, **never in the snapshots**; validated by the server (`Character::validated`).
- *Size:* an encoded `RiderLook` ≤ 128 bytes (the whole character adds ≤ 40 bytes); the server refuses a larger one (the default look) – tested. The name: ≤ 64 bytes, checked (N1).
- *Renaming in a ride (proposal; Q15):* a new optional `BikeChange.display_name`, applied when leaving the workshop like the bike; the name tag, rider list and standings follow; frozen while the rider is an entrant of a running event.

**N13 – Tests (11.4).**
- *Unit:* `name::check` (lengths in graphemes and bytes, NFC, control and bidi characters, emoji, reserved names, the deny-list's folding of case, accents, look-alikes and digits); the server replacing invalid names and suffixing duplicates; `riders.toml` v1 → v2 migration and back, unknown keys; `RiderLook` round trip, an old app's decode (fields ignored, the `body_build` fallback), the 128-byte limit; **physics invariance** (a property test: `physics_profile` and a ride's result are identical for any random character); greying per age and seed; the build marker from weight and height; `random` deterministic per seed and honouring the locks; the editor model in `ocw_client::workshop` (categories, draft, keep / discard, reset, presets, undo, the on-screen keyboard) – for both apps.
- *Geometry:* every hair style × every helmet and the cap (exit zone only), every beard × the strap, every body × 150 / 178 / 205 cm × every bike (`BodyFit`: the legs at 95 %), triangle budgets per file (`ocw-assets validate`).
- *Scenes* (`scripts/scenes.toml`, X11 + Wayland, the browser with `make test-web`; made-up names only): `workshop-character-name` (the locker's card "Ada Rider"), `workshop-character-body` (A / B / C), `workshop-character-age` (20s … 70+), `workshop-character-hair-helmet` (styles under each helmet), `workshop-character-facial-hair`, `character-lineup` (eight presets side by side: "Ada Rider", "Bea Climber", "Cleo Sprinter", "Dara Descender", …), `ride-group-characters` (a varied group at 5, 20 and 60 m for the LODs), and the video `workshop-character-video` (categories, randomise, reset).

**N14 – Milestones (proposal):** **C1** name rules, the server's check, the account's rider name (after Q8 – Q11); **C2** data model v2, migration, protocol fields; **C3** facial hair split, the hair catalogue with the helmet fit, colours with roots; **C4** base bodies (after Q6, Q7) and the build slider (after Q13); **C5** age (after Q12); **C6** the new flow (categories, randomise, presets, on-screen keyboard) and the move into `ocw_client::workshop` / `ocw-ui::workshop` for the browser; **C7** the far-LOD look, extras (after Q14).

**N15 – Open questions (for the user):**
- **Q6 – How many base bodies: decided (2026-11-16, the user): seven body shapes** – the user: "anorexia, skinny, slim, normal, ample, fat, obese". The body choice is a scale of seven named shapes (N2 / N4 build), from very thin to very heavy. **Q6b – decided (2026-11-16, the user): yes, as a second dimension** – "keep the shoulder/hip/chest variants in as a second dimension": the body is chosen in two independent dimensions, the **base body** A / B / C (shoulders, hips, chest; N2) and the **shape** of the seven steps (build; N4); every combination exists.
- **Q7 – How the body choice is labelled: decided (2026-11-16, the user):** with the seven words of Q6 (super skinny – renamed from "anorexia" by the user on 2026-11-19 –, skinny, slim, normal, ample, fat, obese), each with its picture; no pronoun or gender field (unchanged).
- **Q8 – Unique names: decided (2026-11-16, the user): names must be unique** – the user: "names must be unique". No "(2)" suffixes. Where they must be unique is Q22.
- **Q9 – Offensive names: decided (2026-11-16, the user): no filter** – the user: "do not block any names". No deny-list in the editor or on servers; `name::check` keeps only the technical rules of N1 (length, NFC, no control or invisible characters).
- **Q10 – Signed-in name: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): as proposed** – the rider's own **rider name** is stored with the account (one rider per account, 4O) and is what others see; the sign-in provider's name (Google, Strava) is never shown.
- **Q11 – Scripts in names: decided (2026-11-16, the user): all scripts** – the user: "all". Names may use every Unicode script now; the app needs fonts that cover them (a fallback chain with CJK, Arabic, Hebrew, Indic and others; for the browser the extra fonts are loaded on demand, not in the first download).
- **Q12 – Age on the face: decided (2026-11-16, the user): face, body, skin and hair** – the user: "face, body, skin, hair". The appearance age (N3) changes the face (lines at eyes and mouth, a softer jaw), the body (posture and shape), the skin (tone and texture) and the hair (greying, with *Keep my hair colour*). Still appearance only, never physics.
- **Q13 – Visible build vs the physics weight: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard; *the band was replaced by Q23, 2026-11-17: every shape can be chosen, weight and height only propose one*): bounded to a band around the weight, with the *Match my weight* marker, from weight and height** – the user: "free with a Match my weight marker, bounded to a band around the weight). take users height into consideration." The shape (the seven steps of Q6) can be chosen only within a band around the shape that the rider's **weight and height** give (body-mass index → shape, N4); the marker shows that shape and *Match my weight* snaps to it. A change of weight or height in the profile moves the band; a shape outside it is moved to its nearest edge. The band's width is Q23.
- **Q14 – Extras in the first step: decided (2026-11-16, dashboard): later** – none of the extras (muscle slider, earrings, tattoos, freckles, more glasses, prosthetic limbs) is in the first step of 4N; they come in a later step.
- **Q15 – Renaming during a ride: decided (2026-11-16, the user): no** – the name can only be changed between rides, never during a ride or a running event.
- **Q22 – Unique names: where (follow-up of Q8): decided (2026-11-16, the user): unique per account and per server** – the user: "unique per account and server". A rider name is **reserved for one account worldwide** (the backend refuses a name another account holds, 4O), and **every server keeps the names in a session unique**: a rider without an account whose name is taken there picks another when joining (no "(2)" suffixes, Q8).
- **Q23 – The width of the body-shape band (follow-up of Q13): decided (2026-11-17, dashboard): no band – decoupled** – the user: "decouple. make shapes available regardless of the actual shape. just use it as proposal." All seven body shapes can be chosen whatever weight and height say; the shape that weight and height give is only a proposal (the preselected shape and the *Match my weight* marker). Replaces the band of Q13.

**Built (2026-11-17, v4.47; first step of 4N, both apps):**
- *Names (N1, Q8, Q9, Q11, Q15, Q22):* `ocw_core::name` – `check` (2–20 grapheme clusters, ≤ 64 bytes, NFC, spaces trimmed and collapsed, letters and marks of every script, digits, space and `- ' . _`; control, format and invisible characters refused, a zero-width joiner / non-joiner only inside a grapheme; at least one letter; reserved: Echo, Host, Server, OCW, `Rider` with or without digits, `Bot N`; **no word filter**), `key` (NFC, case folded: "Ada Rider" = "ada rider"), `fallback` (`Rider 0042` from the rider id), a made-up-name `dice` (adjective + riding word), `rename_allowed`. Uniqueness behind one interface, `NameRegistry` (claim / release / holder by key) with the in-memory `NameBook<H>`: the game server keeps one per session (holder: the connection) and **refuses a hello whose name another rider holds** (`Reject.name_taken`, "choose another name and join again"; no "(2)"), replaces an invalid name (the default "Rider", empty, invisible, too long, reserved) by `Rider NNNN` and says so in `Welcome.name_note` (with `Welcome.display_name`, the name it shows; both apps print the note); the name is freed when the rider leaves and never changes during the ride (no message renames a rider). **Account side:** `AccountNames = NameBook<AccountId>` behind the same trait, tested in memory – **TODO(4O / W5b): the backend's PostgreSQL store of the account's rider name**, unique by `key`, refusing another account's name (the accounts backend does not keep a rider name yet; signed-in riders still ride under the token's name until W5b). `riders.toml`: new names (add, rename) follow `check` and are stored normalized; old names still load (the 32-character rule) and the rider page marks them "(rename before a shared ride)"; *Add a rider* proposes a dice name. Renaming (Q15): a new name applies from the next ride (as every profile change), and `riders.edit --rename` is refused while the riding rider is an entrant of a running event.
- *Body (N2, N4, Q6, Q6b, Q7, Q13, Q23):* `ocw_core::BaseBody` A / B / C and `BodyShape` (super skinny – id `super-skinny`, the old `anorexia` and `super slim` still read –, skinny, slim, normal, ample, fat, obese) as two dimensions; every combination exists. The proposal `weight_shape` from the body-mass index of the profile's weight and height (steps at 16, 18.5, 21, 25, 28, 32; no height: 1.78 m): a new rider starts with it, the editor marks it (*Match my weight*: "Normal (matches your weight)" / "Ample (your weight: Normal)"), `--match-weight` and the menu's *Match my weight* take it; **every shape can be chosen for any weight and height** (Q23: no band, nothing clamps a shape – not the profile, the editor, the command or the server). In the model (`ocw_assets::rider`): the shape is the girth of the rigid parts (`girth_of`: torso and pelvis alike – the bib under the jersey –, the limbs less, the upper arms move with the shoulders' width (`node_translation`), `girth_transform` scales the pelvis's meshes about the torso's pivot so the layers stay fitted); base body A is today's model (existing characters keep it), B has narrower shoulder caps, wider hips (pelvis, thighs), narrower arms and a chest, C is in between (optional nodes `shoulders_a/b/c`, `chest_b/c` on the jersey, near model only; one far body, N9). The W4 build is still sent (`body_build`, the nearest of three) and read (slim / medium / strong → slim / normal / ample). *Fixed (v4.99; bug found by the user 2026-11-19: "the legs of the rider are not connected to the body"):* the thighs began as open tubes 6 cm under the hip joints (v4.28, to keep the bib under the jersey standing), so a bent hip swung the tube's open end out in front of and beside the seat – from behind a cut-off thigh under a separate seat block; and the hip joints stayed 9 cm apart for every shape, half outside a thin body's narrow seat. Now each thigh's bib (and skinsuit) closes in a dome round the joint (`rider::THIGH_TOP`, `THIGH_DOME`), and the hips are as wide as the seat (`node_translation` for the thighs, the pose's rig with them: `RiderRig::for_body`, so the feet stay on the pedals). Test `ocw_assets::hips`: for every shape on every base body (and the 70+), at 1.50, 1.78 and 2.05 m, in every pose of the pose system (riding, standing, sprint, tuck, the idle stance at the mirror, the photographer), both levels of detail – the hip joints at least 5 mm inside the bib's seat and every point of each leg's top ring within 4 mm of the body (the seat or the jersey above its hem); the old open leg and the old fixed hips fail it. Scenes `hips-*`; `riders/rider-body.glb`, `rider-body-low.glb` and the bikes' far riders re-exported.
- *Age (N3, Q12):* `ocw_core::Age` (20s … 70+): the hair greys from the 40s by a share per age, spread ±25 % per rider from the look itself (the same in every app), off with *Keep my hair colour* (`greying`); the face gets lines at the eyes and mouth from the 40s, deeper with the forehead's from the 60s (nodes `face_lines_light`, `face_lines_deep`, paint slot `skin_line`) and a softer jaw from the 60s (`face_jaw_soft`); the skin is a little less saturated in the 60s and 70+; the body's middle is deeper from the 50s and the limbs a little thinner at 70+; the workshop's idle stance rounds the shoulders from the 60s (`pose::idle_aged`; on the bike the IK pose is unchanged).

Roots, the tails' motion and `hair_helmet` shapes for a rider without a helmet are not built (no view shows a rider without a helmet yet).

The W4 faces migrate (face 1 → full beard, 2 → classic moustache, 3 → stubble).

Options: (a) the lips open a little in a short pulse while a rider is heard speaking – only on the near model, never while muted (the X over the mouth); (b) leave the mouth still. Proposal: a. **Built (v5.27):** the lips are two nodes under the face (`face_lips` with the upper lip and the mouth's dark inside, `face_lip_lower`); while the voice call's speaking cue lists a rider (the own rider: while the own voice is on and heard), `ocw_assets::mouth::MouthAnim` drops the lower lip up to 6.5 mm in eased pulses of 0.14–0.26 s with a random height and short pauses, seeded per rider; never under the X mouth (closes within about 30 ms when it comes on), only on the near model, in both apps. Off the bar the hand follows the forearm: the phone of the status signs held in the right hand's fingers (the phone placed where they close), open hands with the arms up at the finish, loose hands standing (the workshop, the photographer); in between the hand blends, never jumping. *Gloves:* the palm and the base joints are the glove (`glove`), the middle and outer joints `fingertip` – the skin out of the fingerless mitts and gel gloves, the gloves' colour under full and winter gloves (`covers_fingertips`); the near glove nodes are cuffs now (the gel's padded back on the back of the hand), the far rider keeps its mitten. *Fixed (v4.57):* the palm was a plain box – now a rounded slab (`hand::palm`), narrower at the wrist, the heel rounded, the thumb's ball and the little finger's edge raised on the inner face above where the bars lie, the knuckles on the back (≤ 220 triangles; the heaviest look stays under 8,000); standing hands looked loose – the relaxed shape bends every finger a little at each joint (the middle joint most, the little finger most), the thumb along the index finger (`RELAXED_BEND`), the idle wrist a little flexed and swinging with the arm (`pose::idle_wrist`), and the workshop's standing rider now shows the idle pose's shapes (after *Try on the bike* it kept the grip shapes). Tests: the palm closed, tapered, its ball and knuckles, out of every bar and hood; the relaxed curl and the wrist over the idle animation. *Fixed (v4.67; bug found by the user 2026-11-17: "the hand position on the handlebar looks wrong (upside down)"):* the palm's side was chosen by a test against one fixed down-and-forward direction, so with the shoulder high above the tops the palm turned up under the bar, and on the drops and the TT bars it faced outward (fingers round from the inside, knuckles to the frame). **How riders hold each grip** (references, looked at only, nothing copied: *Cyclist.jpg*, Matrixod, CC0 – hands on the hoods; *Cycling pressing brakes on bicycle.jpg*, Alextredz, CC BY-SA 4.0 – hands in the drops; *Ironman Germany 2014 - cycling leg (AP3Q2868).jpg*, Moritz Kosinsky, CC BY-SA 3.0 – a TT bike's base bar and extensions; *Mountain biking Mt Hood National Forest (36376803723).jpg*, U.S. Forest Service Pacific Northwest Region, public domain – flat grips; *Racing Bike Handlebar Cyclist (Unsplash).jpg*, Flo Karr, CC0 – a drop bar from the rider's view; all on Wikimedia Commons): **hoods** – the palm resting on top of the hood, the thumb on its inner side, the index and middle fingers forward over the lever (or round the hood's body), the knuckles up and out, the wrist about straight; **tops** – the palms down on the flat top beside the stem, the fingers over the bar from above and round its front to the underside, the thumbs under or alongside it; **drops** – the hands in the hooks, the palms facing in to the bike, the fingers round the drop from the outside, the thumbs over the top, the index fingers near the levers; **TT extensions and base bar** – the forearms on the pads, the hands loosely round the extensions' ends, the palms in, the fingers round from below and outside, the thumbs on top (on the base bar's ends the same, the thumb forward along the end); **MTB / flat grips** – the palms down and behind the grip, the fingers forward over it from above, the thumbs under it, the index finger near the brake lever. **Now** (`pose::hand_on_bar`): each grip names its palm's side – down on the hoods, the tops and flat grips (the hand on the tops and flat grips lies flatter than the forearm: its long axis follows the forearm by `TOPS_WRIST_FOLLOW` = 0.2, the wrist bent back), inward on the drops, the TT extensions and base bar; the drops are held `DROPS_BACK` = 3.5 cm behind the grip anchor, clear of the hook's bend; the thumb round a bar wraps it against the fingers from the palm's edge over the wrist's side to the far side (`hand::WRAP_THUMB_PHI`: under the tops and flat grips, over the drops and the TT bars), over a hood it hooks down the hood's inner side and forward (`hand::HOOD_THUMB`); holding up the phone the hand turns at the wrist so the palm faces the face, the phone in front of it (`pose::palm_towards`; before, the back of the hand was over the screen). The hoods keep the draped grip (Q31 stays open). Tests: every bike's grips at 1.50, 1.78 and 2.05 m – the palm's normal within 30° of down (hoods, tops, flat grips) or of inward (drops, TT), the thumb inward of and under the palm (hoods, tops, flat) or above the bar (drops, TT), the fingertips under the bar (tops, flat), inside it (drops, TT) or over the hood's front, the left palm the right one's mirror image within 15°; the phone's palm towards the head with the phone on its side; the no-clipping tests unchanged. Scenes `fix-grip-<grip>-<right|left|above>`. Tests: every bike's hoods, tops and drops (the TT extensions and base bar, the MTB and gravel grips) at 1.50, 1.78 and 2.05 m: the hand's shape, no finger or thumb in a bar, a grip or a hood's body (`bikes::held_bars`), the fingertips round or over what is held; the phone in the fingers and the fingers round it; open hands up; loose hands standing; the gloves covering or exposing the fingertips for every glove; the fingertip colour; the pose tests (hands on the grips, the phone's timeline smooth). #### 4O – W5 refined: accounts, inventory and hearts in the backend (planning, 2026-11-16, v3.88)

**Decided by the user (2026-11-16):** "include in ocw-server. build the hosting parts, do the hosting manually later. Accounts are handled by backend and all inventory and hearts balance is saved there. use postgresql. one wallet per account, one rider profile per account. no local wallet. give the rider 5000 hearts start budget, with which he has to buy his bike and shoes, helmet, jerseys and such."

- **In `ocw-server`:** the backend becomes part of the modular monolith (9): the accounts service (`services/accounts`, today its own binary `ocw-accounts`, v3.46) becomes a library linked into `ocw-server`, next to the new **workshop** and **rides** modules. One binary with roles: `ocw-server --game …` (the QUIC game server, as today), `--backend …` (the Axum HTTPS API: `/auth`, `/account`, `/workshop`, `/rides`), or both in one process (a small installation). Workshop actions stay off the QUIC game connection (4E).
- **PostgreSQL** (`sqlx` with checked-in migrations, `ocw-server migrate`): accounts and linked identities, refresh tokens (hashes), the **rider** (one per account: name – unique, 4N Q8 –, character, kit colours, weight, height, FTP), `hearts_ledger` (append-only: delta, reason – ride, workout, event, achievement, purchase, sale, repair, grant –, reference, time; the balance is the sum, cached in the account row inside the same transaction), `items` (catalogue part, price paid, bought at, condition, ridden flag), `bikes` (frame item, slot → item, look, hook), `ride_uploads` and idempotency keys. The JSON store of v3.46 stays only as the test double behind the same trait; the hosted backend uses PostgreSQL only.
- **One account = one wallet = one rider profile.** The local `riders.toml` with several profiles is replaced for signed-in use: the rider comes from the account; another person on the same computer signs in with their own account (switching rider = switching account). Settings that are not the rider (graphics, keys, audio) stay local.
- **No local wallet:** `workshop.toml` and `hearts-ledger.jsonl` go away. Without an account there is no workshop shop and no hearts: the rider rides the **plain default bike and kit** everywhere (as the browser's anonymous riding, Phase 10 Q5, v2.78), the kiosks and show mode included. The local wallets made so far are test data: **not imported** (the one-time import and the 2,000 ♥ for old FIT files of 4E / Q3 are dropped).
- **Start: 5,000 ♥ and nothing owned.** A new account buys its **bike** (frameset with its base parts, 4F) and its **kit** – shoes, helmet, jersey, shorts and the rest of the apparel (4E Q4). Body, skin, hair, glasses and the character (4N) stay free. The earning rate stays (Q3: 1 ♥ per 10 kJ + 1 ♥ per 20 m climbing). With 4H's prices 5,000 ♥ buys an entry or mid-tier bike and a full kit with hearts left over (to be checked against `assets/parts.toml` in W5c; the first-bike flow shows the total).
- **Hosting parts are built, hosting is manual later:** a `deploy/backend/` kit – the systemd units (`ocw-server` backend and game roles), a Caddy (and an nginx) TLS proxy example, the config file template, PostgreSQL setup (role, database, `pg_hba`, migrations), backup and restore (`pg_dump`, a timer) and a health endpoint (`/healthz`), with a README chapter *Hosting the backend* that the user follows. The Google / Strava registrations and the domain stay with the user (9.1.1 *To go live*).

**Stages (each with tests, full checks, merge as usual):**
- **W5a – Backend in `ocw-server` on PostgreSQL:** the accounts library linked into `ocw-server` (roles), the PostgreSQL store with migrations implementing the existing store trait, the account data moved there; tests against a throw-away PostgreSQL on marge (`initdb` in a temp dir, no system service needed; `make test-backend`).
- **W5b – The rider in the account:** the rider profile API (`GET/PUT /account/rider`), the apps read and write it when signed in, the name rules of 4N (unique, all scripts, no filter), `riders.toml` only for the anonymous default.
- **W5c – Ledger, inventory, purchases:** `POST /workshop/purchase` / `sell` / `repair` with idempotency keys, one transaction each (balance, catalogue price, compatibility, ownership), the 5,000 ♥ grant on account creation, the **first-bike flow** in the workshop (an empty wall, the catalogue opens; riding with your own bike needs a frameset, a helmet and shoes – Q17), the apps' workshop switched from the local wallet to the API (the browser too, B6 parity).
- **W5d – Crediting:** game servers credit the hearts of a ride they hosted (Q19), local and offline rides through the uploaded ride summary after the 6.4 plausibility checks (Q20); the server checks ownership of the parts in `BikeChange` (an unknown or not-owned part counts as the base part, 4E).
- **W5e – Hosting kit:** `deploy/backend/` and the README chapter, tested by bringing the whole backend up on marge in a container-free throw-away setup (PostgreSQL, `ocw-server --backend`, Caddy with a local certificate) and running the sign-in and purchase flows against it.
- *Built (v6.23) – the backend part of W5a, W5c and W5d:* **PostgreSQL** under the accounts library (`services/accounts/src/pg.rs`, `storage.kind = "postgres"`, `sqlx` 0.8, migrations `services/accounts/migrations/0001_accounts.sql` and `0002_workshop.sql`, applied at start; the URL from `DATABASE_URL` or `storage.url_env`, never printed): the accounts, identities, refresh tokens and sealed provider tokens behind the existing `Store` trait (the JSON file and memory stores stay for development and their tests), and a new `WorkshopStore` – `accounts.hearts` (the cached balance, `CHECK (hearts >= 0)`), `hearts_ledger` (append-only by a trigger, reasons checked, one `start` and one credit per ride by unique indexes), `items`, `bikes` (hook, profile, paint, slot → item, condition), `kit`, `idempotency` (key, request hash, the first answer), `ride_uploads` (source, server key, status credited / flagged / refused, the hearts it is worth, time window, reasons, the summary). Every change is one transaction with the account row locked (`FOR UPDATE`). **The workshop** (`services/accounts/src/workshop/`): on first use the account gets **5,000 ♥** (`start`) and a free **starter bike** with its base parts, nothing else (Q21 (a); Q16's rusty city bike has no model or profile yet, so the starter is the base road bike until it has); the rules of the local garage (4D) checked against `assets/parts.toml` – a frameset bought is a new bike with **base parts in every slot** (Q18 (a)) and the parts bought with it, parts fit by bike type and frame profile, groupsets with their crankset, cassette and chain, refunds of the price paid (half once ridden 1 km), base parts, the starter and the last bike not for sale, at most 24 bikes. Endpoints (bearer token): `GET /workshop` (balance, garage in the local garage's shape, the newest ledger lines), `GET /workshop/ledger`, `POST /workshop/purchase` (`buy_part`, `buy_bike`) and `/workshop/sell` (`sell`, `sell_bike`) with a required `Idempotency-Key` (a repeat gets the first answer, the key with another request is refused), `POST /workshop/garage` (`equip`, `unequip`, `select`, `paint`); the account's export and deletion include the workshop. **Crediting (Q19 (a)):** `POST /rides/credit` takes a ride credit signed by a game server – `ocw_world::manifest::SignedDocument` (new: any document signed by a certified signing key under its own context, here `OCW ride credit v1`), checked against the roots of `[hearts] roots` and `revoked`, the issue time within the key's validity, at most 7 days old, the hearts recomputed from work and climbing (1 ♥ / 10 kJ + 1 ♥ / 20 m); `POST /rides/summary` takes the app's summary (1 Hz power, cadence and heart rate, devices, work, distance, climbing, weight) and runs the 6.4 checks of `ocw_account_api::plausibility`: refused – malformed, older than 30 days or in the future, virtual power or no power source; flagged and held (no hearts until reviewed) – the power-duration curve above 25 / 12 / 7.5 / 6.6 / 6.2 W/kg at 5 s / 1 / 5 / 20 / 60 min, a sample above 2,500 W, a jump above 1,500 W in a second, more than 60 s of ≥ 150 W without cadence or no cadence at all, the same power for 10 minutes, a flat heart rate under a changing load, work not matching the samples, more than 90 km/h on average or more climbing than the distance allows. Each ride is booked once (its id is the transaction's key), and a ride whose time overlaps a ride credited or held before is refused – no hearts twice for a ride sent both ways; the ridden bike's parts and the worn kit count the distance (refunds). **The apps' side (Q20 (a)):** the new wasm crate `crates/ocw-account-api` has the wire types, the checks, `offline::Synced` (the workshop last synced, per account) with the read-only rule (`allowed`: offline nothing is bought, sold or changed) and `OfflineQueue` (JSON lines, a ride id never twice; `upload` sends in order, keeps everything after the first network error, drops what the backend refuses as a request). Tests: unit tests of the rules, checks and queue; `services/accounts/tests/workshop.rs` end to end over HTTP on the memory store and on PostgreSQL (start balance and base parts, buying and selling, idempotency, eight purchases at once never below zero, signed credit accepted / rogue root, tampered and greedy credits refused, plausible / flagged / virtual / overlapping summaries, the offline queue uploaded once, export and deletion), `tests/postgres.rs` (the `Store` rules on PostgreSQL, the database's own guards); `make test-accounts` runs them against a throw-away PostgreSQL 17.11 (the pinned portable Linux x86_64 build of `io.zonky.test.postgres`, SHA-256 checked, cached in `~/.cache/ocw/`, `initdb` in a temporary directory, nothing installed system-wide). README *Accounts with PostgreSQL: workshop and hearts*. *Not yet (next steps):* the desktop's workshop and wallet on the account when signed in (the local test wallet, marked local, when signed out) with the sync for offline riding and the queued summaries from the ride's recording, the browser app's workshop (B6 parity), the game server sending its signed credits at a ride's end, `ocw-server --backend` roles and `deploy/backend/` (hosting on Fly.io with PostgreSQL, a later step), the rider profile API of W5b, repairs (`/workshop/repair`) and the ownership check of `BikeChange`.
- *Built (v6.42) – the desktop's side of W5c and W5d, the game server's credits:* **The workshop on the account** (`apps/desktop/src/account/workshop.rs`, `workshop/mod.rs` `follow_account`, `wallet.rs` `AccountView`): signed in, the workshop is the account's – its balance, ledger and garage as the backend last answered, also over the free garage of *Ride locally* (Training mode, 3.2.4 Q4, is the signed-out case); signed out, the local test wallet comes back, marked "local test wallet" ("free (Training mode) · local"), never imported (Q21 (a)). Buying, selling, fitting, taking off, selecting, painting and buying or selling a bike – from the console or the workshop's own clicks, which run the same commands – become actions (`ocw_account_api::workshop::Action`) for the `ocw-account` thread, each with a fresh `Idempotency-Key`; the frame loop never waits: the line reads "saving …", the answer (garage and balance, or the backend's refusal) is applied a frame later and printed in the console. Opening the workshop fetches it again. **Waking backends** (a hosted backend that stops when idle answers after a few seconds): 20 s timeouts, one more try after 3 s before going offline, "connecting to your account …" until the first answer, and every minute a new try while offline. **Offline (Q20 (a)):** the workshop last synced is kept per account in `<data dir>/ocw/accounts/<account>/workshop.json` (written atomically), the app rides with it and the workshop is read-only ("account, offline (read-only)"; `offline::allowed`). **The ride's summary:** when a ride is saved, signed in and not credited by the server, the recording becomes a `RideSummary` (`ocw_client::ride_summary`: power, cadence and heart rate once a second, seconds of virtual power – the virtual trainer, keyboard power – count 0 W, none at all: no summary; climbing from the altitude's rises at most 2 m a second; not for captures or `--no-hearts`), queued in `ride-queue.jsonl` beside the cache and uploaded in order by the account thread whenever the backend answers; the backend credits it once after the 6.4 checks. Repairs, hanging a spare frame and `hearts.grant` say they are not available with an account yet. **Game servers crediting (Q19 (a)):** `ocw-server --credit-key FILE` (a signing key of `world-builder keys new-signing`, certified by a root in the backend's `[hearts] roots`) and `--credit-backend URL` (default: the sign-in's issuer): when a signed-in rider leaves, `GameServer` hands the ride – the work and climbing of the hearts meter and the metres ridden with real power – to `ocw_server::credits::BackendCredits`, which signs a `RideCredit` (`OCW ride credit v1`) and posts it to `/rides/credit` on its own thread, retrying every 30 s (20 tries) while the backend does not answer; a ride that earned nothing is not sent, anonymous riders and bots never. `Welcome.hearts_credited` (field 23) tells the apps that this server credits, so they upload no summary of the ride (no hearts twice; the backend refuses overlapping rides as well). The local server credits nothing. Tests: `ride_summary` (a recording passes the checks, virtual seconds earn nothing, who uploads), `account::workshop` (the cache and queue per account over a restart; a ride queued while the backend is down, read-only offline, uploaded and credited once when online, a repeat changing nothing), `workshop::tests::signed_in_the_workshop_is_the_accounts` (against the in-process backend: the account's 5,000 ♥ and starter bike in Training mode, a purchase sent and answered without blocking, a refusal, read-only offline, the cache file, signed out the local wallet again), the server's `a_signed_in_riders_ride_is_credited_when_they_leave` and `tests/credits_backend.rs` (a certified server's credit booked once, a rogue root's never). Screenshot: `scripts/workshop-account-shot.sh`. *Not yet:* the browser app's workshop on the account (B6 parity), repairs (`/workshop/repair`) and the ownership check of `BikeChange`, the rider profile API of W5b, `ocw-server --backend` roles and the hosting kit.
- *Built (v6.43) – W5c in the browser (B6 parity):* the workshop (`apps/desktop/src/workshop/` → `crates/ocw-ui/src/workshop/`: the scene, the input, the pickers, the designer, the garage and wallet, the account's workshop of v6.42) is one module for both apps; what differs is the app's `WorkshopHost` (`local_server`, `capture`, `no_hearts`, `requires_account`, the wallet's folder, the session's start and four account functions: signed in, the workshop's update since a generation, send an action, sync) and the ride, read through `RideAccess` into `RideNow` each frame (the server's hearts, distance, damage, the build's effect, the race mode; the steering given back when the workshop closes). `RiderProfiles` moved to `ocw-ui::profiles` (the desktop keeps them in `ocw.toml [riders]` through a `ProfilesStore`). **The browser** (`apps/web/src/workshop.rs`): signed in, `GET /workshop` at once (the cached copy from `localStorage` first, `ocw.account.<id>.workshop`), the actions as `fetch()` calls with a random `Idempotency-Key`, their answers applied by the frame loop a frame later, offline read-only (Q20 (a)) with a new try every minute; *Workshop* in the menu, which opens the locked page for anonymous riders, opens the workshop once signed in; a ride saved with `ride.save` becomes a ride summary (virtual seconds count no power, not on a server that credits itself) queued in `ocw.account.<id>.rides` and uploaded in order when the backend answers. Signed out, `workshop`, `character`, `kit.design` and the garage commands answer "log in to customize" (`ocw_core::character::may_customize`, Phase 10 Q5): the browser has no local wallet. Tests: the page's account state (`workshop::tests`: cache first, the backend's answer, another account's ignored, an action's answer, offline read-only and the minute's retry, the ride queue kept offline, uploaded once, refused rides dropped), `plugin::tests::a_signed_in_rider_gets_the_accounts_workshop` (anonymous locked; signed in: "connecting", then "5,000 ♥ · account", the workshop opens, a purchase sent without waiting), the desktop's workshop and account tests unchanged on the shared module; `scripts/test-web-account.py` in headless Chromium against `ocw-server --auth-dev`: carbon wheels bought on the account through the redirect sign-in ("balance 3,585 ♥"), the workshop open (screenshot), the copy kept in `localStorage`. *Not yet:* repairs on the account and the ownership check of `BikeChange` (W5d), the rider profile API of W5b.
- *Built (v6.44) – repairs with accounts and the ownership check (W5d, W6):* **Repairs** – `Action::Repair { bike, part }` (`POST /workshop/repair`, an idempotency key, ledger reason `repair`: one part or every damaged one) at the local garage's price, now shared (`ocw_sim::damage::slot_price` – the item's price paid, else the slot's cheapest paid part that fits, else 20 ♥; wheels and tyres half – and `repair_price`), refused when nothing needs it or the balance is short; `Action::Damage { bike, condition, injury }` (`/workshop/garage`, free) keeps the damage a ride left – the bike's parts in per mille and the rider's injury (new `Garage.injury`, columns `accounts.injury_pm` / `injury_at`, migration `0003_injury.sql`) – sent by the app quietly when the server's damage changes (`keep_damage`), one at a time, while the backend answers; `workshop.repair` and the workshop's repair dialog go to the account when signed in. **Ownership check** – `ServerConfig.ownership` (`ocw-server --check-parts`; the garage from `--credit-backend` or the sign-in's issuer): at the hello and at each `BikeChange` of a signed-in rider the server asks `ocw_server::ownership::BackendOwnership` to fetch the garage (`GET /workshop` with the rider's own access token, a thread of its own, one more try after 3 s); `owned_build` keeps only the parts the account owns and base parts, a bike profile the garage has no bike of becomes the starter's (`road`), an anonymous rider or a garage not known yet gets base parts only; when the garage arrives (`take_updated`, checked each tick) the bike the rider asked for last applies again with what they own. Without the check (the local server, the apps' own garages) every part counts as before. Tests: the backend's rules (damage kept and refused, the local rule's price, the frame beyond repair at the full price, too few hearts, unknown parts), the server's `only_owned_parts_count_when_the_server_checks` (owned, not owned, anonymous, a profile not owned, the garage arriving later), the desktop's account workshop test (a repair refused as not needed). *Not yet:* the rider profile API of W5b (built in v6.45).
- *Built (v6.49) – W5b, the rider in the account:* `ocw_account_api::rider::RiderDoc` (the name and the apps' `ocw_client::riders::Rider` as JSON, ≤ 16 KiB); `GET /account/rider` (404 without one) and `PUT /account/rider` (`services/accounts/src/riders.rs`: the name through `ocw_core::name::check` – 2–20 graphemes of every script, no filter, reserved names refused –, unique by `name::key` across accounts, 409 `name_taken`; the account's display name renamed with it, `Store::rename`, so the next tokens and the rides show it); storage: `riders` (account, name, unique `name_key`, `doc` JSONB, `updated_at`; migration `0004_riders.sql`, cascading with the account) on PostgreSQL, in memory otherwise; the rider in the account's export (`modules.rider`) and deleted with it. **The apps** (`ocw_ui::profiles`: `RiderProfiles` and `RiderAccount`, `follow_rider` in both): signed in, the account's rider becomes the riding rider (the local one set aside, back when signed out) and the look applies to the ride (`workshop.apply`); an account without a rider gets the one ridden until then, once and only with a valid name (the default "Rider" is reserved: the rider names themself first); every change of the riding rider (the character editor, the jersey designer, the bike) goes to the account 2 s later; a refused name brings the account's rider back with the reason in the console. The desktop's account thread (`GET` after the sign-in, `PUT`, kept for later while offline), the browser's `fetch()` calls. The account's garage follows a rider renamed (the workshop re-adopts it under the new name). Tests: `RiderDoc` shape and size, the memory store's unique names, `tests/workshop.rs` `rider_of_the_account` on memory and PostgreSQL (none at first, kept trimmed, the account's name follows, another account refused in any case, bad names and shapes refused, in the export, the name free again after the deletion), `profiles::tests::the_account_rider_rides_when_signed_in` (the reserved default not offered, the local rider offered once, the account's arriving, a change sent once after the delay, the local rider back when signed out). *Not yet:* `ocw-server --backend` roles and the hosting kit (W5e), renaming in a ride (Q15).

**Open questions (to the user; proposals in brackets):**
- **Q16 – Before the first purchase: decided (2026-11-17, dashboard): street clothes and an old, rusty city bike** – the user: "A new account user wears sneakers, jeans and hoodie. His bike is an old and rusty city bike. Everything else needs to be purchased." A new account starts in sneakers, jeans and a hoodie on an old, rusty city bike; bike, shoes, helmet, jerseys and every other part or piece of kit are bought with the 5000-heart start budget or earned hearts. *Details not decided (proposals):* the city bike gets its own physics profile (heavy, upright position, slower); the starter outfit and bike are owned from the start, free, and cannot be sold.
- **Q17 – What is needed to ride your own bike: decided (2026-11-17, dashboard): nothing – the starter equipment of Q16 is ridden until something is bought** – the user: "you are equipped with a rusty city bike, sneakers and hoody." A new rider rides the rusty city bike in sneakers, jeans and a hoodie; each item bought (a bike, shoes, helmet, jersey, shorts, …) replaces its starter counterpart when equipped. There is no plain default jersey or shorts and no minimum set to buy before riding.
- **Q18 – Base parts: decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a), base parts included, so 5,000 ♥ buys a complete bike; built in v6.23 (the backend's purchases, *Built (v6.23)* above)** – with accounts every rider starts with 5,000 hearts (♥, the in-game currency; 1 ♥ is about 1 € of the real price) and buys their bike. A bike is a frameset plus parts in its slots – wheels, groupset, tyres and so on. The question: does a bought frameset come with free basic entry-level parts in every slot (the base parts of 4F), so it can be ridden at once, or does every part have to be bought separately? (See 4O *Start: 5,000 ♥ and nothing owned*: "its bike (frameset with its base parts, 4F)" – possibly already answered.) Options: (a) base parts included; (b) every part bought. Proposal: a – base parts included, so 5,000 ♥ buys a complete bike.
- **Q19 – Which game servers credit hearts: decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a), servers signed by the project's root key credit directly, rides elsewhere count through the uploaded ride summary after the plausibility checks; built in v6.23 on the backend (`/rides/credit`, `/rides/summary`), the game server's sending and the desktop's upload in v6.42** – riders earn hearts by riding (1 ♥ per 10 kJ of work plus a little for climbing). Anybody can run an OCW game server – ours, a friend's, or the app's own *Host a ride* – and a modified server could hand out hearts freely. So which servers may add hearts to an account? Options: (a) only servers whose key is signed by our project's root key credit directly; rides on any other server count through the ride summary the app uploads afterwards, which must pass the plausibility checks of 6.4 (power curve, cadence, trusted devices); (b) every server credits directly; (c) only our servers, other rides earn nothing. Proposal: a.
- **Q20 – Offline riding: decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a), offline with the bikes and kit last synced, read-only, the ride's summary queued and credited after the checks; built in v6.23: the backend's once-per-ride crediting and the queue and read-only rule in `ocw-account-api`; the desktop's cache, queue and read-only workshop in v6.42** – bikes, kit and hearts live in the account on the server (4O). A signed-in rider without internet, or with the server down, may still want to ride with their own bike. Options: (a) the rider rides offline with the bikes and kit last synced, read-only (no buying or selling); the ride's summary is queued, uploaded when online and credited after the checks; (b) offline only on the plain default bike and kit, without hearts; (c) no riding without the server. Related: 3.2.4 Q4, the rider of *Ride locally*. Proposal: a.
- **Q21 – Existing riders: decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a), everybody starts fresh with 5,000 ♥ and nothing owned; the local test wallets are not imported; built in v6.23 (the backend's start)** – before accounts, the test riders had a local wallet on their computer with hearts and parts. With accounts the local wallet goes away (4O). Options: (a) everybody starts fresh with 5,000 ♥ and nothing owned; (b) keep something of the old wallets, e.g. the bikes or the balance. (See 4O *No local wallet*: "the local wallets made so far are test data: not imported" – possibly already answered.) Proposal: a.
