Verdict: on the test route SIMD does not change the WebKit RSS (+2 / −17 MB, inside the spread); in Liechtenstein the median is 65 / 70 MB (4 – 5 %) higher with SIMD, but the runs overlap (without 1,315 – 1,368 at the end, with 1,348 – 1,454) and the load swung from run to run – a small rise in the world ride cannot be ruled out, a large one is not there. The phone's count (wasm + WebGL) is the same or 3 MB lower. Linux WebKit's RSS is not iOS's footprint; a real iPhone would settle it. Frame rate (uncapped headless Chromium, `scripts/wasm-size-fps.sh`, 3 rounds alternating, load average 15 – 22; `test-output/wasm-size/q10-fps2/fps/`), medians without → with SIMD: `make web` WebGPU 46.9 → 52.0 fps, WebGL 2 53.3 → 59.6; the preview's WebGPU 54.0 → 38.1, WebGL 2 42.4 → 41.1 – the rounds of one page swung by up to 25 fps, so no difference can be read (a first run of 2 rounds, `q10/fps/`, had timeouts). Tests: the WebKit case `too-old` (`make test-web-webkit`: `WebAssembly.validate` stubbed – the message on the start page and on a ride link, no rides offered, no module fetched, no page error; every other case checks that WebKit has SIMD), `test-web-gpu`'s logic checks (`simd()` with a refusing, missing and throwing WebAssembly; the test module without its v128 parts validates), `test_web_scripts.py` (`WasmSimd`: the section parser, `--require`, the site's refusal).

**B3 – Multiplayer in the browser: done (v3.02).** `?server=https://HOST:47801&cert-hash=HEX&name=Ada` joins a remote `ocw-server` session over WebTransport; desktop (`ocw-desktop --server`), `ocw-bot` and browser riders ride together and see each other.

- **Server:** the WebTransport endpoint of 6.2 (`--webtransport`, `web-transport-quinn` on our quinn endpoint, UDP 47801, path `/ocw/1`; the 13-day ECDSA certificate by hash, kept in `--tls-dir`, rotated two days before the end; `--web-info-file`; per-endpoint counters in `--stats-file`). The startup prints the page options.
- **One client loop:** the browser's `WebSession` runs the shared `ClientCore` (prediction, reconciliation with the snapshot age from the RTT, interpolation of the others) on either the local `FrameServer` or a `RemoteLink`: the wasm-safe `ocw_server::wire::ClientLink` state machine plus a `Transport` that only moves bytes – in the browser `webtransport.rs` (own `wasm-bindgen` bindings for `WebTransport`, its bidirectional stream and datagrams: web-sys has them only behind `web_sys_unstable_apis`), in the tests a fake over an in-memory `GameServer` (datagrams, stream-only, reordering, refusal). Messages are time-stamped when the transport gets them. The HUD shows "Connecting to the server …" / "Disconnected: …" as on the desktop; `net.stats` shows the link, the RTT (`getStats().smoothedRtt`, else Hello → Welcome), counters, the snapshot timing and the riders seen; `window.ocw.netStats()` gives the same as JSON. Dev commands only on the local server.
- **Anonymous rider (Q5):** browser riders send `RiderLook::anonymous()` (grey frame, light grey kit, white helmet, plain) on the standard road bike; no customization until accounts (Phase 5) – only the name (`name=`).
- **Snapshot timing:** `ocw_server::timing::SnapshotTiming` (interval mean / jitter / percentiles, age = arrival wall clock − the snapshot's server instant `world_unix_ms − offset_ms`, meaningful on one machine), used by the browser and `ocw-bot` (its report's `timing`), so both are measured alike. `ocw-bot --server https://…` rides over WebTransport natively.
- **Tests:** `wire` (frames from any chunking, the state machine: queueing, samples on the stream until answered, datagrams only when allowed and small enough, broken frames, the first close reason), `timing`, the certificate (13-day validity in the DER, ECDSA P-256, rotation, kept in the directory, damaged / too-long files replaced), WebTransport URLs, `services/server/tests/webtransport_loopback.rs` (a WebTransport client joins and rides with samples as datagrams; QUIC and WebTransport riders in one session see each other's power; stream-only fallback; a wrong hash and the native certificate are refused; a shutdown reaches the client; rotation while running: the old session goes on, the old hash is refused, the new one joins), the browser session and plugin over the fake transport, the page options. **End to end:** `make test-web-multiplayer` (`scripts/test-web-multiplayer.py`): on marge `ocw-server --listen --webtransport` (Hills, no server bots), two `ocw-bot` riders over QUIC and one over WebTransport (all following the browser rider), headless Chromium on WebGPU joins with the cert hash, sets noon with the time machine (`--time-control anyone`), rides 30 s; checks: joined over WebTransport, ≥ 2 other riders seen, the server applied its samples (`last_input_seq`, the rider at 200 W in the server log, WebTransport datagrams in the statistics), every bot saw the browser rider; screenshot. `--desktop` adds `ocw-desktop --server` (headless X11) to the session.

**Measured (marge, 2026-11-14, everything on one machine, 30 s; `test-output/web/web-mp-20261114-061908.*`):** all checks passed with 2 QUIC bots, 1 WebTransport bot, the desktop client and the browser in one session (5 riders); the browser joined 2.4 s after navigation and saw all 4 others; the server applied its samples up to #121 (4 Hz for 30 s), the WebTransport endpoint received 263 messages from the browser and the WebTransport bot, 255 of them as datagrams.

| snapshots at | interval mean | jitter (σ) | p95 / p99 / max | age mean / p95 / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| browser (WebTransport, Chromium 156) | 100.0 ms | 16.2 ms | 115 / 126 / 226 ms | −5.9 / 8.5 / 239 ms |
| `ocw-bot` over WebTransport | 100.0 ms | 3.7 ms | 104 / 117 / 126 ms | −6.4 / 0.0 / 20 ms |
| `ocw-bot` over QUIC (×2) | 100.0 ms | 3.0–3.6 ms | 104 / 109–119 / 120 ms | −7.6 / −3.5 / 12 ms |

The ages carry a common offset of about −8 ms (the server's tick instant runs slightly ahead of the wall clock), so the one-way delay is a few ms everywhere. WebTransport itself adds nothing measurable (the WebTransport bot equals the QUIC ones); the browser's extra jitter (≈ one 60 Hz frame) comes from its main thread: the datagram reader's promises resolve between the frames Bevy renders, so arrivals are frame-quantised, and a long frame (start-up, shader compilation) delays a few snapshots (max 226 ms). The interpolation delay (6.3, 100–150 ms) covers it. A repeat after rebasing on 3.00 (`web-mp-20261114-063344`): browser jitter 12.9 ms (max 133 ms), the bots 2.8–8.4 ms – the bots' jitter depends on the load of the shared CPU (the desktop client renders in software on it); without the desktop client it was 0.01 ms.

**B3 worker – the WebTransport connections read in a Web Worker: built (v5.81); on by default for the sensor bridge, opt-in for the game link.** The sensor bridge's connection (10D.2) and – with `net-worker=on` – the game connection (B3) are held by a dedicated worker, `web/ocw-net-worker.js` (plain JS, 4 KB, served next to the page and copied into the site's `xr/`); the wasm client logic stays on the page's thread.

- **What it does.** The worker opens the `WebTransport` (`serverCertificateHashes`), the bidirectional stream and the datagrams, and stamps every chunk and datagram with the wall clock (`performance.timeOrigin + performance.now()`) when it comes off the network; it posts them to the page in arrival order with a running number, the bytes **transferred** (`postMessage` with the `ArrayBuffer` in the transfer list, no copy). The page's sends go the other way the same way; the worker also reports `getStats().smoothedRtt` once a second. The page (`ocw-web` `netconn`) gives both users the same events (connected, stream bytes, datagram, stream end, failed, closed, RTT) whichever thread reads: `webtransport.rs` (the game link) and `bridge.rs` (the bridge) no longer hold JS objects themselves.
- **Who reads (page option `net-worker`):** `bridge` (the default) the bridge in the worker, the game link on the page's thread; `on` both in the worker; `off` both on the page's thread; `refuse` the worker refuses every connection (the fallback test). The default follows the measurement below: the bridge gains (its readings 0.37 instead of 11 ms old), the game link's own rider loses.
- **No `SharedArrayBuffer`:** GitHub Pages cannot send the COOP / COEP headers, so the page is not cross-origin isolated there (`make web-serve` sends them, the published preview cannot); `postMessage` with transferables is enough for 10 snapshots and a few frames a second.
- **The stamps in the client** (the game link in the worker). `ClientLink` records the worker's stamp as the message's arrival (snapshot interval, jitter, age, the handshake RTT). `WebSession::receive` hands each message to `ClientCore::on_server_message_at` with its arrival on the game clock (`now − (wall now − stamp)`, at most 1 s back) and the time of the last prediction step (`Time<Fixed>`): a snapshot counts as having come at its arrival (the others' interpolation, the clock, the weather, contacts), and `ArrivalClock::late_ticks_stamped` keeps its lead at arrival (fractional) in the window, so the own prediction extrapolates it by the steps taken since it came, not since an earlier read set the baseline. On the page's thread the reads stay frame-quantised and the client works as before (`on_server_message` with the read time; the desktop and `ocw-bot` too).
- **Fallback to the page's thread** (the code of B3 / 10D.2 as before, behind the same events): no `Worker` constructor, the script fails to load (`onerror`), no hello within 8 s (then three more 0.1 s looks, so a hello queued behind a long world-loading frame still counts – a first bridge run fell back at the 5 s of the time), a worker without `WebTransport` (its hello says so), or the page option. A worker that dies after connecting ends its connections with "the network worker failed: …" (the link shows it as a drop). `net.stats` / `window.ocw.netStats()` say who reads (`reader`: `worker` / `main thread`, `reader_note`: why the page's thread), the worker's numbers (`worker`: messages, gaps in the running number, stamps moved, how long the messages waited for a frame), the riders' motion (`motion`) and the snapshots' lateness (`late_ticks`, `extrapolated_ticks`); the bridge's JSON in `window.ocw.devices()` has `reader` and `reader_note` too.
- **Browsers.** WebTransport is exposed in dedicated workers by the standard (`[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]`), so Chrome / Edge, the Quest browser (Chromium), Firefox and Safari 26.4+ (iOS / iPadOS / macOS; the bridge's support matrix of 10D.2) should read in the worker; each does where its worker's hello reports `WebTransport`, else on the page's thread – the same code as before; only Chromium (headless, marge) was run, Safari, Firefox and the Quest browser are not tested yet (B8 browser matrix).
- **The tests' pacing:** `?frame-ms=40` keeps every frame of the page busy until 40 ms passed (a slow machine at 25 fps; `scripts/test-web-multiplayer.py --frame-ms 40` starts Chromium with `--disable-frame-rate-limit --disable-gpu-vsync`). `scripts/test-web-multiplayer.py` has `--net-worker default|on|off|refuse`, checks who read the connection, and records `motion`, `worker`, the frames per second and (`--video S`) a short video; `scripts/test-bridge.py` records who read the bridge.
- **Tests (11.4):** `netconn` (the worker's messages decoded, broken ones refused; the stamps in order pass unchanged however long they waited, a stamp ahead of the page's clock or before its connection's last is moved and counted, gaps in the running number counted, each connection has its own; the reader modes and who goes to the worker), the page options (`net-worker`, `frame-ms`, the default), `arrival` (`stamped_snapshots_are_late_by_the_steps_since_they_came`), `ocw_client::motion` (v5.40's measure as a meter: a steady ride is smooth at even and uneven frames, a jump is seen, the warm-up not counted, riders who leave and come back), `stamped_snapshots_make_the_others_smoother` (the motion probe with stamped arrivals at 14, 25 and 60 Hz: the others 0.077 → 0.038 m/s RMS at 25 Hz, max 2.96 → 0.30; 0.45 → 0.049 at 14 Hz; the own rider unchanged), the browser session over the fake transport as before; end to end `make test-web-multiplayer` (the default), the same with `--net-worker on` and `--net-worker refuse` (the fallback: read on the page's thread, all checks green) and `make test-bridge` (the bridge in the worker).

**Measured (marge, headless Chromium 156 on WebGPU, 2 QUIC + 1 WebTransport `ocw-bot` following the browser rider on Hills, 40 s per run, 3 rounds alternating; medians; `test-output/web/b3w-fix/`, the final code with the stamped `ArrivalClock`):**

| browser at | game link read on | snapshot jitter (σ) | own rider: velocity change RMS / corrections > 2 cm / mean error | others: velocity change RMS / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 fps | page's thread (default) | 14.8 ms | **0.021 m/s / 43 of 369 / 11.8 mm** | 0.58 / 21.4 m/s |
| 60 fps | worker (`on`) | **0.1 ms** | 0.043 m/s / 57 of 369 / 24.8 mm | **0.064 / 1.49 m/s** |
| 25 fps (`frame-ms=40`) | page's thread (default) | 26.4 ms | **0.033 m/s / 54 of 374 / 13.6 mm** | 1.76 / 17.8 m/s |
| 25 fps | worker (`on`) | **0.1 ms** | 0.062 m/s / 76 of 374 / 27.8 mm | 1.30 / 4.4 m/s |

Before the stamped `ArrivalClock` (`test-output/web/b3w-final/`, the same rounds): the worker's own rider 0.084 m/s / 97 corrections at 25 fps, 0.041 / 52 at 60 fps against 0.037 / 41 and 0.025 / 46 on the page's thread – the stamps in the `ArrivalClock` took a little off, not enough. The bots measure 0.01–0.02 ms jitter in the same runs: the worker's stamps are as good as a native client's, and the others ride much more smoothly (at 60 fps the RMS 9×, the largest jump 14×; at 25 fps the largest jump 4×, the RMS swung between 0.3 and 1.4 m/s from run to run). The own rider, which the prediction already timed by its steps, moves less smoothly with the worker at both rates: the worker's messages reach the page later than the page's own network reads (Chromium runs posted messages behind a busy page's frames; `worker.wait_ms` mean 27 ms at 25 fps), and 17–24 % of the snapshots are still three or more steps late after the stamped count (`late_ticks`; on the page's thread 2–18 %) – the native motion probe with messages held back a frame shows no such errors, so the cause is not settled. The bridge in the worker (`make test-bridge`, 60 s of Liechtenstein, `reader: worker`): the readings are 0.37 ms old when they come off the network (p50, p95 0.41 ms; the same run on the page's thread: 11 / 30 ms, v5.76: 10 / 31 ms – the frame's wait), the control round trip 14 ms (p50). The worker's wait max (0.5 s) is the start-up (shader compilation).

**Open (B3):** the own rider with the game link in the worker (above): why the worker's snapshots are still read three or more steps late and the corrections grow, and then the game link in the worker by default; Safari, Firefox and the Quest browser with the worker (B8 browser matrix); production certificates and no `cert-hash` (B8); a browser rider rides only test routes and packages the server has too (the Welcome check as on the desktop); reconnect after a drop needs a page reload (as on the desktop, 6.3 session hold not built); voice in the browser (B5).

**B4 – Devices in the browser: done (v3.09).** The page's **Devices** panel (bottom right; a page overlay until the menus come with B6) has **+ Trainer**, **+ Power meter** and **+ Heart rate**; each opens Chromium's Bluetooth chooser, and the device then runs **the same code as on the desktop**.

- **One protocol, two links.** `ocw-devices`' `ble` module now builds for wasm32: `protocol` (the pure state machine), `runner::run` and the new `runner::supervise` (connect → run → `Disconnected` → wait 5 s taking commands → connect again; the latest SIM / ERG target is applied on every new connection) no longer need Tokio: a `Timer` gives them time (`TokioTimer` natively, `JsTimer` = `setTimeout` in the browser; `select` of `futures`, `web_time::Instant`). The desktop's btleplug backend (`ble::btle`) uses `supervise` too. `DeviceEvent::Connected { kind }` reports what a device is once it is subscribed ("smart trainer (FTMS)", "smart trainer (Wahoo control)", "power meter", "heart-rate sensor", …); the desktop prints it.
- **The Web Bluetooth `GattLink`** (`ble::web`, pure, tested natively): the boundary `WebGatt` is what the adapter needs from a browser `BluetoothDevice` (connect, connected, discover the permitted services' characteristics with their properties, read, write with / without response, `startNotifications`, the value and `gattserverdisconnected` events, disconnect). `WebGattLink` maps the UUID strings to OCW's numbers (SIG numbers; Wahoo's 128-bit control point in any case), writes with response where the characteristic allows it, and turns the events into the runner's notification stream, which **ends with the disconnect event** (the runner sees a drop at once, not at its 1 s connection check). `run_device` = `supervise` over one device, `gatt.disconnect()` at shutdown. `DeviceKind` (trainer, power meter, heart rate) builds the `requestDevice` options: one filter per service (trainer: FTMS or Cycling Power, and `namePrefix: "KICKR"`; power meter: Cycling Power or CSC; heart rate), and every fitness service plus Wahoo's as `optionalServices` (a site may open only the services it asked for). `Remembered`: the devices this origin used (kind, browser id, name; `localStorage`, newest first, at most 8).
- **The browser side** (wasm32 only, thin): own `wasm-bindgen` bindings for `navigator.bluetooth`, `BluetoothDevice`, its GATT server, services and characteristics (web-sys has them only behind `web_sys_unstable_apis`, a cfg for the whole build; every call is structural, so a test double works as well), `JsGatt` (the `WebGatt`), `WebBluetoothBackend` (a `DeviceBackend`: the JS device waits in a thread-local slot, the backend itself is `Send`; `start` spawns `run_device` on the page's event loop). The chooser must open **in the user gesture**: the panel's click handler calls `window.ocw.connectDevice(kind)`, which calls `requestDevice` synchronously; the console's `devices.connect trainer|power|hr` works too (the Enter key is the gesture). At the start the app asks `getAvailability()` and `getDevices()` (Chromium's permission persistence): permitted devices this origin remembers reconnect **without the chooser**.
- **Shared trainer control.** `TrainerControl` (SIM / ERG, 5.3) and the workout session moved from the desktop into `ocw-client` (the desktop keeps the files, menu and commands); `TrainerControl::follow` is the per-frame step both apps run (god-mode flying, down after a crash, bump pulses, then SIM / ERG), and **SIM now follows the build in force** – `set_profile(ClientCore::effective_profile())`, i.e. the profile with the server's `RiderBuild` effect: the trainer gets the build's Crr and CdA (0.5 · ρ · CdA) and the rider + bike mass, and a change is sent at the next update interval (`SimController::set_profile`; desktop and browser).
- **The browser app** (`apps/web/src/devices.rs`, pure, tested natively): `WebDevices` holds the devices (state connecting / connected / reconnecting, last power and heart rate), the trainer control and the workout. Power comes from the **virtual trainer until a trainer or power meter is connected**, then only from the devices (a heart-rate strap alone keeps the virtual power; while a device reconnects the rider gets no power, as on the desktop; forgetting the last one brings the virtual trainer back); device samples are not virtual (hearts, 14 Phase 4 4E). Every SIM / ERG command goes to every device and to the virtual trainer (ERG: it reports the target). HUD status, e.g. `TICKR 131 bpm | KICKR 234 W | trainer SIM +2.1 % (difficulty 50 %)`; `Virtual trainer 200 W (no Web Bluetooth here)`. Console as on the desktop: `devices.list`, `devices.connect`, `devices.forget <name|id|all>`, `trainer.mode sim|erg|off`, `trainer.difficulty`, `erg.target`, `workout start --example …|stop|skip|pause|resume|status|list` (the bundled examples; the panel shows in the HUD); page option `ftp=`. `window.ocw.devices()` gives the state as JSON (the panel and the tests read it).
- **Without Web Bluetooth** (Firefox, Safari, iOS; Q1): the panel's buttons are disabled with the message "This browser has no Web Bluetooth (Firefox, Safari, iOS): riding with virtual power …"; the console says it once; the HUD says "(no Web Bluetooth here)". No adapter (`getAvailability()` false): "No Bluetooth adapter (or Bluetooth is off)".
- **Tests (no hardware):** `ble::web` against a fake browser device (`FakeDevice`: an FTMS trainer with Device Information, an older KICKR with the upper-case Wahoo UUID, a strap): discovery and write types, notifications ending with the disconnect, **the whole trainer flow through the shared state machine** (connect → subscribe → power events → SIM 3 % / 5 % writes → ERG 200 W → drop → reconnect → control, start and the ERG target again → shutdown disconnects), the KICKR with Wahoo control and a failed reconnect attempt, the strap; `supervise` with a mock (failed attempt, drop, a target set while away applied on reconnect); `SimController` / `TrainerControl` with a new build; `WebDevices` (virtual until a power device, states and messages, commands to every device, a late device gets the latest target, ERG and workouts, the no-Bluetooth wording); the plugin's commands headless.
- **Browser tests on marge (headless Chromium 156, WebGPU):**
  - `make test-web-ble` – a **fake `navigator.bluetooth`** (`scripts/web-ble-fake.js`, injected with `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`; an FTMS trainer at 321 W / 88 rpm that holds ERG targets like an ideal trainer, a strap at 142 bpm; `getDevices` from the session) and real mouse clicks (`Input.dispatchMouseEvent`: `navigator.userActivation` is active in `requestDevice`). 18 checks passed (`test-output/web/web-ble-fake-20261114-092226*`): virtual 120 W first; + Trainer → the rider rides on 321 W from the device; the filters / optional services; + Heart rate; 12 s on the Hills: control, start, **29 SIM writes** with the hills' gradients (3.4 … 2.6 %, then down to −0.8 %); `erg.target 180` → the write `05 b4 00` and the rider at 180 W; a drop (out of range 3 s) → "reconnecting", connected again after the 5 s pause with control, start and ERG 180 re-sent; SIM again; a **reload** → both devices back without a chooser (0 `requestDevice` calls); `#nobt` (no `navigator.bluetooth`) → virtual power, disabled buttons and the message.
  - `make test-web-ble-emulation` – **Chromium's own Web Bluetooth stack** with a simulated peripheral: DevTools `BluetoothEmulation` (on the **browser** target in Chromium 156, not the page) – `simulatePreconnectedPeripheral`, `addService` / `addCharacteristic` and the CCCD descriptor 0x2902 (without it `startNotifications` fails with "GATT Error: Not supported"), the GATT and characteristic operations answered from the test – and the chooser answered with `DeviceAccess.selectPrompt` (**one answer per prompt**: Chromium fires `deviceRequestPrompted` twice and a second `selectPrompt` fails a CHECK, the browser exits). A KICKR-like device (Cycling Power + Wahoo's control point): chooser, connection, discovery ("smart trainer (Wahoo control)"), both subscriptions and the Wahoo writes (unlock, SIM mode, then a grade every 1.5 s) arrive. The emulation cannot send notifications, so no power arrives and no write is answered (the protocol's write timeout releases the next one); power and answers are the fake's part.
  - `make test-web-ble-real` – **the real Wahoo KICKR from the browser:** headless Chromium on marge reaches BlueZ over D-Bus; Web Bluetooth on Linux needs `--enable-experimental-web-platform-features` (without it there is no `navigator.bluetooth`; `getDevices` also with `--enable-features=WebBluetoothNewPermissionsBackend`). The chooser's list comes over `DeviceAccess` (14 devices around marge); the test picks "Wahoo KICKR A208" and rides: connected as **"smart trainer (Wahoo control)"** (this KICKR has Cycling Power + Wahoo's control point, no FTMS), 21 power samples in 20 s (0 W: nobody pedalled), 70 SIM commands with the hills' gradients, ERG (`erg.target 100` sent as 60 W: the ERG controller's low-cadence catch-up, 0.6 × target, with nobody pedalling), back to SIM; no rejected request (`test-output/web/web-ble-real-20261114-092815*`). Connecting took 21 s (BlueZ's first GATT discovery of the KICKR); the first control writes after connecting were partly unanswered within 1.5 s and one failed ("GATT operation failed for unknown reason"), later ones were answered.

**Open (B4):** a rider on the KICKR should try SIM and ERG in the browser (power and the feel of the gradients were not checked with pedalling); the panel is a page overlay until the menus (B6); the console's chooser needs the key press that ran it (works in Chromium; a menu button is the safer gesture); Chromium on Linux needs the experimental flag for Web Bluetooth (Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, Android have it by default); the KICKR's slow first connection on BlueZ; the sensor bridge for browsers without Web Bluetooth (B7); a workouts folder in the browser (files: B6).

**B5 – Audio and voice in the browser: done (v3.21).** The browser app plays the desktop's game sounds and joins the same voice calls; the page's **Sound & voice** panel (bottom right, next to Devices; an overlay until the B6 menus) has the volumes, the game-sound mute, the microphone and speaker switches, the voice volume, voice on / spatial, the microphone and speaker choice and the echo test.

- **Game audio: one mixer, two outputs.** Bevy's audio plugin stays off: it plays decoded sample files (rodio), and every OCW sound is synthesised (3.3). The desktop's sounds, their parameters and the mixer moved unchanged into the new crate **`ocw-audio`** (pure, wasm: `mix`, `ride`, `others`, `spatial`, `weather`, `cues`, `mixer`, `dsp`; the demo ride test with it; cue timestamps on `web_time::Instant`), and the per-frame watching of the ride (own bike, other riders, rain / hail / gusts / thunder with its travel time, menu / countdown / finish / workout cues, bumps, crashes, remounts, the proximity bell, the buckled wheel's rub, the unicorn's chime, wings and hooves) into **`ocw_client::audio::AudioFeed`** – both apps feed the same mixer the same messages. The desktop keeps the cpal engine thread, the device choice and the video recording.
- **Web Audio without a worklet.** Web Audio cannot call into wasm on the page's thread, so the mixer renders in the frame loop: `ocw_audio::schedule::Scheduler` keeps a lead over the context's clock (100 ms, + 40 ms per underrun up to 300 ms, back down after 30 s calm) in 1024-frame chunks; each chunk is an `AudioBuffer` started by an `AudioBufferSourceNode` at its exact time, back to back (sample-exact). A clock that overtook the schedule (a long frame, a background tab) restarts it 30 ms after the clock: the gap is silence, nothing plays late. Voice cues (48 kHz) are resampled and mixed in. `crate::audio::AudioOut` is the boundary (the page's `AudioContext` in `browser_audio.rs`, a fake clock in the tests).
- **The autoplay rule.** The context is made at the start and stays *suspended* until a user gesture; `ocw_audio::unlock::AudioGate` (locked → resuming → running; Safari's *interrupted* and a refused `resume()` lock it again) decides; the page's capture-phase listeners (`pointerdown`, `keydown`, `touchend`, `mousedown`) call `resume()` **inside the handler** (only there it counts in Safari). Before that nothing is rendered and cues are dropped (no burst of old beeps at the first click); the panel and the console show "Sound: click or press a key to start it".
- **Voice: the same controller.** `ocw_voice::web::WebVoiceBackend` (pure, tested natively) turns the controller's commands into JSON for the page's shim `web/ocw-voice.js` (`window.ocwVoice`: `command`, `poll`, `devices`, `levels`, `available`) and its events into `BackendEvent`s; the shim wraps **LiveKit's JS SDK** (`livekit-client` 2.23.0 UMD, Apache-2.0; `scripts/fetch-livekit-client.sh` takes the npm registry's tarball, checks its SHA-256, keeps it in `target/web-vendor/` and copies it with its licence into `target/web/`; never a CDN at runtime, Q4). Rooms and tokens are the desktop's: `VoiceTokenRequest` → `VoiceGrant` over the game connection (WebTransport), so **no server-side piece was needed**; the local server in the page has no voice (a solo ride, as on the desktop). The microphone is published at once and muted by the switch (unmuting is instant); voices are subscribed by the controller's nearest-N and played through their own `AudioContext` (LiveKit's `webAudioMix`) with a stereo panner and the gain per voice; the speaker mute sets them to 0; LiveKit's own reconnect shows as *reconnecting*, a lost call fails and rejoins with a new token after the back-off. The echo test (7 *Echo bot*) runs in the shim on solo rides: `getUserMedia` (echo cancellation, noise suppression, gain control) → record gain → delay → the Echo rider's gain and pan, with level meters; with the server's echo participant the call path is the same as on the desktop. The confirmation sounds play through the game audio.
- **Shared with the desktop:** the per-frame voice logic (`ocw_client::voice::VoiceDriver`: a session's welcome, human riders, the Echo rider request, grants, the HUD's `VoiceHud`, the menu's voice info) and the command logic (`mute_command`, `echo_command`, `status_command`, `mute_who_command`, `group_command`, `devices_command`, `apply_settings`, over a `SettingsStore`); the **settings registry** moved to `ocw_client::settings` – the browser keeps the same TOML as `settings.toml` in `localStorage` (`ocw-settings`) with `set` / `get` (the `audio.*` and `voice.*` keys apply; others are kept for B6) and runs the saved values' apply commands at the start. Console in the browser as on the desktop: `audio.volume / mute / status / play / devices / output` (outputs by name via `AudioContext.setSinkId`, Chromium; labels need the microphone's permission), `voice.status / mute-mic / mute-speaker / mute / group / devices / echo / apply`; **M** / **Shift+M** while riding (the gamepad's Select / R3 come with the B6 gamepad parity). Push-to-talk stays dropped (2.4). `window.ocw.audio()` and `window.ocw.voice()` give the state as JSON (the panel and the tests).
- **Tests (no network, devices or sound card):** `ocw-audio`: the scheduler (back to back at 60 fps, underruns, the lead growing and shrinking, the cap), the gate (gesture, refused resume, interruption, closed, no Web Audio) and the moved mixer / synthesis tests; `ocw_client::audio` (others sent and faded once, cues from the menu, a bump, workouts, the rub's rhythm, the settings' mix); `ocw_client::voice` (peers, settings, echo request, HUD, the driver connecting on a grant and failing on a drop); `ocw_voice::web` (command and event JSON both ways, broken events, devices and levels, **a whole call through the controller against a fake of the shim**: token → connected → subscribed and placed → M / Shift+M with their cues through the app → reconnecting / reconnected → voice off leaves; a refused token and a lost call retried with the back-off; the echo loopback; an unavailable page); `apps/web` (`WebAudio` against a fake context: locked until the gesture, chunks back to back at 44.1 kHz with sound, cues dropped while locked, mute, voice cues resampled, output by name, Safari's interruption; the settings in a memory store, a broken text not overwritten; the voice plugin: switches saved and reloaded, M / Shift+M, a grant joins, the echo and `set` commands).
- **Browser tests** (`scripts/test-web-audio.py`, headless Chromium on WebGPU with `--mute-audio` – the context runs, the speakers stay quiet –, `--autoplay-policy=document-user-activation-required` and Chromium's fake microphone): `make test-web-audio` (the sound locked before a gesture, a real mouse click starts it, chunks at the context's pace with sound in them, `audio.status`, a volume kept over a reload); `make test-web-voice` (`ocw-server --webtransport` with LiveKit keys and the Echo rider, an `ocw-bot` over QUIC, a **fake LiveKit** in the page (`scripts/web-voice-fake.js`) that reads the token's claims: the call, the participant subscribed and panned, active speakers on the HUD, M / Shift+M, a drop and a lost call, the echo test on the fake microphone, the switches over a reload); `make test-web-livekit` (two browser riders in a real `livekit-server --dev` room; skipped when the binary is not installed; the second rider's page opens in its **own window** – a second tab would be hidden, and a hidden page gets no animation frames, so its game loop, its join and its voice controller stand still; the test checks that both pages are visible and joined).

**Measured (marge, 2026-11-14, headless Chromium 156 on WebGPU, localhost):** `make test-web-audio` – 12 checks passed: before a gesture the context is suspended (`locked`, 0 chunks, the panel's hint shown); a mouse click resumed it in **0.28 s**; the context runs at **48 kHz**, the lead stayed at 100 ms with **0 underruns**; 287 chunks in 6.1 s of audio, every one with sound (the own bike at 250 W and three bots; the loudest chunk's RMS 0.023); `audio.status`; `set audio.master 55` kept over a reload (`localStorage`). `make test-web-voice` – 18 checks passed: the browser joined the session over WebTransport, the controller asked for a token, the server's grant (room `ocw-<instance>`, identity `rider-3`) went to the shim, the fake LiveKit connected with it (`webAudioMix` on, the microphone published); the bot rider's participant `rider-2` was subscribed and panned, active speakers reached the HUD ("voice connected (1) - talking: quic-1"); M muted the microphone (the published track muted), Shift+M the speaker (the voice's volume 0); a drop showed *reconnecting* → *connected*; a lost call failed and rejoined with a second token; `voice.echo here` brought the Echo rider 20 m ahead and the shim's loopback played the fake microphone (a 220 Hz voice-like tone from a WAV: Chromium's own fake device only beeps) back through the delay (input RMS 0.12, echo 0.064 – the Echo rider's spatial gain 0.53 at 19 m –, the HUD's meters); the microphone switch survived a reload. The final run of all parts (`web-audio-20261114-165518`): 32 checks passed (the real-LiveKit part skipped: no `livekit-server`). **With a real LiveKit** (v1.13.10 `--dev` on marge, installed with the user's approval; `make test-web-livekit`, `web-audio-20261114-184203`): 8 checks passed – both pages visible and joined the game session, both in the real room with the game server's tokens (the real livekit-client 2.23.0 over `ws://127.0.0.1`, ICE on loopback), each sees the other participant, the other's fake microphone is heard (LiveKit's active speaker), the remote track plays through the shim's panner, a mute in one page shows in the other; no browser errors. Its first run had failed because both pages were tabs of one window (see the test above), not because of LiveKit; the page's 404 was its missing favicon (now an empty one in `index.html`). `ocw_web_bg.wasm` 75.2 MiB raw, 16.7 MiB gzip, 10.6 MiB brotli (B2: 71.7 / 15.8 / 10.0 – other merges in between; `ocw-audio` itself is small); `livekit-client.umd.js` 596 KiB (not compressed yet; loaded with the page).

**Choices made here (proposals, for the user to confirm):** (1) **no AudioWorklet, no cpal Web Audio host:** the mixer renders on the page's thread into scheduled buffers – one code path with the desktop's mixer, no second wasm instance in a worklet; latency 100–300 ms (fine for ride sounds and cues; music is not affected); it stops with the frame loop in a background tab. A worklet ring buffer (and the mixer in a Web Worker) can come later if measured gaps need it. (2) **LiveKit's JS SDK fetched by the build** from the npm registry, pinned (2.23.0) and hash-checked, not vendored in git and not loaded from a CDN. (3) **voices in their own `AudioContext`** (like the desktop's separate voice output; `voice.output` chooses it independently of `audio.output`). (4) **the settings registry shared** (`ocw_client::settings`) and kept in `localStorage` in the same TOML as `settings.toml`, so B6's menus and the account sync (Phase 5) find one format. (5) The *Sound & voice* panel is a page overlay like the Devices panel until the B6 menus.

**Open (B5):** a real call in a real browser with a real microphone and speakers (echo cancellation, the permission prompt, Bluetooth headsets, setSinkId with real devices) – headless runs use Chromium's fake microphone; `wss://` for LiveKit from https pages (a `ws://` LiveKit URL works only from localhost pages: mixed content) – production URL and certificate with B8; the gamepad's Select / R3 and the menus' Audio / Voice pages (done in B6, v3.24); the game sound pauses with the frame loop in a background tab; Safari / Firefox not run yet (B8 matrix).


**B6 – UI parity: done (v3.24).** The browser app has the desktop's in-game menu (Esc / the gamepad's Start), its settings pages, the time and weather machines, local events, the riding aids, the rider list and the HUD – not copied, but the **same code**: what was desktop-only UI logic moved into shared crates, and both apps add the same plugins.

- **One UI, two apps.** The Bevy-free parts moved into `ocw-client`: `menu::model` (pages, stack, focus, paging: six rows and Back, the ten-foot rule), `menu::controls` (keys and buttons → actions), `menu::pages` (the Settings, Workshop, Workouts and World rows, each a console line), `menu::weather` and `menu::time` (the weather and time machines' state, rows, status and grid), `menu::voice`; `riders` (the rider profiles), `recording` (the ride recorder for the FIT file: records once a second, laps at workout steps and event parts, crash and god-mode markers), `view::fill` (the frame's `RideView` from the client: the notices in one order, the proximity arrow, the last-moment warning, the camera's reaction, the damage widget – both HUDs now get the same fields) and `rider_list::RiderListInfo`. The Bevy glue moved into the new shared crate **`ocw-ui`**: `menu` (keys, gamepads, mouse and touch → the model → `MenuView`; results first, the console first, steering held while open), `settings` (`UserSettings` over a `TextStore` – `settings.toml` on the desktop, `localStorage` in the browser – with `set` and `get`), `timemachine` (the zone of the place, the sky, the HUD clock, `time`, World → Time), `weather` (the view's weather and the whole `weather …` family), `collisions` (collisions, damage, the riding aids, `camera.shake`, the dev stages), `events` (`event race | group | tt | cancel | status | dismiss`), `riders_page`, `controls` (the Bevy input, `RidePads`: the ride's gamepad throttle and stick). The shared code reaches each app's client through **`ocw_ui::RideAccess`** (function pointers to the `ClientCore` and the server link: the desktop's `ClientState` and `Link`, the browser's `WebSession`); the app's view writer runs in `RideViewSet`, the shared extras after it. The desktop keeps re-exports (its tests and the rest of its code are unchanged) and adds its own pages through **`MenuHooks`**: the world catalog (Change world, About this world), routes, rides, GPX import, the workouts folder, the rider profiles, god mode's captured pointer.
- **The platform filter** (`ocw_client::menu::model::Platform`, Q6: the same app): items a platform cannot do are left out, never replaced by another menu. The browser has no Quit (the tab closes), no Restart (a reload), no Navi → Routes / Rides / GPX import / Strava (another ride is another page; files; the backend, Phase 5), no Settings → Riders (profiles are files; the anonymous rider has none); its **Workshop** item opens a locked page with "log in to customize" (Q5); its own top item **Captures** takes Quit's place: Screenshot, Video start / stop, Download this ride (FIT). The browser's World page: the world's name, Time, Weather, Unicorn mode (since v3.39). Setting rows of keys the browser does not have (`ocw_client::settings::applies`: fullscreen; god mode's invert, flight and trail until v3.39 – the browser has its own –, the random start, real weather at the start) are hidden; `set` keeps them ("not in this app"), `get` lists the others.
- **Every setting applies in the browser:** the live ones through their console lines – all registered there now (the renderer's `hud`, `hud.units`, `fps`, `camera.mode`, `sky.*`, `ortho`, `road_barriers`; `ocw-ui`'s `ride.collisions`, `ride.chaotic_bots`, `ride.damage`, `ride.proximity_cue`, `ride.hit_warning`, `camera.shake`, `weather.physics`, `weather.provider`; `trainer.difficulty`; `audio.*`, `voice.*`) – at the start and on every change; the ones read at the start (`ride.bots`, `trainer.virtual_power`, `ride.record`, `controls.autodrive`) where the page's query does not give them. Kept in `localStorage` (`ocw-settings`, the same TOML as `settings.toml`).
- **HUD:** the shared view (above) plus the shared weather machine's weather and wind, the time machine's clock, the season (the renderer), REC while a video records. God mode is still desktop-only, so its HUD is too.
- **Console permissions:** the same levels; `Dev` commands (now also the shared `dev.bump`, `dev.crash`, `dev.damage`, `dev.tree`) only with the in-browser local server, `User` on a remote server.
- **Gamepads:** Bevy 0.20's gilrs reads the browser's Gamepad API on wasm32 (gilrs-core's web backend: `navigator.getGamepads()` each frame, the standard mapping), so the pads are the same `Gamepad` entities as on the desktop: the menu (Start, D-pad / stick with repeat, A, B, LB / RB), the ride (`RidePads`, shared with the desktop: D-pad, stick and triggers for faster / stop, A autodrive or the results, X wild, the left stick steers), voice (Select, R3).
- **Captures with timestamps:** `screenshot` hands the renderer's capture to a **`ShotSink`** (`ocw_render::stamp`): the same JPEG (q90, the time and the software in EXIF) as the desktop's file, downloaded as `ocw-YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.jpg` (the local time of the HUD's stamp). `video start | stop | toggle`: the page's `MediaRecorder` on the canvas (30 fps, VP9 / VP8 WebM, 8 Mbit/s) with the game sound (a `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode` fed by the same scheduled buffers as the speakers), downloaded as `ocw-….webm` when it stops; REC in the HUD as on the desktop.
- **FIT download:** the shared recorder records the browser ride (`ride.record`); `ride.save` or Captures → *Download this ride (FIT)* encodes it (`ocw_fit`) and downloads `ocw-ride-YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.fit` (the start, UTC, like the desktop's ride files); a new recording starts. Downloads go through the page's `window.ocwDownload(name, mime, bytes)` (a Blob and a link); `window.ocwDownloads` lists them, `window.ocw.menu()` / `setting(key)` give the menu and the settings to tests.
- **The *Sound & voice* panel is gone:** Settings → Audio (volumes with a test sound, mute, the output from `setSinkId`'s list) and Settings → Voice (switches, volume, participants, devices, the echo test) are the desktop's pages; only the hint "click or press a key" stays on the page until the sound runs. The Devices panel stays (the Bluetooth chooser must open in a click's handler).
- **Tests (no GPU, network or devices):** `ocw-client` – the browser's menu (no Quit, Captures, the locked workshop, no Restart, the Settings page), the ten-foot limits per platform, the moved model, pages, weather, time, voice, rider list and recorder tests; `ocw-ui` – the keyboard and gamepad mapping, `RidePads`, the shared settings (round trip, a broken text kept, `set` / `get` in the browser, the start commands per platform), the menu over a stepped server as the browser (its top page, Captures, the locked workshop, Settings without what it lacks, a setting row through the console) and the browser's pages fitting a 16:9 window; `ocw-web` – the browser rides with the desktop's menu (Esc, World → Weather → the preset grid → hail reaches the server, the rider list, Ride → Workouts), the FIT download from Captures by keys (a valid FIT file), the aids, the damage widget and an event from the shared commands, the settings read at the start; the desktop's menu tests unchanged and green.
- **Browser test (`make test-web`, `scripts/web_ui_test.py`):** after the ride: the menu by keyboard (CDP key events on the canvas), Settings → Display (→ changes `display.units`, saved in `localStorage`), World → Weather → the preset grid, the HUD with a storm's wind and the damage widget, Navi → Riders in this ride, a fake gamepad (`navigator.getGamepads`: Start opens, the D-pad moves, A opens, B goes back), Captures → Screenshot and → Download this ride (FIT) – the downloads saved through CDP and checked (a JPEG with EXIF, a FIT file) –, a 3 s video (a WebM), the setting after a reload.

**Measured (marge, 2026-11-14, headless Chromium 156 on WebGPU, localhost; `test-output/web/web-20261114-194420*`):** all 22 UI checks passed: the top page `Resume, Ride, World, Workshop, Navi, Settings, Captures`; Settings without Riders; Display → `display.units` metric → imperial, in `localStorage`, still imperial after the reload; World (`World: Test Hills`, the time, the weather) → the weather machine ("set by you") → the preset grid (5 columns) → hail in 1 min; the HUD in a storm (heavy rain 10 °C, crosswind 64 km/h) with the damage widget (rider 55 % hurt, bike 91 %, "front wheel buckled"); the rider list ("6 riders, 1 damaged", the dot after the own row); the fake gamepad (Start opened the menu, the D-pad moved the focus 0 → 1, A opened Ride, B went back); the screenshot `ocw-2026-11-14_19-45-01.jpg` (112 kB, EXIF with the software), the ride `ocw-ride-2026-11-14_18-44-22.fit` (1.6 kB, the start in UTC as the desktop's files), a 3 s video `ocw-2026-11-14_19-45-05.webm` (VP9 / Opus, 1.7 MB). `ocw_web_bg.wasm` 75.8 MiB raw, 16.9 MiB gzip, 10.6 MiB brotli (B5: 75.2 / 16.7 / 10.6: the shared UI code was mostly in the desktop only); `make web` 343 s.

**Choices made here (proposals, for the user to confirm):** (1) **a new shared crate `ocw-ui`** for the Bevy glue both apps add (`ocw-client` stays engine-free; `ocw-render` cannot depend on the client) and **function pointers (`RideAccess`)** as the one seam to the apps' clients, instead of moving the desktop's `ClientState` / `Link` and the browser's `WebSession` into one type; (2) **the platform filter on items and setting rows** – the browser shows a subset of the same pages (Q6) – with **Captures** in Quit's place on the top page (seven items, the ten-foot maximum); (3) the browser's World page shows the world but **does not switch** (another world or route is another page, `?world=…&route=…`); (4) **videos as WebM** from `MediaRecorder` (what every browser records; no MP4 / H.264 encoder in the page), with the game sound; (5) **the FIT file on demand** (Captures, `ride.save`): browsers allow no download when a tab closes, and the backend's ride history (Phase 5) is where an automatic save belongs; (6) downloads named `ocw-<local time>` like the HUD's stamp (screenshots, videos) and `ocw-ride-<start>` (rides); (7) the settings the browser lacks are kept in its text (an account sync later carries one file) but hidden and not applied.

**Open (B6):** ~~god mode (and its HUD) in the browser~~ (done, v3.39: Phase 13 G5); the workshop and the character editor for logged-in riders (accounts, Phase 5); routes and world switches inside a browser ride; real weather on the in-browser local server (the providers need an async `fetch` in the frame server; on a remote server it works); touch on real phones and tablets (the pointer events are the desktop's; not tried on a device); the FIT file to the backend / Strava (Phase 5, 2.8); a Devices menu page next to the panel; the video's frame rate under load (MediaRecorder takes what the page renders); Safari / Firefox (B8 matrix).

**B7 – WebGL 2 fallback and quality presets: done (v3.27); the sensor bridge (10D.2) is open** – it relays samples through the backend between two sessions of one account, so it waits for Phase 5 (accounts, the backend). **A local bridge comes first (v5.72, decided by the user 2026-11-24):** the desktop app relays the trainer's samples to a browser session on the same network, paired with a short code, no account; the backend relay follows with Phase 5. **Built (v5.76): 10D.2 *Built (local bridge)*.**

- **Two builds, one page.** Bevy chooses WebGPU or WebGL 2 when it is compiled (its shaders, limits and bind group layouts differ; with both features it takes WebGPU), so `ocw-web` has the features **`webgpu`** and **`webgl2`** – a wasm32 build needs exactly one (a `compile_error!` says so), native builds and tests take neither (the workspace's Bevy stays the desktop's). `scripts/build-web.sh` (`make web`) builds both into `target/web/`: `ocw_web.js` / `ocw_web_bg.wasm` (WebGPU) and `ocw_web_webgl2.js` / `ocw_web_webgl2_bg.wasm`; `WEB_GPU=webgpu` builds one; `make test-web-build` checks both. `index.html` asks `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()`: an adapter → the WebGPU build; no `navigator.gpu`, no adapter or an error → the WebGL 2 build (if the browser has WebGL 2 at all; else the page says what it needs). `?gpu=webgl2` / `?gpu=webgpu` choose; `window.ocwGpu` gives the choice and why. The HUD's build id ends in `web WebGPU` / `web WebGL2`; the console's **`gpu`** prints the API, the adapter (name, backend, driver) and the quality that runs (the desktop too: `gpu: native – adapter …`).
- **What WebGL 2 cannot do degrades, found by running it** (headless Chromium, WebGL 2 through ANGLE on Vulkan). Each check reads the adapter at run time (`RenderAdapter`, `RenderAdapterInfo`), so the desktop and the WebGPU build draw exactly as before:
  - *the atmosphere* (compute shaders, `Rgba16Float` storage textures; the camera's atmosphere put a storage buffer into the fragment stage's view layout, and every PBR pipeline failed validation – Bevy quits on that): `sky::AtmosphereSupport` – without, the **simple sky** whatever `display.sky` says (`sky.mode` tells why);
  - *texture arrays without a texture* (road, ground, houses, gear without the material library): Bevy's fallback is a one-layer texture, which WebGL 2 makes a plain 2D texture ("heuristics assumed … `D2` rather than `D2Array`"); `webgl::ArrayFallback` puts a white **two-layer** array into the empty slots (white like Bevy's fallback: the same look);
  - *cross-fading levels of detail* (`VisibilityRange` with margins: the vertex shader reads Bevy's range table, a 64-entry uniform array on WebGL 2 whose layout Bevy declares as 16 bytes – the pipeline fails validation): on WebGL 2 every range is made **abrupt** at the middle of its margins (houses, riders, unicorns, obstacles, trees switch instead of dithering);
  - *one shadow cascade per light* (Bevy's limit on WebGL 2): the presets ask for at most what the build draws (`quality::MAX_CASCADES`; High on WebGL 2 keeps one cascade over Low's 70 m instead of only the first 20 m of four);
  - what Bevy turns off by itself (OIT, SSAO, GPU culling and preprocessing, environment-map generation) is not used by OCW. Our own WESL shaders needed no change: the gear material already had its non-bindless path (bindings 50–53), the others use uniforms and 2D arrays.
- **Quality presets** (`ocw_render::quality`, pure numbers; `RenderQuality` is what the renderer draws with, applied at once by `quality::apply_quality` and to tiles loaded later):

  | | High (the look before) | Medium | Low |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | sun shadows | 4096² × 4 cascades over 250 m | 2048² × 3 over 180 m | 2048² × 1 over 70 m |
  | MSAA | 4× | 4× | off |
  | view distance (far plane, fog before it) | the world's | 30 km | 8 km |
  | trees drawn (from the tile's centre; beyond: the ground's forest colour) | while loaded | 3 km | 1.2 km |
  | house LOD distances | × 1 | × 0.75 | × 0.5 |
  | weather particles | 40 000 | 20 000 | 10 000 |
  | canvas pixel ratio (browser) | the device's | ≤ 2 | ≤ 1 |

  **One shared setting `display.quality`** (`auto`, `low`, `medium`, `high`; live) in `ocw_client::settings`, resolved by `ocw_client::quality::resolve` from the app's GPU API and the page's device facts (`window.ocwDeviceInfo`: mobile, coarse pointer, cores, memory): **auto = High on the desktop** (its look unchanged) **and on WebGPU, Medium on a small device** (≤ 4 cores or ≤ 4 GB), **Low on WebGL 2 and on phones and tablets**; a level by name always wins. `ocw_ui::quality` (both apps): the console's `quality [auto|low|medium|high]` (what the setting runs; without an argument: what runs and why) and `gpu`; the setting is resolved at the start (the settings' start commands skip default values). The menu: **Settings → Display → Graphics** (Quality, Sky, Fullscreen – the Display page was full, the ten-foot rule; its row shows the setting). Page option `quality=` for one visit (a temporary value, not saved).
- **Tests:** `ocw_render::quality` (High = the numbers world.rs and the camera had, Bevy's default MSAA; every lower level cheaper in every number; the view-distance fog; a level applied to the sun, the camera, the particles, houses and trees, also to ones spawned later, and back), `ocw_render::webgl` (the placeholder, only empty slots filled, abrupt ranges keep an open end, nothing without WebGL), `ocw_client::quality` (auto by API and device, a phone, an iPad as a Mac with a finger, a small laptop, nothing known; a level by name wins on every API; the registry's choices; the page's JSON), `ocw_ui::quality` (the console on a WebGL 2 and a desktop context), `ocw-web` (the page options `quality` and `gpu`, the visit's quality not saved, the pixel-ratio cap), the desktop's page-rows test with the Graphics page. **Browser test `make test-web-webgl2`:** (1) `scripts/test-web.py --gpu webgl2` – Chromium started without WebGPU (on marge `navigator.gpu` stays but gives no adapter, so the page's real fallback runs): the WebGL 2 build loads, rides, `gpu` says WebGL2 and `quality: low (auto: WebGL 2)`, no rendering error (both browser tests now fail on Bevy's "Caught rendering error"), then the whole B6 UI part (menus by keys and gamepad, captures, video, FIT, a setting over a reload) and the frame rate; (2) `scripts/test-web-webgl2.py` – one Chromium with WebGPU loads the same view twice (`gpu=webgpu&quality=high`, then `gpu=webgl2&quality=low`: Hills km 1.2, no bots, 0 W, midsummer noon paused, clear), measures the frame rate, saves each picture and the two side by side; opens Settings → Display → Graphics on WebGL 2; and checks Low's pixel-ratio cap at a device pixel ratio of 2 (the canvas at CSS size).
- **Render distance: fixed or following the frame rate (planned 2026-11-15, asked by the user; both apps):** how far the world is drawn becomes a setting of its own instead of only a part of the preset.
  - **Settings → Display:**
    - **Render distance** (slider `display.view_distance`: 1 – 60 km in 1 km steps, then *unlimited* = the world's reach; default = the preset's value: High unlimited, Medium 30 km, Low 8 km; moving the slider overrides the preset's `view_m`).
    - **Adjust to the frame rate** (checkbox `display.view_distance_auto`, **on by default everywhere**, Q8 decided): the distance follows the measured frame rate; the slider is then the **upper limit**.
    - **Target frame rate** (`display.target_fps`: 30 / 45 / 60 / 72 / 90 / 120 / *display* = the monitor's refresh; default **display** on the desktop, **60** in the browser on every device, Q9 decided).
  - **What the distance drives** (one number → all of them, monotone, from `ocw_render::quality`): the far plane and the fog before it (`limit_view`), the trees' range (`tree_view_m` = 10 % of it, 0.8 – 3 km, beyond the ground's forest colour), the houses' LOD scale (0.5 at 2 km … 1.0 from 20 km), the far terrain's outer ring, and the **tile streaming radius** (browser `tiles` / `keep`, desktop neighbour packages, 4.7) – so a short distance also saves memory and downloads.
  - **The dynamic mode** (`ocw_client::view_distance::Controller`, pure): reads the frame rate of the last second (`ocw_render::frame_rate::FrameRateMeter`, its average and its worst frame) and steps the distance:
    - below 90 % of the target for 2 s → −15 % (multiplicative), at once on a frame over 3 × the target's frame time;
    - above 110 % of the target for 5 s (and the GPU not the limit, where measurable) → +10 %;
    - bounds: at least 1.5 km, at most the slider; a dead band between the thresholds against oscillation; after a change at least 2 s before the next;
    - ignored: the first 5 s after a world loads, a teleport or a time-machine jump, and while the menu, the loading screen or a background tab holds the frame rate down;
    - applied **smoothly**: the fog distance eases over 2 s (no visible jump); the tree and house ranges move in 250 m steps; the tile radius changes at most every 10 s (no streaming thrash).
  - **Visible:** the HUD's frame-rate line gains the distance ("58 fps · 12 km auto"); the console `view [KM|unlimited] [auto on|off] [target FPS]` sets it, `view` alone prints the value, the mode, the target and why (the last step).
  - **VR (Phase 11 / 14):** the target is the headset's refresh (72 Hz on the Quest 1) and the mode is on there, since a missed frame hurts more in a headset.
  - **Tests (11.4):** the controller against synthetic frame-rate traces (a slow GPU converges below the target within 15 s and stays without oscillating; a fast one grows to the slider; spikes and the ignored windows do nothing; bounds; the 2 s spacing), with a cost model (frame time ∝ drawn area) that closes the loop; the mapping distance → fog, trees, houses, tiles (monotone, the presets' values at their distances); the settings registry and the menu rows in both apps; scenes `view-distance-2km`, `view-distance-30km` (the same place, single pictures) and a browser test where auto settles on a throttled GPU (Chromium's CPU throttling).
  - **Built (2026-11-16, v4.23; both apps, B6 parity):**
    - **Pure, Bevy-free logic** in `ocw_client::view_distance`: the settings' words (`DistanceSetting`: `preset` / 1 – 60 / `unlimited`, `TargetSetting`: `auto` / `display` / a rate), the target (`target_fps`: `auto` = the display's refresh on the desktop and **60 in the browser** (Q9); `display` = the refresh; a refresh outside 24 – 500 Hz or none (headless, the browser) counts as unknown → 60; a `--max-fps` cap below it wins), the **controller** (`Controller`, one call per frame with the frame-rate meter's 1 s average and worst frame), the menu rows. The mapping distance → far plane and fog (`limit_view_to`), trees (`tree_view_for`), houses (`house_lod_for`) and the near tile ring (`stream_radius_for`) is pure too, in `ocw_render::quality` (`QualityPreset::with_view_distance`), and the browser's streaming follows the ring (`ocw_web::world::residency_for`).
    - **Settings** in the shared registry: `display.view_distance` (default **`preset`**), `display.view_distance_auto` (default **on**, Q8), `display.target_fps` (default **`auto`**); live; kept in `settings.toml` / `localStorage`. **Menu:** Settings → Display → Graphics → **Render distance** (the Display page was full, the ten-foot rule): the slider (← / → by 1 km from the distance it stands for – `preset` moves from the preset's own –, 60 km → unlimited; Confirm: back to `preset`), *Adjust to the frame rate*, *Target frame rate*, and *Now* (what runs: "12 km, auto, target 60 fps"); the Graphics page's row shows "preset, auto". **Console** (both apps): `view [KM|unlimited|preset] [auto on|off] [target FPS|display|auto]`; `view` alone: the distance, the mode, the limit (and the preset it comes from), the target and why, the trees, the house LOD, the tiles and the last step with its reason; each step is logged (`view distance: 37 km → 31 km: 78 fps below 130 (90 % of 144) for 2 s`). **HUD:** the FPS counter shows "58 fps  max 21 ms · 12 km auto".
    - **With the quality presets** (`display.quality` Low / Medium / High / auto; VR when Phase 11 / 14 come – the headset's refresh as the target): the preset gives the default upper limit (`preset`: High unlimited, Medium 30 km, Low 8 km) and the most its trees and houses get; a distance **below** the preset's draws fewer trees and coarser houses, a distance **above** it moves only the far plane and the fog out (the preset's trees, houses, shadows, MSAA, particles and pixel ratio stay). At the preset's own distance every number is the preset's (tested). Changing the preset or the slider starts the dynamic mode at the new limit.
    - **Mapping** (choices made here, see below): far plane 1.5 × the distance with an exponential fog whose visibility is the distance (as Low / Medium before); trees to 15 % of the distance (at least 800 m, rounded up to 250 m steps, at most the preset's); house LOD scale 0.5 up to 2 km, 1.0 from 20 km, linear between in 0.05 steps, at most the preset's; near tile ring 1 (3 × 3 tiles) below 2.5 km, else 2 (5 × 5, as before; never more); the browser fetches one ring more and keeps three more (the page's own policy as the most). The fog and far plane ease to a new distance over 2 s (95 %), the tile ring changes at most every 10 s (at once on a change by the rider or a jump).
    - **The controller:** down by 15 % after 2 s below 90 % of the target (each 1 s while below a third of it: "a frame over 3 × the target's frame time" read as the meter's 1 s average, so single spikes do nothing); up by 10 % after 5 s **above 110 % of the target, or at ≥ 97 % of it with no frame over 1.5 target frame times** (with vsync the rate never exceeds the refresh, so room shows as "at the target and smooth"); at least 2 s between steps; never below **1.5 km** (a slider below it is kept), never above the slider; from unlimited the first step down is 60 km, above 60 km a step up goes to unlimited. **Hysteresis against oscillation:** after a step down no step up past 95 % of the distance that was too slow for 30 s; **a step up that fails within 10 s goes back to the distance before it** and blocks there for twice as long as the last time (60, 120, 240 s): a GPU at its limit is probed ever more rarely. **No gain:** when a quarter of the distance brought no frames (no rise of 10 % over the rate where the cutting began), the distance is not what limits (the CPU, another program): back to where the cutting began and no steps down for 300 s unless the rate falls below 60 % of what it was. **Ignored:** 5 s after the first rider appears, a teleport or world change (the rider jumps more than 200 m) and a time-machine jump (the clock moves more than 15 min in a frame); while the menu is open or there is no rider yet (loading); a frame over 1 s (a background tab) and the meter's window after it. **Held** in the desktop's `--screenshot` and `--capture` runs (reproducible pictures; the distance is the slider's).
    - **Tests:** `ocw_client::view_distance` (9: the controller closed-loop against the real frame-rate meter and a cost model, frame time = base + k × distance, with and without vsync: a slow GPU from unlimited is at ≤ 14.5 km and ≥ 54 fps after 28 s and stays at the target ≥ 90 % of the time with ≤ 4 changes in 300 s; the dead band; a load that goes away grows back to the slider, and from 60 km to unlimited; spikes (300 ms every 3 s), the settle window, the menu and a background tab do nothing; floor and ceiling, a lower slider at once, a slider below the floor; a frame rate the distance does not change (back to unlimited, then quiet; tries again when much worse); the target on desktop and browser with broken refresh values and the frame cap; the words and the slider's steps; the settings round trip through the TOML text and the menu rows), `ocw_render::quality` (the mapping: the presets at their own distances unchanged, monotone over 1 – 60 km, High at 12 km, Low at 60 km, Medium unlimited, the fog at 2 km; the fog's easing to and from unlimited), `ocw_render::package` (the ring caps riding, never widens, leaves flight alone), `ocw_ui::view_distance` (the console on a WebGL 2 and a desktop context, the preset and the distance together, the settings and the menu page, the tile ring's 10 s rule, a screenshot run holds), `ocw-web` (the streaming's radii), the desktop's page-rows test (every row's command is valid). `make test-web` runs `view` in the page and checks the dynamic mode and the browser's 60 fps target.
    - **Measured** (marge, 2026-11-16, release build, `scripts/measure-fps.sh` – headless weston on the GPU, no vsync, 60 s, the first 20 s left out – `--log` keeps the app's log; `test-output/view-distance-2026-11-16/`). **marge was heavily shared during the runs (load average 23 – 31 on 12 cores)**, so the rates swing between about 75 and 280 fps from one 5 s sample to the next and the means compare poorly:

      | scene | dynamic, target auto (= the headless output's 60 Hz) | fixed (`view auto off`) | dynamic, target 144 |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | Tenerife, TF-21 in Las Cañadas, the Teide 6 km ahead (`canadas-teide.route`, 7 bots) | 144.6 fps mean (min 117); **unlimited**, no step | 108.1 fps (min 72); unlimited | 146.0 fps (min 75); cut unlimited → 60 → … → 31 km in 5 steps (78 – 97 fps), then **back to unlimited** ("still 101 fps with a quarter of the distance: the distance is not the limit"); once more within the same minute (this build lifted the pause below 80 % of the rate where the cutting began, 77 < 0.8 × 97; now: below 60 % of the lower of the two rates) |
      | Black Forest, top of the Schauinsland road (km 19.6, far view) | 134.8 fps (min 74); **unlimited**, no step | 77.1 fps (min 72); unlimited | 74.8 fps (min 73); cut 60 → 31 km once, back to unlimited, then quiet |

      At the default target the dynamic mode never touched the distance (the frame rate stayed above 60); with a target the machine could not reach, the first build (without the no-gain rule) walked down to 12 – 14 km without gaining a frame – the reason for that rule. Browser (`make test-web`, headless Chromium on WebGPU, the Hills test route, `test-output/web/web-20261116-185557*`): **59.6 fps** at the page's 60 Hz, `view: unlimited (auto; limit the high preset's unlimited; target 60 fps: auto: 60 in the browser)` – no step; all UI checks passed.
    - **Screenshots** (`make test-scenes ONLY='view-distance-*'` on marge, 2560 × 1440; `test-output/scenes/2026-11-16-181037/view-distance-{2km,12km,unlimited}.jpg`): the same view at 2 km (the plain and the near hills fogged out; the FPS counter "40 fps max 26 ms · 2 km"), 12 km (the ridges to the left in haze) and unlimited (the far coast).
    - **Choices made here** (proposals, for the user to confirm): (1) the slider's default is the word **`preset`** (the registry needs one default for every preset) and a third setting value **`auto`** for the target (the desktop's display refresh, the browser's 60: one default for both apps); (2) the three settings on **their own page under Display → Graphics** (the Display page is full); (3) **trees at 15 %** of the distance instead of 10 % (with 10 % Low at its 8 km would lose trees it has today) and trees and houses **never above the preset's**; (4) the near tile ring only narrows (1 below 2.5 km), it never widens past today's 5 × 5; (5) "room to spare" also **at the target and smooth** (vsync), with the failed-probe backoff; (6) the **no-gain rule** (not in the plan); (7) **held in screenshot and capture runs**; (8) the console's word `view` and the setting names of the plan (`display.view_distance`, `_auto`, `display.target_fps`), not `display.render_distance`.
    - **Distant terrain fades into the sky (fixed 2026-11-16, the coordinator's request; it was the flat-silhouette defect):** at short distances, and on Low (8 km), far mountains stood in front of the sky as a flat shape in the fog's colour (the Teide 6 km away at 2 km). Two causes: the fog took the light model's horizon colour, which after the tonemapping is darker and bluer than Bevy's atmosphere at the horizon; and the far plane culls nothing (Bevy's infinite reverse-Z projection), so far tiles beyond it were drawn fully fogged. **Fix:**
      - **The fog's colour under the atmosphere is the atmosphere's horizon as drawn:** `ocw_sky::light::atmosphere_fog_srgb(sun elevation)`, a table measured on the atmosphere's renders. Las Cañadas, 13 Nov, the sky just above the horizon against fully fogged terrain at 3 km, `sky.fog R G B`, three rounds of correction in linear light; the values exceed 1 because the fog is mixed in before the tonemapping, which compresses the bright sky. Residual in the last round: sky ÷ fog **0.99 – 1.04** by day (12:00 – 18:00, sun 42° – 2°), 0.88 – 1.13 in the twilight, 0.99 – 1.02 at night; before the fix it was 1.33 – 1.99 by day.
      - **Only where the view is limited:** `ocw_render::quality::horizon_fog_share` – fully up to 30 km (Low, Medium, every slider value up to 30 km), fading out to none at 60 km and unlimited, so **High's unlimited look is unchanged**. A weather fog nearer than the view keeps the weather's colour (mist, rain: unchanged). The clouds' haze and the plain sky keep the light model's colour; the clouds' haze tints the sky, and giving it the brighter fog washed the whole sky white in the first try.
      - **Towards a low sun** (second round, the coordinator's report of a pale band "like a lake" at the Schauinsland): the fog's **directional-light term** (Bevy's `DistanceFog::directional_light_color` / `_exponent`) adds a warm glow straight towards the sun, falling off as cos⁴ of the angle (half at 33°, a quarter at 45°): `ocw_sky::light::sun_glow_lin` (+0.40 red, +0.22 green in the fog's linear input units from 1° to 15° of sun elevation, none from 25° and below the horizon) and `fog_light_colour` (the colour that gives that glow through the renderer's product: light colour × illuminance × exposure). Measured with a black fog (`sky.fog 0 0 0`), the sky just above the horizon every 30° around: at the top of the Schauinsland (1240 m) at 15:00 / 16:00 / 16:30 (sun 14° / 7° / 3°) towards the sun about +0.09 red and +0.05 green over the opposite side; in Las Cañadas (16:30 – 18:10) only +0.01 – 0.02 (the opposite side there is even pinker at 18:00 – the belt of Venus – which one additive glow cannot follow). No glow under clouds (scaled by the clouds' grey), from the moon or where the horizon colour is not used.
      - **The atmosphere's own haze** (its aerial perspective, added over the fogged terrain) grows with the distance, so the farther the fully fogged band lies the less fog colour it needs: the horizon colour is scaled down in linear light from 1 up to 3 km to 0.85 from 10 km on (`ocw_render::quality::horizon_fog_scale`; at 8 – 12 km from the Schauinsland the band was about 0.05 brighter than the sky, at 2 km in Las Cañadas level with it).
      - **Far tiles wholly beyond 2 × the view distance are hidden only where they rise above the eye** (`far_terrain::FarCull`; there the fog leaves e^-6 of them). Hiding all of them (the first round) opened holes below the horizon when seen from a summit: the atmosphere's pale ground haze showed through, the "lake". `far.cull` prints how many are hidden and how many are kept below the eye (Las Cañadas at 2 km: 159 hidden, 2516 kept).
      - Console `sky.fog [legacy|new|R G B]` (**legacy is the default since v4.45**, the user 2026-11-17; `new` – old name `auto` – is this fix) and `far.cull [on|off]` (only with the new fog) for comparisons.
      - Tests: `the_fog_under_the_atmosphere_is_its_horizon` (`ocw-sky`: the keys, brighter than the light model's by day, continuous, warm after sunset, dark at night), `the_fog_glows_towards_a_low_sun` (`ocw-sky`: warm, none high up or below the horizon, the round trip through the renderer's product, the fall-off), `the_fog_colour_follows_the_view_limit` (`ocw-render`: the share by distance and weather, the haze scale, the linear mix), `the_distance_to_a_far_tile`.
      - Before / after side by side (left before: the light model's fog, no culling; right after), 1600 × 900, marge, `test-output/fog-fix-2026-11-16/` with `index.md`. Cases at the Teide view (`tf-…`) and the top of the Schauinsland road (`bf-…`): Low 8 km, Medium 30 km, High at 2 km, 12 km and unlimited, sunset at 12 km and 2 km, mist and rain at 12 km, and **towards and away from the sun** (`tf-sunset-{2,8}km-{toward,away-from}-sun`: 18:00; `bf-low-8km-…` 16:00, `bf-sunset-12km-…` 16:30). The Teide no longer stands out at 2 km, 8 km and at sunset; the Schauinsland's far hills fade into the haze without holes; Medium and unlimited look as before; mist and rain are unchanged.
      - **Still open:** one fog colour per direction cannot fit every distance (the atmosphere's haze grows with it): the fogged band stays a few hundredths off the sky – slightly bright far away from a summit, a faint pale ridge where fully fogged terrain rises well above the horizon (the sky is bluer higher up than at the horizon, the fog has the horizon's colour). A fog that fades into the atmosphere's own sky colour per pixel needs a renderer change (a fog shader that reads the atmosphere's sky-view LUT).
    - **Open:** the far terrain's outer ring is not rebuilt for a short distance; the neighbour packages' loading (4.7) does not follow the distance; "the GPU not the limit" is not measured (the no-gain rule stands in); the target from a real monitor's refresh was not seen (headless outputs report 60 Hz) and the browser cannot read the refresh (Q9: 60 there anyway); the browser test with Chromium's CPU throttling (planned) is not written; VR's headset refresh waits for Phase 11 / 14; real phones.

**Measured (marge, 2026-11-14, headless Chromium 156, 1280 × 720, AMD Radeon RX Vega; `test-output/web/web-20261114-213813*`, `web-webgl2-20261114-214742*`, `web-compare-20261114-214838*`, `web-compare-20261114-220337*`):**

| | WebGPU build | WebGL 2 build |
|---|---|---|
| module (`make web`, `web` profile) | `ocw_web_bg.wasm` 76.0 MiB raw, 16.9 MiB gzip, 10.7 MiB brotli; glue 210 KiB | `ocw_web_webgl2_bg.wasm` 75.8 MiB raw, 16.8 MiB gzip, 10.6 MiB brotli; glue 153 KiB |
| build on marge | 376 s | 284 s (first build of Bevy for WebGL 2: 472 s) |
| `make test-web` / `--gpu webgl2` (auto: High / Low) | 60.1 fps; joined 1.10 s, ticking 4.8 s after navigation; all 25 UI checks | 60.0 fps; joined 1.04 s, ticking 4.5 s; all 25 UI checks (menus, gamepad, captures, video, FIT, reload) |
