**Status (v3.17): K4 and K5 done** (and K7 as far as the local garage goes: persistence and repairs, Phase 4 W6). As built:

- **Model (`ocw-sim::damage`, pure, deterministic, wasm):** the rider condition and seven parts (front / rear wheel, front / rear tyre, drivetrain, handlebar, frame; weights 0.15 / 0.15 / 0.075 / 0.075 / 0.15 / 0.1 / 0.3), the **bike condition** their weighted mean. A soft bump takes `2 % × min(E / 125 J, 1)` (a side contact below 0.5 m/s nothing, a side contact half; a fallen bike or the road edge the bike only; the world half for the rider), a crash `5 + 20 s` % rider and `5 + 25 s` % bike with the severity `s = 0.65 · min(E / 1280 J, 1) + 0.35 · hardness` (head-on and the world 1, road edge 0.8, fallen bike 0.6, rear-end 0.5, wheel contacts 0.3, side 0.2). The bike's loss spreads over the parts by the **impact's side** (from the push: slowed = front – front wheel, tyre, bar, fork; pushed on = rear – rear wheel, tyre, drivetrain; sideways = the side the bike falls to, the derailleur on the right) so that the bike condition drops by exactly the loss; the frame takes its share only from very hard hits (severity above 0.5), what a wrecked part cannot take reaches the frame. **Deterministic:** a tyre hit below 70 % goes **flat**, a drivetrain hit in a crash below 35 % **breaks the chain** (no random numbers). The crash itself is K2's; its time down grows ×1.25 when hurt, ×1.5 (+0.1 per further crash, at most ×2) when injured, ×2 when badly injured.
- **Effects (on the virtual rider only; the trainer and the hearts see the real power):** hurt 3–8 %, injured 10–20 %, badly injured 20 % less power (the virtual drivetrain), after the **medical stop** (60 s) at most 50 % until better than injured; a **buckled wheel** (below 80 %) +10–40 % rolling resistance each (and it wobbles); a **flat** ×4 rolling resistance and at most 15 km/h until mended – standing still for 2 s (↓) or `ride.repair` (`DamageRequest`) starts the 30 s repair, bots mend at once; the **drivetrain** 2–10 % efficiency below 95 %, a broken chain holds the rider for 45 s; a **bent bar** (below 80 %) −20 % manual lean (autodrive unaffected); a **broken bike** (below 10 %) waits 60 s for a spare (afterwards riding the spare, as new; in an event without the organiser's neutral service the rider is DNF first). A stop holds the rider (the power has no effect, braking to a standstill, its time runs once standing; SIM flat like down, no hearts). Easy riding (moving, below half of the FTP, estimated 2.5 W/kg as the server has no FTP) heals 1 % a minute; riding on does not; a stop outside an event fixes nothing but punctures and chains; the organiser's **neutral service** restores the bike after 30 s standing. `ride.damage` off (the default, Q1) or collisions off: no meter changes and no effects, also for carried-over damage.
- **Server and protocol (additive, 6.2):** `Session` owns each rider's `Damage` (bots too: they can be crashed by a human and take damage), takes the hits from the K1–K3 responses (`Response.touch` carries the hardest contact that did not bring the rider down), applies the effects in the step and ticks the stops; `RiderUpdate.damage` (`DamageState`: per mille meters and parts, the affected parts as bits, injury level, flats, chain, the stop and its time left, limited, spare, crashes, abandoned, the last hit) at 2 Hz and in the next snapshot after every change; `ride.damage` in `RulesRequest.damage` (with `collision_access`), `Welcome.damage` / `Snapshot.damage` (in force); the organiser's `DamageRules` (damage on / off, DNF when badly injured, neutral service) in `EventStart.damage` and `EventState.damage`; crashes and the final condition in `EventStanding`; `DamageRequest.repair`; `BikeChange.damage` (the garage's bike condition after a repair or a swap); `DevCommand.damage` (`StageDamage`, `dev.damage`); `ocw-server --damage on|off` (off). The client's prediction rides the same effects (`Predictor::set_damage`) and takes the server's state while stopped.
- **Persistence (Q6):** the client keeps the server's damage of its rider in the local garage (`workshop.toml`: per bike `condition` – damage part → per mille –, per rider `injury` – per mille and the UTC time it was saved), from local and remote servers, never in captures or the kiosk's show mode; the next ride's hello carries it (`Hello.damage`), the injury healed over the real time since (**10 % an hour**, a night heals everything); the bike's parts stay until repaired; a broken bike is ridden as a loaner (fresh, its damage not recorded) until repaired; the garage keeps only a **change** of the server's damage (so a repair is never overwritten before the server has it) and nothing while the workshop is open; a repair or a bike swap in the workshop reaches the ride with the bike (`BikeChange.damage`: the bike's parts and the rider's condition from the garage, applied with the bike – not in an event that is not over), and the ride's damage belongs to the bike it was sent with. The server trusts the hello's condition (a rider can only claim to be fresher, as a new rider is; with accounts the backend keeps it, Phase 5). **Anonymous browser riders never keep damage** (no hello damage, nothing saved).
- **K5 – the widget (`ocw-render::damage_hud`, built by `ocw-client::damage`):** in the bike computer's panel, a rider silhouette (head, body, legs) and a bike silhouette (v5.04: a side-view bicycle drawn in code by `ocw-render::damage_icon`, 48 × 32 px – tyres, rims and hubs, the frame triangle with the stays, head tube and fork, the chainring and chain, stem and drop bar, the saddle; each part its own tinted layer; the rider 22 × 32 px), each with a bar, the percentage and the level word with its icon (● good, ▲ warning, ◆ serious, ■ critical; green, amber, orange, red – never colour alone; "fine", "bruised", "hurt", "injured", "badly injured"; "fine", "scratched", "damaged", "badly damaged", "broken"); the damaged parts light up on the bike icon in their status colour, labels list them ("rear wheel buckled", "front puncture: stop to repair", "chain broken", "handlebar bent", "frame damaged") with a stop's line ("Medical stop: 42 s"; also the HUD notice); on a hit the icon flashes twice, the bar drops over 0.6 s and the loss shows for 2 s ("−8 % rider, −12 % bike"); hidden with damage off; since v5.04 always shown while damage is on (also at 100 % before any hit) and hidden otherwise only with `hud off` (the `display.damage` / `hud.damage` switch is gone). The **results** show a damage dot (an icon: ▲ hurt or damaged, ■ badly injured or broken) and the crashes per rider. **Visible damage** (`ocw-render::damage_look`): up to four scuffs on the down tube by the bike's damage, a bent wheel swinging out of its plane once per turn (up to 0.07 rad), the chain hanging below the chainring when broken, dust on the hip and the back, the kit torn at the hips when hurt – small boxes in the bike's frame, spawned once per damaged avatar.
- **FIT:** a `user_marker` event per crash (`MarkerKind::Crash`, data 3) at its start; no injury data leaves the device.
- **Desktop:** `ride.damage [on|off]` (no argument: the own condition), `ride.repair`, `dev.damage rider|PART PCT|puncture_front|puncture_rear|chain|reset` (local server), setting `ride.damage` (off) on Settings → Controls → *Damage* beside *Collisions* (v5.04; before on Settings → Trainer with a `display.damage` switch, now gone).
- **Tests:** meters per hit type, the spread over the parts and the side, injury levels and their effects on the virtual power, part effects (buckle, drivetrain, bar, profile), punctures and their repair (standing still, asked, bots), the chain, the broken bike and the spare / DNF, the medical stop and the organiser's DNF rule, recovery and the neutral service, real-time healing, the repair formula (exact in per mille), visible damage; in the session: damage off changes nothing (also carried damage), a crash takes off the meters and keeps a hurt rider down longer, the slower virtual rider, the stops holding the rider, DNF in an event, bots; the protocol round trip; on the server the rules request, the hello's carried condition, the damage in the snapshots (2 Hz and on change), the repair request and a workshop repair with the bike change; the client's widget states (fresh, after a hit, the drop, the flash, the 2 s, a repeated hit, damage off), an old hit not animated, dots, notices, carried condition healing and anonymous riders keeping nothing; the wallet's persistence across a restart (file round trip) and the repairs (formula, base parts, pairs, bought parts, Repair all, beyond repair); the HUD widget headless (words, icons, colours, lit parts, bars, flash, hidden); the results' dots; the FIT marker; the visible damage's wheel wobble, scuffs and chain; the rub's rate. Scenes `k4-damage-crash` (and `-video`), `k4-buckled-wheel`, `k5-visible-damage`, `k4-workshop-repair`, `k4-workshop-repair-card`, `k4-workshop-injury` (Wayland and X11).
- **Sound:** a buckled wheel rubs the brake once per turn (a procedural tick, `audio.play rub`, while the own rider rides on it).
- **Not yet (K4 / K5):** the chain noise of a damaged drivetrain, a FIT developer field with the condition, the damaged part shown on the model of the part itself (a damaged deep carbon wheel looks like the shipped wheel with the generic marks), the bandage of an injured rider and the limp, the rider list's dots outside the results (the in-ride position line has none), spatial placement of the marks on the ragdoll (they ride with the bike), damage of neighbouring packages' objects (as K3), a pothole / surface hit (Phase 8), the organiser's rules for remote events beyond the event start (K6).

- **Not yet (open):** the VR fade (12C, with Phase 11), organiser settings on remote servers (K6, also whether the aids are allowed in a race; the neutral service and the DNF rule of 12E are built with K4); the browser app shows the warning, the arrow and the shake once its glue fills the view's fields (the logic is shared). *(Done since: the chase camera's shake and wider orbit, the "last moment" warning and the proximity arrow as graphics, v3.22 below; spatial crash sounds and the client predicting bumps with other riders, v5.22 below; the kiosk's show mode rides with collisions off – `scripts/kiosk-show.args` sends `ride.collisions off` – and now `camera.shake off` too.)*
- **Performance (15):** the collisions of 100 riders take 0.027 ms per tick in a bunch and 0.078 ms in a full crush (~180 contacts; release on marge, `cargo test --release -p ocw-sim a_hundred_riders`); the whole server tick with 100 bots and everything on: 322 µs mean (216 µs with collisions off; `ocw-server --bots 100 --fast`).

**Status (v3.22): wet roads in crashes (with Phase 9 S6), 12C's camera and 12D's aids as graphics.** As built (the choices marked *proposal* are open to the user):

- **The road's grip in the crash rules (`ocw-sim::collide`, pure, deterministic, wasm):** each `Body` carries the grip under it (S6's `WeatherPhysics.grip`: wet 0.75, puddles a little less, slush 0.55, black ice 0.4, at least 0.3; 1 in a tunnel and whenever the weather does not affect the physics; `ocw_sim::weather::grip`). Every crash threshold is multiplied by `crash_scale(grip)` – **linear in the grip** (*proposal*: the sideways friction that catches a bike after a touch is μ·g), never below 0.3, exactly 1 on a dry road: rider against rider (2.5 m/s → 1.9 m/s wet, 1.0 m/s on ice; the lower grip of the two), the wheel touch (1.0 m/s, the hooking lean 10°), head-on, rear-end, both falling (3.5 m/s), the world and the road edge (3.5 m/s, the rider's own grip). The pushes, speeds and wobbles of a contact are unchanged – only whether it brings the rider down. Two autodrive riders still never bring each other down, soft mode (group rides) still never crashes.
- **Skids – a too-fast corner on a wet road (`collide::skid`):** S6 caps a leaning rider's lean at what the grip holds (atan(grip · tan 30°)); asking for more makes the tyres slide (*proposal*): the excess lean builds *slip* (5° of excess for a second = 1, recovering at 2 a second within the grip), the rider loses up to 1 m/s² while sliding, the bike wobbles once when the slide begins (a bump: the trainer's pulse and the tyre squeak), and at slip 1 – at 3 m/s or faster, with the full model – the rider falls: `ContactKind::Slide` ("slid out"; wire `CONTACT_KIND_SLIDE`, 9), a lowside thrown out of the turn at 0.3 × the speed, its damage hardness 0.25 (the softest fall). On a wet road a full lean (30°) slides out in about 0.8 s, on ice in about a third of that; leaning within the grip never skids. Below 2 m/s there is no skid (a foot comes down). **Autodrive never skids** (it is an aid, 12D: it never causes a crash by its own move; S6's slow-down before sharp turns brakes for the grip). The server applies the skid right after the physics step; the client's `Predictor` rides the same skid with the same inputs (the speed lost; the fall comes only from the server) – tested tick for tick against the session.
- **Autodrive on a slippery road (`ocw-sim::avoid`):** `Me.grip`; the look-ahead and the time to collision grow by 1 / grip (*proposal*: braking and steering need more room) and the hold-back brake is gentler (the gain × grip), so a field of bots on ice stays clear of each other (tested: 20 bots on a loop for 3 minutes on ice, no crash, no skid); a dry road plans exactly as before.
- **Off is off:** collisions off – a wet road rides exactly S6's physics (tested against the plain tick); the weather physics off – a storm in the session's weather changes nothing in a field with bumps, a hard lean and a crash, bit for bit (tested).
- **12C – the chase camera after a crash (`ocw_client::camera_fx`, pure; `ocw-render::camera`):** a **shake** after the own rider's crash and after a **hard bump** (a wobble of 0.07 rad or more, closing at about 0.9 m/s; 25–60 % of a crash's strength): the eye jolts up to 12 cm (sums of sines at 5–13 Hz under an envelope: up in 0.04 s, gone after 0.8 s) and rolls up to 2°, added on top of the smoothed eye and taken off again before the next frame's smoothing (the shake never drags the camera; tested); the **wider orbit** while down: up to 1.8 × as far, 0.3 rad higher and turned 0.6 rad to the side of the fall (eased in over the fall, out over the remount; the mouse orbit stays). Everything is a function of the game time since the event (the crash's elapsed time, the bump's server tick), so a capture renders it smoothly. The setting **`display.camera_shake`** (on; console `camera.shake [on|off]`) turns the shake off for motion comfort (*proposal*: the slow wider orbit stays); the kiosk's show mode sends `camera.shake off` (`scripts/kiosk-show.args`). The VR fade waits for Phase 11.
- **12D – the aids as graphics (`ocw_client::aids`, pure; `ocw-render::aids_hud`):** the **"last moment" warning** – the own footprint and the others' (riders and fallen bikes, in the own path frame, also in free ride) moved on with their velocities for 1 s in 0.05 s steps with 0.1 m of margin; the first touch warns (riders already touching do not), and so does a slide (slip ≥ 0.05): an amber warning triangle with an exclamation mark (drawn in code) flashing at 4 Hz under the HUD's top, a small amber arrow pointing at the hit, the word "Careful!" or "Sliding - lean less". Setting **`ride.hit_warning`** (on by default, *proposal*: a warning never steers; console `ride.hit_warning on|off`). The **proximity arrow** (with `ride.proximity_cue`, still off by default as built in K2): a pale arrow on a ring around the own rider pointing at the nearest rider within 1 m beside or 2 m in front or **behind** (behind added, *proposal*); it replaces the text line ("<< rider close on the left"), the bell stays. Neither shows while down or flying. The three switches have their own page, **Settings → Controls → Riding aids** (Controls has six rows, the ten-foot rule).
- **Tests:** the grip in every threshold (rider contacts, a wheel touch, the edge, a post), the scale, soft mode and autodrive pairs on ice; the skid (wet, ice, within the grip, recovery, soft mode, slowly, dry and off exactly nothing), the session's rear-end on a wet road and the slide-out, off = identical (tick and storm), the bots on ice, the predictor in step; avoid's earlier reaction and gentler hold; the shake's envelope (rise, fade, zero after 0.8 s), smoothness, repeatability, hard and soft bumps, the setting, the orbit's widening and easing; the camera system (shaken by the offset in its own axes and rolled, back exactly afterwards, wider while down); the warning's timing (about 1 s before, the same speed never, beside never, touching never, steering into a rider beside, a fallen bike, the nearest first, a slide first), the arrow's direction (beside, behind, in front, too far); the HUD (pictures drawn in code, the ring, the flash, shown and turned, hidden in flight); the Slide on the wire.
- **Scenes:** `k12-wet-slide-video`, `k12-wet-slide-down`, `k12d-warning-arrow` (Wayland and X11).
- **Wet leaves (v5.34, 4.6.2 Q6):** a slide on wet leaves in a fast corner is a crash of its own kind (`ContactKind::Leaves`, wire 10, "wet leaves", hardness 0.25), only with damage on and the full model, never while a group ride runs, only for client riders; it goes through the same crash sequence, damage, sounds and feed (`ocw_sim::leaves`; 4.6.2 Q6 has the numbers). Autodrive riders can slip too: the leaves are the road's, not a move of the aid.

**Status (v3.47): K6 – the organiser's options – done** (except the VR comfort fade, which waits for Phase 11). As built (the choices marked *proposal* are open to the user):

- **The rules** (`ocw_sim::event::Rules`, the organiser's for one event; riders cannot change them until it is over): the collision model (off / soft / full; default by the kind – group rides soft, races full, Q2), the race mode (2.5, 4G), the weather and its physics (Phase 9 S5 / S6), damage on / off, **DNF when badly injured**, the **neutral service** with its **wait** for a spare wheel (a puncture) or a spare bike (`service_s`, at most 600 s; default: the puncture mended in 30 s, the spare bike in 60 s; one wait for both, *proposal*), the **riding aids** (the "last moment" warning, the proximity arrow and bell) allowed or not – **by default allowed in every event, races too** (Q8, decided 2026-11-15; until then: not in races), the organiser may forbid them –, **chaotic bots** (Q3; default the session's switch) and the **time limit** after the winner (30 s – 2 h, *proposal*; default 120 s or a quarter of the winner's time).
- **DNF rules and reasons:** an entrant is DNF when leaving the session, over the time limit, badly injured with the organiser's rule, or with a broken bike in an event without the neutral service; `Entrant.dnf_reason` / `EventStanding.dnf_reason` (`DnfReason`: left, time limit, injured, bike broken).
- **Protocol (additive, 6.2):** `EventStart.aids` (11), `chaotic_bots` (12), `time_limit_s` (13); `EventState.aids` (18, optional: an older server allows them), `chaotic_bots` (19, in force), `time_limit_s` (20); `EventStanding.dnf_reason` (11); `DamageRules.service_s` (4); the state's `DamageRules.damage` carries the damage in force.
- **Server:** `Session::set_event_rules` puts them in force with the event's start; chaotic bots by the event's rule over the session's switch (`chaotic_bots_on`), the time limit in the event's DNF rule, the service's wait in the stops; the answer to the start lists them ("riding aids allowed, chaotic bots, neutral service (spares in 20 s), DNF when badly injured, time limit 300 s"). The aids run in the clients (14 Phase 12D), so the server decides the rule and sends it; the clients turn the warning, the proximity arrow and the bell off while their rider rides in an event that forbids them (until the own finish or DNF) – a modified client could ignore it (*proposal*: acceptable, the aids never steer).
- **Event info and results:** on the start line and under the results "Rules: collisions on, damage on, riding aids not allowed, chaotic bots" and, when set, "Neutral service (spares in 20 s), DNF when badly injured, time limit 5:00 after the winner"; a DNF row says why ("badly injured", "bike broken", "over the time limit", "left"), the HUD "DNF (badly injured)".
- **Setting them:** `event race|group|tt … --collisions off|soft|full --damage on|off --aids on|off --chaotic-bots on|off --neutral-service --service-s S --dnf-injured --time-limit MIN`; without an option the settings `event.collisions`, `event.damage`, `event.aids`, `event.chaotic_bots` (`auto` = the default), `event.neutral_service`, `event.dnf_injured` apply – the page **"Start the event?" → Organiser rules** (six rows; the Ride page is full). The time limit and the service's wait are console options only (the ten-foot rule).
- **Tests:** the rules on the event (aids by kind, the time limit and its range, abandoning with a reason, the reasons of leaving and the time limit), the service's wait for the spares, the protocol round trip (request, state, every reason, an older server), the server putting them in force and ending them, the client's aids off in a race and on with the organiser's rule and after the own finish, the info and results lines, the DNF rows, the console options with the page's settings as defaults and the checks, the page's rows. Scenes `k6-event-rules`, `k6-organiser-rules-menu`, `k6-results-rules`.
- **Not yet (K6):** the VR comfort fade (Phase 11), organiser settings of scheduled events on a remote server (the backend, Phase 5: today the starting rider of a local event is its organiser), per-entrant rules (e.g. aids for some riders only).

**Status (v5.22): spatial crash sounds and the predicted bumps with other riders – done.** As built:

- **Spatial crash sounds (12C *Sound*):** another rider's bump or crash is heard from where it happens – placed like the others' bikes (`ocw_audio::spatial::place`): at that rider's bike 0.4 m above the road, heard at the own head (distance: full level to 2 m, then the inverse-distance law, faded to nothing between 50 and 70 m; direction: equal-power pan, narrowed within 1 m, behind quieter (× 0.75) and duller; the air's low-pass by distance). `ocw_audio::cues::contact_cues` gives each contact cue with its rider (`ContactCue { cue, from }`; `from: None` = the own rider's bump, crash and remount and the proximity bell, played in the centre as before); `ocw_client::audio::AudioFeed` turns the others' into `MixerMsg::SpatialCue(cue, placement, at)`, which the shared mixer plays with the placement's left / right gains through a low-pass at the air's cutoff (on the effects bus; not at all beyond the range; stale ones dropped) – the same in the desktop app (cpal) and the browser (Web Audio; placed cues are dropped while the sound is locked, like the others). When the own rider bumps or crashes in the same frame, that cue stands for the others' of the same kind (the same contact: the other rider is at the own shoulder; no double thud). The ranges stay: bumps within 15 m, crashes within 40 m along the road.
- **The client predicts its own bumps with other riders (12B *Prediction*, 6.1):** `ocw_sim::prediction::Predictor::set_others(frame, bodies)` takes the others' last known bodies – a route's path frame (wrapping on a loop) or, in free ride, the world's plane from each rider's own path; fallen riders are obstacles; riders flying in god mode and the Echo rider are not solid (as on the server); the masses are not sent, so the default profile's (the server's answer corrects the difference). Every predicted tick, after the physics step and before the world's contacts (the server's order), the others are moved on a tick with their speed and `collide::resolve` runs over the own body and the riders within 8 m: the own rider takes the push – at most `PREDICTED_PUSH_MAX_M` = 2.5 cm a tick (a natural contact overlaps by a centimetre or two a tick and is resolved at once as on the server; a large overlap only comes from news – a rider first seen in a snapshot, a teleport – and is pushed out over a few ticks) –, the speed and the heading; the others' responses move the client's copies of them (`Predictor::other_responses`, applied to the last known states) until the next snapshot. `ClientCore` reconciles the own rider after it has read the others of the same snapshot: the server's state is extrapolated over the snapshot's age with those riders (contacts included), so a contact the server already resolved is not counted twice. The others' last known places are moved on by the snapshot's age (half the round trip) – also for drafting and avoidance. A ghost after the join as on the server (`JOIN_GHOST_S` = 2 s from the welcome, then until clear of everyone; `Predictor::rejoin`). The server stays authoritative: its state is blended in as before (0.5 s, a snap only over 5 m); crashes, the wobble, the trainer's bump pulse, damage, the HUD and the sounds come only from it; a predicted bump the server did not see is reconciled away.
- **Measured** (`ocw-client` test `bumps_with_other_riders_are_predicted_and_reconciled`, marge): the own rider leans into a bot riding beside at 25 km/h (steady 250 W, its lane 0.6 m right), 60 ms from the server to the client, 14 soft bumps: the largest lateral error of the prediction against the server **0.6 cm** with the predicted contacts, **4.9 cm** with only the server's bumps blended in (before); the largest sideways step 0.6 cm (the test's limit 6 cm), no snap along; the staged bump of the existing test (`dev.bump`) stays under 6 cm too. In `ocw-sim` alone (no latency, the server's session tick for tick): 0.5 cm against 41 cm.
- ***Fixed* (v6.40):** the test was flaky – the server took its weather seed from the wall clock, and for about one gust seed in ten the bot rode level beside a few millimetres from the own rider's centre, the client's copy of it a hair ahead where the server had it behind: the virtual brake shed 3.4 m/s in one tick on the client only (along step 10.2 cm, limit 10 cm). The brake now sheds at most 5 m/s² on both sides, and the test rides a fixed clock and seed; a second test runs 24 seeds (worst along 3.3 cm).
- **Tests:** the predictor's bump against the session's (the same code, within 1 cm; without the others 41 cm off), the ghost (2 s, then until clear), the capped push, collisions off; the client's group bump with latency (error, step, along) and the staged bump; the contact cues with their riders (own in the centre, others placed, the own standing for the others' of the same kind, the ranges); the feed's placement (left, right, farther quieter and duller, the own crash not placed); the mixer's spatial cue (left / right channel, distance, out of range, stale, the own centred). Scene `k12-group-bump-video`.
- **Not yet:** the others' masses on the wire (the prediction uses the default profile's); a predicted wobble before the server's (the wobble stays the server's, so a bump never shakes without one).

#### 12J – Open questions (for the user)

- **Q1 – Defaults: decided (2026-11-14, dashboard):** **collisions on, damage off** by default (the proposal).
- **Q2 – Group rides: decided (2026-11-14, dashboard):** group rides default to **soft bumps only** (no crashes); **races use the full model** (organisers can still change it per event, 12A).
- **Q3 – Bots' mistakes: decided (2026-11-14, dashboard):** **chaotic bots, as a setting** – bots sometimes make mistakes (late reactions, wheel touches) that can cause crashes; a session / event setting (`ride.chaotic_bots`, off by default; organisers decide in events). With it off, bots ride perfectly with autodrive avoidance (12D).
- **Q4 – Workouts: decided (2026-11-15, the user: "pause the step until you're riding again, so you don't miss part of the interval"):** while the rider is down after a crash the workout's **step waits** – the workout clock stops even if the legs keep spinning on the trainer (`WorkoutRun::set_down`, state *paused: rider down* in the workout panel and `workout status`) – and runs on when the rider rides again; no new ERG target is sent while down, so the trainer keeps the step's power (`ERG_STEP_RUNS_WHILE_DOWN = false`). Was (K2, v2.98): the step kept running.
- **Q5 – Falls: decided (2026-11-14, dashboard):** **straight to a ragdoll with a physics engine** (no scripted fall first). The engine (Avian or Rapier – both MIT / Apache-2.0) is chosen by a short spike in K2; it runs only on the client for the visual fall of the rider and the bike (the crash itself, its timing and the time down stay server-authoritative, 12B / 12C), so riders see plausible but not identical falls. *Engine (K2 spike, v2.98): **Avian** (12I).*
- **Q6 – Persistence: decided (2026-11-14, dashboard):** injuries and bike damage **carry over between rides** – a career / repair-shop mode: bike damage stays until it is repaired in the workshop, paid in hearts (14 Phase 4, 4E: `ceil(price × (1 − condition) × 0.3)` ♥), and injuries heal over real time and easy riding (12E recovery). With `ride.damage` off nothing accumulates; anonymous riders (Phase 10 Q5) never keep damage. This also unblocks Phase 4 W6.
- **Q7 – Gates and barriers on roads: decided (2026-11-14, dashboard):** gates, bollards and barriers on roads are **not shown by default** (and never block the routed road); a setting (`display.road_barriers`, Settings → Display) turns them on. When shown they are drawn but not solid on the routed road; off the road (wild mode) they are solid like other obstacles (12B).
- **Q8 – Riding aids in races: decided (2026-11-15, dashboard: "allow the aids in all races for now"):** the riding aids (the "last moment" warning, the proximity arrow and bell) are **allowed by default in every event, races too** – local and shared; the organiser may still forbid them (`--aids off`, the rules of 12I). `ocw_sim::Event::aids_allowed` defaults to allowed, the setting `event.aids` *auto* means allowed. Was (K6, v3.47): off in races unless allowed.

### Phase 13 – God mode: flying through the world as a unicorn (planned 2026-11-13; G1 – G4 done, v2.61; the guided camera path of G5 and the rider list page, v3.22; G5's browser app, v3.39 – see 13I)

**Goal:** a **god mode** in which the rider leaves the road and flies freely and fast through the world, e.g. to inspect the map, look at a region before riding it, or check a world package. While in god mode the rider turns into a **unicorn**. Toggled by a hotkey; controlled like a flight mode: **+ / −** for altitude, the **mouse** to look around, the **cursor keys** to move in the horizontal plane.

#### 13A – Entering and leaving (decided by the user, 2026-11-13: hotkey, unicorn, fast flight)

- **Hotkey G** (free today; rebindable later with the other keys, 3.2.1 Controls) toggles god mode; console `god [on|off]`; gamepad: Select / Back + North (a chord, so it is not pressed by accident). The menu gets *Ride → God mode* with the same switch.
- **Entering:** a short transformation (0.6 s: a sparkle burst, the rider and bike fade out while the unicorn fades in and rises 3 m), the camera switches from the chase camera to the flight camera behind the unicorn, the mouse pointer is captured (hidden, relative motion).
- **Leaving (G again) – lands where the unicorn is (decided, Q2):** the unicorn glides down (at most 2 s) and turns back into the rider and bike **on the nearest road below it**, standing still: in free ride (2.2.1) the nearest road of the graph (`--start`-like placement, the path starts there); on a fixed route the nearest point of the route (the rider continues along the route from there). The landing spot is marked under the unicorn while flying (a glowing ring on the road), so the rider sees where they will land. **Shift + G** instead flies back to where the rider left the road (a quick, eased flight, at most 2 s however far) and rides on from there. Esc in god mode first releases the pointer (a second Esc opens the menu, 3.2.1).
- **Landing anywhere, in wild mode off the road (asked by the user 2026-11-16, v4.15; changes Q2):** "make it for the unicorn possible to convert into a rider everywhere, turn on wild mode when landing away from road." The unicorn turns back into the rider **where it is**, not only on the nearest road:
  - *On or near a road* (the landing spot within the road's width + 2 m): as before – on the road, the path starts there, wild mode as it was.
  - *Away from a road:* the rider lands **on the terrain below the unicorn** (`Terrain::height`, never inside a building, a tree trunk, water or an obstacle of `OBST` – the landing ring moves to the nearest free spot and shows red where landing is impossible) and **wild mode is switched on** (autodrive off, manual lean steering, 5.2.1). The landing ring shows the spot as now.
  - *Today's model allows at most 60 m beside a road* (5.2.1 *Wild mode*: the rider moves along a path with a lateral offset). Landing within 60 m of a road uses that: the nearest road becomes the path, the offset is the distance. **Farther away needs free 2D riding off the road** (new, below). *As built (v5.53):* every landing away from a road goes into free 2D riding (one model on the terrain, whatever the distance to the road); wild mode's band stays for riders who steer off the road, and in a free ride its edge leads into the terrain.
  - **Free 2D riding off the road (new, server-authoritative 6.1):** a rider in wild mode beyond the 60 m band (or landed there) moves in 2D on the terrain: position (x, z) and heading in the server's state (additive protocol fields, 6.2), the gradient from `Terrain::height` along the heading (not the road's), rolling resistance by the land use under the wheels (meadow, field, forest floor, gravel, rock, sand – the T2 surface classes plus off-road ones), collisions with buildings, trees, walls and fences (K3 `OBST`, the full model), water impassable (the rider stops at the shore). Steering is the lean steering of wild mode; the trainer gets the terrain gradient (SIM). Drafting only with riders within reach as on the road.
  - *Back to the road:* riding onto a road within 2 m of its edge joins it (the path starts there, wild mode stays on until the rider switches it off, as today); **J** (rejoin) glides back to the nearest road like the unicorn's landing (at most 2 s); **G** flies again.
  - *Steep terrain, cliffs and the edge of the world:* see the open questions Q7 – Q9 below.

- **Who may use it:** single player on the local server: always. Shared sessions: the host decides (`ServerConfig.god_access`: anyone / host / nobody, like the world switch and the time machine, sent in `Welcome`); in a running **event** (race, group ride, time trial: from countdown to the rider's finish) god mode is **not available** – before and after it is. The kiosk / show mode never enters it by itself.

#### 13B – Flight controls

- **Touch** (where the device has one, 3.2.2; as built, v2.61): one-finger drag = look (as the mouse), two-finger drag = move in the plane (the fingers' centroid is a stick: full at 90 px from where they came down), spreading / pinching the two fingers = speed scale (as the wheel), on-screen **+ / −** buttons at the right edge (≥ 72 px, shown for 8 s after a touch) = altitude; a third finger cancels. (The proposed ‹ › ˄ ˅ pad was dropped: two fingers do it without covering the view.)
- **Flight model – like a plane (decided by the user, 2026-11-13, v2.67; replaces the strafing "drone" model of v2.51):** the unicorn always flies forward along its heading at a cruise speed (never hovers in flight; ↓ slows it to a slow glide, the minimum speed). **← / →** bank and turn: the unicorn rolls into the turn and turns like a plane in a coordinated turn (turn rate from the bank angle and the speed, `g · tan(bank) / v`), the camera banks with it; letting go levels out smoothly. **↑ / ↓** are the throttle: faster / slower along the heading, within the speed law below (Shift boost, Ctrl precise, wheel scale).
- **Look:** the mouse looks around the unicorn freely (yaw unlimited, pitch −89° … +89°; sensitivity and invert Y from Settings → Controls) **without changing the flight direction**; the view recentres behind the unicorn after a moment without mouse movement, or at once on a key. The direction of flight is the unicorn's heading, set by banking.
- **Keys only on the cursor block:** W / A / S / D are taken by riding (A autodrive, W wild mode; Q3).
- **Altitude (decided by the user, 2026-11-13): + makes the unicorn go up in the air, − makes it go down.** Held = continuous; the nose pitches up / down a little while climbing / descending and levels off when the key is let go; climb rate = half the speed. The keys are matched by the **character they type** (logical key: `+`, `-`, and `=` as + on US layouts), not by their position, so the main-keyboard + / − work on every layout (on a German keyboard + and − sit where a US keyboard has `]` and `/`; matching US positions made them dead there – bug found 2026-11-13); the numeric keypad + / − work too. The altitude stays at least **2 m above the terrain, water, buildings and trees** (also during a banked turn) and at most **8,000 m above sea level**.
- **Speed – much faster than riding:** the base speed grows with the height above ground, so low flight is controllable and high flight covers the map: `v = clamp(20 m/s + 0.5 × height above ground, 20, 400 m/s)` (72 km/h close to the ground, ~250 km/h at 100 m, ~790 km/h at 400 m, 1,440 km/h at 760 m and higher; with the boost and the wheel together at most **1,600 m/s** – 400 m/s × the boost; the wheel cannot go beyond it, so the tile streaming and the server's check can follow, v2.58). **Shift** = ×4 (boost), **Ctrl** = ×0.25 (precise); the **mouse wheel** scales the base speed (×0.25 … ×8, shown in the HUD). Climb rate = half the horizontal speed. Movements are smoothed (0.15 s acceleration, 0.25 s stop), so the flight is fluid at any speed.
- **Gamepad:** left stick ← / → = bank, ↑ / ↓ = throttle; right stick = look around; right / left trigger = climb / descend; A (South) = boost. **Touch:** one finger looks around, the +/− buttons climb and descend, bank and throttle by dragging on the left half (or on-screen buttons).
- **Map limits:** the unicorn can fly over the whole world set (4.7: the home package and its neighbours), softly stopped 200 m outside the outermost package's bounds.

#### 13C – The unicorn

- **Model:** our own low-poly unicorn (made for OCW, licensed like the code – no third-party asset, 13; no brand characters): white body, a spiral golden horn, a rainbow mane and tail (the eight colours of the categorical palette, animated by the wind of the flight) and **large feathered wings like a pegasus** (decided, Q5): they flap with the climb and the acceleration (beat rate up to ~2 Hz), spread wide in gliding and turns (banking with the turn rate), and fold along the body while hovering and when landing. It **gallops in the air**: a gallop cycle whose rate follows the speed, legs tucked in at high speed, a gentle bob while hovering. A faint **rainbow trail** behind it (fading after 2 s; off with Settings → Display → Effects).
- **Rider on it?** The rider is not shown; the unicorn *is* the rider. **No saddle cloth (decided by the user, 2026-11-13: the pink/yellow square on its back is removed)**; the rider's colour shows only in the mane's first band, plus the name tag above it as for riders, so in multiplayer each unicorn stays recognisable.
- **Wings – a bird's wingbeat (decided by the user, 2026-11-14):** the large feathered pegasus wings beat **continuously while flying**, clearly visible from the chase camera: about 1.2–2 Hz, slower and deeper when slow or climbing, faster and shallower when fast, with short glides (wings spread) between bursts of flapping like a large bird. **Organic motion:** each wing has a shoulder and a wrist joint with a phase lag, so the outer wing and the primaries trail the inner wing; the downstroke is faster and stronger than the upstroke; on the upstroke the wing folds slightly and sweeps back, on the downstroke it is fully spread with the primaries fanned out; the body rises a little on each downstroke, the head and neck counter-move, the rainbow tail reacts. In a banked turn the inner wing folds slightly and the outer one stretches; landing ends with big braking flaps, then the wings fold. Each unicorn has its own phase (from the rider id), so several never flap in sync. Transitions are eased; the near and far models flap, the impostor beyond 500 m stays still.
- **Sound** (procedural, 3.3): a chime on transformation, wind rising with the speed (the existing wind voice), soft wing beats when the wings are open, a gallop of hooves on air (muffled) while slow.
- **LOD:** a 3k-triangle model near, 600 far, an impostor beyond 500 m – like the riders (8).

#### 13D – Camera and inspection aids

- **Camera:** behind and slightly above the unicorn (8 m, looking along the view); **C** toggles a first-person view from the unicorn's head (the horn in view) – the pure "fly-through" for inspecting. Field of view widens with speed (+10° at 400 m/s). The camera never goes under the terrain.
- **Inspection HUD** (the bike computer is hidden; a compact flight panel instead): altitude above sea level and above ground, speed, base-speed factor, heading (compass), position (package metres x / z, latitude / longitude, tile id), the local time of the place (Phase 9). A crosshair in the middle: what it points at is named below it – the road (name, OSM way id, class, surface, width, bridge / tunnel, gradient), the area (land use, `LUSE`), building or water, and the elevation there. **I** toggles the panel; **P** puts a pin (a marker kept for the ride, `god.pins` lists them with coordinates, `--start X,Z` ready to copy).
- **World streaming:** the tile loader looks ahead along the flight direction with a radius that grows with altitude and speed (4.7: neighbours load within 3 km of their region, extended to 3 km + 10 s of flight); at high altitude only the far terrain LOD and the colour map are drawn; trees and buildings appear below 1,500 m above ground. Frame time budget as in riding (15); the tile loads keep their own thread.

#### 13E – Simulation and multiplayer (server-authoritative, 6.1)

- **Server state:** the rider enters the state `God` (additive field in `RiderUpdate`, 6.2). In this state the rider is **taken out of the physics**: no speed along the path, no drafting, no collisions (Phase 12), not in standings; the rider's road position is frozen where god mode began; on leaving, the server places the rider at the landing spot (after the plausibility check) or restores the old position (Shift + G). The unicorn's flight is **client-driven**: the client sends its 3D position and view at 10 Hz (`GodPose`), the server checks plausibility (speed ≤ the limits above, inside the world set) and broadcasts it to the others, who see the unicorn interpolated (6.5). The server stays the truth for who is in god mode and where the rider re-enters.
- **Trainer:** SIM mode is set to a flat road (lowest resistance), ERG keeps its target (a workout continues; Q4). Power and cadence keep being shown, but they do not move the unicorn.
- **Ride recording:** ride time continues (the ride never pauses, 3.2.1); **distance and elevation are not credited** while flying, the FIT file gets a marker "god mode" at both ends (Strava sees a pause in movement, not a 1,000 km/h segment). Achievements and leaderboards (Phase 7) ignore god-mode time, and **no hearts** are earned while flying (14 Phase 4, 4E).
- **Others (decided, Q1: visible):** riders see the unicorn flying over them with the rider's name and colours; no sound beyond 100 m. A host can see who is in god mode in the rider list.

#### 13F – Tests (spec 11.4)

- Pure flight model (`ocw-sim::god` or `apps/desktop/src/god.rs`, Bevy-free, wasm): speed law, boost / precise factors, wheel scale, acceleration and stopping, terrain clearance (never below 2 m over a test height field, also over a ridge at full speed), ceiling, world-set limits, moving relative to the yaw only (pitch does not dive), +/− climb rate.
- Input mapping: G, Shift + G, +/− (main and keypad), cursor keys, mouse motion, gamepad mapping; keys of riding (A, W, U, Q / E) do nothing in god mode.
- Server: `God` state excludes the rider from physics, drafting, collisions and standings; road position frozen and restored; plausibility check rejects too-fast poses; refused in running events and when `god_access` forbids it; distance not credited; FIT markers.
- Client: transformation and return, camera never under ground, crosshair inspection names the road under it (a test package); headless screenshots on X11 and Wayland of the unicorn in flight (scene in `scripts/scenes.toml`, also a short video of a flight over Liechtenstein for the build history).

#### 13G – Milestones (proposal)

- **G1 – Flight:** `god` command and G hotkey, flight model and controls, flight camera, pointer capture, terrain clearance, return to the road; the rider's model as a placeholder.
- **G2 – The unicorn:** model, gallop and wing animation, rainbow mane and trail, transformation effect, sounds.
- **G3 – Inspection:** flight panel, crosshair inspection, pins, first-person view, look-ahead tile streaming.
- **G4 – Multiplayer:** `God` state and `GodPose` on the server, access rules, others see the unicorn, recording rules.
- **G5 (later):** god mode in VR (Phase 11: head look instead of the mouse, comfort vignette at speed), a guided camera path for flyover videos (art project; **built, v3.22**, 13I), god mode in the browser app (Phase 10; **built, v3.39**, 13I).

#### 13H – Open questions (for the user)

- **Q1 – Visible to others: decided (2026-11-13):** yes, other riders see the unicorn with name and colours.
- **Q2 – Leaving: decided (2026-11-13):** land where the unicorn is (nearest road or route point below it); Shift + G flies back to where the rider left.
- **Q3 – Keys: decided (2026-11-14, dashboard):** **no WASD for flying** – the keyboard uses the cursor keys and + / − (as built, `WASD_FLIES = false`), and the **gamepad** is the other way to fly (left stick bank / throttle, triggers climb / descend, right stick look, 13B).
- **Q4 – Trainer while flying: decided (2026-11-14, dashboard):** **flat road** (lowest resistance; ERG keeps its target) – as built.
- **Q5 – Wings: decided (2026-11-13):** a classic unicorn with large feathered wings like a pegasus.
- **Q6 – Name in the UI: decided (2026-11-14, dashboard):** **"Unicorn mode"** in the menu, HUD, settings and messages (World → Unicorn mode); the console commands stay `god`, `god.*`.
- **Q7 – Steep terrain off the road: decided (2026-11-23, dashboard): (b), everything rideable at its real gradient – the trainer caps the resistance it can simulate anyway (the virtual trainer and the physics take the full gradient), built v5.53** – since v4.15 the unicorn (Unicorn mode, the flying mode) may land anywhere, and away from roads the rider then rides freely on the terrain (planned: free 2D riding off the road, 13A). Real terrain can be far steeper than any road – 40 % slopes, cliffs. Options: (a) slopes up to 25 % are ridden like a road; steeper uphill the rider stops with a "too steep" notice, as at a wall; steeper downhill is ridden with the speed limited, no tumbling; (b) everything is rideable at its real gradient, however steep. Proposal: a.
- **Q8 – Where landing is allowed: decided (2026-11-23, dashboard): (a), built v5.53** – when the rider leaves Unicorn mode the unicorn lands and turns back into the rider; a ring on the ground shows where. Options: (a) anywhere on land inside the world's tiles, but not on water, buildings or obstacles (the ring shows red there); in events and on fixed routes the unicorn still lands on the route as today, so a race stays on its course; in free ride and solo rides anywhere; (b) anywhere, in events too. (See 13A *Who may use it*: Unicorn mode is not available during a running event – possibly already answered for events.) Proposal: a.
- **Q9 – Riding off the road and the record: decided (2026-11-23, dashboard): (a), built v5.53** – a ride is recorded in a FIT file – distance, elevation, time and the GPS track, uploaded e.g. to Strava – and earns hearts by the work done; while flying nothing is credited (13E). The question is whether riding on the terrain away from roads counts. Options: (a) it counts like any riding – distance, elevation and time in the FIT file, the GPS track following the real off-road position, hearts by work as always (4E); (b) off-road distance is not counted. Proposal: a.
- **Q10 – Trees deep in a wood when riding off the road: decided (2026-11-23, the user): (a), built (v5.60, 13I)** – since v5.53 a rider who landed from the unicorn rides freely on the terrain and collides with buildings, walls, fences, posts, lamp poles and the trees near the roads. Those trees come from the package's obstacle section, which the world builder fills only up to 60 m beside a road (wild mode's reach); deeper in a wood – most of Liechtenstein's and the Black Forest's forest – the drawn trunks are not obstacles, so the rider rides through them. Making them solid means turning the trees the renderer draws (their places come from the land use, the forest cover and a seed) into trunk circles for the server and the prediction near riders off the road – a few thousand trunks per square kilometre of wood, made when a rider comes near (the server would also need the package's forest section, a few MB). Options: (a) every drawn tree is an obstacle off the road (the trunks near the rider made on demand; a crash at speed, a stop at walking pace – a wood is ridden slowly, around the trunks); (b) leave the woods passable beyond 60 m from a road (as built: simpler, never stuck); (c) no trunks, but a wood slows the rider like a thicket (more rolling resistance, no collisions). Proposal: a.

The pose's yaw is the heading; the body's bank on every client is the coordinated one from the turn rate (`god::bank`).
  - Keys: `god::input::LayoutKeys` reads each `KeyboardInput`'s logical key – `+` / `=` climb, `-` / `_` descend – and keeps the role of that physical key for the session (Shift + the German + types `*` and still climbs once the key was pressed alone); the keypad + / − always. The other god-mode and riding keys are letters, arrows and function keys (positional, as before); the console's `` ` `` is the key below Esc (`^` on a German keyboard).

Touch (`god/touch.rs`): a finger on the left half is the stick (bank and throttle from where it came down, full at 90 px), on the right half it looks; two fingers on one half are the stick with the pinch for the speed scale; the + / − buttons as before.

The phase and the rhythm come from the rider id (the same on every client, different riders out of step). The wing sound still beats at `wing_beat_hz` (also during the short glides).
