- **Effort (estimate):** W0 – W3 about 1 – 2 days of agent time, about 2 – 4 million tokens; W4 depends on headset time.
- **Open questions:**
  - **Q6 – Where the headset loads the app from: decided (2026-11-24, the user): (a) as proposed – the GitHub Pages preview, VR test builds under `/xr/`; built v5.77 (see W1, *Published at `/xr/`*)** – the first VR plan runs OCW in the Meta Quest 1's own web browser (WebXR), so the headset opens the browser app from a web address – and WebXR works only over HTTPS. Options: (a) the public preview on GitHub Pages – HTTPS works at once, but every test build is then public; (b) a server on our local network (marge) with HTTPS – the Quest browser warns about a self-made certificate, and a real certificate needs a domain. Proposal: a – the GitHub Pages preview for the first headset run W4, with test builds under a separate path `/xr/`.
  - **Q7 – The trainer in the first runs: decided (2026-11-24, the user): (b) – the sensor bridge (Phase 10, 10D.2) is built first, so the KICKR drives the headset ride; built (the bridge v5.76, its pairing in the XR page v5.77, see W1)** – in the first headset runs the bike has to move. The browser app cannot yet talk to the real trainer (the Wahoo KICKR): that needs the sensor bridge of Phase 10 (10D.2), not built yet. Options: (a) virtual power and autodrive only – the app pedals and steers by itself, enough to measure the frame rate; (b) build the sensor bridge first, so the KICKR drives the headset ride. Proposal: a.
  - **Q8 – Seated or standing reference: decided (2026-11-24, the user): (a) `local-floor`, the eye height from the rider profile's saddle height; built v5.77 (see W1, *The reference space*)** – WebXR needs a reference for where the rider's head is. Options: (a) `local-floor` – the headset knows the floor, and the eye height on the bike comes from the saddle height in the rider profile, so the view sits at the right height whoever rides; (b) `local` – a seated reference, recentred to the bike's eye point when *Enter VR* is pressed, whatever the real height. Proposal: a.

### Phase 15 – Model files: 3D objects in a standard open format (planning, 2026-11-15; **M1 built v4.24** – format, folder, loader and the export of today's bikes, rider, helmets and plants, see 15I; **M2's tools built v4.71** – `model import / export / diff` and the extended validator, see 15J; **M3's helmet switch built v5.09** – the helmets worn from their files, see 15L; **the Blender tooling built v5.10** – `make deps-blender`, the round trip `make test-blender`, `make models-diff`, see 15M; **the props as files built v5.12** – point obstacles and street lamps drawn from `props/*.glb`, see 15N; **M4 and M3's workshop built v5.16** – the unicorn and the workshop pieces drawn from their files, see 15O; **the `vehicle` kind built v6.80** – the traffic's 15 models in `vehicles/`, see Phase 18, 18G; the switch of the other kinds and the generator removal open)

**Goal (asked by the user, 2026-11-15):** stop encoding the shapes of 3D objects in code. Every object that can be a file becomes a model file in one standardised, open format, stored in **`artwork/3dmodels/`**. Artists can open these files in Blender and other tools, edit them and bring them back. The work has three parts:
- choose the format (15A);
- write the importer, exporter and loader (15D);
- move the current objects into that format where feasible (15E).

This revisits the Phase 4 decision "generated in code" (2.5 *Asset decisions*). The generators may stay where a model follows from numbers (Q1), but **at run time the app reads files, not shape code.**

#### 15A – The format: proposal glTF 2.0, binary `.glb` (to be confirmed, Q1 – Q4)

8.1 already names glTF 2.0, and the bikes and the rider are `.glb` files today: generated by `ocw-assets generate`, read by `ocw_assets::glb`, embedded with `include_bytes!`. Everything else is built from code at start:
- in `ocw-render`: `unicorn.rs`, `workshop.rs`, `obstacles.rs`, `street_lamps.rs`, the trees in `package.rs`, `gear.rs`;
- in `ocw-assets`: `helmet.rs` and the room in `workshop.rs`.

The candidates:

| Format | Standard / licence | Blender | Rust / Bevy / wasm | Features | Efficiency | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **glTF 2.0** (`.glb` binary, `.gltf` + `.bin` text) | Khronos open standard, royalty-free, ISO/IEC 12113:2022 | Built-in importer and exporter (the Khronos glTF-Blender-IO add-on, Apache-2.0, shipped with Blender); custom properties ↔ `extras` | `gltf` crate (MIT/Apache-2.0, already in the workspace, pure Rust, wasm-safe); Bevy's own loader uses the same crate | Node hierarchy, PBR metallic-roughness materials, textures, UVs, vertex colours, skins, morph targets, animation clips, cameras, lights (`KHR_lights_punctual`), instancing (`EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing`), `extras` for our metadata | Binary buffers are laid out as GPU vertex and index buffers, so loading is a copy, not a parse. Optional `KHR_mesh_quantization` (16-bit/8-bit attributes, about −40 %), `EXT_meshopt_compression`, `KHR_draco_mesh_compression`, `KHR_texture_basisu` (KTX2) | **Proposed** |
| FBX | Proprietary (Autodesk), no public specification, SDK under a closed licence | Import and export, but lossy and version-dependent | No maintained pure-Rust reader | Everything, including animation | Binary, compact | Rejected: closed |
| OBJ + MTL | De-facto standard, open, very old | Import and export | Simple crates (`tobj`) | Meshes and simple materials only: no hierarchy, rig, animation or PBR | Text: large and slow to parse | Too little: no nodes, so no anchors or hotspots |
| USD / USDZ | Open (Pixar, Apache-2.0-style licence), AOUSD | Import and export | No mature Rust reader; the C++ library is large and not wasm-friendly | Very rich: scenes, layers, variants | Good, but heavy tooling | Too heavy for a game client; fine for film pipelines |
| COLLADA (`.dae`) | Khronos, open, superseded by glTF | Removed from Blender 4.2+ (legacy) | Old crates only | Hierarchy, skins, animation | XML: large, slow | Obsolete |
| VRM | Open (on glTF 2.0) for humanoid avatars | Add-on | Through glTF | Humanoid rig, expressions | As glTF | Possible later as a rider *import* profile (a glTF variant, no new reader) |
| STL / PLY | Open | Import and export | Easy | Triangles and colours only | Compact (binary) | For 3D printing and scans only |
| `.blend` | Blender's own (GPL tool; the file format is undocumented and changes between versions) | Native | No reader | Everything | — | Source file at most, never a shipped format (Q1) |

**Why glTF – pros:**
- **Open and free:** a royalty-free Khronos standard with ISO standing; every tool on the path is open source, under Apache-2.0 or MIT. Blender is GPL, but that does not bind the files it exports.
- **Tools:**
  - Blender 2.8+ imports and exports it without add-ons;
  - other editors read it too: Godot, three.js editor, Babylon, Maya and 3ds Max (through Autodesk's glTF plug-ins), Substance;
  - viewers: Windows 3D Viewer, macOS Quick Look (through USDZ conversion), gltf-viewer, <https://gltf-viewer.donmccurdy.com>;
  - the Khronos **glTF-Validator** (Apache-2.0) and **glTF-Transform** (MIT; prune, dedup, quantise, meshopt, KTX2) work on the command line.
- **Already ours:** the reader and writer exist (`ocw_assets::glb`, 370 lines), the validator exists (`ocw-assets validate`, 8.1), and the bikes and rider already ship as `.glb`. There is no new dependency.
- **Efficient:** loading is a buffer copy. The format is web-native (it is what three.js and Babylon use), so the browser app gets the same files. `.glb` compresses well with the gzip/brotli of the web server (the Pages preview gzips, B8a).
- **Rich enough:** rigs, morph targets and clips are in the standard, for when the rider or the unicorn gets a real skin (2.6). Our metadata (kind, anchors, LOD, paint slots, physics profile name) fits in node names and `extras`, with no private extension.

**Cons and limits, and how we handle them:**
- **Parametric shapes:** glTF stores finished meshes, not "a frame from its geometry numbers". The bike frames, the helmets around the skull and the workshop room for N bikes follow from numbers today. Two answers:
  - keep a generator that **exports** files (it is then a modelling tool, not run-time code);
  - split the object into fixed pieces plus a layout in code (15E). Which one per object is Q1.
- **Fitting variants:** body build changes girth per region today (`rider::girth`). In glTF this becomes **morph targets** (Blender shape keys) or stays a per-node scale in code. Proposal: per-node scale for now, morph targets when the rider gets a skin.
- **No standard LOD:** `MSFT_lod` is a vendor extension that Blender does not export. We keep our convention: a `lod1` node, or separate `…-lod1` nodes per species, described in 15B.
- **Blender round trip pitfalls:**
  - duplicate names get `.001` suffixes;
  - the exporter must use "+Y up" and "apply modifiers";
  - custom properties go to `extras` only when *Include → Custom Properties* is ticked;
  - Blender's front view looks along −Y, which becomes glTF +Z;
  - material names must stay paint-slot names.

  The importer normalises or rejects all of these (15D), and an export preset documents the settings.
- **Compression extensions:**
  - Draco needs a C++ decoder (not wasm-friendly for us).
  - `EXT_meshopt_compression` needs the meshoptimizer decoder. It is C, or a Rust port that has to be checked for wasm.
  - Proposal: **no compression extension in the first stage**. Plain `.glb` plus transport gzip, and later `KHR_mesh_quantization` (trivial to decode, pure Rust) if size matters. Our models are small: 1.9 MB for all eight files today.
- **Textures:** today's models use only colour per material (paint slots). The reader learns embedded PNG and KTX2 textures (we already write KTX2 for the material library, 4.6, `ocw_assets::ktx2`), but shipped models stay texture-light. The look comes from slots and the material library, which keeps file sizes and the WebGL 2 limits in check (B7).

**Scope of the format:**
- **In scope:** objects with a fixed shape that are placed in the world or attached to riders:
  - rider, bikes, parts, helmets and other wearables;
  - the unicorn;
  - workshop furniture;
  - props: bollards, gates, barriers, lamps, benches, signs, later fountains and chapels;
  - plant species and other creatures (Phase 11/14 hands later).
- **Out of scope:** geometry computed from world data per place:
  - terrain, roads, kerbs and corners, junctions, bridges, tunnels;
  - OSM buildings (footprints and straight-skeleton roofs);
  - line obstacles swept along their line (walls, hedges, fences, guard rails);
  - sky, stars, clouds, weather particles, bolts, spray;
  - the unicorn's trail;
  - the HUD.

  These stay procedural, though their *parts* can be files: a window, a balcony, a chimney, a fence post, a lamp head.

#### 15B – The model contract (conventions every file follows)

- **Units and axes:** metres, +Y up, glTF's +Z is the model's front. The reader turns it to the app's −Z, as today (`ocw_assets::model`). In Blender, the model faces −Y (the *Front* view) and is exported with "+Y up".
- **Origin per kind:**

  | Kind | Origin |
  |---|---|
  | bike | ground contact under the bottom bracket, as the generator does today |
  | rider | between the sit bones |
  | wearable | its anchor on the rider (`head`, `face`, `foot_l`, …) |
  | prop | the foot centre, on the ground |
  | plant | the stem base |
  | creature | under the body's centre |
  | vehicle (v6.80, 18G) | on the ground under the centre of the wheelbase; aircraft, balloon, UFO under the body's centre |

  The table lives in `ocw_assets::kinds` and in `artwork/3dmodels/README.md`.
- **Node names are the interface:**
  - anchors `anchor_<name>`;
  - workshop hotspots `hs_<slot>` (8.2);
  - moving parts by their role (`wheel_front`, `crank`, `pedal_l`, the 2.6 rig names, the unicorn's `wing_l_shoulder`, `wing_l_wrist`, …);
  - LOD nodes `lod1` (and `lod2`, `billboard` for plants);
  - collision proxies `col_<shape>` (boxes and cylinders for Phase 12; never drawn).

  Every kind has a list of required and optional nodes, checked by the validator.
- **Materials are paint slots:**
  - a material's name is a slot from `ocw_assets::slots`, extended with prop slots: `wood`, `steel`, `stone`, `paint_red`, `paint_white`, `reflector`, `glass`, `bulb`, `leaf`, `blossom`, `fruit`, `bark`, `needle`, …;
  - the app maps slots to the material library (4.6), seasons (9 phenology tints `leaf`, `blossom` and `fruit`), the rider's look, and emissive lights at night (`bulb`);
  - colours in the file are the defaults.
- **Metadata in `extras`, never physics (2.5):**
  - asset-level `extras.ocw = { schema = 1, kind, id }`;
  - per kind: a bike's `profile` name, a plant's `species` and `height_m`, a prop's `osm` tags it stands for (`barrier=bollard`);
  - `shade_scale` (v5.54, Q11 (a)): vertex colours stay at most 1 (Blender keeps them as 8 bits, clamped to 1); a file whose shading reaches above its paint colour stores them divided by `shade_scale` (a number in 1 – 2, checked by the validator) and every app draws its vertex colours times it.

  The validator rejects physics keys, as today.
- **Budgets** (triangles; checked by the validator):

  | Object | Near | Far |
  |---|---|---|
  | bike | 15 000 | 4 000 |
  | rider | 8 000 | 4 000 |
  | unicorn | 3 500 | 800 (v5.16: the unicorn of Phase 13C has 3 014 / 682; it was 3 000 / 600 before it was a file) |
  | wearable | 1 500 | — |
  | prop | 1 500 | 300 |
  | plant | 2 000 | 200, plus a billboard |
  | workshop piece | 10 000 | — |
  | vehicle (v6.80, 18G; per class `extras.ocw.class`) | car, van 2 000; lorry, bus 3 000; motorbike 1 500; tractor 2 000; airliner 3 000; small plane, glider 1 500; helicopter 2 500; balloon 1 000; UFO 1 500 | 300; 400; 250; 300; 300; 200; 300; 150; 200 |

  Textures: at most 1024², power of two, base colour sRGB, embedded in the `.glb`.
- **Deterministic files:**
  - the writer produces byte-identical output for the same model (sorted, no timestamps, no generator version in the bytes, only `asset.generator = "ocw-assets"`);
  - a re-export without changes leaves git clean;
  - `generate --check` keeps working.

#### 15C – Storage: `artwork/3dmodels/` (decided by the user)

```
artwork/3dmodels/
├── README.md            # the contract (15B), the Blender export preset, how to add a model
├── manifest.toml        # one [[asset]] per file: file, kind, id, license, source, author (+ profile, species, …)
├── riders/              # rider.glb, rider-low.glb
├── bikes/               # bike-road.glb … bike-mtb.glb (today in assets/models/)
├── wear/                # helmets, glasses, caps (attach to anchors)
├── parts/               # catalogue parts by slot: wheels/, saddles/, bars/ … (assets/parts.toml `model`)
├── workshop/            # room pieces, bench, stand, hook, tool wall, lamp
├── creatures/           # unicorn.glb
├── flora/               # one file per species (ocw_world::flora), with lod1 / billboard
├── props/               # bollard, post, pylon, block, gate, lift-gate, cycle-barrier, street lamps, …
├── vehicles/            # the traffic of Phase 18 (v6.80, 18G): cars, van, lorries, bus, motorbike, tractor, aircraft, balloon, UFO
└── sources/             # the Blender sources (.blend, LFS) of every model, not loaded (Q1)
```

- **`assets/models/` moves here.** The include paths and `generate --out` follow, and the `assets/models` folder is removed. Textures of the material library stay in `assets/materials/` (4.6): they are not models.
- **Git LFS (decided by the user 2026-11-15, Q2):** `*.glb`, `*.gltf` buffers (`*.bin`), textures and `*.blend` under `artwork/3dmodels/` are LFS objects (`.gitattributes`); the validator still warns above **2 MB per model file**. Notes:
  - the free quota (10 GiB storage, 10 GiB download a month) is **per account** and shared with the art project's LFS media (OCW-ART), so the models' share is watched by the same budget check;
  - every CI job that builds the app needs the models (they are embedded with `include_bytes!`), so CI checks out LFS (`lfs: true`) and caches the objects (`actions/cache` keyed on the LFS pointers' hash) – a fresh download per run would eat the bandwidth;
  - `scripts/remote.sh` copies the working tree, so the build machines need no `git-lfs`; deb (the coordinator) and every clone that builds need it (`make deps`: git-lfs is added there when M1 lands);
  - GitHub Pages does not serve LFS objects, but the web build embeds the models, so that is no blocker.
- **Licence:** each file has a manifest entry (`license`, `source`, `author`; 8.1, 13). Own models are MIT OR Apache-2.0 like `artwork/`. Third-party models are accepted under licences that **only require attribution** (decided by the user 2026-11-15, Q3): CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD – with the author, the source URL and the attribution text in the manifest, shown on the credits pages; never share-alike, non-commercial or no-derivatives licences, never brands.

#### 15D – Importer, exporter and loader

All of it lives in `ocw-assets` (pure, wasm-safe except the CLI's file access) plus a thin Bevy side in `ocw-render`.

- **Reader / writer (`ocw_assets::glb`, extended):**
  - Today's limits are lifted step by step: embedded textures and UVs, vertex colours, `extras`, multiple scenes ignored (first scene), morph targets and skins read and kept (drawn when the renderer needs them), `KHR_materials_emissive_strength`, `KHR_texture_transform`, and later `KHR_mesh_quantization`.
  - Unsupported extensions in `extensionsRequired` are a clear error that names the extension.
  - It also reads `.gltf` with separate `.bin` files and textures (for diffs and Blender), not only `.glb`.
- **CLI `ocw-assets model …`:**
  - **`import SRC --kind K --id ID [--license … --source … --author …]`:**
    - reads a `.glb` or `.gltf` from Blender or any tool, then normalises it:
      - strips Blender's `.001` suffixes where unambiguous;
      - checks the axes from the bounds (a model lying on its back is an error with a hint);
      - merges primitives per material, drops unused nodes, materials and textures, and recomputes missing normals;
    - checks it against the contract (15B);
    - writes the canonical `.glb` to `artwork/3dmodels/<kind dir>/<id>.glb` and adds or updates the manifest entry.
  - **`export ID [--gltf] --out DIR`:** writes an editable copy (a `.glb`, or a `.gltf` + `.bin` + PNG set with readable JSON) for Blender, with `extras` kept as custom properties.
  - **`generate [--check]`** (exists): runs the remaining generators (Q1) and writes their files into `artwork/3dmodels/`.
  - **`validate [DIR]`** (exists, extended):
    - kinds, required nodes and slots per kind, `extras` schema, budgets, file and folder sizes, licences;
    - optionally runs the Khronos `gltf_validator` when it is installed (marge).
  - **`info FILE`** (exists): nodes, materials, triangle counts and bounds.
  - **`diff A B`:** a structural comparison for reviews of binary files (nodes added or removed, triangle counts, bounds, materials). `make models-diff` shows it for the files changed against `main`.
  - **`optimize FILE`** (later): quantisation and generating a `lod1` or billboard with a simplifier (a pure Rust one, checked for licence and wasm).
- **Run-time loader (`ocw_assets::library::ModelLibrary`):**
  - an index of the manifest, read once;
  - `get(kind, id) -> Arc<Model>`, parsed lazily and cached.
  - **Sources:**
    - **embedded** (default; a `build.rs` generates the `include_bytes!` table from the manifest, so release builds, the AppImage and the browser need no asset paths, as 2.5 decided);
    - **from a folder** in dev builds (`ocw-desktop --models artwork/3dmodels`, `OCW_MODELS=…`), with **hot reload** on the desktop: a changed file is re-read and the objects using it are rebuilt in the running app, so an artist sees an export from Blender at once.
  - The server and headless tools use the same library for anchors, bounds and collision proxies, without Bevy.
- **Bevy side (`ocw-render::models`):**
  - one place turns a `Model` into meshes and materials, generalising today's `riders::plain_mesh` and `gear::gear_mesh` (slots → materials, region colours, seasons);
  - meshes are **shared per model**: every bollard uses one mesh handle and many entities or GPU instances;
  - placed objects that today are merged into tile meshes (trees, obstacles) keep being merged per tile from the model's arrays, so the draw-call budget (15, Phase 14) does not grow.
- **Why our own loader and not `bevy_gltf`:** as decided in 2.5 (synchronous spawn, no asset paths, one reader for the validator, the server and the app). Paint slots, kit regions, seasons and the `gear.wesl` material are ours anyway. Bevy's loader may still be used in a dev **model viewer**.
- **Model viewer:**
  - `ocw-desktop --model-viewer FILE|ID` shows one model on a turntable with the anchors and LODs switchable, under the day/night light;
  - `drive.sh shot` takes its screenshots, which become the visual test of 15G and pictures for the art project.
- **Blender side:**
  - `artwork/3dmodels/README.md` gives the export settings (glTF Binary, +Y up, apply modifiers, custom properties on, no Draco, materials export, selected objects) and the import steps;
  - optional later: a small Blender add-on (`tools/blender/ocw_models/`: an export preset, a panel that sets `kind` and `id`, a node-name picker for anchors and hotspots, a budget check). Add-ons that use `bpy` count as GPL-derived, so it would be licensed **GPL-2.0-or-later** in its own folder, separate from the MIT/Apache code (Q4).

#### 15E – Migration plan: which objects move

| Object | Today | Target | How | Stage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rider (near, far) | `.glb` generated by `ocw_assets::rider` | `riders/rider.glb`, `rider-low.glb` | Move the files; the generator stays an exporter until Q1. Girth per body build stays per-node scale | M1 |
| Bikes (6 profiles, near + `lod1`) | `.glb` generated by `ocw_assets::bikes` (frame from geometry numbers) | `bikes/*.glb` | Move the files; generator as exporter (Q1). The rig numbers (`BikeRig`) are read from the file's nodes, so a hand-made bike works too | M1 |
| Helmets (4 styles, near / far) | Code, `ocw_assets::helmet`, fitted to the skull centre | `wear/helmet-*.glb` on `anchor_head` | Export once at the reference skull; the fit becomes the anchor's transform | M3 (**built v5.09**, 15L) |
| Glasses, caps, overshoes, … | Nodes of the rider file | Stay in the rider file, or `wear/` when they get variants | — | M3 |
| Catalogue parts (wheels, saddles, bars, …) | Variants inside the bike generator | `parts/<slot>/<id>.glb` (`parts.toml` `model`) | Hotspots `hs_<slot>` place them (8.2); budgets per slot | M3 |
| Workshop room and furniture | Code, `ocw_assets::workshop::room` and `ocw-render::workshop` (≈ 2 000 lines) | `workshop/*.glb` pieces | Wall and floor segments, bench, stand, hook, tool wall and lamp as files. `workshop::layout` stays code and places them for N bikes | M3 (**built v5.16**, 15O: 20 pieces) |
| Unicorn | Code, `ocw-render::unicorn` (≈ 2 100 lines of shapes and procedural animation) | `creatures/unicorn.glb` (near, `lod1`) | A node hierarchy with named joints (neck, legs, wing shoulder and wrist, tail and mane segments; mane bands as slots). The flight animation **stays procedural**, driving the named nodes. Later it can become a skin with clips | M4 (**built v5.16**, 15O: `creatures/unicorn-winged.glb`) |
| Point obstacles (bollard, post, pylon, block, gate, lift gate, cycle barrier) | Code prisms, `ocw-render::obstacles` | `props/*.glb` | One file per kind with a `col_*` proxy (Phase 12; the server collides with the proxies since v5.43); placement and merging per tile stay | M2 |
| Street lamps | Code, `ocw-render::street_lamps` | `props/lamp-*.glb` | Pole and head types per region style; `bulb` slot emissive at night (9) | M2 Placement rule: never in a road, only beside it (4.x *Street lamps*; **built v5.38**, `ocw_world::lamps::place_lamp`, lint `lamp.foot.*` = 0); OSM `highway=street_lamp` nodes placed and the poles solid **v5.43**. |
| Trees and plants (OSM, landuse and forest trees; the 32 species of the vegetation work) | Code, `ocw-render::package` tree arrays and seasons, `flora` | `flora/<species>.glb` with `lod1` and `billboard` | Seasons tint the `leaf`, `blossom` and `fruit` slots; per-tile merging stays (draw calls). Needs the vegetation branch merged first | M5 |
| Line obstacles, roads, terrain, bridges, tunnels, OSM houses, sky, weather, trail, wheel-contact test meshes | Code from world data | **Stay procedural** | Optional later: building details (windows, balconies, chimneys, the cathedral spire) and fence posts as kit files the generators place | M6 (optional) |

**Stages (each with tests, full checks, merge and deploy as usual):**
- **M1 – Format, folder, loader:**
  - the reader and writer extended (textures, `extras`, `.gltf`);
  - `ModelLibrary` with the embedded table and the dev folder;
  - `assets/models/` moved to `artwork/3dmodels/` with the new manifest fields, the README and the contract.
  - **No visible change:** screenshots before and after must match.
- **MX – Export all and switch (15H, asked by the user 2026-11-16):** every model the code draws exported into `artwork/3dmodels/`, named by function and shape; the apps load the files instead of the code, kind by kind; `export-all --check` keeps generators and files in step. After MX, M2 – M5 refine the files instead of moving objects.
- **M2 – Tools, first props:**
  - `model import / export / diff`, the extended validator, and the Blender round-trip test; **built v4.71 except the Blender round trip** (15J);
  - point obstacles and street lamps as files; **built v5.12** (15N).
- **M3 – Rider wear and the workshop:** helmets and parts as files, the workshop pieces, the model viewer (helmets **built v5.09**, 15L; the workshop pieces **built v5.16**, 15O).
- **M4 – The unicorn as a file**, with its procedural animation on named nodes (**built v5.16**, 15O).
- **M5 – Flora:** the species models with LODs and billboards. This comes after the vegetation merge, and is checked against the frame-time budget (15) on marge and in the browser (WebGL 2).
- **M6 – Optional:** the Blender add-on (Q4), building kit parts, `KHR_mesh_quantization`, `optimize`.

#### 15H – Export of today's models into files, and using the files (asked by the user 2026-11-16)

**Goal:** every model the code draws today is exported **once** into its own file, named by its **function and shape**, and the apps then load **these files instead of building the meshes in code**. Afterwards a model is changed by editing (or regenerating) its file, and a new or better model is a file swap, not a code change.

**Status before this step (2026-11-16):** none of Phase 15 is built. The reader and writer (`ocw_assets::glb`) and the validator exist; only the rider and the 6 bikes are files (`assets/models/*.glb`, written by `ocw_assets::generate`). Everything else is drawn in code: helmets and glasses (`ocw_assets::helmet`), the catalogue parts (inside the bike generator), the workshop room and furniture (`ocw-render::workshop`), the unicorn (`ocw-render::unicorn`), the point obstacles (`ocw-render::obstacles`: bollard, post, gate, lift gate, block, cycle barrier, pylon), the street lamps (`ocw-render::street_lamps`, per `LampKind`) and the flora (`ocw-render::flora` / `vegetation`: the OSM, forest and landuse trees and the vegetation species).

**The export (`ocw-assets model export-all`):**
- Runs **every generator** in the code and writes one `.glb` per model (and per variant actually used) into `artwork/3dmodels/` (15C), with a manifest entry each (`id`, `kind`, `license`, `source = "generator"`, the generator's name and its parameters).
- **Variants:** a parametric model is exported for each variant the game uses, not as a parameter space: the 6 bikes with their `lod1`, each helmet style (near and far), each catalogue part of `parts.toml`, each `LampKind`, each obstacle kind, and **three shape variants per tree species** (`-a`, `-b`, `-c`; size, rotation and tint stay per instance, as today), each with its `lod1` and billboard (*proposal*, Q8).
- **What stays fitting in code:** placing, scaling and tinting per instance; the rider's body build (per-node scale, later morph targets, 15A); the bike's fit to the rider (anchors); the workshop layout for N bikes (`workshop::layout` places the exported pieces); the unicorn's procedural flight animation, which drives the named nodes of its file (15E, M4).
- **Never exported:** the per-place world geometry of 15E (roads, terrain, OSM houses, bridges, tunnels, line obstacles, sky, weather).

**Names: function first, then shape** – `<category>/<function>-<shape>[-<detail>][-<variant>].glb`, lower-case ASCII with hyphens, no colours (colours are paint slots, 15B), no version numbers; the file's id is its path without `.glb`. Categories are the folders of 15C. Examples (the exporter's table is the source; the names below are the pattern):

| Code today | File |
|---|---|
| Rider (near, far) | `riders/rider-body.glb`, `riders/rider-body-low.glb` |
| Bike profiles | `bikes/bike-road-endurance.glb`, `bikes/bike-road-aero.glb`, `bikes/bike-road-climbing.glb`, `bikes/bike-gravel.glb`, `bikes/bike-mtb-hardtail.glb`, `bikes/bike-tt.glb` |
| Helmet styles | `wear/helmet-road-vented.glb`, `wear/helmet-road-lightweight.glb`, `wear/helmet-aero-road.glb`, `wear/helmet-tt-teardrop.glb` |
| Wear | `wear/glasses-wrap.glb`, `wear/cap-cycling.glb`, `wear/overshoe-aero.glb` |
| Catalogue parts | `parts/wheel/wheel-carbon-deep-60mm.glb`, `parts/saddle/saddle-short-nose.glb`, `parts/bar/bar-drop-compact.glb` |
| Workshop | `workshop/stand-repair-clamp.glb`, `workshop/bench-work-wood.glb`, `workshop/hook-wall-bike.glb`, `workshop/wall-tool-pegboard.glb`, `workshop/lamp-pendant-shade.glb`, `workshop/wall-segment.glb`, `workshop/floor-segment.glb`, `workshop/mirror-standing.glb` |
| Unicorn | `creatures/unicorn-winged.glb` (with `lod1`) |
| Point obstacles | `props/bollard-round.glb`, `props/post-hexagonal.glb`, `props/gate-swing.glb`, `props/barrier-lift-arm.glb`, `props/block-concrete-box.glb`, `props/barrier-cycle-staggered.glb`, `props/pylon-pyramid.glb`, `props/barrier-post-hexagonal.glb` (built v5.12, named by the shapes drawn: the post is a hexagonal pole, the pylon a four-sided frustum, the block a box) |
| Street lamps | `props/lamp-street-<pole>-<head>.glb` per lamp type; built v5.12: `props/lamp-street-arm-main.glb` (8 m, main roads), `-road` (6 m), `-path` (4.5 m) – the code has one shape in three heights, no `LampKind` yet |
| Flora | `flora/tree-spruce-conical-a.glb`, `flora/tree-beech-round-a.glb`, `flora/tree-larch-conical-a.glb`, `flora/palm-canary-fan-a.glb`, `flora/shrub-euphorbia-candelabra-a.glb`, … (`-b`, `-c` the other variants) |

The validator checks every name against the pattern, that ids are unique, and that every file is used by the game or listed as spare.

**Using the files instead of the code (the switch):**
- The apps load **only** files, through `ModelLibrary` (15D): obstacles, lamps, flora, helmets, parts, the workshop pieces and the unicorn are spawned from their files; the mesh-building code leaves `ocw-render` and the apps. The generators move into the exporter (`ocw-assets`, not linked into the apps; the browser's wasm gets smaller by their code).
- **Generator and file stay in step (Q1: the generators are kept):** `ocw-assets model export-all --check` regenerates every file whose manifest says `source = "generator"` and fails when a byte differs (the writer is deterministic, 15B), so a generator change without a new file – or a hand edit of a generated file – is caught in `make check`. A model edited in Blender is marked `source = "blender"` (its `.blend` committed, 15C) and its generator is retired (Q6).
- **No visible change:** for every switched object, the screenshots of its scenes before and after differ by less than the threshold of 15F (X11, Wayland and the browser), and the frame time on marge and in the browser (WebGL 2) does not rise; per-tile merging of obstacles and flora stays (draw calls).

**Stage:** the export and the switch are a new stage **MX** right after M1 (the loader and library): **MX – Export all, then switch kind by kind** (props → wear and parts → workshop → unicorn → flora), each kind a merge of its own with its screenshots. M2 – M5 then no longer move objects; they refine the files (Blender sources, colliders `col_*`, better LODs, the model viewer, the round-trip test).

**Tests (11.4):** the export is deterministic (two runs, identical bytes); every generator in the code is in the exporter's table (a test lists the mesh builders); names follow the pattern; each exported file passes the validator and the budgets (15B); loading a file gives the same mesh as the generator (vertex positions, normals, indices, slots within 1e-5); the scenes before and after match; `--check` fails on a changed generator and on a hand-edited generated file.

#### 15J – Built (M2's tools, v4.71)

**What was built (branch `worktree-agent-a64cacd30a467fa11`, 2026-11-17):**
- **The extended validator (`ocw_assets::check`):** every check is a `Finding` – a stable code (`node.blender-suffix`, `material.not-slot`, `budget.triangles`, `bounds.below-ground`, …), the severity (error fails the validator, warning is listed), the target (the file, a manifest key, a node, a material), the message and, where the fix is clear, a `Fix` (rename `wheel_front.001` to `wheel_front` when the plain name is free, rename `Frame.001` / `Bar Tape` to their paint slot, remove an unused material, write `extras.ocw` from the entry, set the copyright of own work). It checks:
  - the entry: `license`, `source`, `author`, the licence rule (13), **an attribution licence needs its source URL** (warning), the name (15H), the kind's keys (`profile`, `species`, `anchor` – which must be a rider node);
  - the file: copyright, `extras.ocw` (schema, kind, id, no physics), materials are slots and used, names unique, Blender suffixes;
  - **the contract names:** required nodes and the rig per kind, hotspots `hs_<slot>` of the workshop's slots (bikes only), anchors `anchor_*` empty, collision proxies `col_box*` / `col_cylinder*` / `col_capsule*`, a prop's proxy (warning), `lod1` for plants (and for creatures, warning);
  - the budgets per kind (near and `lod1`), the file size;
  - **the bounds:** the kind's origin (bikes, props, plants, creatures and workshop pieces on the ground within 5 cm), a rider or plant lying on its back (exported without "+Y up"), a model in centimetres or millimetres.

  `ocw-assets validate [DIR] [--json]` (also `model validate`) prints the findings with their fixes, `--json` one object per line; `manifest::report` gives them to code; `manifest::validate` keeps its old form (the errors as lines). **On the committed models (191 files): no error; 14 warnings** – three plant species reach below or float above their stem base (`cactus-pear-paddle-*` 0.10 m and `shrub-broom-teide-*` 0.67 m below, `shrub-alder-mountain-*` 0.05 m and `succulent-agave-rosette-*` 0.10 m above: the generators' crowns and paddles, Q10) and the phone prop (`props/phone-slab`, held in the hand: its origin is its centre by design, no collision proxy).
- **`model diff A B [--json]` (`ocw_assets::diff`):** files or ids of the model folder; a totals line (nodes, materials, triangles, vertices with the change), bounds, then one line per change – nodes added / removed / re-parented / moved / turned / scaled, meshes (triangles, vertices, materials, or "geometry changed (same counts)" within 1e-4; since v5.10 compared as drawn, with what moved, 15M), node extras, materials added / removed / changed (colour, metallic, roughness), the asset's copyright and generator, `extras` flattened to paths (`ocw.frame.stack_m`), and the two manifest entries; exit 1 when they differ.
- **`model import SRC --kind K --id ID [--license --source --author --profile --species --variant --anchor] [--out] [--dry-run]` (`ocw_assets::import`):** reads a `.glb` or `.gltf` (with its `.bin`), computes missing normals (the reader's lenient mode), strips Blender's `.001` suffixes where the plain name is free and wanted once, renames materials close to a slot and merges materials of one slot, merges a node's primitives per material (vertex colours and UVs filled where only some have them), drops unused materials, stamps `extras.ocw`, the copyright and generator, then checks the canonical bytes: a rider or plant lying on its back and every contract error refuse the import with the findings and their fixes; it prints what it normalised, the warnings and the diff against the file it replaces, and adds or updates the manifest entry (sorted). Importing the canonical file again changes nothing.
- **`model export ID|FILE [--gltf] --out DIR`:** the editable copy – the canonical `.glb`, or a `.gltf` with pretty-printed JSON (extras kept, Blender's custom properties) and its `.bin`.
- `artwork/3dmodels/README.md` lists the tools and what the import cleans up.

**Tests (11.4, 15F):** fixtures built in the tests – a post shaped like a Blender export (suffixes, a material in Blender case, two primitives of one material, an unused material, no extras), a primitive without normals, a plant lying on its back, a material that is no slot – are normalised or refused with the expected message; every finding's code and fix, the JSON form; `apply_fixes` leaves a clean model; diff: a model against itself and after a write and read is empty, node / mesh / material / extras / manifest changes are reported, moved geometry at the same counts; the manifest upsert is stable; **on every committed model** the validator finds no error (the warnings listed), the diff against itself is empty, the `.gltf` export reads back with an empty diff and imported again under its own entry gives the same model.

**Open:**
- **The Blender round trip (15F):** **built v5.10** (`make deps-blender`, `make test-blender`, 15M); the `.gltf` export → import round trip above stays its Blender-free half.
- **Point obstacles and street lamps as files (M2's second part):** built v5.12 (15N).

#### 15K – Bug fix: the fork raked forward (v4.83)

**Reported by the user (2026-11-18):** "turn around the bike fork (check images), it should point forward, not backwards as of now." **The cause:** the axle position was right – `bikes::Frame` puts the front hub ahead of the steering axis by the design's offset (`rake`: road 45 mm, gravel 50 mm, MTB 44 mm) – but the rigid blades were drawn through a middle point at 0.85 × the offset halfway down, so they took the rake high up, then ran parallel to the head tube to the dropouts: in the side view the blades bent *backwards* at the bottom, the opposite of a real fork (straight down the steering axis from the crown, bending or angled forward to the dropouts; compared with openly licensed side views on Wikimedia Commons of a classic road bike, a gravel bike and a hardtail – looked at only). The suspension fork had its stanchions on the axis and the lowers kinked forward. **The fix (`crates/ocw-assets/src/bikes.rs`):** `Frame::fork_blade` – six points from the crown on the axis to the axle, the offset growing as s^1.6 (`FORK_BEND`), so the blade always lies between the axis and the crown–axle line and bends forward near the dropouts; the suspension fork carries the offset in its crown (stanchions and lowers parallel to the axis, ahead of it by the offset, the arch with them); `rake_dir`, `steer_foot`, `fork_offset` and `trail` for code and tests. Unchanged: the axle (so the wheels, wheelbase, trail – road 57 mm, gravel 64 mm, MTB 117 mm – and the rig: saddle, bars, hands, head tube), the brakes (rim calliper at the crown, disc calliper behind the left blade above the axle) and the physics (nothing in `ocw-sim` or the server reads the fork geometry; it is visual only). All six bike files re-exported on marge (`model export-all`, `--check` clean; the manifest unchanged); the runtime bikes with fitted parts (`build_with`) use the same code. **There is no steering animation:** the front wheel only spins (`riders.rs`: `wheel_wobble` about X), the fork is part of the `bike` node, and nothing turns the bars at junctions – a steering animation (fork, wheel and bars about the steering axis, `Frame::steer_foot` / `steer_dir`) would need a `fork` node in the files and is open.

**Tests:** `forks_are_raked_forward` (every profile: the axis leans back, the axle ahead of it by exactly the design's offset – the sign regression –, the trail in a bike's range, the crown on the axis, the blade's offset only growing downwards and never ahead of the crown–axle line) and `exported_bikes_have_forward_raked_forks` (every committed file: the front hub where the frame puts it, its offset from the head angle's axis, the fork's cross-section ahead of the axis at the dropouts and, on rigid forks, under half the offset halfway down – fails on the old files with 0.79 × the offset). **Screenshots** (`test-output/fork-rake/before/` and `after/`, X11 and Wayland on marge, `scripts/fork-shots.sh`): each bike from the drive side in the Studio's model viewer, its front end close up, the workshop's bike stand and riding from the side.

#### 15M – Built: Blender on marge, the round trip and `make models-diff` (v5.10)

**What was built (branch `worktree-agent-aba757ec954e4a338`, 2026-11-19):**
- **`make deps-blender` (Q4):** `scripts/deps-blender.sh` installs the official Blender release – **5.2.4 LTS** (the LTS of 2026), the one place where the version and the SHA-256 of `blender-5.2.4-linux-x64.tar.xz` (from the release's own `blender-5.2.4.sha256`) are pinned – from download.blender.org into `~/.local/opt/blender-5.2.4`, links `~/.local/bin/blender` and prints the version; no sudo, nothing outside the home; it downloads next to the target (never into `/tmp`), checks the SHA-256 before unpacking and moves the release in place in one step; run again it only checks the link; a new pin installs next to the old version. Installed on marge (2026-11-19: `Blender 5.2.4 LTS`). Linux x64 only (marge); elsewhere it says so.
- **The round trip (15F), `make test-blender`:** `scripts/blender-roundtrip.py` takes every file of the manifest (`MODELS="bikes/*"` limits it): one `blender -b --factory-startup` runs `tools/blender/roundtrip.py`, which imports each `.glb` into an empty scene and exports it with the preset of `artwork/3dmodels/README.md` (glTF Binary, +Y up, modifiers applied, custom properties, materials, no Draco, the vertex colours kept; options this Blender lacks are named); then `ocw-assets model import` takes each export back under its own manifest entry into a copy of the model folder (so it replaces the file as it would in `artwork/3dmodels/`), and `model diff --ignore-manifest` against the committed file must be empty. It writes `summary.md` (the failures with the stage, the known cause and what differs; the files per folder), `roundtrip.log` (every command) and `results.json` into `test-output/blender-roundtrip/DATE/` with a line in `test-output/index.md`; exit 1 when a file fails. Without Blender it is skipped with a notice (`--require` makes that a failure). `make test-blender` also runs the scripts' own tests.
- **What the round trip needed in `ocw-assets`:**
  - **`model diff` compares meshes as drawn:** the triangles with their corners (position, normal, colour, UV) in any order, from any corner, with the same winding; re-indexed, split, merged or unused vertices are no change (the vertex count stays in the totals line); normals within 2e-3 (about 0.1°: Blender moves them by up to 7e-4) and colours within 5e-3 (Blender keeps vertex colours as 8-bit sRGB, `BYTE_COLOR`: up to 0.003) count as the same. A changed mesh says what alone explains it: `normals`, `colours` or `positions` (the shape, the winding or the UVs). `--ignore-manifest` compares only the models.
  - **`model import` keeps what Blender drops:** Blender's glTF importer loses the asset's `extras` and the copyright (node extras survive as custom properties), so a bike's `extras.ocw.frame` / `sizing`, a plant's `height_m`, `pick`, `species`, `variant` and a wearable's `anchor` / `rider_node` were lost; the import now keeps the keys of the file it replaces that the import lacks (never overwriting one it brings) and names them in its notes.
  - **The validator warns of vertex colours above 1** (`mesh.color-above-one`, per node): Blender clamps them.
- **`make models-diff` (15D):** `scripts/models-diff.sh` lists every `.glb` / `.gltf` under `artwork/3dmodels/` that differs between the merge base with `main` (`BASE=…`) and the working tree – committed, staged, unstaged or untracked – and prints its `model diff` (the old file from git, an LFS pointer smudged into the model), the added files (with copyright and extras), the removed ones and the manifest lines changed; `MACHINE=marge` stages the old files here (`--stage`, a tar) and diffs them there (`--staged`), for a coordinator that does not build.

**Results on marge (Blender 5.2.4, 189 files, 15 s):** **114 files without a structural change** – the 6 bikes, the rider and its far model, the 72 wearables, the phone and 33 of the 108 plant files. **75 plant files fail at the diff**, all with a known cause: 63 have vertex colours above 1 (the crown shading, up to 1.098; Blender clamps them: `colours`), 21 have normals Blender rewrites (`normals`: on the needle crowns of spruce, larch and Douglas fir about 20 triangles each come back pointing straight up; on the agave, the date and slender palms and the banana, leaf normals turned away from their triangle's front come back turned to it); 9 have both; none moved in shape (`positions`). Q11 asks how to fix the plant generator. The bikes, riders and helmets also have normals turned away from their face here and there (wheels, shoes, helmet edges) – Blender keeps those, so the turned normal alone is not the cause and the validator does not warn of it. Summary: `test-output/blender-roundtrip/`.

**Tests (11.4):** `scripts/test-deps-blender.sh` (a fake release on a `file://` mirror: install, the link, no second download, a missing link restored, a wrong SHA-256 refused without leaving anything, a new pin next to the old one, `--print-version` is the pin); `scripts/test-models-diff.sh` (a throwaway repository with LFS models where git-lfs is installed: nothing changed, a committed change with its structural diff, a removed file, an untracked new one, a manifest entry changed alone, the staged form gives the same output, an unknown base exits 2); `diff`: re-indexed, split and turned triangles with unused vertices and normals 5e-4 off are the same mesh, a vertex moved by 1 mm, a flipped triangle and a normal 1° off are changes with what moved, an index out of range is a change; `import`: the extras Blender drops are kept from the replaced file without overwriting; `check`: the colour warning.

**Since then:** v5.54 (15P) brought the plants back unchanged (219 of 221), v5.62 the unicorn's head and the rider's lips (**221 of 221**: every model file survives Blender). A triangle without area, or a smooth normal far from Blender's own corner-angle normal, is what Blender rewrites; a normal turned away from its face alone it keeps.

**Open:** ~~Q11 (the plant files)~~ decided (a) and built (v5.54, 15P); the Blender sources (`artwork/3dmodels/sources/`, Q1: `tools/blender/glb_to_blend.py`) are not made yet – for the plants nothing waits any more; marge has no `git-lfs`, so `test-models-diff.sh` checks the LFS path only where it is installed (deb); the Khronos `gltf_validator`.

#### 15P – Built: plant files that survive Blender (Q11 (a), v5.54)

**What was built (branch `worktree-agent-a11958feda96480f3`, 2026-11-23):** the plant generator was fixed as decided in Q11 (a) and the 108 plant files were exported again (`export-flora`); **all 108 now come back from Blender 5.2.4 unchanged** (`make test-blender`).
- **The shading kept at most 1 – `extras.ocw.shade_scale`:**
  - The crown's vertex colours are its shading: up to 1.098 × the paint colour on the sunlit side.
  - `Model::fit_shading` (`ocw_assets::model`) divides every vertex colour of a file by the factor that brings the brightest to 1, rounded up to 1/1000, and writes it as `extras.ocw.shade_scale`. On 63 files it is between 1.01 and 1.098; the other 45 have no colour above 1 and get no key.
  - `Model::shade_scale()` reads the factor back (1 without the key; clamped into 1 – 2). The renderer multiplies every vertex colour of the file by it: `flora_files::draw`, the same code in the desktop and the browser app. OCW Studio's viewer does the same (`models_view::tri_mesh`).
  - Drawn, every colour is the one before, within the float's precision.
  - Blender drops the asset's extras. `model import` keeps the key from the file it replaces (15M), so the round trip keeps it.
  - The contract (15B *Metadata*, `artwork/3dmodels/README.md`) names the key. The validator rejects a `shade_scale` that is not a number or lies outside 1 – 2 (`extras.shade-scale`, an error).
- **Every leaf triangle has its normals on its front (`ocw-render::flora`):**
  - **Blades (palm fronds, the banana's leaves, the agave, the dead fronds; also the ferns of the ground detail, which use the same blade):** both faces already were their own triangles, but each face carried the other face's normal (the upper face's normal pointed down, the lower face's up). Now each face has the normal of its own front: `tangent × side` for the upper face, the opposite for the lower one.
  - **The blade's tip is one vertex.** Before, the last segment closed on two vertices at the same point: two triangles without area per blade (on each face).
  - **Needle tiers (spruce, fir, Douglas fir, larch near; the far cone of every conifer):** the underside and the upper side met at a shared rim, and its normal pointed down, away from the upper side's front. That is why Blender turned about 20 triangles per tree straight up. Now `two_sided_cone` draws each side with its own rim vertices and normals (+7 vertices per tier near, +5 far).
  - The bark keeps its normals: the tube caps' rims stand at right angles to the cap, which Blender keeps.
- **Triangles (budget per plant file: 2,000 in all, 200 in `lod1`; before → after, the whole file / `lod1`):**
  - date palm 532 → 468 / 64 → 52;
  - slender palm 284 → 248 / 64 → 52;
  - banana 112 → 92 / 48 → 40;
  - agave 188 → 150 / 20 → 10 (the triangles without area at the tips are gone);
  - every other plant is unchanged.

  Both faces of a leaf were already there, so nothing was added and every file stays well within its budget.
- **Files:** 83 of the 108 plant files changed (the other 25 had neither a colour above 1 nor a tier or blade), and the manifest is unchanged. `export-flora --check` and `model export-all --check` are clean.

**Round trip (marge, Blender 5.2.4, `make test-blender`):**

- Summaries: `test-output/blender-roundtrip/2026-11-23-135447/` (before), `…/2026-11-23-142216/` (after).

**What looks different:**
- **The shading (shade_scale):** nothing. The broadleaf woods of Liechtenstein, July and November, near and far, are the same picture before and after. The far / near crown rule of v5.44 (`flora::crown_form`) is unchanged.
- **The normals:** the leaves that had the wrong normals are now lit from their own side.
  - Banana plantations and palm crowns seen from above are sunlit green where they were in shadow before.
  - Fronds seen from below are in shade where they were lit before.
  - The upper rims of the spruce and fir tiers are a little lighter.

- `ocw-render::flora_files`:
  - `no_plant_file_has_a_vertex_colour_above_one`: the export and the shipped files; the scale in 1 – 1.1, the same in both, exactly 63 files scaled, no colour warning.
  - `leaf_normals_are_on_the_triangles_front`: every `leaf`, `needle` and `dry` triangle has an area and every corner normal is on its front (cos > 0.05), in the export and the shipped files.

  - The existing `plants_from_files_are_the_generators_plants`, drawn through `shade_scale`, still matches the generator.
- `ocw-studio` `plant_colours_are_drawn_times_the_shade_scale`.
- The Blender round trip of the plants: `make test-blender`, above.

**Built after it (v5.62): the unicorn's head and the rider's lips survive Blender too – `make test-blender` 221 of 221.** The two causes were not the same as the plants':
- **The unicorn (`creatures/unicorn-winged.glb`, `head` and `head_lod1`):** the ears (near and far) and the far horn were `unicorn::tube` with an end radius of 0 – a frustum whose top ring was one point, so each cone had a side triangle and a top-cap triangle per side **without area**, with zero normals (20 near, 20 far). Blender gives such a triangle a normal of its own. A tube with end radius 0 is now a cone: one tip vertex, sides and base (`unicorn::cone`). Triangles: near 3,014 → 2,994 (head's coat 160 → 140), far 682 → 662 (coat 54 → 42, horn 16 → 8); the creature budget is 3,500 / 800. Bounds and area of every part are the old ones, so the look is the same: the triangles that went were never drawn.
- **The rider (`riders/rider-body.glb`, `face_lip_lower`):** two things. (1) The mouth's dark inside (in `face_lips` and `face_lip_lower`) was a coarse smooth ellipsoid whose normals lay behind four of its triangles each (cos down to −0.06): Blender keeps those, but they are against the rule. (2) What Blender actually changed: the lower lip's smooth normals were area-weighted, Blender's own are weighted by the corner angle; Blender stores a custom normal relative to its own, and where the difference lay within 0.8° of the reference edge's direction it snapped it onto that edge – the normal came back 0.002 off (just over `model diff`'s 2e-3) at six vertices. Both lips and both copies of the inside are now **smoothed by corner angle** as Blender does (`mesh::Shape::smooth_by_angle`), so Blender stores the normals as its own and gives them back exactly – and by angle the inside's normals all lie on their triangles' fronts (cos ≥ 0.35), so no vertex had to be split (same vertices and triangles as before). The upper lip did not fail, by chance; it gets the same treatment. The lips move by up to 8° in normal at a few vertices of their 1-cm-wide rims; on the screen the same.
- **Files:** only these two changed (`model export-all --check` clean); the far rider (`rider-body-low`) has no lips.

**Tests (11.4):** `ocw_assets::unicorn` `every_triangle_has_its_normals_on_its_front` (the generator and the shipped file: every triangle has an area and its face's normal; a cone is a tip and a base, facing out); `the_parts_match_the_old_generated_unicorn` with the head's coat (near, far) and the far horn at their new counts and vertex centres (same bounds and area); `ocw_assets::rider` `the_lips_normals_lie_on_their_triangles_fronts` (both lips' nodes, the generator and the file: every triangle has an area and its normals on its front, cos > 0.05; every normal is the corner-angle one); `ocw_assets::mesh` `angle_weighted_normals` (the weighting; the mouth's inside has normals behind a triangle by area and none by angle); the lips' mouth frames (`the_lips_open_in_their_own_nodes`: the inside hidden when closed, showing when open) and `ocw-render`'s `the_lips_move_while_heard_speaking` unchanged and green; `make test-blender` 221 of 221 on marge.

**Open:** the Blender sources of the plants (Q1, `tools/blender/glb_to_blend.py`) can now be made.

### Phase 16 – OCW Studio: the editor for models, worlds and routes (planning, 2026-11-15; the E1 core – the studio shell – built v4.03, see 16A; the Routes workspace (E1) and BRouter (E2) built v4.27, see 16D; the Models workspace's view (E3) built v4.71, see 16B; its edits (E4) built v5.45, see 16B *Built (E4)*)

**Goal (asked by the user, 2026-11-15):** an editor in which one can:
- view and edit the 3D objects of Phase 15;
- view and edit the **world packages** (4);
- **import, edit and export GPX tracks** in a world;
- plan routes with the help of **open routing planners** (BRouter / bikerouter.de, GraphHopper and similar).

The technical and licence check is in 16E. The editor uses the game's own renderer, so what one sees there is what the rider sees.

**Logo (v4.66):** the studio has its own icon, `artwork/logos/ocw-studio.svg` – a horn-gold pencil drawing the rainbow on drafting paper, the sibling of the game's unicorn logo – on Windows (exe resource, taskbar), Linux (window icon, app id and desktop entry `ocw-studio`) and macOS (`OCW Studio.app` with its own `.icns`); 11.3 *OCW Studio's icon*.

#### 16A – Shape of the editor (proposal; Q1)

- **A separate desktop app, `apps/studio` (`ocw-studio`).**
  - It is built from the same crates as the game:
    - `ocw-render` draws the models and the world exactly as in a ride;
    - `ocw-ui` and `bevy_egui` (already in the workspace) provide the panels;
    - `ocw-assets` handles models (Phase 15), and `ocw-world` packages, the road graph, GPX, map matching and graph routes;
    - `world-builder`'s library builds packages.
  - Why separate and not a mode of `ocw-desktop`:
    - the editor needs files, many panels, a mouse workflow and long builds;
    - the game stays small and kiosk-safe;
    - both share every crate, so no code is duplicated.
  - **Test ride:** a button that starts `ocw-desktop --world <edited package> [--route <edited route>]`, or the shared client in a window inside the studio, on the local server.
- **Three workspaces** with one 3D view and a 2D map view:
  - **Models** (16B);
  - **World** (16C);
  - **Routes** (16D).
- **Navigation:**
  - an orbit camera for models;
  - in the world, the **unicorn flight controls** of Phase 13 (the same `ocw-ui::god` input, without the unicorn) plus a top-down 2D map (roads, land use, buildings from the package, the ortho colour map where present; never online tiles, 4).
- **The document core is Bevy-free and tested: a new crate `ocw-edit`.**
  - It holds the open documents, a selection, and **edit operations as commands with undo / redo** (an unlimited history per document, saved with the session).
  - It has dirty flags, autosave to `<data dir>/ocw/studio/autosave/`, and the validators run on every change: the Phase 15 model contract, the world patch checks of 16C, and route continuity.
  - The Bevy app only shows and sends commands, like `ClientCore` in the game (10).
- **Platforms:**
  - Linux first, then Windows and macOS, like the game (11.1).
  - A **browser version** later (Q4): the core is wasm-safe. Files would go through the File System Access API and downloads; world builds run on the server.
- **Built (v4.03, stage E1 core – the studio shell):**
  - **`crates/ocw-edit`** (Bevy-free, wasm-safe, in `make test-wasm`):
    - `Document<D>` over a `DocumentKind` (the content type, its `Op` enum, `apply` returning the exact inverse, `merges`, `contains`): commands with **unlimited undo / redo** per document; consecutive operations that `merges` accepts (a drag, typing a name) are one undo step while they come within 1 s and the step is not sealed;
    - **dirty flags** by history state ids that are never reused (undoing back to the saved state is clean again, redoing to it too; a merge into the saved step is a change); `mark_saved`, `needs_autosave`, `autosave_due` (changed and left alone for 5 s);
    - a **selection** per document (not in the history; it drops what a change removed) and **validators** that run after every execute, undo and redo (`Finding`: severity, message, target);
    - `Session`: the open documents of every kind (`AnyDocument`), the active one (undo / redo of the Edit menu act on it), `autosave` of all that are due;
    - **autosave**: one JSON record per document – content and the whole history, so undo / redo work on after a restore – in an `AutosaveStore` (`DirStore`: `<data dir>/ocw/studio/autosave/`, written to a temporary file and renamed; `MemoryStore` for tests and later the browser); record names `world-<file>-<FNV-1a hash of the path>.json`;
    - `ocw_edit::world`: the World workspace's document (`WorldDoc`: the package opened – spec, id, version – and the **saved views**, named camera positions; `WorldOp` add / remove / rename / move with their inverses; the `check_views` validator). **The world patch operations of 16C (E5) plug in as further `WorldOp`s or a document kind of their own**; nothing of the patch format is assumed.
  - **`apps/studio` (`ocw-studio`)**: `--world PATH.ocwpkg` (or File → Open world… with a path field, or `studio open PATH`), loaded and verified like the game (`ocw_worldstore`: signature, trust, the installed neighbours) and drawn by `ocw-render` exactly as in a ride (the game's `PackageWorld`, now built by the shared `ocw_ui::worlds::package_world`; `RideView` without riders, as a free ride);
    - the **3D view** flown with the **unicorn's controls** (the shared `ocw_ui::god::{flight_keys, pad_flight}` and `input` mapping, `ocw_sim::god::Flight` over the terrain, buildings and tree crowns, inside the world set's bounds) as the renderer's first-person flight camera, no unicorn drawn; the mouse looks while a button is held over the view; *hover* by default (the camera stays put without input), *plane* in View → Flight or with `--plane`; the 3D camera draws into the window's free middle (its viewport), the panels have their own camera;
    - the **2D map** of the package (right panel): the land use as a colour raster (one texel per land-use cell, coarser above 2048 texels a side), the buildings as triangles from 6 m per point in, the road graph's roads by class (minor ones only zoomed in), the camera's position and heading, the saved views, a scale bar and "© OpenStreetMap contributors"; drag pans, the wheel zooms at the pointer, a double-click flies the camera there; never online tiles; **Fixed (v6.07):** the land use was missing (a dark home area) because its texture was made once in the frame the console gave egui's primary context to another camera – into the old context, whose textures bevy_egui drops with it; the texture (`map::LandTexture`) is now made in the context that draws the map, again when that context changes, and at most the context's largest texture side (`fit_raster`), and the aerial tiles of an old context are dropped too;
    - **map labels (v4.77, *Map labels*):** the place names of the package's section `PLCE` (4.7) on the 2D map, a dot and the name above it with a dark halo, sized and weighted by rank – cities 18 points bold, towns 15 bold, villages 13, hamlets and suburbs 11.5, neighbourhoods 10.5, localities and isolated dwellings 10, up to 20 % larger as the map zooms in past the rank's threshold – and drawn from a zoom on: cities always, towns from 150 m per point, villages from 40, hamlets and suburbs from 15, neighbourhoods from 8, localities from 4 (`ocw_world::places::label_style`). **Decluttering** every frame (`ocw_world::places::layout_labels`, pure): the labels whose place is in view are taken in priority order – rank, population (in factors of two), shown in the last frame, distance to the view's centre, index – and one is drawn only if its box (+2 points) overlaps no box drawn before it, so the smaller places disappear first when it is crowded and appear as the map zooms in; **hysteresis**: a label that was not shown needs 4 points more free space to appear, and a shown one is preferred over a new one of the same rank and population class, so panning (which moves all boxes alike) never swaps two labels and labels only go by leaving the view or by a more important one coming in. Tests: a crowded set keeps the cities and the town and drops most villages with no two boxes overlapping, zooming in reveals villages and hamlets, the same input gives the same output, 40 panning steps drop no label that stays in view; the section's round trip, newer layouts and fields, old packages without it, the builder on an OSM XML fixture of made-up places (nodes, a closed way, a two-way multipolygon, a nameless place, a place off the tiles). The game's HUD navigation map (3.2 *Navigation map*) draws the same places with the same `layout_labels` at its own zoom levels. **Peaks and passes (v5.03):** the package's section `LMRK` (4.7) adds the peaks – a brown triangle on the summit, the name and elevation beside it ("Teide 3715 m") – and the passes (a dot, ")( Col del Teide 2294 m") from 40 m per point in (with the villages), laid out in the same pass with rank 3 (after the towns and villages, with the hamlets; the higher first); viewpoints are not drawn (`landmark_candidates`, test: the town first, the highest peak and the pass named, crowded peaks dropped, no overlap). Open: the name language (the `name:*` are stored, the maps show `name`);
    - **neighbours, border and aerial photo on the 2D map (v6.02, 16H Q15 (a)):** the **neighbouring packages the game joins on** (2.2.2; found and verified as the game does, `ocw_worldstore::neighbourhood`, the skeletons the studio loads for its 3D view anyway – no tiles, nothing more read for the map) are drawn **dimmed** under the package: their region a dim ground, their roads from the joined graph half way to the map's background and 20 % thinner, their outline and name grey; they are not pickable (picking reads the open package's graph; a click inside a neighbour edits nothing). **The world's own border** is a thin light line with a dark halo, from the region (`REGN` rings and holes cut to its box, as a `--bbox` part of a `.poly` covers only that; else the box; without a region the tiles' extent), so the map shows whether it simply ends there – nothing beyond it, as for Liechtenstein and Tenerife – or a neighbour joins (the Black Forest's middle between north and south). A neighbour **signed by a user key not trusted here** is neither joined nor opened (16H Q14): only the box its manifest states is drawn, dashed orange, "<world> – unknown key ('<claimed name>'), not opened" (`unknown_key_neighbours`, which reads the manifests only). **The aerial photo** – the package's orthophoto corridor (`ORTC`, 4.7) – is a layer **off by default**, switched with View → *Aerial photo (O)*, the key O or `studio layer aerial on|off|toggle` (disabled where the package has none); while on, the corridor tiles in view are decoded by two background threads, nearest the map's middle first, into one texture per 1 km tile at about one texel per point (64 … 2048 a side; the coarser level stays until the finer one is there), the corridor weight as alpha, drawn over the land use and under the roads; at most 192 MB are kept (the least recently drawn go first) and above 8 m per point the map says "zoom in". `studio layer [aerial|neighbours|border] [on|off|toggle]` (no argument: the states), `studio map-fit [all]` and View → *Fit the world and its neighbours*. Tests: `unknown_key_neighbours` (a user-signed neighbour listed and not joined, joined and no longer listed once trusted), the middle of three packages with both neighbours and their roads, the border from a region box, a polygon with a hole and the tiles, the unknown-key outline, the layers (aerial off by default, on / off / toggle), a corridor tile decoded with its weight as alpha and its missing chunks transparent, the texture level per zoom; screenshots (`scripts/studio-map-shots.sh`, `test-output/studio-map-q15/`);
    - **panels** (`bevy_egui`): the menu bar (File, Edit with *Undo …* / *Redo …* named after the step, Ctrl + Z / Ctrl + Shift + Z / Ctrl + Y, View), the workspace tabs **Models / World / Routes** (Models and Routes are placeholders), the **World** workspace with the package facts (region, id, version, signing and trust – verified, unofficial with the claimed signer, unsigned, untrusted –, origin, bounds, extent, tiles, area, elevation, roads – edges, km, vertices –, buildings, routes, the package's sections with their sizes, time zone, joined neighbours, file size, credits), the saved views (rename, go, set, delete; *Save the camera's view*), the validator's findings, and the autosave offer (*Restore* / *Discard*) when an earlier session left one; the status line (last message, changed, findings, the autosave folder); the window title marks unsaved changes;
    - the UI only **sends commands** (`StudioCommand`, carried out in one place, like `ClientCore`): undo, redo, views, open, fly; the console has them as `studio undo | redo | status | open PATH | fly X Z [H] | view add [NAME] | list | go ID | delete ID`; the autosave runs every frame for what is due and at quit;
    - shared with the game rather than copied: the window-system log (`ocw_render::platform`), `--screenshot` (`ocw_render::autoshot`), the package facts (`ocw_worldstore::details::WorldDetails`, the World menu's *About this world*);
    - tests: `ocw-edit` (undo / redo sequences, 200 random sequences of commands, undos, redos, seals and saves checked against a replayed model and undone to the empty document, merging, dirty tracking, validators on every change, the selection, autosave round trips through a memory and a directory store, records of another kind or format refused), the studio's pure parts (map raster, view pan / zoom, package rows, flight view, the document commands, autosave restore / discard, title and status line), and a headless screenshot (`OCW_PACKAGE=ocw-studio drive.sh shot-wayland …`, archived in `test-output/`).
  - **Still open in E1:** the **Routes workspace** (**built in v4.27**, 16D *Built*); saving a world document (**built in v4.21**: its file is the world patch, 16C *Built (E5 step 2)*; the views stay in the autosave); the trust dialog for a package signed by an unknown user key (**built in v6.00**); neighbouring packages, the world's border and the aerial photo on the 2D map (**built in v6.02**, above); Windows / macOS checks of the studio.

#### 16B – Models workspace

- **View:**
  - any model of `artwork/3dmodels/` or a `.glb` / `.gltf` file;
  - turntable and orbit, day / night / overcast light (the Phase 9 light model), a ground plane, wireframe, normals;
  - per-material and per-node highlighting;
  - LOD switch (`lod1`, billboard) with the switching distance shown;
  - **gizmos** for anchors (`anchor_*`), hotspots (`hs_*`) and collision proxies (`col_*`).
- **Stats:** triangle and vertex counts against the kind's budget (15B), bounds, file size, and the validator's findings live (errors, warnings, and "fix" buttons where the fix is clear, for example renaming `wheel_front.001`).
- **Edit (what the studio does; simple mesh tools since Q5, no full modeller):**
  - **Node edits:** transform nodes with a move / rotate / scale gizmo and snapping, rename nodes to contract names (a picker of the kind's required and optional names), re-parent, delete.
  - **Points and proxies:** add or move anchors, hotspots and LOD nodes; add collision proxies (box, cylinder, capsule).
  - **Materials:** assign paint slots to materials (picker of `ocw_assets::slots`), edit default colour, metallic, roughness and emissive.
  - **Metadata:** edit `extras.ocw` (kind, id, profile, species, …) and the manifest entry (licence, source, author; 13 rules).
- **Simple mesh tools (Q5, stage E4b):** select faces or parts, extrude, move / scale / rotate parts, delete, flip and recompute normals, merge vertices – undoable, contract and budgets checked live. **Larger shape work stays in Blender.** *Open in Blender* exports an editable copy (15D `model export`) and starts Blender with it when it is installed. On return, the studio watches the file and re-imports it (15D `model import`), keeping the studio's own edits (names, slots, anchors, proxies) where the new mesh still matches them.
- **Try it on:**
  - a helmet or glasses on the rider, at each body build;
  - a catalogue part on each bike's hotspot (8.2);
  - the rider on the bike in the riding poses (`ocw_assets::pose`, the animations of 2.6);
  - the unicorn's wing and gallop cycles on its named nodes;
  - a prop or plant placed in a world scene, with season and weather switchable.
- **Save:** the canonical `.glb` and manifest entry through the Phase 15 writer (deterministic bytes), and `model diff` against the last committed version.

- **Built (v4.71, stage E3 – view; branch `worktree-agent-a64cacd30a467fa11`):**
  - **The browser:** every entry of the model folder (`--models DIR`, `OCW_MODELS`, `artwork/3dmodels` in the working directory, else the embedded models), grouped by folder in the order of the kinds (`parts/<slot>/` its own group), searched by every word in the id and the kind's keys (profile, species, variant, anchor); or a `.glb` / `.gltf` file by its path (checked as its `extras.ocw` or its folder says). `ocw-studio --model ID|FILE` starts in the workspace with it. A folder's changed file is read again within a second (an export from Blender shows at once).
  - **The viewer:** the model on its own render layer with its own camera (the world camera rests meanwhile): orbit (drag), pan (right / shift drag), zoom (wheel), turntable, *Frame*; the light presets **day, dusk, night, overcast** from the Phase 9 light model (`ocw_sky::light` at the preset's sun, overcast with `ocw_weather::light`'s cloud light of the weather preset), the background its horizon colour; a ground plane; **wireframe** and **normals** as line meshes; **highlighting** a node (and what is below it) or a material from the node tree, the material list or a finding; the **level of detail** by the camera's distance with the game's switching distance shown (bikes, riders and wear 40 m – `riders::LOD_DISTANCE_M`; plants 270 m – the middle of `vegetation::NEAR_FADE_M`), or `near` / `lod1` / `billboard` chosen (billboard disabled while no file has one); **gizmos with labels** for `anchor_*` (yellow, with axes), `hs_*` (cyan) and `col_*` (red: box, cylinder or capsule from the proxy's mesh bounds, else its node's unit shape) at their nodes' transforms.
  - **Stats:** triangles against the kind's budget (bikes and riders the whole file, as the validator counts) and `lod1` against the far budget as bars, vertices, nodes, materials, size and bounds, the kind's origin, the file size (over 2 MB marked), the licence.
  - **The validator's findings, live** (15J's `ocw_assets::check` on every open and reload): errors and warnings with their code and the **fix as a hint**; a finding about a node or a material highlights it. E4 applies them (with undo, see *Built (E4)*); `model import` applies the normalising ones.
  - **Try it on:** a **wearable on the rider** at its anchor (head, torso, hands) for every body shape (the seven of 4N) and height 150 – 205 cm, the rider standing at ease, the rider's own piece of the same function hidden (helmet off for head wear, `hair-…` hides `hair_*`); a **part at a bike's hotspot** `hs_<slot>` of each of the six bikes (no part file is committed yet: M3); **the rider on a bike** (a rider or a bike opened) with the game's fit to the height (`BodyFit::sized`, the saddle moved) in nine riding poses of `ocw_assets::pose` (hoods, tops, drops, tuck, standing, arms up, sit up, the throw, a stop), pedalling at 85 rpm; **a plant or prop in a small scene** (six of them on grass, turned and sized) with the **seasons** (spring, summer, autumn, winter: the crown tinted by `ocw_render::flora::crown_colour`, a deciduous crown off in winter, snow on the ground) and the light presets as the weather's light.
  - **The console:** `model open ID|FILE | list [WORDS] | info | show wireframe|normals|ground|gizmos|labels|turntable on|off | light day|dusk|night|overcast | lod auto|near|lod1|billboard | select node N|material M|none | orbit YAW PITCH [DIST] | zoom DIST | frame | try off|rider SHAPE [CM]|bike PROFILE|ride PROFILE [POSE] [SHAPE] [CM]|scene SEASON | pose POSE`.
  - E3 was view-only; E4 adds the model document (below).
  - **Tests (11.4, 16G):** the browser's groups, order, sorting and search; **every committed model opens without an error and with no error finding**, and its kind's try-on is accepted; the orbit, the light presets (day brighter than dusk and night, overcast without hard shadows), the level switch at the game's distance; **gizmo positions are the node transforms** (every bike's hotspots, the rider's anchors, a proxy through a write and read); the tree and the stats against the budget; **try-on placement at the anchor for every body shape and height** (the head wear on the scaled head, the torso wear at the torso's girth about its centre, the scene's offset the same); parts at every bike's hotspots; the rider fitted and posed on every bike in every pose; the wire and normal lines; the seasons' tints; files outside the folder; the console's lines. **Screenshots** (Wayland, headless weston on marge, `scripts/models-workspace-shots.sh`): `test-output/models-e3/` with its `index.md`.

- **Built (v5.45, stage E4 – edit; branch `worktree-agent-a6f5aa9dab2456bee`):**
  - **The model document** (`ocw_edit::model`): the model as the Phase 15 reader gives it, its manifest entry and a **stable id per node** (a delete, an insert or a re-parent renumbers the nodes, the ids stay; a new node takes the largest id plus one, so undo gives back the identical document). Opening a model in the viewer opens its document in the studio's session (the active one in the Models workspace: undo / redo, dirty flags, autosave as for worlds and routes); every change goes back to the viewer – a transform alone moves the drawn nodes, anything else rebuilds the model – with the findings, stats and gizmos of the edited model.
  - **Operations with exact inverses:** a node's transform (consecutive drags of one node merge into one undo step), name, parent (*keep its place*: the local transform is worked out from the model-space one; else it moves with the new parent; the list is re-ordered so parents stay first, undo restores the order), insert and remove (a subtree with its places), node `extras`, a material, the asset's `extras`, the copyright, the manifest entry (its file and kind stay), the whole content replaced (a slot merge, a re-import) and batches (*Fix all*).
