#### 16G – Tests (11.4)

- **`ocw-edit`:**
  - every command applies and undoes to the identical document (property tests over random command sequences);
  - autosave restores;
  - validators run on change.
- **Routes:**
  - GPX fixtures (the existing ones plus planner exports from BRouter and GraphHopper, saved as files) import, match and export again with the same edge list;
  - drag and via-point edits keep continuity;
  - the built-in planner finds known routes in the test packages and respects the profiles (a road-bike route avoids gravel where a path exists);
  - the GPX we write reads back in our reader and passes an XML schema check.
- **Planners:**
  - the HTTP clients are tested against recorded responses (no network in unit tests, 11.4);
  - a live test against the self-hosted BRouter on marge runs in `make test-studio-planners` (**built v6.18**, 16D);
  - the hosted services are never called by tests.
- **World patches:**
  - each operation on the pilot package gives the expected change: an edge's surface, a profile point's height, a placed object at `Terrain::height`;
  - a patch survives a rebuild from a newer extract, and missing targets are reported;
  - an identical patch gives a byte-identical package (`scripts/world-profile.sh`).
- **The studio:**
  - headless screenshots of each workspace (X11 and Wayland via `drive.sh`, an `ocw-studio` target) and a short video of a route being dragged;
  - archived in `test-output/` and sent as single pictures.

#### 16H – Open questions (to the user)

- **Q1 – Separate app or a mode: decided (2026-11-15, dashboard: "ocw-studio as its own desktop app"):** `apps/studio` (`ocw-studio`), its own desktop app on the shared crates (16A).
- **Q2 – World editing: decided (2026-11-15, the user: "(b) and (c), make world shareable with user key"):** edits are **world patches on the sources** applied by `world-builder` at build (16C (b)), plus the **"Fix in OSM"** link for real map errors (16C (c); never an automatic upload). A user-edited package is **signed with the user's own key and may be shared**: others add that key to trust it, and the World menu shows such packages as *unofficial* with the signer's name; official packages stay signed by our root after review of the patch.
- **Q3 – Planners: decided (2026-11-15, the user: "use brouter and leave the server to choose open for now"):** **BRouter is the first external planner** (MIT). The server is a **setting with no default** (`route.planner.brouter_url`, empty): the rider enters one – a self-hosted BRouter, a friend's, or brouter.de for personal use; no server is built in until its operator agrees (brouter.de publishes no usage policy) or we host one (B8 stage 2). Checked 2026-11-15 with one request to brouter.de: `…/brouter?lonlats=LON,LAT|LON,LAT&profile=trekking&alternativeidx=0&format=geojson` answers GeoJSON (track length, ascent, time; elevation per point) with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so the **browser app can call it directly** as well as the desktop. Self-hosting on marge stays possible for tests (marge is not reachable from the internet). GraphHopper, Valhalla, OSRM, openrouteservice stay later options behind the same `RoutePlanner` trait. **Plan (not started):**
  - `ocw_world::plan` – the `RoutePlanner` trait (via-points + profile → polyline with optional elevation), the built-in planner on the package's road graph (default), and the result → HMM map matching → graph route (the existing `matching`, `graph_route`); pure, wasm-safe;
  - the BRouter client in `ocw-client` (native HTTP / browser `fetch` behind one async interface): URL and profile from settings (`route.planner`, `route.planner.brouter_url`, `route.planner.brouter_profile`: trekking, fastbike, safety, MTB, gravel as the server offers), a clear User-Agent, timeouts, at most one request at a time, GeoJSON parsing, errors shown plainly;
  - **in the game before the studio exists:** *Navi → Plan route* next to GPX import – start, via points and end picked on the world's 2D map or by name, the planner chosen (built-in / BRouter), the result shown with its unmatched sections and profile, then ridden; console `route plan --via LAT,LON … [--planner builtin|brouter] [--profile P]`; the studio (16D, E2) reuses the same code;
  - privacy (12): the via-points leave the device only when the rider picks BRouter, and the app says so on first use; attribution "Routing: BRouter, © OpenStreetMap contributors" with every planned route;
  - tests: the trait and the built-in planner on the test packages; GeoJSON parsing from recorded BRouter answers (no network in unit tests); matching a recorded Vaduz–Malbun BRouter track onto the Liechtenstein graph; a live test against a configured server only on request (`make test-planner-live URL=…`).
- **Q4 – Browser studio: decided (2026-11-15, dashboard: "a browser version later"):** desktop first; the browser version comes later (after E5, as proposed) – the core `ocw-edit` stays wasm-safe for it.
- **Q5 – Mesh editing: decided (2026-11-15, dashboard: "add simple mesh tools in the studio (extrude, scale parts)"):** the Models workspace (16B) gets **simple mesh tools**: select faces / parts of a node, extrude, move, scale and rotate parts, delete, flip normals, recompute normals, merge vertices – with undo, the model contract (15B) and the budgets checked live; anything beyond (sculpting, UV unwrapping, retopology, rigging) stays in Blender. A new stage **E4b** after E4.
- **Q6 – A road closed for bikes (world patches, E5): decided (2026-11-26, the user): neither (a) nor (b) – "put warning signs, but let it be ridable": a road closed for bikes stays drawn and rideable, with warning signs at its ends; built (v6.47): the road stays in the network, a "no bicycles" sign stands at each end beside the carriageway facing the approaching rider, older patches' roads come back** – in OCW Studio the world is edited through a **world patch**: a file of changes – remove a road, change its surface, raise it – applied when the world package is built. One change is *closed for bikes*. Today it takes the road out of the rideable network, as OSM's own `bicycle=no` does, so the road also disappears from view – an odd gap, e.g. in a town. Options: (a) a closed road stays drawn, with a barrier sign at its ends, and junctions offer no exit onto it (a new flag in the road network); (b) keep it as now – closed means gone. Proposal: a.
- **Q7 – A patch target that is gone in a build (world patches, E5): decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a), our official builds fail on it with `--strict-patch`, users' own builds only warn; built (v6.47): `package --strict-patch` from `scripts/world-patches.sh`, a red warning in the studio's Build dialog** – a world patch points at roads by their OpenStreetMap ids. When a world is built again from newer OSM data, a road the patch changes may no longer exist, because it was deleted or redrawn in OSM. Today the build reports it and goes on, so that change is quietly lost. Options: (a) our official builds fail on it (a `--strict-patch` flag in our build scripts) so someone fixes the patch, while users' own builds only warn; (b) always only warn. Proposal: a.
- **Q8 – Height points and the gradient limits (world patches, E5): decided (2026-11-25, the user): (a), the user's height wins, as built** – a world patch can contain **height points**: the user says "the road passes this spot at this height", and the road's profile bends to it over about 100 m. Normally the builder smooths each class of road to a maximum gradient (4.3). A height point does not apply that limit again, so a steep ramp the user wants stays as asked, and the build report says what moved. Options: (a) keep it so – the user's height wins; (b) limit the result to the class's gradient and report the difference. Proposal: a.
- **Q9 – Shipping the patch with the package (world patches, E5; the ODbL offer of 16C Licences): decided (2026-11-25, the user): (a), built (v5.99)** – the patch goes next to the package as `<package>.ocwpatch` (a stack as `<package>.2.ocwpatch`, …), the manifest's optional `patches` list records each file's name, size and SHA-256, `world-builder publish` and `scripts/prepare-world-release.sh` ship it; a missing or changed patch is a warning in the report and not shipped, never a load failure (4.7 *World patches*). *Was asked:* a package built with a patch contains data derived from OpenStreetMap, so under OSM's licence (ODbL) the changes must be offered with it (16C *Licences*). How does the patch travel with the package? Options: (a) as its own file `<package>.ocwpatch` next to the package, its checksum (SHA-256) in the package's manifest, copied by `world-builder publish` and into the release zips; (b) inside the package as an extra section. Proposal: a.
- **Q10 – Where our official patches live (world patches, E5): decided (2026-11-25, the user): (a), built (v5.99)** – `worlds/<region>/patches/` for Liechtenstein, the Black Forest and Tenerife with a README each; the build scripts take them through `scripts/world-patches.sh` and read the old `data/<region>/patches/` with a notice (16C *Signing and trust*). *Was asked:* the project's own patches – fixes we apply to the official worlds – were planned in `data/<region>/patches/` (16C), but the `data/` folder is not in git (it holds the large downloads), so they would be neither versioned nor reviewed. Options: (a) a folder in git, `worlds/<region>/patches/`, reviewed like code; (b) keep them in `data/` and copy them by hand. Proposal: a.
- **Q11 – Defaults for height points (world patches, E5): decided (2026-11-25, the user): (a), keep 15 m and 100 m, as built** – when the user clicks to place a height point (Q8), it snaps to a road within **15 m** of the click, and its correction fades out over **100 m** along the road. Both can be changed for each point. Options: (a) keep 100 m and 15 m; (b) other values, e.g. a shorter blend for small fixes. Proposal: a.
- **Q12 – The studio camera's default (E1): decided (2026-11-25, the user): (a), hover by default** – OCW Studio's 3D view flies with the unicorn's controls in two modes: *hover* – the camera stays where it is when no key is pressed, handy while editing – and *plane* – it keeps flying forward as the unicorn does in the game. Options: (a) hover by default, the plane under View → Flight or `--plane`; (b) the plane by default, as in the game. Proposal: a.
- **Q13 – Saved camera views in the studio (E1): decided (2026-11-26, the user): (b), the views are stored in the world patch file and shared with it; built (v6.47): an optional `[[view]]` section, autosaved views move into the file on its next save, a patch opened with views offers them** – in the studio one can save named camera views (bookmarks such as "Vaduz") to jump back to. Today they are kept per user in the studio's autosave, not in the package. Options: (a) keep them per user in the studio session; (b) store them in the world patch file, so they are shared with the patch; (c) drop them. Proposal: a.
- **Q14 – Opening a package signed by an unknown user key in the studio (E1): decided (2026-11-25, the user): (a), the studio asks with the game's trust dialog and uses the same trusted-keys list; built (v6.00)** – every world package is signed. The official worlds are signed with the project's key, which every app knows. A world that a user edits in OCW Studio and shares is signed with **that user's own key** (4.7 *User keys*), which another computer does not know yet. Example: a friend fixes a few roads round Vaduz in their studio and sends you `liechtenstein.ocwpkg`, signed "Ada Rider". In the **game**, choosing that world opens the trust dialog – the world's name and version, "signed by 'Ada Rider' (unverified name)", the key's fingerprint in large digits (to compare with the friend, e.g. by phone), the data sources – with *Trust this key* (remembered, listed in Settings → Account → Trusted world keys), *Load once* (until the app quits) and *Cancel* (focused). In **OCW Studio** today, *Open package* on the same file only shows the loader's error ("untrusted key"), so the friend's world cannot be opened to look at or edit further unless the key was first trusted in the game. A damaged file or a bad signature is refused in both apps and never asked about – the question is only about an intact world by a key not trusted yet. The game keeps the trusted keys once per computer (`<data dir>/ocw/trusted-keys.json`); the studio does not read that list yet. Options: (a) **the studio asks with the same trust dialog as the game** – *Trust this key*, *Load once*, *Cancel*, the fingerprint and the claimed name shown alike; a key trusted there is trusted in the game too; (b) **the studio refuses** and says "trust this key in the game first (Settings → Account → Trusted world keys)" – one place where trust is granted, but an extra round trip for every new key. Either way the studio's *Build package* signs the result with the studio user's own key, not with the friend's. Proposal: a – the same dialog, one shared list, no detour through the game. **Built (v6.00):** *Open package*, `studio open` and `--world` check the package first (`ocw_worldstore::consent_needed`); an intact package by a user key not trusted here opens the game's trust dialog – the shared menu page `ConfirmTrust` with its keys, pad, mouse and touch input (`ocw_ui::menu`, `ocw_ui::trust`), drawn over the 3D view; Esc and Start open no game menu in the studio – and the package opens after *Trust this key* or *Load once*. Both apps read and write the same file (`ocw_worldstore::userkeys::default_path`: `$OCW_TRUSTED_KEYS`, else `<data dir>/ocw/trusted-keys.json`, one function for both apps, so the same `<data dir>`; the studio's loader read that file before but could not add to it). The studio's console has `world trust list | add | remove | show | accept | once | decline`. *Build package* is unchanged: it passes no key, so the friend's key never signs the result (signing with the studio user's own key is still open, 4.21).
- **Q15 – More on the studio's 2D map (E1): decided (2026-11-25, the user): (a), the joined neighbouring packages drawn dimmed where there are any, and the aerial-photo colour map as a layer to switch on and off; the world's own border drawn as a thin line, so it shows whether the map simply ends there (no neighbouring world: nothing beyond it, as now) or a neighbour joins; built in v6.02** (16A *Built*, *neighbours, border and aerial photo on the 2D map*; a neighbour by an unknown user key is drawn as a dashed outline marked "unknown key", never opened) – the studio's 2D map today draws the package's land use, roads, buildings and the camera. It does not show the neighbouring packages (the next region, which the game joins on) or the aerial-photo colour map. Options: (a) also draw the joined neighbouring packages, dimmed, and – where the package has it – the aerial-photo colour map as a layer that can be switched on and off; (b) keep it to the package alone. Proposal: a.
- **Q16 – Loading the patch next to a package (studio, E5): decided (2026-11-26, the user): (b), the studio asks first whether to load the patch; built (v6.12):** the shared dialog style (page `ConfirmPatch`), after the trust dialog, *Load it* focused, *Open without it*, never remembered, `studio patch load | skip`, `--patch ask|load|skip` – when the studio opens a package, it at once loads the patch file `<package>.ocwpatch` next to it, if there is one, so the user's earlier changes show (as built). The user may not notice that what they see includes a patch. Options: (a) keep it, with a notice "patch loaded: N operations" and Undo to unload it; (b) ask first whether to load the patch. Proposal: a.
- **Q17 – Where Build package writes and what it runs (studio, E5): decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a), `patched/` next to the package and a build recipe shipped with each official package, so the studio runs the full chain when the source data is there; built (v6.12):** `<package>.recipe.toml` (`ocw_world::recipe`, its SHA-256 in the manifest's `recipe`), written by the build scripts (`world-builder recipe write`), shipped by `publish` and the release script; the studio runs the whole chain when the named sources are found, else the basic step with a note – *Build package* in the studio applies the patch and builds a new package. Today it writes `patched/<name>.ocwpkg` next to the original and runs only the basic package step (`world-builder package`), not the further steps of our official builds (routes, calibration, forest and vegetation), so a user's package lacks those. Options: (a) keep `patched/` next to the package, and ship a small build recipe with each official package – the steps, their arguments and the sources named – so the studio can run the full chain when the source data is there; (b) only the basic step for users. Proposal: a.
- **Q18 – What a road edit acts on by default (studio, E5): decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a), the whole OSM way by default, the single edge as the switch; built (v6.12):** the whole way highlighted and edited by its tags, *this edge only* as the switch, edge edits of older patches still applied and edited on their edge – a road in OSM is a *way* – often hundreds of metres through several junctions; OCW splits it into *edges* between junctions. When the user clicks a road in the studio and changes it, today only the clicked edge changes, with *the whole way* as a switch. Options: (a) the whole OSM way by default – way edits change OSM's tags, so rideability and the road's look follow, and they survive newer OSM data better than edge ids – with the single edge as the switch; (b) keep the edge by default. Proposal: a.
- **Q19 – Where the studio's routes go so the game lists them (Routes, E1): decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a), and documented in the README; built in v6.08** (16D *In the game*; no browser equivalent: the browser app reads no folders, it lists the package's own routes) – in the studio's Routes workspace a route can be drawn or imported and saved: *Save route* writes it as `<package folder>/routes/<name>.ocwroute`, and *Test ride* starts the game on it. The game's own route list (Ride → Change ride) does not read that folder yet, so a saved route is not offered there. Options: (a) the game lists the package's own routes plus every `routes/*.ocwroute` next to the package, and `<data dir>/ocw/routes/` for routes without a package folder, marked as the user's; (b) only `<data dir>/ocw/routes/`. Proposal: a.
- **Q20 – The planner settings in the game's settings (Routes, E2): decided (2026-11-26, the user): (b), the studio keeps its own `planner.json` and the game gets its own planner settings when it gets *Navi → Plan route*; the studio's file as built** – route planning has three settings: which planner (the built-in one, or BRouter, an external route-planning server), the BRouter server's address (empty until the rider enters one) and its profile (trekking, fastbike, …). The studio keeps them in its own file, `<config dir>/ocw/studio/planner.json`, because the game's settings list cannot yet hold a text that may be empty. Options: (a) when the game gets *Navi → Plan route* (Q3), the three move into the game's `settings.toml`, shared by game and studio; (b) keep the studio's file and give the game its own. Proposal: a.
- **Q21 – Asking before via-points go to a BRouter server (Routes, E2, 12): decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a), the answer remembered per server in the planner settings; built in v6.18** (16D *Built (v6.18)*) – planning with BRouter sends the route's via-points – the places the rider wants to pass – to that server, which is private data (12). Today the studio asks once per server and session with a tick box "Send the via-points to SERVER …", and again when the server changes. Options: (a) remember the answer per server in the planner settings, so a self-hosted server is asked about only once; (b) ask every session, as built. Proposal: a.
- **Q22 – The self-hosted BRouter on marge for tests (E2, 16G): decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a), the routing data built on marge from our own OSM extracts and elevation data; built in v6.18** (16D *Built (v6.18)*) – to test planning with BRouter without a public server, we run BRouter on our build machine marge during the planner tests. BRouter needs routing data for the region (its `rd5` files). Options: (a) build that data ourselves from our own OSM extracts and elevation data with BRouter's map tool on marge, run the server only during `make test-studio-planners`, and check that a planned Vaduz – Malbun route matches the Liechtenstein package; (b) download the ready files once from brouter.de, a third-party server. Proposal: a.
- **Q23 – Via-points of an imported track (Routes, E1): decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a), keep one every kilometre, as built** – when a GPX track is imported into the studio, it gets a via-point – a handle that can be dragged – every kilometre, so dragging one re-plans only the kilometre around it. Options: (a) keep 1 km; (b) fewer, e.g. every 5 km, or only start and end – a drag then re-plans the whole track; (c) one at every turn of the track. Proposal: a.
- **Q24 – The level-of-detail distance of props, creatures and workshop pieces (Models, E3): decided (2026-11-24, the user): (a), built (v5.75, 16B *Built (Q24)*)** – models have a simpler version (`lod1`) that is drawn when they are far away. The game switches bikes, riders and their wear at 40 m and plants at 270 m; props (benches, signs, …) and the workshop pieces have no switch distance yet, and the unicorn switches at 80 m in the game (Phase 13C; kept when it became a file, Phase 15 M4, v5.16) but not in the studio, so the studio's *auto* view shows their simple version only when it is chosen by hand. Options: (a) props switch at 60 m, the unicorn at 40 m like the riders, workshop pieces never, since they are only seen up close – set in the renderer when props and the unicorn are drawn from their files (MX, M4); (b) other distances; (c) a rule by size on screen for all kinds. Proposal: a.

### Phase 17 – ANT+ sensors: heart rate first (planning 2026-11-18; A1 – A3 built 2026-11-26 without hardware, v6.50; Q8 decided; Q7 open)

**Goal:** heart rate from ANT+ straps through an ANT USB stick in the desktop app, as a second `DeviceBackend` next to BLE (3.4.1 has the hardware, the protocol, the licensing facts, the Rust design and the integration). Asked by the user (2026-11-18): *"plan for ANT+ heart rate sensor support"*. The base it lays (codec, stick service, channels, search, reconnect) carries power meters, speed / cadence and FE-C trainers (3.4.1 *Later scope*; Q5: power and FE-C in this phase). **Status:** A1 – A3 are built and tested without hardware (17D); the real-stick run (A4) waits for a stick (Q2); power is decoded already, FE-C, the torque pages and WebUSB are the next steps (17E).

#### 17A – Milestones (proposal; effort in agent time)

- **A1 – Codec, channel and heart-rate decoder (pure):** `ocw-devices::ant::{codec, channel, hr}` with their unit tests; builds for wasm. About **0.5 day**.
- **A2 – Stick service, runner and USB link:** `ant::stick`, `ant::runner` with the supervise loop, the mock stick, `AntLink` over `nusb` (native), `AntDevice: DeviceBackend`, `ant::scan_live`, the `ant` example (`sticks | scan | monitor`). About **0.5 – 1 day**.
- **A3 – Desktop integration:** `DeviceIo` with ANT, the Devices page (transport in the value, *ANT+: no stick*, *network key needed* if Q1 says so), `devices.toml` `transport = "ant"`, reconnect at start, the heart-rate source rule (Q6), the new `FailReason`s; the desktop flow test with a mock ANT stack. About **0.5 – 1 day**.
- **A4 – Hardware step (needs a stick and an ANT+ strap, Q2):** on marge (Linux, X11 and Wayland): plug in, scan, connect, ride 10 min, take the strap off and on (reconnect), unplug the stick (reconnect), a second strap if there is one; the captured messages become test fixtures; then Win11Builder (WinUSB, Q7) and the Mac. About **0.5 day on Linux + 0.5 day Windows / macOS**, once the hardware is there. **We have no ANT stick today** – the user has to say which one to buy or lend (Q2).
- **A5 – Browser (only if Q3 says so):** an `AntLink` over WebUSB in `ocw-devices::ant::web` (as `ble::web`), *Add an ANT+ stick* in the browser's Devices page. About **1 day** plus a Chromium hardware run.
- **A6 – FIT `device_info` for ANT sensors (optional):** source type, device number, manufacturer, product, battery. About **0.25 day**.

Total for heart rate on the desktop (A1 – A4): about **2.5 – 3.5 agent days**; with A5 / A6 about 4 – 5. Each milestone with tests, full checks on the build machines, merge and deploy as usual (11.4).

#### 17B – Tests (11.4: no step without tests)

- **Codec:** encode → decode round trips for every message we send; checksum and length errors dropped; the stream decoder resyncs after garbage, split reads and two messages in one read; byte-exact setup messages against the values of the protocol document (channel ID with device type 120, period 8070, frequency 57, the search timeouts, lib config `0x80`).
- **Channel state machine:** the setup sequence waits for each response; a failed response (e.g. `CHANNEL_IN_WRONG_STATE`) ends with `Failed`; search → tracking → `EVENT_RX_FAIL` (value kept) → `EVENT_RX_FAIL_GO_TO_SEARCH` (`Disconnected`) → tracking again (`Connected`); search timeout and channel closed → reopened after `RECONNECT_DELAY`; the device number learned from extended data on a wildcard channel, and from a requested channel ID on a stick without extended messages.
- **Heart-rate decoder:** pages 0 – 7 with the toggle bit; a legacy strap (no toggling; only bytes 4 – 7 used); computed heart rate 0 → no sample; beat time and beat count rollovers; RR intervals from page 4 and from consecutive messages, none across a missed beat; staleness after 5 s without a new beat; manufacturer / product / battery pages. **Fixtures:** the examples of the ANT+ heart-rate profile document and published captures where their licence allows (to be found in A1), replaced or joined by our own captures from A4; until then hand-made sequences that follow the profile.
- **Mock stick runner:** a scripted stick (answers, broadcasts, events) in-process – two straps on two channels, a strap lost and found, the stick unplugged and back (all channels reopened), the stick busy (*busy with another app*), no permission; scan with exclusion lists finding three straps one after the other.
- **Desktop flow:** as the BLE flow test (`devices::DeviceIo` mock): scan lists BLE and ANT+ devices together → connect an ANT+ strap → remembered with `transport = "ant"` in a temp `devices.toml` → next start reconnects; old files without `transport` read as BLE; a BLE and an ANT+ strap together give one heart-rate source (Q6 rule).
- **Wasm:** `ant::{codec, channel, hr, stick}` in the `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` of `ocw-devices`.
- **Hardware (A4):** `cargo run -p ocw-devices --example ant -- scan` / `monitor` on the build machine with the stick, and the Devices page driven headless as `scripts/test-devices-menu.sh` does for BLE (screenshots per step, sent to the user and kept for the art project).

#### 17D – Built (A1 – A3, 2026-11-26, v6.50; without hardware)

- **A1 – decoding (`ocw-devices::ant`, pure, builds for wasm):** `codec` (the messages we send, byte-exact against the protocol values – channel ID with device type 120, period 8070, 57, the search timeouts, lib config; the stream decoder with resync, split reads, padding; `Debug` never shows the network key), `channel` (the setup one command at a time, each waiting for its response; failed response or 2 s without one → failed; searching → tracking → missed → lost → found again; closed; exclusion lists; the channel ID requested on sticks without extended data), `hr` (the pages with the toggle bit, legacy straps after 10 messages without a toggle, computed heart rate 0 = none, beat time / count rollovers, R-R from page 4 or consecutive beats, none across a missed beat without page 4, staleness after 5 s, manufacturer / product / battery), `power` (the power-only page 0x10: average power from the accumulated power over the events, cadence, coasting after 3 s, the common pages 0x50 / 0x52). `NetworkKey` reads the key as people copy it (16 hex digits, spaces, commas, `0x`).
- **A2 – the stick service:** `stick::StickCore` (pure: reset with or without a start-up message, capabilities, the network key, extended data with signal – or ID only, or none; channels handed out to sensors first, then the scan; pages → `DeviceEvent`s; reconnect after the search timeout and `RECONNECT_DELAY`; an unplugged stick fails every sensor with *no ANT stick* and sets them all up again when it is back; a key change sets the stick up again; the scan: a wildcard channel per profile with an exclusion list, each find reported and excluded, the channel reopened until the scan ends). The native service (`AntStick`): one thread over an `AntTransport` / `AntLink`, opens the stick only while a sensor or a scan needs it and closes it 3 s after the last; looks for a stick every 5 s otherwise (the Devices page's state); permission and busy errors are reported neutrally. Transports: `usb::UsbTransport` (`nusb`: `0fcf:1008` / `1009`, interface 0 with the kernel driver detached, the bulk endpoints; feature `ant-usb`, the desktop turns it on) and `SimTransport` (`ant::sim::SimRadio`: a simulated stick that answers like one and broadcasts simulated straps and power meters at their periods, with the toggle bit, background pages, R-R timing, the signal, missed messages, lost sensors, search timeouts; it hears sensors only with its key, so a wrong key finds nothing; one program at a time). `cargo run -p ocw-devices --features ant-usb --example ant -- sticks | scan | monitor ID` for A4 (the key from a file `OCW_ANT_KEY_FILE` names, never printed).
- **A3 – the desktop:** `DeviceIo` has the stick next to Bluetooth (`--ant-sim hr:N:BPM,power:N:W` a simulated stick, `--no-ant` none); one scan runs both; an `ant:` id connects through the stick; remembered with `transport = "ant"` and reconnected at the start. Devices → **ANT+ (USB stick)** shows the stick (*no stick*, *cannot open the stick (permission)*, *busy with another app*, *network key needed*) and **Enter the network key**: a field typed like Ride → Join's (shown as `*` only, with the count of hex digits; Enter saves, Esc cancels, Ctrl+V pastes), kept in `secrets.toml [ant]` (mode 0600, never in `ocw.toml`, the console or the log; `network_key` is in `SECRET_KEYS`); *Remove the key*. Device rows say *ANT+*. **Two heart-rate sources** (Q6 (c)): only one heart rate is used – the one chosen with **Use for heart rate** (`devices.hr ID`, saved as `heart_rate` in `devices.toml`), else the first device that sent; when the source disconnects, the ride has no heart rate (no switching, no frozen value); a stale ANT+ strap sends 0 = none. The heart rate takes the BLE path from there (`ClientCore`, samples, HUD, FIT, workouts, multiplayer, the sensor bridge to a browser).
- **Tests:** unit tests of every layer (the list of 17B, with the simulated stick in place of a mock stick: two straps on two channels, a strap lost and found, the stick unplugged and back, busy, no permission, no key, a wrong key, three straps found one after the other plus a power meter, a stick without extended data or start-up message, a key change, a strap going stale); the service on its thread (scan, connect, unplug, reconnect, closing when unused); the menu model (ANT+ row, the key page, *Use for heart rate*); the desktop end to end with the simulated stick (the key entered and kept in `secrets.toml` with mode 0600 and nowhere else, scan, pair, remembered with `transport = "ant"`, the heart rate in the ride and in the FIT records, the next start reconnecting with the saved key, removing the key; a BLE and an ANT+ strap with the choice by hand; a stick without permission named neutrally). Pictures: `scripts/test-ant-devices.sh` (three riders: the Devices page with two simulated straps, the ANT+ page, *Use for heart rate*, the key field, the HUD with the heart rate).

- **Built (Q7 / Q8, v6.66; without hardware):**
  - **Windows, Q7 (d):** `ant::libusb0::Libusb0Transport` drives Garmin's libusb-win32 driver: the libusb-0.1 calls (`usb_find_busses` / `usb_find_devices` / `usb_get_busses`, `usb_open`, `usb_set_configuration(1)`, `usb_claim_interface(0)`, `usb_control_msg` GET_DESCRIPTOR for the configuration – the first bulk IN / OUT endpoints of interface 0, else 0x81 / 0x01 –, `usb_bulk_write` / `usb_bulk_read`, `usb_release_interface`, `usb_close`) sit behind the `Usb0` seam; on Windows with `ant-usb` it is the system's `libusb0.dll`, loaded at run time with `libloading` (ISC) from the system folder only (`LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32`, where Garmin's driver package puts it; never the app folder) – nothing of libusb-win32 (LGPL) is shipped or linked; only the fields of `usb_bus` / `usb_device` up to the device descriptor are read, whose offsets do not depend on the header's packing. A missing DLL is `DeviceError::StickDriver` ("libusb0.dll not found: Garmin's ANT driver is not installed", loaded again on the next try); `-EBUSY` → busy, `-EACCES` / `-EPERM` → permission, `-ENODEV` → unplugged; read timeouts (116, 110, 138) are no data. `ant::Fallback` tries `nusb` (a stick bound to WinUSB with Zadig) first, then Garmin's driver; when neither opens it the error says the most useful thing (busy wins; a stick only `nusb` saw needs a driver) and the stick's state is *the stick needs a driver* (`StickStatus::NoDriver`, `FailReason::NoDriver`). The Devices page's ANT+ page then has **Driver for the ANT stick** (Windows, for no driver or no permission): its page explains (1) Windows Update installs Garmin's driver, on Windows 11 under *Optional updates* – the usual case for Zwift users –, (2) Zadig / WinUSB as the fallback (Garmin Express and Zwift then lose the stick), and that only one program can use the stick at a time. `examples/ant.rs` opens the stick the same way and `sticks` names both routes. `ocw-devices` denies unsafe code instead of forbidding it, with the FFI module the only exception (as `ocw-xr-openxr`).
  - **Linux, Q8 (b):** `ocw-desktop --install-udev-rule [--replace-udev-rule]` and Devices → ANT+ → **Install access for the ANT stick** (offered when opening fails for permission on Linux; console `ant.access.install`, on a thread while the password dialog waits) install `/etc/udev/rules.d/60-ocw-ant.rules`: `SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="0fcf", ATTRS{idProduct}=="1004|1008|1009", MODE="0660", TAG+="uaccess"` and the same with `SUBSYSTEM=="tty"`. `pkexec /bin/sh -c SCRIPT sh RULE PATH MODE` runs a small root script that gets the rule as an argument (so it works the same from the AppImage, whose FUSE mount root cannot read, and from the tar.xz), refuses a different rule unless asked (exit 3; the user check before is repeated there), writes the file with mode 0644 by rename and runs `udevadm control --reload-rules && udevadm trigger`. The same rule there already: nothing runs (idempotent). A different one: not replaced without asking (*y* in a terminal or `--replace-udev-rule`). No `pkexec`, the dialog dismissed (126) or polkit refusing (127): nothing changes, and the console / terminal shows the rule and the manual command (`printf … | sudo tee … && sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger`). The page keeps the last try's line. There is no `.deb` yet; a package would install the rule file itself.
  - **Tests:** a fake `libusb0` behind `Usb0` (open by ids among other devices, configuration and claim, the message stream on the bulk endpoints, timeouts, the USB2 with other endpoints from the descriptor, no descriptor, not found, the USB1 ignored, a missing DLL said and retried, busy, permission, open failing, unplugged, short writes, closed with the link), the descriptor parser, `Fallback` with the simulated stick (WinUSB first, then Garmin's driver, none → needs a driver, busy) and its error rule; the rule text, installing through a fake `pkexec` that runs the script on a temp file with a fake `udevadm` (mode 0644, the reload and trigger, the rule passed as an argument), idempotence, a different rule kept (also by the script itself) and replaced only when asked, no pkexec / dismissed / not authorised with the rule and the manual command; the menu model (the fix row per system, the driver and access pages, their notes ASCII, the rows' limits) and the desktop with the simulated stick denied (the offer on Linux, *Install access* refused without pkexec, the console with the rule and the command, nothing written). pkexec and udevadm are never run in tests or on the build machines. **Waits for hardware (A4):** a real stick on Windows through Garmin's driver (and through WinUSB), and the rule on a Linux desktop with a real stick.

#### 17E – Next steps

- **A4 – the real stick** (when one is there, Q2): `examples/ant.rs` `sticks` / `scan` / `monitor` on marge with an ANT USB-m and a strap; the 10-minute ride, strap off and on, stick out and in; the captured messages become fixtures next to the synthetic ones; then Windows (Garmin's libusb-win32 driver and WinUSB, Q7 (d), built in v6.66) and macOS; on Linux the `--install-udev-rule` helper with a real stick (Q8 (b), built in v6.66). Unknowns to check there: the USB2's endpoints and whether it needs anything before bulk transfers (the USB2 has native USB in its nRF24AP2-USB, no CP210x – that was the USB1; openant and GoldenCheetah drive `0fcf:1008` and `1009` the same way over bulk endpoints), the RSSI field of real sticks, detaching `usb_serial_simple` (Q8).
- **Power meters, the rest:** connecting a power meter works now (page 0x10, replaces the virtual trainer like a BLE power meter); next the torque pages 0x11 (wheel) / 0x12 (crank) for meters that send no power-only page, calibration (page 0x01, a *Calibrate* row on the device page) and speed / cadence sensors (types 121 – 123, as `gatt::cadence`).
- **FE-C trainers** (Q5 (b)): a profile `AntProfile::FitnessEquipment` (type 17, period 8192) on the same stick core: data from pages 16 (speed, distance) and 25 (power, cadence) → `DeviceEvent::Power`; **control** from the `DeviceCommand`s the service already routes to each sensor (now ignored): `SetSimulation` → page 51 track resistance (gradient, Crr) and page 50 wind resistance (`cw_kg_per_m`, the headwind), `SetTargetPower` → page 49, sent as acknowledged messages (`0x4F`) one at a time, answered by `EVENT_TRANSFER_TX_COMPLETED` / `_FAILED`, retried and replaced by the newest as `ble::protocol` queues FTMS writes; the role *trainer* (it replaces the virtual trainer and takes SIM / ERG); the simulated stick gets a simulated FE-C trainer that follows the pages it is sent. About 1 agent day.
- **The browser** (Q3 (a) + (b)): ANT+ heart rate already reaches a browser through the sensor bridge (the desktop relays every device event, ANT+ ones included); **WebUSB** (A5): an `AntLink` over `navigator.usb` (filter `0fcf:1008/1009`, Chromium) driving the same pure `StickCore` on the page's event loop – the stick core and the simulated stick build for wasm already – and *Add an ANT+ stick* in the browser's Devices page; the key entry in the browser keeps the key in the page's storage only.
- **A6 – FIT `device_info`** for ANT+ sensors (source type, device number, manufacturer, product, battery – the decoder keeps them already).
- **Packaging:** built in v6.66 (17D *Built (Q7 / Q8)*): on Linux the `--install-udev-rule` helper (Q8 (b); its rule covers the USB device and the tty, 3.4.1), on Windows Garmin's libusb-win32 driver (Q7 (d)) with Zadig / WinUSB as the fallback. A `.deb` or distribution package, if one comes, installs the rule file itself.

#### 17C – Open questions (for the user)

- **Q1 – The ANT+ network key: decided (2026-11-26, the user): (b) for now – the user enters the key once (kept in `secrets.toml`), our source and releases ship without it; (c) or (d) may follow later** – many heart-rate straps send over ANT+ as well as Bluetooth; the app would hear them through a small ANT USB stick, which hears ANT+ straps only when given the ANT+ network key, a short code. Garmin, who owns ANT+, shows the key on its developer site *"subject to the ANT+ Adopter Agreement"*, for ANT+ devices only, and its terms say not to publish it or source code containing it; openant (MIT) and GoldenCheetah (GPL) ship it in their source anyway, ant-rs (MIT / Apache) leaves it to the user (3.4.1, with sources). Options – the choice is yours: (a) ship the key in our source; (b) the user enters the key once (kept in `secrets.toml`), source and releases without it; (c) the project becomes an ANT+ adopter (free, with your account) and only release builds carry the key from a build secret, source builds as b; (d) ask Garmin first, b until the answer. Second question: may the app name "ANT+" in its texts (no logo without certification)? Blocks everything that talks to a real strap. Proposal: d, and naming ANT+ in plain text – a suggestion, the spec leaves it to the user.
- **Q2 – Which ANT stick and strap for the tests: decided (2026-11-26, the user): the hardware test is postponed – "postpone the hw test, just prepare and build": everything is built and tested without hardware (decoding against recorded and synthetic ANT+ messages, a simulated stick for the stick service and the Devices page), and the run with a real stick and strap (A4) comes when one is there; which stick is decided then** – no build machine has an ANT stick, so nothing can be tried on real hardware. Which stick do you have or will you buy: (a) an ANT USB-m (`0fcf:1009`, the current Garmin stick); (b) an ANT USB2 (`0fcf:1008`); (c) a clone? And is there an ANT+ heart-rate strap – one that sends both ANT+ and Bluetooth tests Q6 too? Proposal: a, on marge first for Linux, later moved to Win11Builder and the Mac for their checks.
- **Q3 – Desktop only, or the browser too: decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a) and also (b) – the desktop app first (Linux, then Windows, macOS), the browser through the sensor bridge, and WebUSB in the browser too (Chromium browsers; on Windows with the WinUSB driver of Q7)** – the plan builds ANT+ for the desktop app. The browser app could reach a stick through WebUSB (Chromium browsers only, on Windows only with the WinUSB driver of Q7), or get the heart rate from a small helper program through the sensor bridge (Phase 10, 10D.2, planned). Options: (a) the desktop app first (Linux, then Windows, macOS), the browser through the sensor bridge, and WebUSB later if wanted; (b) WebUSB in the browser right away; (c) never in the browser. Proposal: a.
- **Q4 – Priority: decided (2026-11-26, the user): (b) sooner – start now, without hardware (Q2)** – heart rate on the desktop takes about 2.5 – 3.5 agent days. The first three steps (A1 – A3: decoding, the stick service, the Devices page) need no hardware; A4 needs the stick and a strap (Q2). Options: (a) after the open work of the phases in progress, A1 – A3 whenever an agent slot is free, A4 when the stick is there; (b) sooner – before which phase?; (c) later. Proposal: a.
- **Q5 – Heart rate only, or further: decided (2026-11-26, the user): (a) and (b) – heart rate first, and power meters and FE-C (trainer control over ANT+) planned straight away as part of this phase** – ANT+ carries more than heart rate: power meters, speed / cadence sensors, and FE-C, the ANT+ way to control a smart trainer (useful for trainers without Bluetooth). Options: (a) heart rate first (this plan), then decide about power, speed / cadence and FE-C; (b) plan FE-C (and power) straight away as part of this phase. Proposal: a.
- **Q6 – A BLE and an ANT+ heart-rate strap at once: decided (2026-11-26, the user): (c) – only the rider's choice by hand (*Use for heart rate* on a device's page); no automatic switching** – many straps send over Bluetooth (BLE) and ANT+ at the same time, and a rider may have two straps; if the app took both, their values would mix. Options: (a) **one heart-rate source** – the first remembered strap that connects; the other takes over after 5 s without data; *Use for heart rate* on a device's page picks one by hand; (b) always prefer one transport, BLE or ANT+; (c) only the rider's choice by hand. Proposal: a.
- **Q7 – The driver route on Windows: decided (2026-11-26, the user): (d) – drive Garmin's own libusb-win32 driver as GoldenCheetah does (a Windows-only `ant::libusb0` link behind `AntTransport`, the system's `libusb0.dll`, nothing shipped), with Zadig / WinUSB (a) as the fallback; built (v6.66, 17D *Built (Q7 / Q8)*)** – on Windows our app talks to the ANT USB stick through the generic WinUSB driver, which the user binds to the stick with the free tool Zadig; after that Garmin Express, Zwift, TrainerRoad and the other ANT programs no longer see the stick until the driver is rolled back in the Device Manager. Checked 2026-11-26 (3.4.1 *The driver route on Windows*, with sources): the serial route asked about is **not possible** – the ANT USB-m (`0fcf:1009`), the ANT USB2 (`0fcf:1008`) and the CooSpo / CYCPLUS / Anself clones (Dynastream's ids) have **no COM port on Windows**: they have no USB-to-serial chip, and Garmin's own driver, which Windows Update installs (on Windows 11 often only under *Optional updates*), is a libusb-win32 driver; only the old USB1 of 2007 (`0fcf:1004`, a CP2102) was serial, and no baud rate applies to the others. But that Garmin driver can be used directly: GoldenCheetah does so (it loads the system's `libusb0.dll`), with nothing for the user to install beyond what Zwift needs, and Garmin's programs keep working (one program at a time, as always). Options: (a) document Zadig (WinUSB) for now, an installer step later; (b) a serial (COM-port) driver – ruled out by the facts above; (c) use Garmin's closed `ANT_DLL` library; (d) drive Garmin's libusb-win32 driver directly (a Windows-only link next to the WinUSB one: Garmin's driver first, WinUSB if the user bound it with Zadig; about 0.5 day plus the run with a real stick in A4). Proposal: d, with a as the fallback for a stick without Garmin's driver.
- **Q8 – The udev rule on Linux: decided (2026-11-26, the user): (b) – a helper `ocw-desktop --install-udev-rule` that installs the rule after asking for the password with `pkexec`; built (v6.66, 17D *Built (Q7 / Q8)*)** – on Linux an ordinary user may open the USB stick only when a udev rule (a small system file) allows it, or – for the serial route – when the user is in the `dialout` group. An AppImage cannot install such a rule itself. Options: (a) the Devices page shows the one-line rule and the command to install it, and the `.deb` / distribution package installs it itself; (b) a helper `ocw-desktop --install-udev-rule` that asks for the password with `pkexec`. Proposal: a.

### Phase 18 – Traffic: cars, lorries, motorbikes, aircraft and UFOs (planning, 2026-11-26; T1 built (v6.79), T2 built (v6.77), T3 built (v6.78), T6 built (v6.80, 18G); Q1 – Q11 decided)

**Goal:** the world gets traffic that can be switched on in Settings: cars, vans, lorries, buses, motorbikes, tractors and parked cars on the roads; airliners, small planes, helicopters, gliders and balloons in the sky; and UFOs as a fun extra that fits the unicorn of Phase 13. Asked by the user (2026-11-26): *"planning: make a switch in settings for turning on traffic. this are cars, lorries, motobikes planes, helicopters, ufos and such. investigate if its possible to get any real time data on density / jams as well as flight data, eg flightradar24 or similiar."* The traffic is **simulated** from the package's road graph and from statistics; real-time data is looked at in 18D (sources, terms, verdicts). Nothing here changes the riders' physics model (5.2): vehicles are other road users the riders meet, never a source of power or speed.

#### 18A – The setting

- **Settings → Traffic** (both apps, shared page in `ocw_client::menu`, full parity desktop / browser; registry section `[traffic]`, scope *live*, console `set traffic.road normal`):
  - `traffic.enabled` (on | off) – the master switch; off = today's empty roads and sky.
  - `traffic.road` (off | light | normal | busy) – cars, vans, lorries, buses, motorbikes, tractors, parked cars. *Normal* follows the time of day and the day of the week (18B *Demand*); *light* is a quarter of it, *busy* 1.5 ×; never more than the budget of the quality level (below).
  - `traffic.air` (off | simulated | live) – aircraft of 18C; *live* uses real positions where a feed is reachable (18D), falling back to *simulated* without a word of error in the ride (a small "live" / "simulated" label in Settings).
  - `traffic.ufo` (off | rare | often) – 18C *UFOs*.
  - `traffic.sound` (on | off) – vehicle and aircraft sounds (the mixer's existing spatial voices, 3.3).
  - `traffic.live_road` (on | off, default off) – *Live traffic data* (Q5): live road events or density where the world has a suitable source; greyed with "no live data for this world yet" elsewhere. Behaviour, sources and the fallback: 18D *The* Live traffic data *switch*.
  Defaults: Q1. The page shows the source of live data and its attribution (18D) when *live* is chosen.
- **Multiplayer (server-authoritative, 6.1):** two kinds of traffic, treated differently.
  - **Road traffic touches the ride** (it overtakes riders, waits behind them, can be hit in collision mode), so it is **simulated by the game server** and is the same for every rider of a session. It is a **session setting**: on the local server it follows the rider's settings; in a shared session the host sets it (`ServerConfig.traffic_access`: host / anyone / nobody, like `collision_access`, 12A); in organiser-set events the organiser sets it per event; **races default to no road traffic**. Sent in `Welcome` / `EventState` (additive fields, 6.2). A rider cannot hide road vehicles that can touch them; *light* / *normal* / *busy* is the session's choice (Q2).
  - **Aircraft and UFOs never touch a rider** (the unicorn flies through them; no collisions), so they are a **rider's own view setting**: each client draws them for itself. To keep group rides consistent anyway, the server sends one **air seed** in `Welcome` and every client simulates the same flights from it and the world clock (`WorldClock`, Phase 9) – riders who have aircraft on see the same planes in the same places, riders who have them off see none. Live aircraft come through the game server in a shared session (one fetch for all, 18D), so all see the same live picture.
- **How the server simulates and sends road traffic (proposal, Q3 has the alternatives):** vehicles move in 1D along the road graph like riders (distance along an edge, lane offset; 5.2), in a new module `ocw-sim::traffic` (pure, deterministic, wasm). Each vehicle is spawned with a **plan** (kind, look seed, route over edges, desired speed per edge, start tick) sent once (`TrafficSpawn`, about 40 bytes); clients extrapolate it along the graph and the server sends a **plan change** only when the vehicle deviates (it brakes behind a rider, waits, overtakes, stops at a light) and a sparse correction (position, speed) every 2 s for vehicles within 300 m of a rider. Vehicles far from every rider (> 1.5 km) are not simulated at all; they are respawned at the edge of the riders' bubbles so traffic always seems to come from somewhere. Interest management: a client gets only the vehicles within 1.5 km of its rider. Bandwidth estimate: 100 vehicles near a rider ≈ 1 – 2 kB/s, well below a rider's 10 Hz snapshots.
- **Performance budgets** (vehicles drawn at once / aircraft; by the quality level of `ocw-render::quality` and `display.quality auto`):

  | Level | Road vehicles near (≤ 300 m, full LOD) | Road vehicles far (≤ 1.5 km, LOD1 / impostor) | Aircraft |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | High (desktop) | 60 | 150 | 30 |
  | Medium | 30 | 80 | 20 |
  | Low / browser WebGL 2 / iPhone | 15 | 40 | 10 |
  | `quest1` (Phase 14) | 8 | 20 | 6, no contrails |

  Vehicles are **instanced** (one draw call per model and LOD), no shadow casting beyond 100 m, headlights as emissive `bulb` slots (no real lights except the nearest four at night). The server's cost: the car-following step is O(n) per edge; 500 simulated vehicles at 10 Hz (50 Hz within 50 m of a rider) is a budget of ≤ 1 ms per tick on the Fly.io machine (11.5), measured in T3.
- **LOD:** near model (≤ 150 m), LOD1 (≤ 600 m), an impostor beyond (as plants and riders); aircraft above 2 km distance as a lit sprite with navigation lights at night, airliners at cruise as a dot with a contrail.
- **Sound** (procedural, `ocw-audio`, 3.3): tyre roar + engine by kind and speed with Doppler, lorry air brakes, a bus's door, a motorbike's rasp; jets as a delayed rumble (sound arrives at 343 m/s, so a high airliner is heard behind where it is seen), turboprops, helicopter blade slap, a glider's whistle, a balloon's burner. At most the 8 nearest vehicle voices and 2 aircraft voices; everything quieter under wind and rain (Phase 9). No horns by default (Q8).

#### 18B – Road traffic

- **Data from the package (new additive section `TRFC`, written by `world-builder`):** per road-graph edge the OSM class (already in the graph), `oneway` (motor vehicles; `oneway:bicycle=no` only frees riders), `lanes` / `lanes:forward` / `:backward` (already read by the dressing, 4.8), `maxspeed` (with the country's implied limits when untagged: DE 50 in town / 100 outside / no limit but 130 advised on motorways, CH and LI 50 / 80 / 120, ES 50 / 90 / 120, *in town* from `place` areas and `maxspeed:type`), `access`, `motor_vehicle`, `motorcar`, `hgv` (lorries only where allowed, plus `maxweight` / `maxheight`), `bus` / `psv` and the `route=bus` relations (bus lines with their stops, `highway=bus_stop`), `junction=roundabout`, `highway=traffic_signals`, `stop`, `give_way` (nodes and their direction), `parking:lane:*` / `parking:both` / `parking:left|right` (parked cars), `amenity=parking` areas (cars arriving and leaving), and tracks with `tracktype` / `agricultural` for tractors. Roads riders may use but cars may not (cycleways, paths, `motor_vehicle=no`, pedestrian streets) carry no traffic. Package format: an additive section, old packages read as "no traffic data" and get traffic only on roads by class with implied speeds.
  - *Built (T2, v6.77):* `world-builder` writes `TRFC` in `package` and adds it to a built package with `world-builder traffic --world PKG --pbf …` (with `AERO`; the manifest is renewed). The data model is `ocw_world::traffic` (pure, wasm): `TrafficData` (the package's `Country`; `EdgeRules` per edge by stable `EdgeId`; `NodeControl`s sorted by edge and position; `BusStop`s, `BusRoute`s, `ParkingArea`s) and `RoadRules` (the rules the traffic core reads: `RoadRules::of(&package)`, `edge(&Edge)`, `aligned(&graph)` by edge index as `RoadNetwork` numbers them, `controls_on(EdgeId)`; a package without `TRFC` gets `EdgeRules::implied` by class and the country of its time zone). `EdgeRules`: `access` (bits for cars, lorries, buses, motorbikes, tractors; `access` → `vehicle` → `motor_vehicle` → `motorcar` / `hgv` / `psv`, `bus` / `motorcycle` / `agricultural`, `forestry`; tracks are for tractors only unless opened, cycleways, paths and pedestrian streets carry none), `destination_only`, `oneway` (motor vehicles, along the edge: the builder turns the way's forward / backward and left / right round for an edge that runs against its way), `lanes` per direction, `single_track`, `maxspeed` per direction (`SpeedLimit`: km/h, walking pace 7 km/h, no limit with the advised speed), `speed_source` (tagged, typed, implied, default), `country`, `urban`, `maxweight_t`, `maxheight_m`, `parking` left / right (current and old `parking:` schemes), `roundabout`, `no_overtaking` per direction and `flow` (the demand factor of T11, 1 until then); helpers `allows(vehicle, forward)`, `limit(forward)`, `kerb_parking(forward)`, `target_kmh` (a driving guess below the limit on small roads). Implied limits (`Country::implied`): DE 50 / 100 / none (130 advised), living streets walking pace; CH and LI 50 / 80 / 120, living streets 20; ES 90 outside, 120 on motorways, in town 50 with two or more lanes per direction and 30 with one (RD 970/2020, in force since 2021); AD 50 / 90; AT 50 / 100 / 130; FR 50 / 80 / 130; elsewhere 50 / 90 / 120. Typed values (`maxspeed:type`, `source:maxspeed`, `zone:maxspeed`, "DE:urban", "DE:zone30", "CH:trunk", "DE:bicycle_road") set the setting or the limit. *Country* per edge: inside a complete country outline of the extract (`admin_level=2` with its ISO code), else the package's (its outline at the origin, else its time zone). *In town:* within a place's radius (city 1.5 km, town 900 m, suburb 600 m, village 450 m, neighbourhood 300 m, hamlet 150 m), on residential or commercial land use, residential and living streets always. Signals (`highway=traffic_signals`; with `crossing=traffic_signals` or on `highway=crossing` as crossing lights), `stop` and `give_way` nodes: at a junction vertex on every motor arm towards it (signs only on the minor roads), along an edge by `direction` / `traffic_signals:direction` or towards the nearer end. Bus lines: the member ways chained into the driving order, only the part between where the bus enters and leaves a way, roundabouts left to the core; stops by role `stop…`, else `platform…`. Car parks: `capacity`, else 25 m² a car. Layout: the module documentation of `ocw_world::traffic`.
- **Vehicles:** cars (three body shapes: hatchback, saloon / estate, SUV), vans, lorries (rigid and articulated; only on `hgv` roads, mostly trunk / primary / motorway), buses on their OSM lines and stopping at their stops, motorbikes (more on mountain roads on summer weekends: the Black Forest's B500, Tenerife's TF-21 to the Teide), tractors on tracks and country roads in the Black Forest (season of Phase 9: hay and harvest), parked cars (static, at the kerb outside the riding lane), delivery vans stopping briefly in town streets.
- **Behaviour (`ocw-sim::traffic`):** car following with the Intelligent Driver Model (desired speed = `maxspeed` × a per-driver factor 0.85 – 1.05, lower in curves by the curve radius of 4.4 and on wet or snowy roads of Phase 9), lane keeping with the region's side (4.7), junctions by the graph's rules (2.2.1): signals with deterministic cycle times from the tick, roundabouts yield to the circle, `stop` / `give_way`, otherwise the priority of the higher class, and right before left on equal residential roads in DE / CH / LI / ES. Jams appear by themselves where the demand exceeds a road's capacity (a stop-and-go wave on the TF-5 at La Laguna in the morning peak), not by a script.
- **Around riders – polite and legal, never through a rider:**
  - **Overtaking** only with the legal lateral distance (DE: 1.5 m in town, 2 m outside – StVO 5 (4); ES: 1.5 m, and a car may cross the solid line to pass a cyclist; CH / LI: "sufficient", we use 1.5 m), when the oncoming lane is free for the whole manoeuvre and the road allows it (`overtaking=no`, double lines except ES, blind curves by the sight distance along the graph); otherwise the vehicle **waits behind the rider** at the rider's speed with a 10 m gap, and passes later.
  - **A group of riders** is overtaken as one block; on a narrow road a queue of cars may form behind a bunch – that is realistic and harmless.
  - **Junctions:** vehicles always yield to riders, wherever they come from (riders never have to stop; traffic lights are drawn but do not stop riders in this phase).
  - **Oncoming traffic** keeps to its lane; a rider who steers into the oncoming lane (manual steering, wild mode) is met by a vehicle that brakes and swerves as far as it can.
  - **Collisions** only with `ride.collisions on` (12A): a vehicle is a solid body for the collision model (12B: a box from the model's `col_` proxies); the rider can ride into a vehicle (manual steering, wild mode); whether a vehicle can ever hit a rider is Q4. Damage only with `ride.damage on` (12E).
  - **Slipstream and wind:** a lorry passing at speed gives a short side gust (the weather's gust model, Phase 9, a few tenths of a second, a lean wobble of 12B's size); **no drafting behind vehicles** (no help to the rider's power or speed; and it would be unsafe advice).
  - **Autodrive and bots** (12D) see vehicles as obstacles and keep right; the proximity cue (12D) also sounds for a vehicle closing in from behind.
- **Demand – time of day, day of week, season:** the local time of the place (`WorldClock`, `ocw_sky` time zones, public holidays from a small table per region) picks an hourly profile per road class: weekday double peak (07 – 09, 16 – 19), a flatter Saturday, a quiet Sunday morning with more motorbikes and leisure traffic, little at night. The volume per road comes from **open counts where they exist** (18D: Tenerife's daily counts per station, Liechtenstein's permanent stations, the Swiss counters near the border, Baden-Württemberg's counts) and otherwise from the road class (an annual average daily traffic per class, tuned by the counted roads). The counts become a per-edge factor in `TRFC`, built once by the world builder (T11), never fetched during a ride.
- **Riders' physics (5.2, 6.1):** unchanged: a rider never waits for a vehicle – vehicles never block a rider's lane, they wait or pass. In time trials the ghost has no traffic; the session's traffic is deterministic from the seed and the riders' moves, so a replay shows the same vehicles.
- **Models (Phase 15 contract, 15B):** a new kind `vehicle` in `ocw_assets::kinds` (origin on the ground under the centre of the wheelbase; +Z front), files in `artwork/3dmodels/vehicles/` (Git LFS):
  - node names `wheel_fl`, `wheel_fr`, `wheel_rl`, `wheel_rr` (and `wheel_r2_*` for lorries; spun and steered), `rotor_main`, `rotor_tail`, `prop`, `door_*` (buses), `light_head_l/r`, `light_brake_l/r`, `light_indicator_*`, LOD nodes `lod1`, collision proxies `col_box`;
  - paint slots `body` (varied per vehicle by its look seed from a palette of real-world car colours: many greys, whites, blacks, a few colours), `glass`, `tyre`, `chrome`, `bulb` (emissive at night), `reflector`, `livery` (buses: a made-up local operator's colours, no real company);
  - **no brands or real makes** (generic shapes, no logos, made-up names only on buses and lorries – like the rest of the project);
  - budgets: car / van 2,000 near / 300 far, lorry / bus 3,000 / 400, motorbike 1,500 (rider included, wearing our generic kit) / 250, tractor 2,000 / 300, airliner 3,000 / 300, small plane / glider 1,500 / 200, helicopter 2,500 / 300, balloon 1,000 / 150, UFO 1,500 / 200; textures ≤ 512²;
  - **Blender-proof:** every file passes `make test-blender` (15M, the round trip) and the validator; made by our generator or in Blender, licensed like the code.

#### 18C – Aircraft and UFOs

- **Data from the package (new additive section `AERO`):** OSM `aeroway=aerodrome` (with `aerodrome:type`, ICAO code), `runway` (with its heading and length), `helipad` / `heliport` (hospitals, e.g. rescue helicopters), gliding sites (`aerodrome:type=gliding` or `sport=gliding`), plus a list of airports just outside the package that matter for its sky (TFN and TFS for Tenerife, Zurich and Friedrichshafen for Liechtenstein, Karlsruhe / Baden-Baden, Strasbourg and Stuttgart for the Black Forest).
  - *Built (T2, v6.77):* `ocw_world::aero` – `Aero` with `Aerodrome`s (name, ICAO, IATA, `AerodromeKind`: international, regional, airfield, private, military, gliding, ultralight, heliport; position, elevation, `outside`), `Runway`s (reference, ends, true heading, length, width, surface, its aerodrome; from a runway line's ends or an area's farthest corners) and `Helipad`s (`hospital` within 300 m of a hospital or `emergency=yes`, `heliport`). The nearby airports come from a small hand-made table (`aero::NEARBY`, positions and runway headings approximate): TFN, TFS; Zurich, St. Gallen-Altenrhein, Friedrichshafen; Karlsruhe / Baden-Baden, Strasbourg, Stuttgart, Basel-Mulhouse; Andorra-La Seu d'Urgell, Barcelona, Toulouse – those within 170 km of the package's centre that it does not hold itself.
- **Airliners at altitude:** overflights at 9 – 12 km on a handful of airways across the region (from a small hand-made table per region, checked against the real picture of 18D), one every few minutes over the Black Forest and the Rhine valley, fewer over Tenerife's west; **contrails** when the upper air is cold and humid enough (from the weather state of Phase 9: more on clear cold days, none on a warm dry one), fading by wind. Drawn in the sky pass behind the terrain, so the far clip does not cut them.
- **Approaches and departures:** at Tenerife North (TFN, close to the Puerto de la Cruz world) airliners climb out and land on the real runway direction, at 300 – 3,000 m in view of the riders; Tenerife South (TFS) as distant traffic.
- **Small planes:** circuits around small airfields (1,000 ft above the field), a few cross-country flights at 1 – 3 km on fine days; **helicopters:** the heliport of Balzers (Liechtenstein) and rescue flights to hospital helipads (a few a day, generic red-white livery, no real organisation's name); **gliders** near gliding sites on days with thermals (sun, cumulus, Phase 9 weather; afternoons, spring and summer), circling; **balloons** on calm mornings; **paragliders** from known launch sites (optional, later).
- **Flight paths:** splines through waypoints with realistic speeds (airliners 230 – 250 m/s at cruise, 70 – 80 m/s on approach; small planes 50 m/s; helicopters 60 m/s; gliders 25 – 30 m/s, balloons with the wind), all from the air seed and the world clock (18A) – the same for every rider, no server work.
- **Unicorn mode (Phase 13):** the unicorn can fly among aircraft; no collisions, but aircraft show their navigation lights and the sound grows near them; above 9 km the flight panel names the nearest airliner's altitude ("airliner 600 m above"). In *live* mode the flight panel's crosshair names an aircraft's **type class only** (e.g. "jet airliner, 11,200 m"), never its registration or callsign (privacy, 18D).
- **UFOs (`traffic.ufo`, a fun extra):** a classic flying saucer (our own model: a rim of coloured lights, a soft glow, a hum). *Rare*: now and then on clear nights a UFO hovers over fields or a lake far from the road, moves in sudden jumps and vanishes; *often*: also in the dusk and by day high in the sky. **With the unicorn**, UFOs come closer: they follow it curiously at a distance, circle it, flash their lights in its mane colours, and zip away when the unicorn flies straight at them. They never touch a rider, never land on the road, are never in races or events (unless the organiser allows them), and they leave no trace in recordings. Behaviour choices: Q7.

#### 18D – Real-time data: sources, terms and verdicts (researched 2026-11-26, web; road sources checked again in depth 2026-11-26 for Q5; re-check before building)

**Road density and jams.** Our worlds: Liechtenstein (and the Swiss Rhine valley next to it), the Black Forest (Baden-Württemberg; the A5 runs along the western edge of its packages), Tenerife (Canary Islands). What we look for: **live or near-live** density, speeds or jams that our game server may fetch once and turn into a **derived** traffic level for every player of a session (an open-source game, no keys in the source, no per-player cost). The second research pass (2026-11-26, Q5) checked the EU national access points (NAP) under the ITS directive – Germany's Mobilithek, Switzerland's opentransportdata.swiss, Spain's NAP –, the regional and city portals, the partner and "free for open source" programmes and crowd sources. Links were opened on 2026-11-26 unless marked.

*Kinds of data:* **density / flow** (vehicles per minute and speed at a counter, or a level of service per road section) is what drives our traffic; **events** (jams reported as an incident, closures, roadworks, accidents, broken-down vehicles) change single roads; **statistics** (daily, monthly, yearly counts) give the demand profiles of 18B and are no live data.

| Source | Coverage of our worlds | Live? Update rate | Format, access, key | Cost | Licence – may our server pass a derived level to all players? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DGT NAP – incidents DATEX II v3.7** ([dataset](https://nap.dgt.es/en/dataset/incidencias-dgt-datex2-v3-7), feed `https://nap.dgt.es/datex2/v3/dgt/SituationPublication/datex2_v37.xml`) | Spain except Catalonia and the Basque Country, **the Canary Islands included** (NUTS ES7). **Checked:** the feed of 2026-11-26 11:45 held 2,843 records, 29 in the province of Santa Cruz de Tenerife (roadworks with lane closures on the TF-5 and TF-1, short closures, a closed road after a rock fall, broken-down vehicles on the TF-5, TF-82, TF-375 …) | **yes, every minute**; events only (jams as `AbnormalTraffic` when reported, closures, roadworks, obstructions, speed limits) – no counts | DATEX II XML (about 7 MB for all of Spain), plain HTTPS pull, **no key, no registration** (registration optional, for e-mail notices) | free | **CC BY** (named on the dataset page; legal notice [dgt.es](https://www.dgt.es/contenido/aviso-legal/)): use, change and pass on with attribution ("Fuente: DGT"); caching allowed | **Suits us now – for Tenerife's live events** (closures, roadworks, incidents, reported jams), not for density. The first and only source that fits Q5's conditions for one of our worlds today (see *Proposed first step* below). The first pass's "DGT no Canaries" was wrong: it looked at the panels, not the incidents |

That would be the best live density source for Tenerife |

**Road verdict (second pass, 2026-11-26):** one source **suits us now: the DGT incidents feed for Tenerife** – live, every minute, CC BY, no key, no cost; it gives events (closures, roadworks, incidents, reported jams), not density. **Live density** exists for two of our worlds, each behind a registration: the **Swiss A13 counters** next to Liechtenstein (FEDRO TDP: free, a key, six-month access, attribution, no raw relay) and the **A5 motorway** at the Black Forest (Autobahn GmbH on the Mobilithek: free, an account, the provider's approval, a machine certificate); Baden-Württemberg's **traffic reports** (every 10 minutes, DL-DE-BY 2.0) need the same Mobilithek account. Whether to register is Q11. No live density source for Tenerife's roads is open (the Cabildo's live map has no API). Open **statistics** cover all three worlds (Tenerife CC BY, Liechtenstein open with the source named – licence now checked –, ASTRA, BW DL-DE-BY 2.0) and stay the basis of the demand (18B, T11). **Privacy:** only counts, speeds per road and events are used, never single vehicles, cameras or people's tracks.

**Sources that suit us (ranked, 2026-11-26):**

1. **DGT incidents DATEX II (Tenerife; all of Spain but Catalonia and the Basque Country)** – suits us now: live events on Tenerife's roads, CC BY, no key.
2. **FEDRO TDP real-time counters (the A13 next to Liechtenstein)** – live density every minute; suits us once an account and key are accepted (Q11 (b)).
3. **Landesmeldestelle BW traffic reports (all Black Forest roads)** – live events every 10 minutes, open licence; needs a Mobilithek account (Q11 (c)).
4. **Autobahn GmbH Südwest measuring sections (the A5)** – live density every minute, GeoNutzV; needs the Mobilithek account, the provider's approval and a certificate (Q11 (c)).
5. Statistics for the demand profiles (T11, no live data): Tenerife's daily counts (CC BY), Liechtenstein's monthly counts and yearly reports (open, source named), ASTRA (open, source named), Baden-Württemberg's counts (DL-DE-BY 2.0).
6. Watched, not usable yet: the Cabildo's live road map (to ask), the Autobahn API (no licence stated).

**The *Live traffic data* switch (Q5, built with the road traffic; desktop only, Q9):**

- **Setting:** `traffic.live_road` (on | off, default off) on Settings → Traffic, below *Road traffic*; in group rides part of the host's road-traffic choice (Q2), in events the organiser's; never in races. It only matters while road traffic is on (greyed otherwise, "turn on road traffic first").
- **Per world:** the game server keeps a small table of live road sources by world (the package's region box), each with its kind (events / density), attribution and whether it is configured on this server (a source with a key counts only when the key is in the server's secret config – never in the repository or a package). A world without a configured source shows the row **greyed with "no live data for this world yet"**; a world with one shows it switchable with the source and its attribution under it, e.g. *"Live: closures, roadworks and reported jams – Fuente: DGT"* (Tenerife) or *"Live: traffic counters on the A13 – Data source: Federal Roads Office (FEDRO) Traffic Data Platform (TDP)"*. The attribution is also listed in Settings → About → Data sources while it is in use.
- **When on:** the server fetches the source for the session's world (one fetch for all riders, like live aircraft, 18D *Flights*): events every 2 minutes (the DGT feed every minute is more than we need), counters every minute; only while someone rides with it on; with back-off when the source fails. It maps each event or counter to the package's road edges (by coordinates, road ref and kilometre point) and changes the simulated traffic, never the riders' physics: a **closure** – no vehicles spawn on or route over the closed part (riders may still ride it; a "Road closed" sign stands at its ends); **roadworks / a lane closed** – lower desired speeds and one lane, with the queues the car-following model makes from it; a **reported jam** or a **congested level of service** – the demand on those edges and their approaches raised until the model forms a queue of about the reported length, at walking speed for *stationary*; a **live counter** – the demand factor of the counted road and its neighbourhood set to the measured flow divided by the statistic's expected flow for that hour (clamped 0.3 – 2.5), so the whole valley gets busier or quieter with the real one.
- **Fallback:** when the source is down, slow or stale (older than 15 minutes for counters, 30 for events), the traffic quietly goes back to the statistics within a minute; the row says "live data not reachable – using statistics" – no error in the ride.
- **What is kept and sent:** the server keeps only the current fetch in memory (the derived per-edge factors and events), sends clients only what the traffic simulation already sends (vehicles, plus a closure sign as a world object), never the raw feed (FEDRO's terms) and nothing about single vehicles.

**Proposed first step (not built; after T1 – T5 of Q10):** **T13 – Live road events for Tenerife (DGT)**, about 1 day: a `LiveRoadSource` trait (events / density) in the server with a `DgtDatex2` source (pull the v3.7 feed, keep only records inside the world's box, map them to edges, cache), the per-world source table, the greyed / active row and the attribution in both menus' model (desktop only by Q9), the effects on `ocw-sim::traffic` above, the fallback. Tests on a recorded excerpt of the feed (our own fetch, CC BY, with the attribution in the fixture's header): Tenerife's records found and mapped to the right TF-5 / TF-1 edges; a closure keeps every vehicle off the closed part in a simulated hour; a lane closure forms a queue; a stale or broken feed falls back to statistics; the row is greyed for Liechtenstein and the Black Forest; no raw record in any message. The Swiss counters (T14, about 1 day: a `FedroTdp` density source with the SOAP pull filtered to the nine A13 sites) and the Mobilithek sources follow only after Q11.

**Flights (live aircraft positions from ADS-B).**

| Source | Coverage | Cost / free tier | Licence (open-source game?) | API, key | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **adsb.lol** ([OpenAPI](https://api.adsb.lol/api/openapi.json), [API repo](https://github.com/adsblol/api), [plans](https://www.adsb.lol/sponsor)) | worldwide community receivers; good over Central Europe, Tenerife to be measured | free; without a key 500 requests a day per IP, more with a free (feeder / ad-hoc) key; sponsor plans from €20 a month (6,000 a day) | **ODbL** for the API and all its data – the same licence as our OSM data: attribution, share-alike for a derived database | REST / JSON, `/v2/point/{lat}/{lon}/{radius}` (≤ 250 nm); key in `x-api-key` (announced to become required) | **Usable – the first choice** |
| **OpenSky Network** ([API docs](https://openskynetwork.github.io/opensky-api/), [REST](https://openskynetwork.github.io/opensky-api/rest.html), [data licence](https://zenodo.org/records/6325961/files/LICENSE.txt?download=1)) | worldwide research network | free: 400 credits a day anonymous, 4,000 registered, 8,000 for feeders; a bounding box up to 25 square degrees costs 1 credit (5 s resolution) | **research and non-commercial use only**; commercial on request; a game is not clearly covered (to ask) | REST, OAuth2 client credentials (a **secret** on our server) | **Fallback, after asking OpenSky** |

| **airplanes.live** ([API guide](https://airplanes.live/api-guide)) | worldwide community | free, 1 request a second, no uptime guarantee | **non-commercial**; feeder access may become required | REST, no key now | **Fallback for single player**, as adsb.fi |
| **ADS-B Exchange** ([developer hub](https://www.adsbexchange.com/community/developer-hub/), [commercial use](https://adsbexchange.com/?p=19798)) | worldwide | community API non-commercial; personal API through RapidAPI $10 a month (10,000 requests); enterprise for commercial use | proprietary since its sale (2023) | REST, **key** | **Not chosen** (costs, closed terms) |
